Following this story, several commentaries come before us. One commentary comes after the natural covenant; in it is drawn a picture of the condition of the person to whom Allah gave His signs and who then departed from them. For example, the Children of Israel and all the other nations to whom Allah gave His signs but who did not abide by them. This is a commentary in which all the forms, all the movements and all the indications come before our eyes, and scenes and sights like those of Surah al-An'am come before us.

﴿And recite to them the story of him to whom We gave Our signs, but he detached himself from them, so Satan pursued him, and he became of those who go astray. And had We willed, We would have elevated him thereby, but he inclined toward the earth and followed his own desire. So his example is like that of the dog: if you chase him, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants. That is the example of the people who denied Our signs. So relate the narratives that perhaps they will reflect. Evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs, and they were wronging themselves. Whomever Allah guides is the one rightly guided, but whomever He leaves astray — it is those who are the losers. And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind. They have hearts with which they do not understand, they have eyes with which they do not see, and they have ears with which they do not hear. They are like livestock; rather, they are more astray. Those are the heedless.﴾ (7:175–179)

Now direct doctrinal discussions come. Along with the doctrinal discussions, some cosmic evidences and effects are also presented, and people are warned of Allah's punishment and His severe seizing. Their hearts are probed so that they reflect, ponder the signs of Allah, and think about this Messenger and his message.

﴿And to Allah belong the best names, so invoke Him by them and leave those who deviate concerning His names. They will be recompensed for what they used to do. And among those We created is a community who guide by truth and by it establish justice. But those who denied Our signs — We will progressively lead them from where they do not know. And I will extend for them; indeed, My plan is firm. Have they not reflected? There is no madness in their companion; he is not but a clear warner. Have they not considered the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever things Allah has created, and that perhaps their term has come near? So in what statement after this will they believe? Whomever Allah leaves astray, there is no guide for him, and He leaves them in their transgression, wandering blindly.﴾ (7:180–186)

After this, Allah commands the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to inform these people of the nature of his call and the limits of the Messenger's role in this system of life. This statement comes in answer to their question, in which they demanded that he specify the time of the Resurrection with which he constantly warned them.

﴿They ask you about the Hour — when is its appointed time? Say, "Its knowledge is only with my Lord. None will reveal its time except Him. It has burdened the heavens and the earth. It will not come to you except suddenly." They ask you as if you were well-informed about it. Say, "Its knowledge is only with Allah, but most of the people do not know." Say, "I do not possess for myself any benefit or harm except as Allah wills. And if I knew the unseen, I would have acquired much good, and no harm would have touched me. I am but a warner and a bringer of good tidings to a people who believe."﴾ (7:187–188)

After this, the Qur'an explains how the human soul, to which Allah took a covenant that it would remain upon the path of guidance, abandons the belief in tawhid that its nature had affirmed. Here, after describing the abhorrence of shirk and the weakness of the associated deities, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is commanded to challenge them to show how powerless they are.

﴿Say, "Call your partners, then plot against me and give me no respite. Indeed, my protector is Allah, who revealed the Book, and He protects the righteous. And those you invoke other than Him cannot help you, nor can they help themselves. And if you call them to guidance, they do not hear; and you see them looking at you, but they do not see."﴾ (7:195–198)

From here, the address is directed solely to the Messenger ﷺ and continues to the end. It should be remembered that the beginning of the Surah also opened with direct address to the Messenger ﷺ. Here the Messenger ﷺ is instructed on how he is to conduct himself with the people, how he is to advance the call, how he is to overcome the difficulties on the way, and how he is to overcome the plots and harassment of the people. It also shows how he and the believers are to listen attentively to the Qur'an, how they are to remember Allah at all times, and how they are to maintain a connection with Him. It is also explained how the angels remember Allah in His presence.

﴿Take what is easy, enjoin what is good, and turn away from the ignorant. And if an evil suggestion from Satan comes to you, then seek refuge in Allah; indeed, He is Hearing and Knowing. Indeed, those who fear Allah — when an impulse from Satan touches them, they remember, and at once they see clearly. But their brothers (the devils) drag them further into error, and they do not stop short. And when you do not bring them a sign, they say, "Why did you not invent one?" Say, "I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord. These are insights from your Lord, and guidance and mercy for a people who believe." And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent, that you may receive mercy. And remember your Lord within yourself in humility and fear, without loudness of speech, in the mornings and evenings, and do not be among the heedless. Indeed, those who are near your Lord do not disdain from His worship; they exalt Him and prostrate to Him.﴾ (7:199–206)

It is hoped that through this summary and these excerpts the outline of Surah al-A'raf has become clear, and that the distinction between it and Surah al-An'am has also become evident, namely how the two surahs present the same subject in different manners. The subject of both is Islamic belief and the system of life. As for detailed discussion of each topic, it will come in the detailed discussion of the texts, God willing, by Allah's grace and generosity!

(Al-Mas) Alif Lam Mim Sad. The Surah begins with these disjointed letters (huruf muqatta'at). We discussed them at the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah, and likewise at the beginning of Surah Al 'Imran. In explaining them, we preferred the view that they mean this Surah is composed of such letters, and all people use these letters of the Arabic alphabet, yet no one can produce a speech like the Qur'an from this material. This itself is a witness that the Qur'an is not a human composition, because these letters and the words of the Arabic language are before them, yet they cannot produce the Qur'an from them. We have adopted this view as the preferred one; we cannot state anything with certainty. Allah knows best.

In this light, the grammatical structure would be: "Al-Mas" is the subject (mubtada'), and "Kitab unzila ilayka" is its predicate (khabar). That is, this Book, composed of these letters and words, is what We have revealed to you. It may also be said that "(Al-Mas)" is only a signal from which this meaning is derived, and "Kitab" is the predicate, with an omitted subject, i.e., (hadha kitab).

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 7, verse 2 (part 1 of 2):

Verses 1 to 2.

This Book has been sent down to you so that you may warn people, remind them of the lesson they have forgotten, and frighten them of an evil end. Declare clearly to the people the truth that is in it, and do not concern yourself with whether people like it or not. This Book has come precisely to present to people those realities which they do not like. It has come to eliminate false beliefs, customs and wrong relationships, and to confront false systems of government, false laws and false societies. Therefore the path of this Book is full of difficulties. Whoever comes forward with its message must be prepared to face these difficulties. Only the person who takes up its message can comprehend this aspect of the Book, as we said at the time of commenting on the Surah. He must proclaim the ideas of this Book openly and bear the hardships that come in its path. Only the person who sets his goals in the light of its teachings, and who has within himself the resolve to uproot the Jahili society from its roots, its trunk and its branches, and to bring about a complete transformation and revolution in its place, can understand this truth, just as the first bearer of this Book, Muhammad (ﷺ), took it up, brought about a revolution in the world, confronted tyranny (taghut) and Jahiliyyah (the state of ignorance and pre-Islamic barbarism), and first transformed the Arabian Peninsula and then the whole world.

This attitude towards the Book was not confined to the revolution that came about in the Arabian Peninsula and its surroundings at that time, because Islam is not an incident or a piece of history, such that it occurred during one period of history and people then began to record it in history. Islam is rather a permanent movement against humanity, and this movement will continue until the Day of Resurrection. The message of Islam for people is the same as it was fourteen hundred years ago. Whenever humanity deviates from the straight path, Islam stops it and returns it to the right path, because under historical forces humanity repeatedly returns to Jahiliyyah. This is its backwardness and regression, but the Islamic movement advances at this stage; Islam is renewed again, and after this weakness Islam rises again as a force and once more places humanity on the path of progress and civilisation. In every age, the leaders of this movement face the same difficulties that the first caller faced, because when humanity is steeped in the filthy mire of Jahiliyyah, they have to drag the whole of humanity back. In Jahiliyyah, humanity is afflicted with intellectual error; its concepts become dark; it is caught in the darknesses of carnal desires; it becomes the victim of oppression and humiliation, slavery, and personal desires and interests. Whoever wishes to bring humanity out of this Jahiliyyah and filth must face difficulties of this kind, because he launches a movement to purify this world from these filths, and in this movement he can well understand this guidance of Allah.

Verse: Alif, Lam, Mim, Sad. This is a Book that has been sent down to you, so let there be no constraint in your heart concerning it, that you may warn by it, and as a reminder for the believers. (7:1-2)

"Alif, Lam, Mim, Sad. This is a Book sent down to you; so let there be no uneasiness in your breast about it. [It is sent down] that you may warn with it, and as a reminder to the believers."

A believer, from the conditions of his society, understands who the believers are who are to be given counsel, and who the non-believers are for whom the command is to warn. For the worker of this movement, this Qur'an is a living Book, which, as he reads it, he feels as though it is being sent down right now. This Book is a fresh message for him when he takes it up as a message and begins to struggle against the whole world.

The state of all humanity at this time is just as it was when this Book was sent down upon Muhammad (ﷺ). At that time the Messenger (ﷺ) was commanded to fulfil the duty of reminding and warning, and when he rose against Jahiliyyah, there should be no hesitation in his heart. Within him there should be the resolve to uproot Jahiliyyah from its roots.

Today the revolution of time has brought the conditions to the very same point at which they were at the time of the revelation of the Qur'an, fourteen hundred years ago. At this time the world has completely returned to Jahiliyyah. It has adopted Jahiliyyah in both its principles and its branches; its outer and inner, its surface and depth, are all in Jahiliyyah.

At this time, all the concepts and ideologies of humanity are Jahili. Even those whose forefathers were believers and sincere believers have fully adopted Jahili ideas. The meaning of the religion of Islam that is in reality no longer remains in their thoughts and notions. They have changed the very meaning of the Islamic system.

This religion came into this world so that it might change the very features of this earth and give it a new form in its place. Here it should establish the supreme authority of Allah alone and end the authority of taghut. This world should be a world in which there is complete worship of Allah alone, and no human being should make others worship him apart from Allah. It should be a world in which people freely come out of the servitude of human beings. In this world, free, noble and chaste human beings should be born, who are free even from their own base desires and free from the slavery of other people.

This religion came so that it might establish in the world this principle: (La ilaha illa Allah), meaning that there is no sovereign and supreme authority except Allah. All the prophets in human history came with this call. This Surah and the other texts and verses of the Holy Qur'an make this explicit: that the meaning of (La ilaha illa Allah) is solely that supreme sovereignty belongs to none other than Allah, and just as Allah rules over this universe, so He rules over human life as well. He governs this universe and natural life of man through His system of decree and destiny, and therefore He is also sovereign over matters concerning the legal and personal system of human beings. Under this principle, just as a Muslim believes that there is no partner with Allah in the creative life of this world, that He alone is the one who disposes of affairs, and just as a Muslim performs the rites of worship before Allah alone, so in constitution and law he is obedient to Allah alone. He also derives his values and the standards of good and evil from Him. He takes his beliefs and ideas from Allah too, and he never permits any taghut to claim a share of Allah's supreme authority for himself or to become a partner with Allah.

In short, in terms of belief and ideology, this is the fundamental principle of this religion. In the light of this principle, if we cast our eyes upon the world today, we find that the world has abandoned this foundational principle. In this world there are sects upon sects, and all these sects are immersed in Jahiliyyah.

One group is that of the atheists, who wholly deny the existence of the Creator; there is no need for any comment on them. Another group is that of the idolaters, who acknowledge the existence of one God but associate other gods with that God, and have made many lords. For example, such people are found in India, Central Africa and some other regions.

One group is that of the People of the Book, namely the Jews and Christians. These people believe in a son of Allah, make the son a partner of Allah, and regard their rabbis and monks in the same way, because they have accepted the supreme authority and the right of legislation of the rabbis and monks, although they do not pray to them, nor prostrate before them, nor bow down to them. In the present age, the Christians have excluded the authority of Allah from their lives, and have devised systems of life for themselves, which they call capitalism, socialism and other names. They have also devised systems of government for themselves, which they describe as democracy and dictatorship. In this way they have completely abandoned the principles and constitution of Allah, just as the Greek and Roman Jahiliyyah, by abandoning the supreme authority of Allah, fabricated their own system of life and system of government.

One group is that which calls itself Muslim, but in its life it is subservient to the system of the People of the Book. It lives completely in accordance with the Christians of the Western world. This sect, having abandoned the system of Allah, has adopted the system of the Western world. The religion of Allah is the Qur'an, the Sunnah and the Islamic Shariah, and this is the Islamic system of law and constitution, whereas the religion of human beings is a constitution and law fashioned by human beings.

Therefore the truth is that the revolution of time has come round to the very same point at which it stood when Islam first came for the guidance of humanity. People have abandoned the religion of Islam and returned to Jahiliyyah, and have split into sects, yet no sect is obedient to the religion of Islam. Today the Qur'an is for the whole of humanity the same call to thought and action as it was at the time of its revelation. The aim of this religion today is still to bring people into Islam first from the angle of belief and ideas, and then to mould the system of life and the field of action according to Islam. Therefore, whoever today takes up the Qur'anic call will face the same kinds of difficulties that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) faced, because when he addressed humanity, it was defiled by the filth of Jahiliyyah, it was lost in the desert of Jahiliyyah, it had submitted itself before Satan and was going astray. Therefore the first goal today should be that an Islamic outlook on life and Islamic thinking, in accordance with the testimony of faith, be created in the hearts of people, and that a system be established in the world in which only Allah is worshipped and there is no other sovereign and supreme authority except Allah. Thus a new Islamic life should be granted to humanity, in which human beings, freed from the servitude of other human beings and freed from their own desires, enter wholly into the worship of Allah alone.

Islam is not a historical incident which occurred once, after which the period before it and the period after it both become history. Today too it must play the same role it once played. It will work in the same way as it worked before: in circumstances and events, in systems and societies, in beliefs and concepts, in values and standards, and it will confront the false system as it did before.

Remember that Jahiliyyah is a state of affairs; Jahiliyyah is not the name of a particular period of history. At this time this Jahiliyyah has spread over the whole world. In all sects, all concepts, all religions and all systems of life, Jahiliyyah is firmly established. Its fundamental principle is that human beings are slaves of human beings, and that there is a denial of the all-encompassing sovereignty and supreme authority of Allah. Its second principle is that it is founded upon human desires, whatever their form may be. Its important characteristic is that the Shariah of Allah is not accepted as a system of government within it. After that, its appearance, its features, its flags and symbols, its names and titles, its groups, religions and sects, though they may differ, all contain the above-mentioned fundamental precepts and principles.

In the light of these principles, if we look at the world today, Jahiliyyah reigns everywhere in it. Indeed, at this time Jahiliyyah rules the whole world. At this time the Islamic system of life is suspended in the world, and those who are today calling people in the world to the Islamic system of life face the same difficulties as those faced by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Their goal is the same as that of the Messenger of Allah, and today this verse addresses them in the same way as it addressed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Verse: "This is a Book that has been sent down to you; so let there be no uneasiness in your breast about it, that you may warn by it, and as a reminder to the believers." (7:2)

"This is a Book sent down to you; so let there be no uneasiness in your breast about it."

At this time, all the societies that exist in the world are Jahili societies. This is why they are backward and regressive societies, because they have returned again to Jahiliyyah, although Islam had delivered them from that Jahiliyyah. Even today it is Islam's duty to deliver these Jahili societies from regression and backwardness, and to undertake their leadership in attaining progress and civilisation according to its guidance.

When supreme authority becomes exclusively for Allah, and this authority takes the form of a society in which the Islamic Shariah is implemented, then this will be the one condition in which humanity will be fully free from the slavery of human beings. It will be free from the slavery of its carnal desires and self-interest, and only this condition will be an Islamic and civilised condition in accordance with Islamic values, because the civilisation that Allah the Exalted desires for human beings is founded upon the principle of the complete freedom and dignity of every individual. Allah does not approve of any civilisation in which a human being is enslaved to other human beings, and in which human beings become lords and gods of human beings, and their rulers and legislators. Some are subservient and others are masters and rulers. Legislation does not mean merely formal laws; it also means the standards of good and evil, morality and customs. These are all laws and regulations, and people are subject to them, whether people are conscious of their obligation to them or not. Societies of this kind are regarded as regressive and backward societies, and in Islamic terminology they are called Jahili societies.

When a society's collective life is founded on a worldview, and on a system of life built upon that foundation, and when both this conception and this system originate from the Being of God, not from the desire of any individual or the will of any single person, then that society will be a developed and civilised society. In Islamic terminology it will be called a rabbani (divinely oriented) and Muslim society, because in such a society collectivity is founded not on human characteristics but on spiritual and intellectual conceptions.

But if the foundation of a collective system and society is based on nation, race, or similar factors, and on land, then such a society will be called a regressive and backward society, or, in Islamic terms, it will be called a jahili (ignorant) and mushrik (polytheistic) society. This is because nation, race, land and colour are not supreme human authorities. Whatever nation, race, land or colour a human being belongs to, he remains a human being. And if there is any difference within him, it comes through the soul and the intellect.

A human being, through his free choice and will (and this choice and will are the great honour bestowed upon humankind), can change his beliefs and his conceptions, provided that, through the perception of his understanding, he inclines in a direction and becomes satisfied. In that case he can abandon error and adopt guidance, and he can adopt a good system of life. But no human being can change his lineage, his colour, his nation, or this country of his, nor can he determine his land. Therefore, a society and a collective system that people have adopted of their own free will is better, whereas a system in which a person is oppressed and compelled, and in which his freedom and will have no role, is inferior. It is evident that the former situation is more elevated and exalted for the dignity of humanity, and it can be called more progressive.

If in a society human beings' humanity itself is regarded as the supreme value, and human characteristics are deemed worthy of importance and consideration, then that society will be considered a progressive and civilised society, and in Islamic terminology it will be a rabbani and Muslim society. But if the foundation of a society is based on matter, in whatever form it may be, and matter itself is the supreme value, whether it is according to Marxist theories or according to the theory of material production, for example, all the societies of Europe and America where the supreme value and worth is material production, for which they have sacrificed all supreme human values and human characteristics, and for which these societies have given all ethical values a secondary status, then this society will be regarded as backward and regressive, and in Islamic terminology it will be called a jahili and polytheistic society.

The rabbani society of Islam also does not look upon matter with contempt, neither from the perspective that this entire universe has been formed from this matter, nor from the perspective that human beings should derive benefit from it by obtaining production from it, because matter and material production on this earth are extremely necessary for human beings to fulfil their duties of khilafah (vicegerency). Islam permits, and even invites, benefiting from the lawful things of the world, as we shall explain further on in this surah. But Islam does not declare matter and material production to be the supreme value of this universe, for the sake of whose acquisition human values are sacrificed, as all jahili and materialistic societies do.

If human values and human ethics prevail in a society, in the manner in which God Almighty has established them, then this society will be a civilised and rabbani society. Now the question is: what are human ethics, and what are human values? This is not a hidden or incomprehensible matter, nor do ethics and values change or remain in no fixed state, as those people hold who want to create anarchy in the ethical system of Islam. Supreme values and supreme ethical standards highlight those characteristics of human beings in which they are distinct from other animals. They make the human aspect of a person dominant over his animal aspect. Ethical values do not nurture the shared characteristics between humans and animals. If this matter is approached in this manner, then a clear dividing line will be established between supreme values and ethics and mere animality, and supreme values can be properly understood. Thus, all the philosophies of the progressives collapse, and no division remains such as capitalist ethics, socialist ethics, the ethics of the poor and the ethics of the wealthy; only human ethics and animal ethics remain. In this way, the division between social ethics and economic ethics will no longer be a permanent division, and these matters will not be counted as permanent factors in the building of ethics, and their effect on the building of ethics will be considered decisive. From this standpoint, on the one hand there will be human ethics and human values, and these will be the ethics of Islamic society; and on the other hand there will be animal ethics and values, and this will be called backward. In Islamic terminology, this division is called Islamic and rabbani ethics and values, and regressive jahili ethics and values.

Those societies over which animal desires and inclinations prevail can never become civilised societies, even if they are highly developed sexually and economically. This criterion of human progress has never proven to be wrong.

The jahili societies of the modern age have removed supreme ethics and supreme values from all those spheres that are related to the animal aspect of human beings. In these societies the principle of free sex prevails. Among these people, even the most vulgar sexual acts are considered permissible. Among them, if some national interest demands it, they believe in ethics in personal affairs, economic relations and politics, but only within the bounds of their national interests. The journalists, writers and all the branches of the media of these countries teach young people sexual promiscuity, and in them sexual intercourse is not counted among the base vices.

From the Islamic point of view, such societies are backward societies, and from the human perspective they are very degraded. From an Islamic standpoint, they are rejected because Islam restrains the animal desires of human beings, softens their human aspects, and makes the human aspect dominant over the animal aspect.

We cannot discuss today's human societies in greater detail here. These societies are in fact immersed in jahiliyyah (ignorance), from their theories to their ethics, and from their conceptions to their conduct. I think these indications are sufficient here to clarify the features of these societies. In the present age, an introduction to them is provided by these indications. In our time, such an introduction is sufficient for the goals of the Islamic movement, the Islamic call and the revival of religion. The aim of today's call to religion and the Islamic movement is simply that humanity be invited afresh to Islam, in terms of theories, in terms of ethics, and in terms of the system of life. This is the same struggle that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) began. The starting point of our call should also be the same point from which the first caller began. Just as the first caller adopted a certain attitude towards this Book, that same attitude should be ours too, and we should once again reflect upon this verse:

(This is a Book revealed to you, so let there be no hesitation in your heart about it.)

God revealed this Book to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) first presented the Book to the people. Until the Day of Resurrection, whenever anyone presents this Book to any people, he will first instruct those people to follow the commands contained in this Book. Do not take any other as a guardian and protector besides God, because the central axis of the Islamic call is precisely that Islamic commands be followed, instead of following other people. Those who follow this Book are Muslims, and if they follow others, they are polytheists. Regarding the People of the Book, there are only these two positions: either Muslim or polytheist.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 3:

Verse No. 3.

This is the foundational issue of this religion: either one follows this revelation, and then it is Islam, and in it there is acknowledgment of Allah's lordship (rububiyyah). In it there is acknowledgment of the sovereignty (hakimiyyah) of Allah alone: Allah commands and people obey. If Allah does not command, people refrain. Or, if people make for themselves other people as guardians (sarparast), then this is shirk, and the meaning of shirk is that people do not accept Allah alone as Lord, because lordship and supreme authority belong to Allah alone.

When addressing the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, it was said: ﴿A Book has been sent down to you﴾ (7:2), meaning the revelation descended upon his person. And when the people were addressed, it was said: ﴿Follow what has been sent down to you from your Lord﴾ (7:3). For the Messenger, the Book was revealed so that he would believe in it, convey it to the people, and warn them of the evil end. For the people, the descent of the Book means that they should believe in it, act upon it, and not obey anyone else besides it. In both cases, through the words "ilaika" (to you) and "ilaikum" (to you, plural), the honour of the Messenger ﷺ and of his ummah has been raised, and their resolve has been strengthened, because the one to whom Allah sends a Book and chooses for this great task, and bestows upon him this favour, is deserving that he also give thanks for it, fulfil this obligation well, and not be negligent in it.

Since this is a great struggle, its aim is to uproot jahiliyyah (the state of ignorance before Islam) from its very roots. Its concepts, its ideas, its values, its customs, its rituals, its administrative arrangements, its collective habits and manners, its economic system, and its relationship with the universe and with human beings, all are to be completely eliminated. This is a great struggle, so here the consciences of people are shaken strongly and human nerves are made sensitive. The aim is to awaken them and to rouse their dormant nature, which in the age of jahiliyyah was immersed in jahili concepts and ways. For this purpose, a glimpse of the end of the deniers of earlier times is shown before the people, and it is also made clear that after the disgrace of this world, they will be ruined even more in the Hereafter.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verses 4–9:

The fates of earlier peoples are instructive; they are a most elevated warning. The Qur'an presents the instructive parts of the histories of earlier nations in a highly effective manner, by which a person awakens from the slumber of heedlessness, and the veils of heedlessness are lifted from the heart.

There are countless townships which, because of their heedlessness, became deserving of Allah's punishment. When destruction came upon them, they were intoxicated in the slumber of heedlessness. This punishment came upon them at night, or during the day while they were sleeping. Generally, people rest at midday, and at that time they desire to remain in peace and security.

﴿And how many a township have We destroyed! Our punishment came upon them by night, or while they were resting at midday.﴾ (7:4)

These two states, the state of midday rest (qaylulah) and the state of sleep at night, are conditions in which a person is carefree, at peace, and in heedlessness. For someone to be seized and afflicted with punishment in such a state is extremely frightening and highly effective. As a result, fear, the gaining of instruction, and caution and God-consciousness (taqwa) can be attained with greater ease.

In such circumstances, when these criminals were seized and punishment came upon them, what was their response? Confession, and nothing but confession of their guilt. Apart from acknowledgment, they had no other excuse left.

"So when Our punishment came upon them, their only utterance was that they said, 'Indeed, we were wrongdoers.'" (Qur'an 7:5)

Man seeks every kind of excuse, but confession is a difficult thing for him. He does not admit until the last moment. But the punishment of Allah overtook these people so suddenly that, apart from confession, they had no other argument left, for they were placed in an extremely frightening and awe-inspiring position, a position in which confession and acknowledgment become the final effort. Here they confessed to zulm, that is, shirk.

Here, by zulm they mean shirk. In most of the expressions of the Holy Quran, zulm means shirk. It is evident that shirk is zulm and zulm is shirk, for who could be a greater wrongdoer than the one who associates another with his Creator?

Now look, the scene of the punishment of this world is before our eyes: those who denied are in the grip of the punishment of Allah, and they are acknowledging that indeed they were wrongdoers. The truth becomes clear before them and they even accept the truth, but now this acknowledgment is of no benefit to them. This punishment cannot now be averted by remorse and confession, nor is repentance now beneficial, because the time for repentance and remorse has passed and the door of repentance is closed.

This scene is still going on, and on the surface of the world they are being crushed by the punishment of Allah, when suddenly those who were watching find themselves in the field of Resurrection. There is no interval between them. The flow of the discourse runs on a single connected track, and scene follows scene. The bounds of time and place are stretched, and this world and the Hereafter merge together. The punishment of this world has not yet ended when the punishment of the Hereafter begins. Suddenly the second scene is before us.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verses 6–9:

"So We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers. Then We will surely relate to them with knowledge, and We were not absent. And the weighing on that Day is the truth. As for those whose scales are heavy, they are the successful. And as for those whose scales are light, they are the ones who have lost themselves, because they were unjust toward Our signs."

This manner of depiction is a characteristic of Qur'anic expression. This mode of expression takes us on a tour of the entire world in an instant. Then, in a single line of the Qur'an, this world and the Hereafter meet, and the beginning and the end become one.

In this world these people are afflicted with the punishment of God, and in this world they are being questioned. And when the punishment came and they were heedless, then suddenly they began to confess and said, "Indeed, we were wrongdoers" (inna kunna zalimin). But that was in this world.

"So We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers. "

This question is extremely comprehensive and conclusive. It will be asked of the messengers and also of their nations. This question and answer will take place in an open assembly, a great gathering, and all secrets will be revealed in it. The community of the call will be questioned and will acknowledge; the messengers too will be called to account and they will answer. After this, God will present the record of people's deeds in full detail, because God was present with everything; nothing was hidden from Him. This is an extremely impactful touch.

"And the weighing on that Day is the truth." On that day there will be no possibility of error in the weighing, nor any error in the judgment. The disputes and quarrels that occur over judgments in this world will not exist.

"As for those whose scales are heavy, they are the successful." God's scale is true. Now that it has become heavy, protection from the Fire has been achieved; the journey to Paradise has begun, and this is the final destination of that long journey.

"And as for those whose scales are light, they are the ones who have lost themselves, because they were unjust toward Our signs."

There is no possibility of error in God's scale. These people have suffered loss. Now the time for earning is over. A person earns for himself; when there has been a loss in the business, what will he earn and what will remain? They disbelieved and lost their own souls. Because they behaved unjustly toward the signs of God, as has been said, zulm (injustice) here means shirk, since shirk is a great injustice. "Indeed, shirk is a great injustice" (Luqman 31:13). Here we do not enter into the discussion of what the form of the weighing and the measure will be. There have been discussions on this in the history of Islamic doctrine, because the form, manner and quantity of God's actions have no parallel, and God Himself has no parallel: "There is nothing like unto Him" (42:11). Therefore we content ourselves with the words of the Qur'an, that on that Day the reckoning will be true, such that no good deed of a person will be diminished, nor will it be overlooked in the count, nor will it be lost.

Lesson No. 73: Explanation of the Verses

Verses 10 to 25

Here begins the great journey of humanity, and the trusteeship of the earth is handed over to the human race. This sentence serves as an introduction to the story of humanity; the details are coming ahead.

Verse 10.

It is the Creator of this earth and of human beings who settled humans here, and it is He who created within the earth those resources and properties which are conducive to human life, which provide for humans their strength and needs, and which take care of them, including the means of sustenance and livelihood.

It is Allah who placed the globe at a point favourable for the growth of human beings. The earth, with its composition, its size, its fixed distance from the sun and the moon, its rotation around the sun, its inclination in its own way, and the speed of its rotation, is beneficial for human life. Then it is Allah who has deposited in the earth treasures without measure or limit, and has created in it most things in abundance for human food and use, which are the cause of this human being's growth and progress here. Then it is He who has made the human species the master of this earth. It has become capable of subduing these forces and using them for its comfort. Then Allah has given human beings such a rational power by which they have gained access to some hidden secrets of this universe, and they are now using this knowledge for their needs.

Had Allah not given human beings this power, this weak human being could not have "subdued" the cosmic forces (in the way the champions of ancient and modern jahiliyyah use this word), and could not have confronted the forces of this vast universe and this wide world.

The modern civilisation is stamped with the Roman and Greek jahili ideas. These jahili concepts consider the cosmic forces to be enemy forces of humans. According to them these forces are hostile to the existence of human beings and their activities. According to these notions there is a constant war between humans and the cosmic forces. Therefore, when a human being discovers some secret of this universe, these people describe it with the words "conquest of nature." But these notions are wrong, and behind them lies hidden malice.

If these cosmic forces were enemies of humans, opposed to their life, arrayed against them, opposing them, and if behind them no purposeful Being's will were at work, as these people think, then the human being would never have come into existence at all. And if he had come into existence, he could never have grown in this universe. For according to these notions the entire universe is an enemy of humans merely because he has come into existence; therefore, that he lives here is not a reasonable explanation, because if this whole universe is an enemy of humans, how could he move about here? The notion of these people was that this universe is self-sufficient and has no sovereign authority above it.

In contrast to these notions, the Islamic concept of the universe is the only true concept which fully explains all the parts of the universe. It is that it is the Being of Allah who created this universe; it is He who created the human being; and it is this same Allah who has so shaped the nature of the universe that by its very structure it is helpful and supportive to humans. Within the human being, this same Allah has deposited such powers by which he is able to use the forces of the universe for his interests. This harmony and this accord is the noteworthy secret because of which Allah made the creation of everything the best. It is not that the forces of the universe are at war with one another.

According to this Islamic concept, the human being lives with the universe like a companion and friend, under the supervision of a managing power, namely the Creator. His heart is at peace, his soul is happy, his steps are firm, and with full confidence he is carrying out his duties of human vicegerency on this globe. He is the intimate companion of the universe and is grateful to Allah that He has granted him the secret of this universe. As soon as he discovers any of the hidden secrets of this universe which aid his duties, his progress, comfort and prosperity increase.

The concept of this universe which Islam gives does not prevent a human being from seeking further secrets of this universe. Rather, this concept encourages him in that and gives him a state of complete tranquillity and self-confidence, because his movement is in the company of a friend who is not miserly, who does not withhold his secrets from him. Nor does He withdraw His cooperation and help. Because of this, the human being has no connection with an enemy who opposes him at every moment, places obstacles in his path and dashes his wishes and hopes.

The great tragedy of the philosophy of existentialism is that it holds a bad and malicious concept about this universe. The cosmic concept of this philosophy is that this entire universe, and within it the collective system of humanity, is an enemy of the individual existence of the human being, and that the burden of this universe, and then the burden of the collectivity of humanity, is destructive for the human being. This is a concept such that the person who believes in it retreats into reactionary attitudes, a relative seclusion, or even into the lap of non-existence; or else from it arise individualism, wilfulness and rebellion. In both states the human being is afflicted with restlessness and anguish, a burden he cannot bear; intellect and reason become a calamity for him. He falls prey to practical and psychological confusions, and either takes the path of rebellion or wanders lost in the desert of non-existence, and both these states are the same kind of calamity.

This tragedy is not confined to the existentialist school of European thought; it is the tragedy of the whole philosophy of the whole world. All the schools of thought and trends of Europe are caught in this very tragedy, indeed every kind of jahili system in every age and in every society suffers from this tragedy. Only the Islamic system of thought and action confronts this tragedy, because Islam alone gives the human being a friendly outlook towards this universe. Indeed, it also gives a reasonable concept of the realm beyond the universe.

The human being is a son of this earth; he is a product of this universe. He was created from this earth and grew up in it. The arrangements for his dwelling and growth are in this earth, and he has been given here such a rational power by which he gains access to the hidden secrets of this world, and these secrets and forces are conducive to human existence. When a human being attains access to these secrets, they become his helpers and interpret and explain his life.

But the human being! The majority of human beings are ungrateful, because they are lost on the path of their ignorance and jahiliyyah. Those who have become acquainted with the hidden secrets of this universe also do not render the due of gratitude. How can they offer thanks and praise when Allah does not accept from them this honour at all? (They prove their animality instead of their humanity.)

Verse: "And We have certainly established you on the earth and made for you therein means of livelihood; little are you grateful."

"We have settled you on the earth with authority and provided for you here the means of livelihood, yet you are seldom grateful."

Now the interesting events of the story of humanity are related. In a great assembly, a ceremony of the birth of humanity is held. This is a magnificent ceremony in the exalted assembly. Allah, who is a great and exalted King, makes the announcement of the creation of Adam; the King of the universe Himself makes the proclamation. This is a great honour for this human servant. All the angels are present in this assembly. Among them Iblis is also present. Although in reality he was not an angel, yet in this ceremony the whole universe and its creatures are present, because this is a most important event and a magnificent matter, whose significance is central in the scheme of the whole universe.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 7, verse 11:

Verses 11 to 18.

This is the first scene of the story: extremely interesting and extremely important. We will present the scenes of this story before its exegesis (tafsir). After concluding these scenes, we will present the allusions and effects of this story.

﴿And We did certainly create you, then We gave you shape, then We said to the angels, "Prostrate yourselves before Adam," and they prostrated, except Iblis; he was not among those who prostrated.﴾ (11)

"Indeed We began your creation, then We fashioned your form, then We said to the angels: prostrate before Adam. On this command all prostrated, except Iblis, who did not become among those who prostrated."

The word khalq (creation) sometimes comes merely in the sense of bringing into existence. Likewise, the meaning of taswir (giving form) sometimes is that something is given shape, appearance and characteristics. In this sense, khalq and taswir do not occur as two stages of creation but arise simultaneously in one act of creation. This is because it is not necessary that the word thumma (then) always be used for chronological sequence. It also comes in the sense of progression in meaning. In terms of meaning, being given form is a more developed stage than mere existence, because the term existence is applied even to mere matter. However, taswir means that you have not only been granted bare existence but have been given existence as a developed, formed being endowed with characteristics and perfections. Elsewhere there is the verse: ﴿Who gave everything its creation, then guided it﴾. Because Allah gave everything its characteristics, and its purposes and duties, at the very time He created them, and at the time of creation He guided them that they should act for these functions and duties, and there was no temporal gap between creation and guidance. Even if guidance is taken to mean guidance from the Lord, the meaning does not change, because at the moment of creating man, Allah had guided him. Similarly, Adam was also given the characteristics of humanity at the time of his creation. And the word thumma here is in the sense of progression and elevation of rank, not in the sense of a preceding or subsequent time. In our view this meaning is correct.

In any case, all the texts that have come concerning the creation of Adam, and the verses that have come concerning the human race on this earth, confirm that man was given his human characteristics and his responsibilities at the time of his creation, and the progress seen in human history has occurred only through the manifestation of those capacities. Increase in human experience and skill certainly occurs, but this progress has not occurred in human existence or in human mental capacity. Therefore the philosophy that Darwin fabricated, that man's structure has been progressively developing, is completely false.

Darwin's theory that species of animals developed progressively is based on archaeology and the excavation of rocks, and is mere conjecture and estimation. Even from the standpoint of geology, determining the age of rocks and mountains is not a certain matter. These are merely conjectural and estimated judgments, such as determining the age of stars by means of rays. These sciences, which are based on mere conjecture, estimation and hypotheses, may be countered by other hypotheses that may be more reasonable than them.

Even if it is assumed that the age of stones and rocks has been definitively determined, it is still possible that from ancient times different kinds of animals existed in their present form. In those eras conditions were favorable for them, but later conditions were no longer favorable for them and their species disappeared from the world. But this does not prove that one of these species is a developed form of another species. We can accept both as independent species. Darwin's excavations and the species discovered after him can prove nothing more than this. These rock images prove only that a more developed species than some other species existed at a certain time, and it can be interpreted that at that time conditions were favorable for the existence of that species, and later, because conditions became unfavorable, that species disappeared, and in its place another kind of animal came into existence and developed.

Therefore we believe that the human species has been the same from the first day as it is today, and Allah Almighty brought it into existence on earth when conditions here were made favorable for humans. All the Qur'anic texts confirm this.

Moreover, humans are so unique physically, physiologically, intellectually and spiritually that even modern Darwinists have been compelled to accept that man is not a developed species of another species and that he has no physiological resemblance to any other species. Although some of them do not even believe in the Divine Being, their acknowledgment is a kind of admission that the existence and development of man is entirely unique. In any case, Allah Almighty announced the creation of man in an assembly of angels, and this assembly took place in the higher realm.

﴿Then We said to the angels, "Prostrate before Adam," and they prostrated, except Iblis; he was not among those who prostrated.﴾ (11)

Then We said to the angels: prostrate before Adam. They all prostrated on this command, except Iblis, who did not become among those who prostrated.

The angels are a distinct creation of Allah, and they have their own characteristics and duties. We know about them only as much as Allah has told us. In Zilal al-Quran we have previously given a note about the angels. Likewise Iblis belongs to a distinct species of creation. The Qur'an says: ﴿He was of the jinn, so he defied the command of his Lord﴾. The jinn are a creation separate from the angels. About them too we know only as much as Allah has told us. We have also given a brief note about them in this same part. Later in this surah it will be stated that Iblis was created from fire, so he belongs to a creation other than the angels. Iblis too was commanded to prostrate before Adam (peace be upon him), because he was among the ranks of the angels and was present at that assembly in the higher realm where the ceremony of Adam's creation took place.

As for the angels, they are a creation who do not disobey Allah's commands, and they carry out whatever they are commanded. Therefore, being obedient, they prostrated and carried out Allah's command. For they neither hesitate in any matter, nor are they arrogant, nor can they even think of disobeying Allah, whatever the cause or justification might be. This is their nature. This obedience is their distinguishing feature and is part of their assigned duties. From this it becomes clear how honored the person of the human being is in the sight of Allah, and it also becomes evident that the angels are absolutely obedient to Allah.

As for Iblis, he did not comply with the command and disobeyed. It will come later what caused unease in his heart, and what thoughts overcame him that emboldened him to disobey. Although he knew that Allah is the Lord of the worlds, and is also his Creator, and that He is the master of his affairs and of his very existence, he had no doubt in these matters.

In this scene there are three examples of Allah's creation. One example is that which is completely obedient in every respect, and whose nature is to carry out commands. The second example is that which is completely disobedient, and whose nature is arrogance and disobedience. The third creation is the human creation, whose qualities, weaknesses and perfections will also be discussed shortly. The first kind of creation is purely divine, and they fulfilled their duty fully in that very assembly. Details about the other two kinds of creation will come shortly, regarding what their inclinations are.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 12:

Verse: "He said, 'What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?' He said, 'I am better than he. You created me from fire and created him from clay.'"

Iblis's fault was that, despite a clear text (nass sarih), he thought he could act upon his own opinion, and that if there were some cause and reason (illah) behind the command, the command could be set aside. Yet when a clear text has come, there is no room left for deliberation and reflection. The only course that remains is to obey and implement the command.

Consider now the accursed Iblis: despite knowing that Allah is the Creator and Owner, the Provider and the Governor, and that nothing in this world can happen without His knowledge and permission, he does not obey the command that has reached him. He brings forward his own logic: "I am better than him, since You created me from fire and him from clay." For this sophistry he is immediately punished.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 13:

Verse: "He said, 'Then descend from it, for it is not for you to be arrogant therein. So get out; indeed, you are among the debased.'" (7:13)

"He said: 'Very well, then descend from here. It is not for you to show arrogance here. Get out, for you are truly among those who bring their own humiliation upon themselves.'"

Here his knowledge no longer benefits him. He is aware of the being and attributes of Allah, yet this knowledge is of no benefit to him. The same will be the condition of every person to whom the command of Allah reaches and who then sets the steeds of his thought and reasoning galloping, and himself decides whether to accept it or not. A matter has been decided by the court of Allah, yet he does not acknowledge it; he makes his own decision and, through it, rejects the decision of Allah. Therefore this is disbelief committed knowingly and with full understanding. Iblis did not lack knowledge and recognition; his belief was not wavering.

So he was cast out of Paradise, deprived of the mercy of Allah, and a curse was written upon him. Disgrace was imposed upon him. Yet this obstinate nature does not even try to understand that because of Adam he was rejected from the presence of Allah. Thus, instead of repenting, he takes to vengeance. Now he takes upon himself those responsibilities which are fitting for the evil in which he has become entangled.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah al-A'raf (7), verses 14–17:

Verse: "He said: 'Grant me respite until the day they are raised.' He said: 'You are indeed among those granted respite.' He said: 'Because You have sent me astray, I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path. Then I will come to them from before them and behind them, from their right and from their left. And You will not find most of them thankful.'" (7:14–17)

It appears that he is determined to persist in his mischief. He has fully resolved to go astray and to lead further people astray. This also shows that the nature of the satanic creation is steeped in misguidance, and this is its primary characteristic. This is not accidental, temporary or superficial; it is deliberate, purposeful and deliberate, and is founded upon a profoundly deep enmity.

This verse is a living picture of intellectual, spiritual and psychological movements, and in it living scenes are visible.

Iblis requests that he be granted respite until the Resurrection, because he knows that whatever he wishes cannot reach its object without the will and decree of Allah. Allah, the Exalted, accepts his request for respite and reprieve, but only until a known term, as has been made clear in other surahs. Narrations state that this respite extends to the day of the first blast of the Trumpet, on which all creation will die, and not until the Day of Resurrection.

Now, after the decision regarding the respite has been taken, Iblis announces with great audacity and inner malice that he will take revenge for his misguidance and rejection upon Allah's creation by leading astray this noble creation of Allah, and he announces this programme in such a decisive manner.

Verse: "I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path. Then I will come to them from before them and behind them, from their right and from their left."

That is, I will set up my posts on the straight path You have designated for them. I will strive to block them from that path. The path leading to Allah is clearly not a sensory path, since it cannot be conceived that Allah is in one place and this path leads to Him. The path of Allah is the path of faith and obedience, which results in attaining Allah's pleasure. Therefore Satan attacks people from every direction: from the front, from behind, from the right and from the left. In this way he prevents people from the path of their faith and action. This is, as it were, a scene that is alive and continuously in motion. Iblis attacks people from every side, constantly leading them astray, and people, caught in his snare, are deprived of the knowledge of Allah and of thanking Him. Yet a small number escape his snare and follow the commands of Allah.

Verse: "And You will not find most of them thankful."

Here the mention of gratitude is made in harmony with the mention of gratitude at the beginning of the surah. At the outset it was said: "Little do you give thanks" (7:10). The purpose here is to show what the cause is for which man does not remain thankful, since Satan secretly works against the thankful. He is posted on every path, so people should be fully vigilant; the enemy sits in ambush. He prevents them from guidance by every means, and they should take precautionary measures against this, since they know by what route this calamity is coming upon them.

Iblis's request was granted because the requirement of Allah's will was also that man should make his own path by his own free choice, since his nature contains the capacity for both good and evil. He has also been given the faculty of reason, which prefers good over evil. Then, by sending messengers with a message, he was warned of the evil end of wickedness, and then he was given the code of the religion of Islam and set upon the right path. He was told that the requirement of the divine will was that he should adopt guidance or misguidance, and that there should be a struggle between good and evil within his personality, and that he should arrive at one of two ends, and that the divine practice (sunnah ilahiyyah) should operate upon him in accordance with Allah's will, whether he takes the path of guidance or a decision of error is made.

However, in the context here, the accursed Iblis is not explicitly granted permission in the sense of "Go, you are permitted to mislead people," as, just as his first request was accepted and he was granted respite until the Resurrection, here no comment is made on his machinations, and it is declared that you are being removed from here in disgrace and humiliation, and he is threatened that you and your companions will be cast into Hell.

The verse: "He said: Get out of it, disgraced and expelled. Whoever of them follows you, I will surely fill Hell with you all."

Some people, knowing Allah, follow Satan, and they also hold the belief that Allah is our Lord; but along with this knowledge and belief, they deny Allah's sovereignty, supreme authority, and judging according to Allah's laws, and they claim that they may review Allah's commands and decide whether or not to implement them. Then Satan misguides them to such an extent that they do not acknowledge God at all. Both kinds of people are followers of Satan and will deserve Hell.

Allah has given Iblis and his party the opportunity to make an independent effort to lead people astray, and has given Adam and his offspring the choice to adopt whatever path they wish by their own will. Both have occasions of trial, and it was the demand of Allah's will that He tests humanity in this way. Thus He gives man the station of a unique and honoured creature of this universe, so that man is neither an angel nor a devil, but plays his own role: neither a satanic role nor the role of the angels.

Now this scene ends, and after it another scene appears. After casting Iblis out of Paradise, Allah addresses Hazrat Adam and his wife. Here we are told only this much: Adam's wife also existed, and she was of his own kind, but it is not known how she was created. The verse under discussion and other similar verses in the Holy Qur'an say nothing on this matter, and the narrations about the creation of Hawwa contain effects of Isra'iliyyat, so we cannot say anything certain about who she was created from. It is certain that Allah created Adam's wife of his own kind, and thus they became a pair. Allah has created pairs among all His creatures.

"And of everything We created pairs, that you may remember" (Qur'an 51:49). This is the sunnah jariyah (continuing practice) of Allah and the fundamental principle of this universe. When we adopt an opinion according to this principle, we must adopt the view that the creation of Hawwa also took place soon after the creation of Adam, and that Hazrat Hawwa was created in the same manner as Hazrat Adam (peace be upon him).

Now the address is directed to Hazrat Adam and his wife Hazrat Hawwa, so that first of all Allah may give them commands about their life, they may be trained, and they may be prepared for the fundamental role they are to play on earth, since Adam was created precisely so that he might carry out the duty of Allah's vicegerency (khilafah) on this earth, as is clearly stated in the verse of Surah al-Baqarah:

"When your Lord said to the angels, 'Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a khalifah (vicegerent).'" (Qur'an 2:30)

Verse 19

The Qur'an does not name the tree, because naming the tree would make no difference. The essential point was simply to forbid them. Allah had permitted them the use of all lawful things and had restrained them from the use of what was forbidden. The limit on what is forbidden was necessary so that the human being would know that he cannot go beyond it, and so that, by using the freedom of will and choice that has been granted to him, he would learn to control his desires and inclinations, and to gain mastery over them. He should not be a slave of his desires like the animals, but their ruler. For the very difference between a human being and an animal lies in this: the human being keeps his desires under control, while the animal has no control over its desires.

Now Iblis begins that task for which he has dedicated himself. This is the human being, whom Allah honoured and whose creation was announced in that great assembly of the higher realm, to whom all the angels prostrated in salutation, and because of whose prostration Iblis was expelled from the higher realm. This creature possesses two capacities within itself: it can move in both directions. And within this creature there are also weak points through which it can be seized, unless it stands firm upon the command of Allah. From these weak points an attack can be launched upon it, and it can be brought under control. Among these weak points is one: the desires of the self (shahawat nafsaniyah)... Just see how Satan gains control over a person through these points.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verses 20–21:

Verses 20–21

It is not known how the satanic whisper operates, because we do not know the reality of Satan by which we could become aware of the nature of his actions, or determine how he gains access to a human being and how he misleads him. But we have knowledge, through the Truthful Informant, that Satan misleads a human being in some way, and regarding these unseen realities, the Truthful Informant, Muhammad (ﷺ), is the only true and certain source of knowledge.

Satan misleads a human being through various methods, and all of these methods are carried out through weak points in the human personality. Human beings have natural weaknesses, and a person can be protected from them only through firm faith and the remembrance of Allah. When faith and remembrance are present, the situation becomes such that Satan has no control over the person; his schemes become weak and have no effect on him.

In this way, Satan led them astray, and their private parts, which had been concealed from each other, were revealed to them. His real purpose was their private parts, and they needed to cover them with some other material thing. Satan did not disclose his plan to them; rather, he entered through the avenue of their desires. He said: "Your Lord has forbidden you from this tree only lest you become angels or lest you become of those who abide forever."

Thus Satan played upon human desires. Every human being has the desire to live forever, or to live a long life, to attain immortality, and to obtain a kingdom that extends beyond limited life.

In some recitations, the word (مَلِكَيْن), with a kasra on the letter lam (لِ), has been reported. (Malakayn) means "two kings" or "two angels" in its sense of ruling.

In Surah Taha, verse 120: "Shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?" (20:120). In this case, Satan offered them everlasting life and everlasting dominion. These two things are at the very top of human desires. The true reality of the sexual desire is also that through sexual union a person seeks immortality, that is, to have offspring and to remain alive generation after generation. And if one reads "malakayn," the meaning is that both of you would become angels and be freed from the physical needs of a human being, and their life would be eternal like that of the angels. However, the first recitation, although it is not the well-known recitation, is more consistent with the verse of Surah Taha, and in this Surah, Satan's deception also remains within the limits of human desires.

Since the accursed Satan knew that Allah had explicitly forbidden them from that tree, and that because of Allah's prohibition there is a misgiving in their hearts, and that a power of resistance is present within them, therefore, in his whisper, while exploiting human desires and weaknesses, he also presents himself as a sincere advisor and swears oaths, saying:

﴿And he swore to them, "Indeed, I am to you a sincere advisor."﴾ (7:21)

Adam and his wife forget Allah's warning that Satan is their enemy. This forgetfulness is caused by their personal desire and by Satan's oaths. Yet Allah had commanded them to obey the divine commands, whether or not they understood the reason behind any command. They also forgot that nothing can happen except by the decree and command of Allah. If Allah had not decreed for them eternity and everlasting dominion, how could this goal be achieved?
