Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 7, verse 22:

Verse No. 22.

Now this deception was complete, and its result came before us. Shaitan (Satan) turned them away from obedience to Allah and afflicted them with disobedience to Allah, and he did all of this through deep scheming and deception. Therefore Allah sent this pair down to the earth. ﴿So he brought about their fall through deception.﴾ (7:22) He achieved his purpose by deceiving them.

Now they became aware that they had private parts in their bodies. Those private parts had previously been hidden from their sight. So they began joining together leaves of the trees of the Garden and placing them over their private parts. From these words it appears that the "private parts" refer to those bodily parts whose exposure naturally causes a person shame, and that only a person whose nature has been corrupted by some jahili (ignorant) society can expose and display those places.

﴿So he brought about their fall through deception. And when they tasted the tree, their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to cover themselves with leaves from the Garden. And their Lord called out to them: "Did I not forbid you from that tree and tell you that Shaitan is a clear enemy to you?"﴾ (7:22)

Then their Lord called to them: "Did I not forbid you from that tree, and did I not tell you that Shaitan is your clear enemy?"

They heard this questioning from Allah because they had forgotten the advice and disobeyed. The question is: what was the manner of this call from Allah? Just as He addressed them the first time, in the same way He addressed the angels and in the same way He addressed Iblis. All these matters are unseen, and concerning them we only hold the assumption that it was likely so, and Allah does what He wills.

In contrast to this call, it appears that the human being, this unique creature of the universe, has another important aspect to his personality. It is that he also forgets, mistakes occur from him, and he has weaknesses through which Shaitan gains influence over him. Moreover, this human is not always in error, nor is he always on the right path. Rather, he realizes his error and slip, and after this realization he seeks forgiveness, feels remorse, returns and repents, and does not persist in sin as Shaitan did. He does not seek help from his Lord in sin.

This is the commentary of Sayyid Qutb in Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation) on Surah al-A'raf (7), verse 23:

Verse 23

This is the quality of human beings that keeps them connected to their Lord and keeps open the doors through which they can reach Him: the confession of wrongdoing, repentance and seeking forgiveness (istighfar), awareness of one's own weakness, seeking help from Allah and seeking His mercy, and the conviction that there is no source of power other than Allah and that no one else can give assistance. If Allah's mercy and help are not there, a person falls into a great loss.

Here the first experience of man is completed, and the major features of his personality become clear. A person comes to know himself, his weaknesses and his capacities and abilities, which have been given to him for fulfilling the duty of khilafah (vicegerency) on the earth. An important part of this duty is that on this earth man must wage a continuous struggle against his enemy, Satan.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 24 (part 1 of 3):

Verses 24 to 25.

"Go down, all of you, and settle on the earth." The question arises: where were these beings at that time? Where is Paradise? These are matters of the unseen (ghayb), and about them we know only as much as the Being in whose hand are the keys of the unseen tells us. Now that the process of revelation has ended, any human search for these unseen matters and places would be a futile effort. Likewise, those who deny these matters, and do so on the basis of their scientific and uncertain information, are also transgressing their own limits, and their position is nothing but arrogance and obstinacy. This is because they speak of a realm of the unseen to which they have no access, yet their arrogance goes so far that they deny the unseen outright, although the unseen has encompassed man from every side. The subject of these people's knowledge is matter, and even in the world of matter, what is unknown so far far exceeds what is known.

In any case, all of them descended. They came down to the earth: Adam, Eve, Iblis, and their associates and allies. They came down here so that on this field the battle between Adam and Iblis would begin, they would become enemies of one another, and a conflict would start between two dispositions. One disposition is one hundred percent mischievous, while the other has the capacity for both good and evil. This is so that the scheme of trial which the Divine Will has devised may be carried out, and so that the decree and destiny of Allah may reach its end.

Allah appointed residence on the earth for Adam and his offspring, that they should settle here, benefit from the produce of the world, for a fixed term. They should live and die here, and at the appointed time they will be raised, so that they may give account before their Lord. The people of Paradise will go to Paradise, and the people of the Fire to the Fire. This will be the outcome of this great journey of humanity.

Now this first round has ended. After this, there will be new rounds of the battle between Adam and Iblis. In these, man will succeed only if he has taken refuge in his Lord, and if he has made his enemy a friend, it is obvious that he will be defeated.

Here it is necessary to keep in mind that this is not a story or a tale; rather, these verses clarify the reality of man, so that the facts may come to light concerning his temperament, his growth, his environment, the system of decree and destiny that affects his life, the system that Allah has chosen for him, the trial that he must face, and the end that he must reach. These are matters that form part of the foundations of the Islamic conception of life.

Insofar as the method of Fi Zilal al-Quran will permit, we shall note its fundamental points; details we leave to our book "Khasa'is al-Tasawwur al-Islami," which discusses this subject in detail.

As we have said before, from the account of the creation of humanity the first reality that becomes apparent is that there is a natural harmony between the creation of this universe and the creation of man. Both operate within the system of Allah's decree and destiny. By grasping this reality, we arrive at the conclusion that the creation of man, which took place according to a destiny and a plan, was not a merely accidental matter, and that there is complete concord between this universe, man, and the system of decree and destiny.

Those who are deprived of the knowledge of Allah cannot esteem the Divine Being as is His due. They measure Allah's works and the system of His decree by the standards that have been set for the small affairs and plans of man. When they look, the only thing that they understand is that man too is a creature like the other creatures of this world. When they saw that in this vast universe the earth is like an atom, they said that it is not a reasonable matter to seek a purpose behind the creation of man, and therefore man has no special significance in this universe. Some people have said that the existence of man here is merely by chance, and that the universe around man is strongly opposed to his existence and growth. These are merely conjectures that these people make about the acts of Allah and His system of decree, and that too only according to their limited human standards of intellect and wisdom.

The truth is that if this whole universe were the property of man, he would not regard this small earth, nor would he care for the tiny creature that moves upon it. For man cannot manage the great kingdom of this entire universe; nor can he direct every thing in it, nor can he determine everything, nor can he create harmony among all the things of this world. But the reality is that the King of this world is Allah, and not even one atom in the heavens and the earth is hidden from His sight. Allah is the Holder of this great universe, and no thing in this universe can remain in its place if Allah does not command it. Nothing here can come into existence without the Will of Allah. When man abandons the guidance of Allah and begins to follow his carnal desires, he becomes afflicted with calamity. If he calls that calamity "knowledge," that is his choice. He analogizes Allah to himself and analogizes Allah's acts and deeds to his own acts, although the acts and decrees of Allah lie beyond the grasp of human analogy. It is man's error that, because of his own narrowness of vision, he takes his desire to be reality.

Sir James Jeans, in his book "The Mysterious Universe," speaking of the misguided conceptions of man, says:

"When we stand on this earth, which is a small grain of sand, we try to know the nature and essence of this whole universe that surrounds us and is spread out in the unimaginable vastness of time and space. We also want to know what is the purpose and aim of bringing it into existence. When we look at this universe, first of all we are seized with bewilderment and our eyes are dazzled. The truth is that how should this universe not frighten us when its vastness is so great that our intellect cannot comprehend it. Then a long period has passed over this very universe, and we cannot even imagine it, and in comparison to those eras the storehouse of human knowledge, which is history, is a single moment. Then it is also frightening in this respect, that within it there is a terrible unity. Then it is frightening because our homeland, this earth, within this universe is so small that, if one of the little pebbles of the sands of the oceans of the world were divided into a million pieces, it would be even less than that. But the most frightening aspect of this universe is that it is a purposeless thing, as our life shows it to be purposeless. Our emotions, our aims, our actions, our arts, and our religions are all alien to the system of this universe and without affinity with its system. If we were to say that between this universe and our life there is a permanent enmity and contradiction, it would not be wrong, because the atmosphere of most of this universe is so cold that life is not possible in it. All kinds of living beings there become frozen, and most of the material components are so hot that to remain alive in them is impossible. In this atmosphere of the universe, such rays constantly collide with one another, just as celestial bodies constantly collide, and these rays can at times be enemies of life, and indeed can end life at any moment."

"The universe in which circumstances have thrown us, if it is not true that we are alive here because of some error on the part of this universe, then it is at any rate reasonable to conclude that the existence of man here has come about merely by accident and coincidence."

These are the views of those people. It should be remembered that earlier we discussed the point that the universe being hostile to life, and assuming that it is without any governing and controlling power, and that the emergence of a creature like man and absolute life within it is merely by chance, is not a matter that comes within the comprehension of an ordinary person, much less that a great scholar or scientist should say such things. The question arises: if this universe is a killer of every kind of life that exists within it, and there is no governing power over it, how did this life come into being? The question is whether this life is stronger than the universe, that it came into being in spite of the universe, even though the universe was opposed to its coming into being. Was man, before coming into existence, more powerful than this vast universe, so that he forcibly came and stood here?

I say that this is a line of thought to which no attention should even be paid. If these so-called scholars had been content merely to say that our means of knowledge cannot explain and interpret this universe, and had not uttered those absurdities which they utter about metaphysics, for which they have no authority, then they would have discharged their duty, though even that duty would have been incomplete. They would have said that the universe around us is a riddle. But they go far beyond the bounds of their knowledge and sink into a quagmire of hypotheses, baseless conceptions, and artificial fancies produced by human desires, which are unsafe territories.

We Muslims, praise be to Allah, when we look upon this universe, neither fear overtakes us nor do we fall into the bewilderment expressed by Sir James Jeans. Rather, we are made to tremble before the Creator of this universe, and we see that majesty and splendour by which this universe becomes our friend, because it too has been created by the Creator, and so have we. There is complete concord and harmony between the two. We are indeed astonished by its vastness and its subtlety, but we are not frightened, nor does the awareness and feeling seize us that we are being destroyed today or tomorrow, because our Lord and the Lord of this universe is one. We deal with Him with the utmost affection, trust, and certainty. We expect that our sustenance, our needs, and the stores of our livelihood and economy are in Him, and we must be grateful to the Creator of this universe.

Verse: "And We had certainly established you upon the earth and made for you therein means of livelihood; little are you grateful." (7:10)

"We have settled you on the earth with authority and provided for you means of livelihood here, but you rarely give thanks."

From the story of the creation of Adam, the second reality that becomes apparent to us is that, in comparison with all the living creatures of this universe, man is an honoured, exalted, and noble creature. He has a most important role to play in this world. He has to strive in a most extensive field, and several worlds are involved with him here. But all these matters lie within the limits of the worship and servitude of Allah alone. Man does not occupy here the position that those schools of thought give him which are confined within the five senses and materialism. These schools do not regard man as an effective agent in this universe. In these doctrines and conceptions, all importance is given to matter and its effects. Likewise, the proponents of the theory of evolution assign him an even lower status, namely one animal among the animals. These people have no concern or connection with the human characteristics of man. Or they view him from the angle of Freud's theory of sexuality, which regards man as merely a worm in the filthy pond of sex, who advances only through that filthy pond. But the honour and dignity that Islam bestows upon this unique creature, man, does not reach the point where he becomes a god, as the conceptions of life born in the age of modern enlightenment have made him a god. The Islamic conception of life grants him the station of truth and moderation, which is correct and healthy.

Then the announcement of the creation of this unique creature, Man, was made in a most dignified assembly of the higher world, and, as we have said in the light of the Quranic texts, in that assembly a complete human being was presented. In it was also announced that he is the vicegerent (khalifah) on this earth. The trial that came upon him in Paradise was also for this very purpose, that he might become ready to discharge the duties of vicegerency, as other verses indicate, that this entire universe, not only the earth, has been created for man. It is beneficial and helpful to him, and whatever is in the heavens and the earth has been made subservient to him.

Then it is known from this that the role which Allah has entrusted to man in this world is also very great. To develop this entire terrestrial globe and to establish upon it the system of Allah's vicegerency, whether the earth's span be large or small, is in any case a great responsibility that has been entrusted to man.

From this story and from other verses of the Quran it is also known that man is a unique creature, and that he is unique not only on this earth but in the whole universe. Among the other stars there are angels, jinn, and all those creatures of which only Allah has knowledge. These creatures have other duties; each of them has its own distinct temperament and nature, and its nature is suited to its duties. But man is a unique creature whose duties and functions are also unique, and to this the following verse of the Quran points:

"Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it; but man bore it. Indeed, he has always been a wrongdoer, ignorant." (33:72)

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 24 (part 2 of 3):

"We offered the Trust to the heavens, the earth and the mountains, and they refused to bear it and were afraid of it, but man bore it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant."

Thus man, with his particular characteristics, is unique in this whole universe. These characteristics include both injustice and ignorance. Together with this injustice and ignorance, he has been given personal freedom of choice, the capacity for knowledge and understanding, and personal will. And to the same degree that he is capable of ignorance and injustice, he is also capable of justice and knowledge. In short, this diversity of human capacities is his most important characteristic.

Along with all these characteristics, it is no longer significant that the earth on which man lives is very small in size compared with the vastness of this entire universe. This is because size is not important in every matter. For example, the rational faculty which perceives things, and man's being purposeful and acting according to his own preference, even if within the wider sphere of the worship of Allah, all these things nevertheless increase man's worth and make him a unique creature. Merely because the earth is small in size, people such as Sir James Jeans diminish the worth of man. This is not correct.

The honour that these verses and these narratives confer upon man is not limited to his duty of being Allah's vicegerent (khilafah); rather, the honour and importance of this unique creature becomes even clearer when we look at the horizons and the vast expanses of the universe in which it carries out its work.

Now consider that the affair of this unique creature is directly with its Lord. He created it with His own hands, then announced it in the dignified assembly of the higher world, and granted it speech. Then He placed it in Paradise and said: eat from wherever you wish, except from the forbidden tree. After that He granted it the station of khilafah, through His own speech. Then Allah taught it, as we explained in the commentary on the verse in Surah al-Baqarah, that the "names" mean the meanings of words, that is, the word and the referent, which is the thing upon which the exchange of knowledge and understanding has become possible. Through these, the knowledge of all human beings has increased. Allah gave Adam counsel both in Paradise and after it, and granted him special abilities found only in man and not given to any other creature. Then, by sending guidance further, He sent messengers. Then Allah made it binding upon Himself to show mercy to His creatures, so that if they repent and seek forgiveness, they are forgiven. This is the final bounty of Allah upon this unique creature.

This human being is also a companion in the higher world. The angels prostrate in honour of him. Then angels are appointed to protect him. Some of them carry out the duty of bringing revelation, and upon the servants of Allah who say, "Allah is our Lord," and then remain steadfast, Allah sends down angels who give them good news. In the same way, the angels support those who strive in the way of Allah and give them the good news of victory. Then these angels are set upon the disbelievers, who kill them and also punish their spirits. In short, these and other matters are such that man has contact and dealings with the world of angels as well.

Then man also has dealings with the jinn, with their righteous ones as well as with their wicked ones. The reader has already learned about the struggle between man and the great Satan. This great struggle is still continuing and will continue until the Day of Resurrection. However, the mutual connection of man with righteous jinn is also mentioned in some verses, and the subjugation of the jinn is also established from the Qur'an, as mentioned in the story of Hadrat Sulayman (peace be upon him), that he subjected the jinn to himself.

In the same way, this human being is also connected with the whole material universe, especially with the earth and the stars and planets around it. On this earth, man is Allah's khalifah and deputy. All his forces have been subjected to man, and his treasures and produce are dedicated to man. And within man has been deposited a power and capacity which continually reaches into the depths of his nature, and keeps unveiling the natural laws of things, and in this way he plays a great role on this earth. Thus he has a connection with all the living creatures of this universe. Then, because of the variegated nature of his disposition, he runs the horses of knowledge deep into his own self. He attains ascension to the heavens and even goes beyond the stations of the angels. But this happens when he is a special servant of Allah. Yet if he falls, he descends even to the level of a mere animal, when he makes his desires his god. Then his humanity wallows in a filthy animal pond. Between these two extremes there is a vast and wide field of levels, which extends within the world of the senses and beyond it, up to the limits of what lies beyond the senses, and in which he has his dealings. ... It should be remembered that these stations do not exist for any creature other than man, as we learn from this narrative.

The third truth is that this unique creature, despite its uniqueness, is also weak in some respects, and because of these weaknesses there is a possibility that it can be drawn towards evil. It can fall to the lowest level by pursuing personal and base desires. One of its weaknesses is that it wishes to remain here. Then it is also hungry for power, and there is a strong desire for authority within it. When it casts aside the guidance of Allah, its weaknesses increase further, and it becomes purely a slave of carnal desires, or it becomes a follower of that enemy Satan who has taken upon himself the duty of misguiding it, and who will continue tireless effort toward this aim and will employ every means and resource to achieve it.

This is why Allah, out of His mercy, His grace and His bounty, has not left it completely to its nature, nor handed it over entirely to its own intellect and reasoning. Rather, He has sent a succession of messengers to guide it and to warn it of the evil end. Accordingly, a careful commentary on this narrative is coming in the tafsir of the following verses. And this is the first step to human success. In this way, freed from the jungle of its desires, it comes back to Allah, and thus it is saved from its hidden enemy. This salvation is obtained through the remembrance of Allah, His remembrance, the motivation to obtain His mercy and His reward, and fear of His reproach.

All these matters give it strength, and through them it gains control over its weaknesses and lusts. In this regard, its first training was that a tree in Paradise was made forbidden to it, so that by avoiding it, it would strengthen its will and resist the pull of weakness and disobedience. Although it did not succeed in this first experience and first trial, later this failure became instructive for it.

Because of these weaknesses, Allah showed mercy and kept open the door of repentance for it: when it forgets and then remembers, and becomes remorseful; when it falls and then rises; when it strays from the straight path and repents, turns back, and adopts the right way, then the door of repentance is open to it at all times. Allah accepts its repentance and forgives its error. It is not the case that if someone makes a mistake, he must surely be seized; or that a curse should be upon him and his offspring should also be stained with that accusation, for no sin is eternal. How can one bearing a burden bear the burden of another?

This conception of the Islamic system of life refutes the story which the distorted notions of the Church imposed upon humanity, and as a result of which many unnatural beliefs and rituals were imposed upon the Christian religion, and that religion became lost in superstitions instead of correct beliefs. It is a strange notion that the lapse of Adam now hangs around the neck of all humanity and is a permanent curse, even to the extent that it clings to their self-made god, the Messiah. Their souls are freed from it only when this human god is crucified, and the garment of humanity is cleansed only then. And what happens? Those who accept Christianity until the Day of Resurrection also have their sins forgiven. Very good!

By contrast, in the Islamic conception of life, how much simpler and more intelligible the matter is: Adam forgot, and a lapse occurred from him. He repented, and Allah forgave him, and thus the matter of that first lapse came to an end, and it was preserved in history as an instructive experience for man, so that man may learn a lesson from it. Look how simple this conception is, how clear, and how simple and easy its own... is.

The fourth truth is that the struggle between man and Satan here is a real struggle. It is a continuous and most severe struggle. This narrative shows that this enemy of man has announced that he will continue his operations against man in every state, and he has openly declared that he will attack man from every side and every direction and will continue his assaults without interruption. He declares war in these words:

"Then, because You have led me astray, I will indeed lie in wait for them on Your straight path. Then I will come to them from before them and behind them, from their right and from their left, and You will not find most of them grateful."

The accursed Satan adopted the course of continuing his deceit against humanity, and he asked for respite for this operation. Against this, he abandoned the straight path that lay before him. The straight path was that, when he heard the commands of Allah properly in the presence of the Divine Being and committed disobedience, he would have been remorseful and sought forgiveness from Allah. On the contrary, he declared that he would sit on every roadside to misguide them, and would attack them from every direction and every side, and would leave them misguided.

Satan attacks humans from the points which are weak from the standpoint of defence. These weak points are sexual desires and the desire to attain status. Human beings can correct these weak points only through fear of God and remembrance of Allah, and the method is that a person suppresses his personal desires; this is a struggle against his own desires and adherence to the guidance sent by Allah. And only those who possess lofty ideals and lofty resolve can rise to eminence by overcoming material desires, because here Satan, with his entire army, is on one side of the field, and he can be confronted only when the Shariah is enforced upon this earth. Thus this struggle continues both on the field of ideas and conscience and on the practical field of life. A simultaneous struggle on both fields is necessary.

The shayatin who sit in the world run people according to their own sharia and their own invented values. They have set up their own standards of good and evil here, which deny the sovereignty of Allah, His supreme authority and His Shariah, and which run against the authority that issues from the religion of Islam. These are human shayatin, and the jinn shayatin give them instructions. This political struggle with these human shayatin is also a struggle against the real Satan himself; it is not a separate matter from him.

Thus this great conflict that has been set up in this world is in reality a great battle with Satan. It is a battle against the friends of Satan. When a Muslim of sound thinking enters this battle, he is in fact at war with his own material desires. Then he is at war against those friends of Satan who have themselves established their supreme authority on this earth. He is at war against all the mischiefs which these shayatin and their friends have set up in the world, and when a believer is engaged in this all-encompassing war, he fully recognises that he is fighting this all-encompassing war against Satan, who is his real enemy and against whom Allah has declared continuous war. This war will continue until the Day of Resurrection, and this is why a hadith states: "Jihad will continue until the Day of Resurrection," meaning that jihad will continue and will carry on in every form and on every field.

The final point which this narrative makes clear, as the details coming up will show, is that within the nature, disposition and temperament of man himself there exists something, namely modesty and shame. Man by nature dislikes nakedness, especially the nakedness of the private parts.

"Satan whispered to them so as to expose to them what was hidden from them of their private parts." (7:20)

"So he led them on by deception. Then when they tasted the tree, their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to cover themselves with leaves of the Garden." (7:22)

"O children of Adam, We have sent down to you clothing to cover your private parts and as an adornment; but the clothing of righteousness, that is best. That is among the signs of Allah." (7:26)

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 7, verse 24 (part 3 of 3):

"O children of Adam, We have sent down to you clothing to cover your private parts and as an adornment for you; and the best clothing is the clothing of taqwa (God-consciousness). That is one of the signs of Allah, that they may remember."

The verse: "O children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you as he removed your parents from the Garden, stripping them of their clothing to show them their private parts" (7:27).

"Let not Satan tempt you as he removed your parents from the Garden, stripping them of their clothing to expose their private parts to one another."

All these instructions and observations point to the fact that this is a very important and extremely natural matter, and that the impulse to wear clothing and cover one's private parts lies in the deepest part of human nature. Clothing is an adornment and a covering for the human being, while the clothing of taqwa is a covering (satr) for the spiritual private parts of the human being.

Sound human nature has always striven to cover its physical and spiritual private parts, and it has always been eager to conceal these weaknesses. Those who wish to strip the human body of clothing, who wish to strip the human self bare by depriving it of the clothing of taqwa, who wish to remove modesty and shame before Allah and before people, those whose tongues, pens, and media are busy day and night, by various methods and through various wicked and satanic means, in stripping people of these natural impulses, they in reality want to take away from humankind those natural qualities because of which a human is human. These people want to bend humanity before that Satan who is their enemy, who began his satanic work by exposing the private parts of the human being. Then these people want to complete the Zionist plans which the Jews have prepared for the destruction of humanity, and according to those plans they want to weaken the whole of humanity so much that it cannot rise up against them, and its condition becomes such that no human quality remains within it.

Nakedness is by nature an animal characteristic. A human can be inclined toward it only when he falls from the station of humanity and descends to the level of animals. Moreover, only those whose human taste has been destroyed can perceive nakedness as beauty. Thus, the extremely backward peoples of Central Africa go about completely naked, and when Islam enters among them, the first thing it does is clothe them. Today, the so-called progressive intellectuals of the West are pushing humanity into that pit of nakedness from which Islam had rescued them; after rescuing them, Islam made them highly civilized, and made them civilized according to Islamic meaning and objectives. In Islam, the meaning of civilization and progress is that the human qualities within a person be developed and manifested to the greatest possible extent.

The nakedness of the self is that a person bids farewell to shame and modesty, and this is the goal for which the media, pens, voices and screens of Europe are working. This is such a regression into backwardness and ignorance as it once was; it cannot be called progress, culture or civilization in any sense, as the satanic media of the West is now presenting to Muslims.

The story of the creation of humankind points to all these values and standards. Thanks be to Allah, who guided the Muslims to this, saved them from all satanic whisperings, and extracted the Muslims from the filthy pond of ignorance. The Qur'an has presented this story for precisely these purposes.

Lesson No. 74 At a Glance:

The lesson before us is one of the pauses in this surah. After the first scene, this is a long pause in which a great account of the creation of mankind is related. Throughout this surah such pauses occur, as though the listeners are being told: "Stop. Consider what you have seen so far, and before moving on, understand what lessons and admonitions this scene holds for mankind."

This pause takes place in the presence of the two forces that stand ready for battle: on one side mankind, and on the other side Satan. In this pause it is explained how Satan enters, by what style and by what path, what his plan is, and in what form it appears.

The style of the Holy Quran is that it gives guidance only when a situation actually exists, is present, and a problem has arisen. Whatever stories it relates, it relates them because there are real circumstances within the Islamic movement to which that story applies. The stories of the Quran, as has been said above, are not merely for artistic and literary purposes, nor does the Quran discuss an issue merely from a theoretical standpoint. The realism and seriousness of Islam required that its guidance concern problems that the Islamic movement was actually facing at that time.

The pause that comes after this first stage of the story of humanity is connected with the real situation of Arab jahiliyyah. The Quraysh had reserved certain rights for themselves in preference to the other Arabs. People came from outside for the Hajj to the House of Allah, which the Quraysh had turned into a house of idols, and they reserved these rights for themselves on the basis of certain fabricated notions, and declared them to be the Shariah of Allah. They had given these notions the form of law and called it Shariah, so that other polytheists would follow these laws. In every jahiliyyah, soothsayers, chieftains and custodians of shrines invent such principles for the common people. The Quraysh had adopted a special title for themselves: they called themselves "Hums." They had reserved for themselves certain rights which were not available to other Arabs. Among these rights were some concerning the circumambulation (tawaf) of the House of Allah. Only they had the right to perform tawaf in the clothes they were using, whereas other Arabs could not perform Hajj in clothes that anyone had ever worn. Now these people had two options: either they would borrow clothes from the Quraysh in order to perform tawaf, or they would have new clothes made for themselves. And if they could not act upon either of these two options, then they would perform tawaf naked, and women too would be among them.

Allamah Ibn Kathir says: "Apart from the Quraysh, the other Arabs could not perform tawaf in the clothes they had worn previously. The basis of this belief was that, since they had disobeyed Allah while wearing those clothes, it was not proper for them to perform tawaf in them. The Quraysh, who were called Hums, had the right to perform tawaf in their own clothes; if someone had new clothes, he too could perform tawaf in them, but after the tawaf he would throw them away, and they would not become anyone's property. If someone could obtain neither new clothes nor borrowed ones from among the people of Quraysh, he would perform tawaf naked. Sometimes it would happen that a woman was performing tawaf naked; in that case she would cover her private parts. But women who had to perform tawaf in such a state would often perform it at night. They had fabricated these customs on their own, and had been acting upon them since the time of their forefathers. They held the belief that this ancestral practice was based on the divine Shariah. Allah the Exalted criticised them for this claim."

The verse: "And when they commit an indecency, they say, 'We found our fathers doing it, and Allah has commanded us to do it.'" (7:28)

"Say: 'Allah does not command indecency.'" (7:28) That is, what you are doing is an indecent act and is abhorrent, and Allah never commands such abhorrent acts.

"Do you attribute to Allah what you do not know?" (7:28) That is, you attribute to Allah matters whose truth you yourselves are not certain of.

"Say: 'My Lord has commanded justice.'" (7:29)

"Say: 'My Lord has commanded justice, and that you set your faces upright at every place of prayer and call upon Him, sincere to Him in religion.'" (7:29)

That is: what He has commanded is that you keep worship and places of worship in their proper state, obey the messengers who came with miracles, and worship Allah alone, because Allah does not accept the worship of anyone except on these two fundamental conditions: that it conform to the Shariah, and that it be free from shirk.

This commentary has come concerning the practical situation that existed at that time in the jahili society of the Arabs regarding the Shariah rulings on worship, tawaf and clothing, and matters of food, which they considered to be the Shariah sent down by Allah. This commentary has come within the context of the great story of the creation of mankind. Mention of food was in the context of the forbidden tree, and mention of clothing was in the incident of the removal of garments, when Adam (peace be upon him) and Hawwa were stripped of their garments through the plot of Satan. Having fallen victim to this plot, they had eaten the fruit of that forbidden tree, and the innate modesty of man was also mentioned in it: when the garment of Paradise was removed from them, they began to stitch together leaves of the trees of Paradise over themselves, and thus they began to cover their nakedness.

In short, the events that came in this story, and the comment that followed upon them, reflect the jahili situation existing among the Arabs. This story will also appear in other surahs of the Quran, but at that time its purposes for being brought will be different, and the comments and conclusions drawn from it will also be different. The Holy Quran, wherever it brings any story, presents it in relation to some practical situation of human beings, and its comments upon it are likewise in accordance with those purposes and situations. Thus the Holy Quran presents the relevant link of the story according to the circumstances of each place, and gives its details according to the temperament of each place.

(For details, see the chapter on stories in my book Al-Tasweer al-Fanni fi al-Quran.)

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 7, verse 26:

Verse No. 26.

This is a heartfelt call from Allah to humankind, and it comes after the scene of the creation of mankind's story, especially after the part in which, through Satan's conspiracy, the garment of Paradise was stripped from the bodies of Adam and Hawwa (Eve), and in which the two were seen affixing leaves of Paradise upon their bodies. They had to face this condition because they disobeyed Allah, since they had been explicitly forbidden to eat the fruit of a particular tree. This was a lapse, and its nature was not such as the details found in the distorted books of the People of the Book, the Torah and the Gospel, which contain stories whose influence is clearly visible today across all the sciences and arts of the West. In the modern age, the ideas of Freud are added to this. In these myths and idle tales it is said that the forbidden tree was the tree of knowledge and the tree of life, and that if Adam and Hawwa had eaten its fruit, Allah feared they would become gods like Him. Nor was that prohibition a prohibition of sexual intercourse, as Freud, Western sciences and arts, and Western art reflect, and on the basis of these stories they have adopted the philosophy of sexual licentiousness in the form of Freud's ideas.

In short, in view of the scene of Adam (peace be upon him) being stripped of his garment as a result of his lapse, and then the situation of circumambulating the Ka'bah naked in the Age of Ignorance (Jahiliyyah), this call comes: O human being, how much mercy and kindness Allah has shown you, by arranging clothing to cover your adornment and your private parts, and by making it a binding law for your modesty. Without clothing, you would appear in nakedness in a most repulsive state. The word (anzalna) indicates that clothing is required as a law. The term libas (clothing) sometimes applies to the covering of the private parts, that is, what is within the private parts, while the term riysh applies to the clothing used for beauty and adornment, that is, outer clothing. The word riysh also carries the meanings of luxury and wealth. All these meanings are interconnected and are mutually inclusive.

The verse: "O children of Adam, We have sent down to you clothing to cover your private parts and as an adornment; and the clothing of righteousness, that is best." (7:26)

Thereafter Allah mentions the garment of taqwa (God-consciousness) and adds that this clothing is the clothing of taqwa. This is one of the signs of Allah.

Abdul Rahman ibn Aslam has said: "If one fears Allah and covers one's private parts, that is the clothing of taqwa." The clothing of covering and the clothing of taqwa are mutually inclusive in the Shari'ah. The clothing of covering is for concealing the body and for adornment, while the clothing of taqwa conceals the shameful states of the heart and becomes the adornment of the heart. Both are mutually inclusive, because it is through the awareness of fearing Allah and being modest before Him that a person regards leaving the shameful parts of the body exposed as ugly, and the one who is not modest before Allah and does not fear Him finds bodily nakedness to be no cause for blame. Thus, in the view of Islam, being devoid of taqwa and modesty and removing one's clothing are equally ugly acts.

Concealing the body is natural modesty, and its connection is not merely with the customs of a family or society, as some people who wish to remove modesty from Islamic society proclaim, so that they may destroy the humanity of Muslims; and this is exactly in line with the plan which the Zionist leaders devised for the destruction of humanity. Rather, it is a natural impulse which Allah has placed within human beings. Furthermore, it is a legal requirement revealed by Allah. Allah has granted humans the ability to enforce this law in the world, because this earth has been placed by Allah in human authority and He has made it a place of sustenance for them.

Allah reminds humankind that through this clothing and the law of covering the body, a great mercy has been bestowed upon them. Thus Allah has saved the treasure of humanity from the fate of descending to the level of animals. Then Allah, by reminding them of all these matters, expects of them that (la'allahum yadhdhakkaroon) "perhaps they may take heed" (7:26). At this point, a Muslim can clearly understand that the great effort being made, under the names of adornment, fashion, progressivism and love, to corrupt human morals and to strip people bodily naked, is exactly in line with the Jewish conspiracy which they have prepared for the destruction of humanity. This conspiracy has been prepared by the Jews so that the strength of the Muslims may quickly be destroyed and they may quickly be enslaved; moreover, this plan has also been made for the complete uprooting of the love for the religion of Islam that still remains in the depths of people's hearts. And for this purpose, the pens, films, all educational institutions and the media of Jews and their agents continuously strive, although for humanity, adornment lies not in nakedness but in covering. Nakedness is the adornment of animals, yet today's human being is returning to ignorance and backwardness and is turning from a human into an animal. Is the human not remembering the blessing which Allah has bestowed upon him in making him a human being?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verses 27-30:

Verses 27 to 30.

This is the second call from Allah addressed to humanity. It comes within the pause for reflection that follows the story of their parents, Adam and Hawwa (Eve). In particular, it is a comment on the scene in which Satan, through his deep plotting, stripped them of their clothing: they fell victim to that plot, forgot Allah's clear command, and through Satan's whispering they committed a slip. Moreover, in light of what we said about the naked circumambulation (tawaf) in the age of jahiliyyah (the period of ignorance before Islam), it also becomes well understood why Allah addressed mankind in this manner, since they regarded this nakedness as a shari'ah (law) from Allah.

In the first call, mankind was reminded of what befell their forefather and how Allah provided for the covering of their private parts and then for their adornment. As for this second call, it is a reminder addressed generally to the children of Adam and specifically to the polytheists of Makkah, the first audience Islam addressed. It warns them not to follow Satan, not to devise for themselves a system of life, customs and law of their own, and thus not to fall into the trial of Satan, for he plotted exactly this against your father: by his scheming he had him expelled from Paradise, and by depriving them of the garment of Paradise he exposed their private parts before them. Therefore every movement that calls to nakedness is a satanic movement and a jahili movement, whether it belongs to ancient times or to the modern age. This movement is the movement of your enemy. Satan was your open enemy, and he is the perpetual enemy of Adam and his progeny. The movement for nakedness is also one aspect of the all-encompassing movement of enmity between humans and Satan. Therefore the children of Adam should not give their enemy the opportunity to succeed in this battle, and thus become a cause by which humans and jinn fill Hell.

﴿O children of Adam! Let not Satan tempt you as he expelled your parents from the Garden, stripping off from them their clothing to show them their private parts.﴾ (7:27)

To frighten mankind further, Allah informs them that Satan and his tribe see you while you cannot see them. Therefore he is more capable, through his hidden means, of leading you astray. Hence they should fear and take extreme caution, remaining alert at all times and being most watchful, lest he catch you while you are unaware.

﴿Indeed, he and his tribe see you from where you do not see them.﴾ (7:27)

Now comes the last part of this statement, which is most effective and guides toward caution: the order of Allah's decree has appointed Satan as a companion to those who do not believe. And what ruin awaits the one whose companion is Satan! Clearly he will take possession of them, mislead them, and lead them wherever he wills by the reins, and they will have no helper or supporter, nor will Allah be their friend.

﴿Indeed, We have made the devils allies of those who do not believe.﴾ (7:27)

This is a great truth: those who do not believe have Satan as their friend and helper. And in contrast, those who believe have Allah as their protector and helper. This is a frightening truth, and its consequences are frightening too, and here it is presented as a general principle. After this, an example of this principle is also presented, which is in fact present in the lives of the polytheists. Thus it becomes clear how Satan acts as a protector and helper, and how his guardianship operates in people's beliefs and practical lives. Behold the example.

﴿And when they commit an indecency, they say, "We found our fathers doing it, and Allah has commanded us to it."﴾ (7:28)

The Arab polytheists held this belief and acted upon it. They would perform tawaf naked around the Sacred House, committing this indecency, and their women participated in it too, yet they claimed that this was Allah's command, on the basis that Allah had commanded their forefathers to do so, so they had continued doing it, and that this custom had come down to them by inheritance, so they too did it.

Although they were polytheists, they were not as arrogant and rebellious as the ignorance of the modern age. Today's people say: what does religion have to do with the affairs of life? It is the right of the people to devise for themselves whatever laws, authority and customs they wish; Allah has no say in this. The followers of the old jahiliyyah committed only the offence of devising laws and a way of life for themselves and then claiming that this was the command of Allah. This error may well be more grievous and deserving of greater blame, since it is deception and fraud in the name of religion, and an exploitation of people's religious feeling. Yet in terms of self-will and arrogance, they were less than those who claim that the right of legislation for people belongs to them alone, and that they alone are entitled to decide what is beneficial for people.

Allah instructs His Prophet ﷺ to address them thus: that you are attributing a pure falsehood to Allah, and that Allah's law and its legal system, by their very nature, do not approve of indecency. So how could Allah command you to commit indecency and nakedness?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 28:

Verse: "Say: Indeed, Allah does not enjoin immorality. Do you attribute to Allah that which you do not know?" (7:28)

"Say to them: Allah has never commanded indecency. Do you speak against Allah things about which you have no knowledge that they come from Allah?"

Allah is opposed to immorality (fahsha') in every form, and the meaning of fahsha' is that a person exceeds the prescribed limit in any matter. Nakedness also falls within its definition, so how could Allah command it? Allah has set limits, and He does not command that the limits He has set be broken. He has commanded modesty, shame and God-consciousness (taqwa), so how could a command to nakedness be issued? Furthermore, the question is: who informed them of this command of Allah? The commands and laws of Allah are not established merely by claim. The commands and laws of Allah are known through His Books and His Messengers. There is no other means by which the commands of Allah can be known. No person can claim that something has come from Allah and His Messenger unless it is established from the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Therefore, no statement may be accepted in the religion of Allah without authority, otherwise there would be no resolution to that intellectual confusion in which people say things on their own yet attribute them to Allah.

Jahiliyyah (the state of ignorance before divine guidance) is, after all, jahiliyyah, and the fundamental elements of it are present in every jahiliyyah. Whenever people return to jahiliyyah, they say the same kind of thing and their thinking is of the same kind, despite the fact that a long span of time lies between the ancient and modern jahiliyyahs and they are very distant from one another in place. In the jahiliyyah in which we live today, someone rises up, a liar, and begins to say things dictated by his carnal desires, and then says, "This is the Shari'ah of Allah." Then another arrogant and rebellious person rises and denies the clear and self-evident matters of Allah's religion. He claims that Allah's religion cannot contain such rulings. How can religion issue these commands, how can religion forbid those matters? And if such people are asked for proof, they have no proof other than their own desires. We say:

"Do you attribute to Allah that which you do not know?" (7:28)

After refuting their claim that Allah has not commanded this kind of immorality, the commands of Allah are, in fact, the complete opposite and reverse of this. Allah commands justice and moderation and forbids transgressing limits; He by no means commands the transgression of boundaries or immorality. Allah's command is that in worship, in the matters of life and in calling upon Him, you should serve Allah alone, as Allah has given clear guidance in the Book He revealed. Allah has not left this matter such that every person may hold whatever opinion he wishes about it and then claim that it is from Allah. Rather, Allah has commanded that religion be purely for Allah, and that there be complete servitude to Allah alone. No one shall be a slave and obedient to another, and no one shall be bound by another's personal commands.

"Say: My Lord has commanded justice, and set your faces upright at every place of worship, and call upon Him, making your religion sincerely His." (7:29)

"O Prophet (ﷺ), say to them: My Lord has indeed commanded righteousness and justice, and His command is that you keep your direction right in every act of worship and call upon Him, keeping the religion pure for Him."

These are the commands from Allah, and they are the opposite of the situation upon which they stand. They also oppose their obedience to their forefathers and to the laws of their forefathers, since those too were servants like us; and moreover, they believe that this comes from Allah. Furthermore, these commands oppose that nakedness and bareness, since Allah bestowed a favour upon Adam and Eve by giving them clothing and adornment, and commanded them to cover themselves and make their appearance good. Again, these commands opposed the situation in which they had introduced shirk into their beliefs and their system of life.

Here the tone becomes somewhat harsh, and the lesson is recalled in severe words. They are warned of an evil end and told that at the close of this short span of life they must appear before Allah. The scene of their presentation will be that they become two parties: one party that is upon the path of Allah and bound by the command of Allah, and the other party that will be the followers of the commands of Satan.

This verse is like a beautiful cluster of fruit, within which both the starting point and the ending point of this great journey of humanity have come together.

﴿As He originated you, so you will return.﴾ (29)

Your life began in pairs: Adam and Eve, and Satan and his companions. In the same way you will be created again. One group will be obedient and submissive to Allah, and they will be among the category of Adam and Eve, and they will be believers. The other group will be of the followers and companions of Iblis, and Allah will fill Hell with them. They will be the friends of Iblis, and Iblis will be their friend, and for this reason they will enter Hell, even though they will think that they are upon guidance.

The one whose friend is Allah will be upon guidance, and the one whose friend is Satan will be astray, and in this way both these groups will return. (﴿A group He has guided, and a group upon whom misguidance has become due﴾) "He has shown a group the straight path, but upon another group misguidance has settled, because they have taken the devils as their guardians instead of Allah, and they think that they are upon the straight path." In this way they will be returning. In short, in a single moment the journey began, and in another moment its outcome was portrayed. This is the miraculous style of expression of the Holy Qur'an, and no text other than the Qur'an has ever possessed this style up to today.

Now the children of Adam are called again, and this third call is also within the same interval. Ahead, the great journey of humanity is about to begin again, which will continue according to its determined plan.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 7, verse 31:

Verses 31 to 33.

This is a further emphasis on the fundamental beliefs of the Islamic view of life. The stress is on the point that, in contrast to the jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance) of the Arabs, the foundation of Islam rests on these matters. This outlook has been prescribed for all of humanity, and it has been introduced in the context of the discussion concerning the story of the creation of this earth and of all humanity.

Among these truths, the most important is that Allah, the Exalted, has created for His creature, man, certain things, and some of these things are themselves declared forbidden by some people, and they do so without the permission of Allah and without any authority from the law of Allah, whereas this act of theirs, that is, this prohibiting and permitting, is an act of shirk. Then, it is also a fabrication against Allah, and their own personal assumption.

Accordingly, Allah calls out to them that Allah has created provisions for your adornment, so remain adorned with them. In Arabic this is called "rish" (adornment), especially at the time of worship, and worship includes tawaf (circumambulation), which they used to perform in a state of nakedness. They declared forbidden such garments which Allah had not forbidden, but which were a favour and a blessing for His servants. Therefore, it is better for them to worship Allah while adorned with the adornment Allah has provided, and not to do so naked, nor while committing indecency.

﴿O children of Adam, take your adornment at every place of worship﴾ (7:31)

And along with this, Allah the Exalted also commands all of humanity to make use of pure things here and to employ all kinds of food and drink. But do not be extravagant, and secondly, make use of pure things.

﴿And eat and drink, but do not be excessive. Indeed, He does not love those who are excessive.﴾ (7:31)

It is mentioned in the ahadith that just as they sometimes declared garments forbidden, in the same way they considered it forbidden to wear certain clothes. And these matters were fabricated by the Quraysh on their own account.

In Sahih Muslim, there is a narration from Hisham ibn Urwah that the Arabs used to perform tawaf of the House of Allah in a state of nakedness, except for the Quraysh and their offspring. These people would perform tawaf naked, unless the Quraysh gave them clothes. So the men of the Quraysh would give clothes to men, and the women would give clothes to women. Moreover, the Quraysh did not go beyond Muzdalifah, whereas other people would go as far as Arafat. The Quraysh used to say, "We are the people of the Haram, so it is not permissible for any Arab to perform tawaf in any clothes other than our clothes." Similarly, when any Arab entered the Haram, he could eat only the food of the people of the Quraysh, because if an Arab did not have a friend in Makkah who could lend him clothes, or if he did not have the facility to buy rented clothes, then two paths were open to him: one, that he perform tawaf in a state of nakedness, or two, that he perform tawaf in clothes and then throw those clothes away. Such clothes were called "luqa," and then no one would touch them.

Qurtubi, in Ahkam al-Quran, writes: It is said that the Arabs, during the Hajj, would not eat rich food, and ate only a little, and performed tawaf in a state of nakedness. They were told: "Adorn yourselves at every time of worship, and eat and drink, and do not exceed the limits." That is, do not be extravagant in declaring forbidden those things which have not been declared forbidden for you. For extravagance means exceeding limits, and exceeding limits also includes declaring lawful things to be unlawful. Breaking the bounds in permitting and going beyond the limits in forbidding are both included in transgressions.

Here the Holy Qur'an does not merely suffice with the instruction that you should go to every place of worship only wearing clothes, and benefit from the pure sustenance created by Allah, and eat and drink, but rather, by way of rebuke, it asks these people: who has declared forbidden the adornments that Allah has created for people, and who has declared forbidden the pure food that He has created? For to make lawful sustenance lawful on one's own, and to make adornment forbidden for oneself, by whose authority is this done, since the determination of what is lawful and unlawful is from the Lawgiver.

﴿Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He brought forth for His servants, and the good things of provision?﴾ (7:32)

﴿O Prophet (ﷺ), say to them: Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He brought forth for His servants, and who has prohibited the good provisions bestowed by Allah?﴾

After this admonishing question, it is declared that these garments and this pure sustenance are the right of the believers, because they are believers, and they are those who believe in the Lord who created these things. Although non-believers share these things with them in this world, yet in the Hereafter, these things are exclusively for the believers, and there will be no share for the disbelievers.

﴿Say: They are for those who believe in the life of this world, and exclusively for them on the Day of Resurrection.﴾ (7:32)

﴿Say: These things are for those who believed in the life of the world, and purely for them on the Day of Judgment.﴾

Therefore, if this is the situation, how can these be forbidden? How can a thing be specific to Muslims in the Hereafter and yet be forbidden here?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 7, verses 32–33:

Verse: "Kadhalika nufassilu al-ayati li-qawmin ya'lamun" (32)

"Thus do We explain Our signs clearly for those who have knowledge."

And it is those who understand the reality of this religion who can benefit from this explanation.

As for that which Allah has declared unlawful, if it relates to clothing, then it is also not healthy clothing. If it relates to food and the like, then it is not tayyib (good and wholesome), except for extravagance and arrogance. The things that are truly forbidden are those which they are committing day and night.

Verse: "Qul innama harrama rabbiya al-fawahisha ma zahara minha wa ma batana wal-ithma wal-baghya bighayri al-haqqi wa an tushriku billahi ma lam yunazzil bihi sultanan wa an taqulu 'ala Allahi ma la ta'lamun" (33)

Say, O Prophet (ﷺ) to them: "My Lord has forbidden only the shameful deeds, whether apparent or hidden, sin, unjust oppression against the truth, that you associate with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority, and that you say about Allah what you do not know" (that it is truly from Him).

These are the things which Allah has declared unlawful. The shameful acts that exceed the limits set by Allah, whether they are open or secret. "Ithm" refers to every disobedience. "Baghy bighayri al-haqq" is the oppression that is contrary to truth and justice, and associating anyone with Allah, when there is no proof or power behind that shirk. This includes the shirk that existed in the Arab jahiliyyah and in all other jahiliyyahs: legislating alongside Allah, whereas legislation and the making of law is one of the essential attributes of Allah. Attributing to Allah things that are not known even to the one attributing them, such as their declaring things lawful and unlawful when they had no knowledge of them, and they ascribed them to Allah without knowledge and certainty. This itself is shirk.

In this regard, al-Kalbi has narrated a strange report: when these addresses were directed at the polytheists and they were taken to task, their state was that "when the Muslims wore clothes and performed tawaf around the Ka'bah, the polytheists shamed them and tried to embarrass them."

This shows the extent to which every jahiliyyah takes its followers. Some people performed tawaf of the Ka'bah naked. Their nature had altered their condition, and their nature had been deprived of that true modesty which, in the story of Adam and Iblis, is clearly described as being present in Adam and Eve, because "when they tasted the tree, their private parts became apparent, and they began to cover themselves with the leaves of the trees of Paradise." When the disbelievers saw that the Muslims performed tawaf in clothing, adorned and with dignity and modesty, so that human qualities in accordance with the natural disposition would flourish in them and they would be protected from nakedness like animals, when the Muslims adopted this natural state, they began to criticize it.

This is the achievement of jahiliyyah. It distorts people's nature, their souls, their concepts, and their values and standards. Today the jahiliyyah of the modern age is doing to people exactly what the Arab jahiliyyah did to them, or what the Greek jahiliyyah did before it, or the Roman jahiliyyah, or the polytheistic jahiliyyah of Persia. In short, in every region and every age, these have been the features of jahiliyyah.

What is the modern jahiliyyah doing? Only this: it is stripping people naked. It is removing from their bodies the garment of modesty and piety. It calls this action progress and civilization. After this, it taunts the noble sons and noble daughters, calling them reactionary, blindly traditionalist, and rustic.

What else can the distortion of nature be called but distortion? Turning away from nature can only be called corruption of nature. The change of the scales of good and evil can only be called the alteration of the conscience, and if anyone takes pride in it, that will only be his foolish arrogance, indeed a clear rebellion. Because this disease, this animality, and this rebellion are connected with shirk; they are in fact the legislation and codification of "arbaban min dun Allah" (lords other than Allah), and they have mutually bequeathed it to one another.

The Arab polytheists took such instructions from the rulers of their regions, and these rulers exploited them merely because of their ignorance, and by making them do such unreasonable acts they imposed their leadership and lordship over them, among whom were the soothsayers, chiefs and nobles. Even today, people take such instructions from their worldly leaderships, and obedience to their directives is made obligatory like divine commands. No one can reject them.

Today, the shops of adornment and those who plan them, as well as those who plan fashion, are the lords by whose net all the women and men living in the modern jahiliyyah are ensnared. These lords issue their commands, and all those who exist across the world in the form of naked flocks carry them out, and these people carry out the orders of these planners in a state of utmost helplessness. These people do not see whether the fashion prepared for them for the new year is suitable for their circumstances and needs. Nor do they see whether this clothing is beneficial for them. Rather, with great humility, they follow their signals. If they do not follow, other cattle and animals find fault with them and taunt them.

The question is: which forces are working behind adornment and fashion houses? And which forces are they that are stripping people naked? What purposes are working behind novels and films? Which forces are behind magazines and newspapers? Some newspapers are continuously spreading moral degradation and moral corruption. The question is: what hidden power stands behind these things? The reality is that behind all global corruption stands the power of the Jews. It is these Jews who in fact have become gods for those people who have placed their reins in their hands. They achieve their aims by creating these kinds of waves in the world, and the whole world works for those aims, paying a heavy price. For these aims they spread psychological restlessness among people, change human nature, and man has been made a plaything in the hands of fashion and sexual licentiousness. Through this extravagance, wastefulness and moral corruption, this Jewish power fulfils its economic aims, because the factories of fashion, make-up and luxury goods have been set up by international Judaism, and by creating demand among people they then sell these goods back to them.

The matter of clothing and fashion is not separate from the Islamic Shari'ah. The Islamic system of life has a rule for it as well, and for this reason it has been linked with the fundamental question of faith and of tawhid and shirk. For various reasons this question is connected with doctrines and Shari'ah.

- Clothing is related to the sovereignty of Allah, because Allah is the being to whom we must turn in this matter, since clothing is something whose effects fall upon morals, the economy and other important matters of life.

- Through clothing, human distinctive qualities become manifest, and by suppressing the animal side of human personality, the human side is highlighted.

Every jahiliyyah has this characteristic: it changes the taste of the common people, their morals, and their standards of good and bad, and it calls nakedness and animality progress. And it calls modesty and the covering of the body reactionism and backwardness. In such a situation there is no need to distort human nature at all.

Today there are ignorant people among us who say: what is the connection between clothing and religion? What does religion have to do with women's clothing? What is the relationship between religion and adornment? This is the intellectual corruption that jahiliyyah produces in every age and every place.

Apparently the matter of clothing seems a minor issue, but in Islam and with the Lord the Most High it holds great importance, because on the one hand it is connected with the question of tawhid and shirk, and on the other hand it is connected with the reform or corruption of human morals and society. For this reason a very forceful and emphatic comment has been made on it here. This comment is generally made in the Qur'an after discussing major and important issues. In this comment, the children of Adam are warned that they should also reflect upon their true reality, which is that their living and dwelling here is in any case for a limited period, and one day they must depart from here, the time of which is fixed. When that time comes, not a single moment can be delayed or advanced.
