The change of the scales of good and evil can only be called the alteration of the conscience, and if anyone takes pride in it, that will only be his foolish arrogance, indeed a clear rebellion. Because this disease, this animality, and this rebellion are connected with shirk; they are in fact the legislation and codification of "arbaban min dun Allah" (lords other than Allah), and they have mutually bequeathed it to one another.

The Arab polytheists took such instructions from the rulers of their regions, and these rulers exploited them merely because of their ignorance, and by making them do such unreasonable acts they imposed their leadership and lordship over them, among whom were the soothsayers, chiefs and nobles. Even today, people take such instructions from their worldly leaderships, and obedience to their directives is made obligatory like divine commands. No one can reject them.

Today, the shops of adornment and those who plan them, as well as those who plan fashion, are the lords by whose net all the women and men living in the modern jahiliyyah are ensnared. These lords issue their commands, and all those who exist across the world in the form of naked flocks carry them out, and these people carry out the orders of these planners in a state of utmost helplessness. These people do not see whether the fashion prepared for them for the new year is suitable for their circumstances and needs. Nor do they see whether this clothing is beneficial for them. Rather, with great humility, they follow their signals. If they do not follow, other cattle and animals find fault with them and taunt them.

The question is: which forces are working behind adornment and fashion houses? And which forces are they that are stripping people naked? What purposes are working behind novels and films? Which forces are behind magazines and newspapers? Some newspapers are continuously spreading moral degradation and moral corruption. The question is: what hidden power stands behind these things? The reality is that behind all global corruption stands the power of the Jews. It is these Jews who in fact have become gods for those people who have placed their reins in their hands. They achieve their aims by creating these kinds of waves in the world, and the whole world works for those aims, paying a heavy price. For these aims they spread psychological restlessness among people, change human nature, and man has been made a plaything in the hands of fashion and sexual licentiousness. Through this extravagance, wastefulness and moral corruption, this Jewish power fulfils its economic aims, because the factories of fashion, make-up and luxury goods have been set up by international Judaism, and by creating demand among people they then sell these goods back to them.

The matter of clothing and fashion is not separate from the Islamic Shari'ah. The Islamic system of life has a rule for it as well, and for this reason it has been linked with the fundamental question of faith and of tawhid and shirk. For various reasons this question is connected with doctrines and Shari'ah.

- Clothing is related to the sovereignty of Allah, because Allah is the being to whom we must turn in this matter, since clothing is something whose effects fall upon morals, the economy and other important matters of life.

- Through clothing, human distinctive qualities become manifest, and by suppressing the animal side of human personality, the human side is highlighted.

Every jahiliyyah has this characteristic: it changes the taste of the common people, their morals, and their standards of good and bad, and it calls nakedness and animality progress. And it calls modesty and the covering of the body reactionism and backwardness. In such a situation there is no need to distort human nature at all.

Today there are ignorant people among us who say: what is the connection between clothing and religion? What does religion have to do with women's clothing? What is the relationship between religion and adornment? This is the intellectual corruption that jahiliyyah produces in every age and every place.

Apparently the matter of clothing seems a minor issue, but in Islam and with the Lord the Most High it holds great importance, because on the one hand it is connected with the question of tawhid and shirk, and on the other hand it is connected with the reform or corruption of human morals and society. For this reason a very forceful and emphatic comment has been made on it here. This comment is generally made in the Qur'an after discussing major and important issues. In this comment, the children of Adam are warned that they should also reflect upon their true reality, which is that their living and dwelling here is in any case for a limited period, and one day they must depart from here, the time of which is fixed. When that time comes, not a single moment can be delayed or advanced.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 34:

Verse 34.

This is a foundational belief in the Islamic conception of life, and the Qur'an repeatedly awakens heedless and ungrateful hearts to it, so that they do not consider this life and its limited respite to be everlasting, and do not adopt rebellion.

Here, this respite (muhlah) may also mean that for the present human species there is a natural limit of life, and it may also mean the natural lifespan of a religious community (millat) and civilization (tehzeeb), in which a fixed time is appointed for its supreme authority (iqtidar-e-aala) and its superiority in the world. Whether what is meant is the natural lifespan of a generation or the natural lifespan of a community, in any case, when the respite ends, then after that their survival, or their remaining in supreme authority, is not possible.

Before concluding this discussion, it is necessary to comment on a remarkable point. In Surah al-An'am and Surah al-A'raf, the methodology the Qur'an adopted, from the perspective of jahiliyyah, on matters of vows and offerings and the determination of lawful and unlawful, and the discussion on matters of clothing, food and dishes, contain a remarkable similarity.

There, the discussion on slaughtered animals, vows and offerings, livestock and foods began by first bringing forward the situation that was practically present, and it was said that to describe this situation as shari'ah from Allah is a fabrication upon Allah. After this it was said that you should present some proof for it, if you have any authority. It was said: ﴿Or were you witnesses when Allah enjoined this upon you?﴾ That is, when Allah made this law and instructed you to act upon it, were you yourselves present at that time? If not, then who could be a greater wrongdoer than the one who lies, and lies in order to mislead people without knowledge? Such a person is a wrongdoer, and Allah does not guide wrongdoers. After this, the statement proceeded thus: the disbelievers said that what they are associating is by the command of God, and if Allah had not willed it, it would not have happened. ﴿Those who associated will say: "If Allah had willed, we would not have associated, nor would our fathers, nor would we have made anything unlawful."﴾ Likewise, those before them also denied until they tasted Our punishment. Say, O Messenger: "Do you have any knowledge that you can bring it out for us? You only follow conjecture and assumption, and rather you invent statements from yourselves. Say: 'With Allah alone is the conclusive proof. Had He willed, He would have guided all of you.' Say: 'Bring your witnesses who testify that Allah has forbidden these things.' O Messenger, if any witness testifies, do not testify with them, and do not follow the desires of those who have denied Our signs, who do not believe in the Hereafter, and who set up equals with their Lord."

After this, their claims and fabrications were described there as ridiculous, and it was said: come, we will tell you what Allah has made unlawful, since the authority to declare lawful and unlawful belongs to Allah, and only He can make something unlawful or lawful. He said: ﴿Say: "Come, I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden you: that you associate nothing with Him..."﴾ Say: "Come, I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden you."

Here too, the same methodology has been adopted. The same stages of discussion are present here as well. First their situation was presented, that they commit shirk and set up limits of lawful and unlawful on their own, especially in matters of clothing and food. Then they were warned that they are involved in dangerous sins such as indecency and shirk, and this reality was placed before them, that Satan stripped your father of his garment in Paradise, and then it was said that the garment of covering and the garment of adornment have been sent down for you, and this is a blessing of the Lord. After this they were warned that their claim is mistaken, that these lawful and unlawful matters which you follow have been fixed by Allah and are the shari'ah of Allah. ﴿Say: "Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has brought forth for His servants?"﴾ And then the pure provision... ﴿Say: "They are, in the life of this world, for those who believe, and on the Day of Resurrection, exclusively for them. Thus do We detail the signs for a people who know."﴾ The mention of detailed signs points to certain knowledge, and following them is necessary. The conjecture and assumption that people follow regarding worship and shari'ah is not correct, and all their claims in this regard are false. After this, at the end, it is stated: come, we will tell you what Allah has forbidden. ﴿Say: "My Lord has only forbidden indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is hidden, sin, unjust transgression, and that you associate with Allah without authority, and that you say about Allah what you do not know."﴾

And just as Allah gave commands regarding clothing and food, so too He gave commands regarding worship and eating and drinking. ﴿Say: "My Lord has commanded justice"﴾ (7:29), ﴿Say: My Lord has commanded justice, and set your faces upright at every place of worship, and eat and drink, but do not be excessive; indeed, He does not love those who commit excess.﴾

In these two discussions the matter of lawful and unlawful has been linked with faith and shirk, because legislation of lawful and unlawful relates to the question of supreme sovereignty, and no human can be the supreme sovereign among men. Moreover, these matters relate to the question of whom people will serve. In short, the issue is one at both places, the methodology of discussion is one, and the steps prepared for the discussion are the same. (Sadaqa Allah al-'Azim.) And this is evidence that if this Qur'an were not from Allah, an observer would find differences in it. The importance of unity of methodology is doubled when we see that the subjects of discussion in Surah al-An'am and Surah al-A'raf are different. But when the Islamic system is confronted with jahiliyyah, the methodology of discussion becomes the same, especially when the matter concerns foundational subjects and concepts.

Lesson No. 75: Explanation of the Verses

Verses 35 to 53

This was a long pause to comment on the story of the creation of humanity. In that commentary it was said what kind of jahiliyyah (ignorance, the state of pre-Islamic darkness) humanity is now immersed in, and where Arab jahiliyyah stands in comparison. The jahiliyyah has been compared in the light of a few foundational issues, namely the covering of the body and the covering of the soul with the garment of taqwa (God-consciousness). The covering of body and soul is connected with the foundational belief of the Islamic worldview, the belief in tawhid (the oneness of God) and shirk (associating partners with God), which is the basic creed of the Islamic worldview.

From here onward begins a second call addressed to humanity. This call and summons is connected both with the matter of clothing and with the matter of humans taking guidance and following it in all affairs of life. It is connected with the question of legislation, and with the establishment of the sovereignty of Allah in the world, so that people may clearly and anew realize that the authority to take guidance on these matters belongs to the authority of the Messengers (qawwam al-risalah). And at the end of the present stage of life, on the Day of Judgment, the reckoning will be made from this viewpoint: who took guidance from the Messengers and followed them, and who disobeyed them?

Verses 35 to 36

From the very beginning of the creation of the children of Adam, Allah gave them clear guidance, and this was also a necessary condition for the authority and vicegerency (khilafah) of the children of Adam on this earth, because Allah created this earth. In it He created the necessities of human life, and upon it He bestowed authority and choice upon man so that man could play his appropriate role here. Otherwise every kind of human action would be rejected and no Muslim would accept it. In the Hereafter too it will be a sin, will cause entry into Hell, and no recompense will be able to save from that punishment.

﴿Then whoever fears (Allah) and reforms himself, there shall be no fear for them, nor shall they grieve.﴾ (35)

Because only taqwa can keep them away from sins and immoralities. The greatest immorality is committing shirk with Allah, then encroaching upon the right of Allah's supreme sovereignty and claiming divine attributes. Taqwa alone moves a person to obey God and to do good deeds, and by freeing him from fear it admits him into the abode of security, and through it attaining the pleasure of Allah becomes possible.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 7, verse 36:

Verse: "And those who deny Our signs and turn arrogantly away from them, they are the companions of the Fire; therein they will abide forever." (36)

[Urdu text: "اور جو لوگ ہماری آیات کو جھٹلائیں گے اور ان کے مقابلے میں سرکشی برتیں گے وہی اہل دوزخ ہوں گے جہاں وہ ہمیشہ رہیں گے ۔"]

Because they forgot Allah's covenant and admonition, and because of arrogance and denial, these people have joined their friend Satan, and upon them has been enforced the decree of Allah: "Whoever among you follows him, I will fill Hell with all of you."

Now from here begins the scene of appearance before Allah, to which a reference was made at the end of the previous lesson.

Verse: "And for every nation there is a term appointed; when their term comes, they cannot delay it an hour, nor can they advance it." (34)

[Urdu text: "ہر قوم کے لئے مہلت کی ایک مدت مقرر ہے ‘ پھر جب کسی قوم کی مدت آن پوری ہوتی ہے تو ایک گھڑی بھر کی تاخیر وتقدیم بھی نہیں ہوتی ۔"]

After this begins the scene of the Day of Reckoning; scenes of judgment, reward and punishment come. That is, it is a detail of the end of the pious and the arrogant. This scene is presented in the manner in which the Qur'an presents scenes of the Resurrection; readers see as though events are actually taking place.

In describing the scenes of the Resurrection, the Qur'an has adopted a particular style. In describing gathering and scattering, reckoning and accounting, reward and favour, and punishment and chastisement, it has adopted an extremely effective style. Here, the Qur'an does not merely enumerate some qualities of the world to come after the present world; rather, it presents its scenes in such a way that they appear tangible and embodied. Within them, individuals are seen moving, walking and alive, in a very clear form and shape. When a Muslim lives in the world of the Qur'an, he sees these witnessings and scenes everywhere with his own eyes. He is affected by them: sometimes his heart pounds, sometimes his hair stands on end, sometimes he is greatly frightened, sometimes he is fully at peace and cheerful. Sometimes he sees the flames of Hell before him, and sometimes he feels the breeze of Paradise. This is why the believer who lives with the Qur'an is fully aware of that Day, and those who read the verses about these scenes attentively feel that in comparison with this world they are actually living in the place of gathering. They become lost in the world of the Qur'an in the way a person moves from one place to another, from one region to another, and this movement is felt physically. In short, in their awareness and consciousness the Hereafter is not a future to come but a present state which they are witnessing.

The scenes presented here are among the longest scenes, and life appears fully vivid in them. These are continuous scenes, and the dialogues of these people are also present, and living and full dialogues are transmitted in astonishing words, completely, in the way one who sees a scene with his own eyes preserves it.

As we said earlier, these scenes come after commentary on the story of Adam, when Adam was removed from Paradise. His wife was also expelled with him, and this expulsion came about as a result of Satan's whispering. After this, the children of Adam were also warned to beware of the temptations of Satan, lest he harm them in the same way that he caused their father to be expelled from Paradise through his deceit. With this warning, that if they abandon the messengers who would come and follow Satan, they would deserve the punishment of Hell. After these matters, witnesses for appearance before Allah on the Day of Resurrection were presented. These witnesses were presented as though this story were occurring immediately after the story of Adam. Suddenly the appearance of the messengers and their aims come before us; suddenly the scene of those who are Satan's followers appears; suddenly those who oppose Satan and are heirs of Paradise appear. They hear a call from the higher world: "This is the Paradise of which you are the heirs, because of your good deeds." Verse: "Such is the Paradise which you have been made to inherit." It appears as though travellers are returning to their homes, emigrants are returning to their dwellings, and now they are to remain forever in this abode of bliss.

The harmony between this story and this commentary is that first the story comes, and its scenes are presented in the higher world. After that comes the commentary upon it, and perhaps the Resurrection. The beauty of this harmony is beyond description. This account begins among the angels in the higher world. At that time there was the auspicious ceremony of the creation of Adam and Eve. Adam and Eve were placed in Paradise, and the events of their expulsion from Paradise through Satan's whispering took place. The expulsion occurred because they did not render complete obedience and servitude; and in the higher world itself these scenes of beginning and end are joined, and between them the long scenes of human life are interwoven. As if on a single stage, all these scenes of beginning, middle and end have been presented. They are in extremely fine harmony and appropriate manner and style.

Now we have arrived in the place of gathering, and in it there is presented before Allah those who fabricate lies against Allah. The fabrication and calumny of these people is that they inherited from their forefathers certain customs and regulations, and have themselves devised certain rules and laws on their own part, and they say that these are from Allah. There is also the appearance of those who denied the messengers sent by Allah, although they had brought a certain Shariah. Against it, they relied on conjecture and speculation and rejected knowledge and certainty. These people continued in worldly luxury and spent the period of trial in great revelry, and the message that the messengers presented to them also reached them, which it was not their destiny to accept.

Now look at those who fabricated lies against Allah and denied His signs, although messengers from their Lord had come to them. In this scene, their souls are first seized, as though the accused are being arrested. Then the following dialogue takes place between them. The angels will say: "Tell us, where are now those deities you used to call upon besides Allah?" They will say: ﴿They have vanished from us.﴾

Where now are those claims through which you used to fabricate lies against Allah, and where are those gods you had taken as friends in the world, through whom you fell into trial and abandoned the call brought by the messengers? Why are these powers not coming to your aid at this critical hour, when your lives are being taken and you find no helper who can delay death for even a moment? In such circumstances, their only answer can be this: ﴿They will say, "They have vanished from us."﴾ (7:37)

They have vanished from us in such a way, and have disappeared so completely, that we find no trace of them. They are no longer coming toward us. In short, these people will be in such a wretched state that their gods will not be able to turn their attention to them, nor will they be able to help them in such dire circumstances. And who could be more losing than gods who cannot reach their servants, in such difficult times?

﴿And they will bear witness against themselves that they were indeed disbelievers.﴾ (7:37) Earlier, when punishment came upon them in the world, they too made this same admission. ﴿So when Our punishment came to them, their only plea was that they said, "Indeed, we were wrongdoers."﴾

Now the scene of the presentation before the Divine Court is over, and the next scene comes into view. These criminals are now in the Fire of Hell. The intermediate links between these two scenes are absent. The events of death and the events of resurrection and gathering are missing from between them, as though they were seized and thrown straight into Hell.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verses 38–39:

Verse 38 to 39.

Verse: "He will say, 'Enter into the Fire among nations that have passed away before you, of jinn and mankind.' (7:38)

"That is, join your companions: among mankind and jinn, join those who are your friends, but in Hell. Did you not know that Iblis disobeyed his Lord? Did he not cause Adam and his wife to be removed from Paradise? Did Satan not lead the children of Adam astray? Did Allah not warn that very Satan that he and all his followers would be thrown into Hell? So now, all of you enter Hell willingly: some go ahead and some follow behind them. You are all friends of one another, and all of you equally deserve it."

These nations, peoples and communities were so bound together in friendship, alliance and attachment that the last nation was a follower of the first nation, and the subordinate community took its guidance from the community it followed. But today the situation is that enmity has arisen between them, and they are cursing one another.

Verse: "Every time a nation enters, it curses its sister nation." (7:38)

"Observe how a son will be cursing his father; how wretched is this end. A friend will be reviling his friend. When the later ones join the earlier ones, and those far and near are all in one place, then the dispute and contention among them will begin thus."

Verse: "Until, when they have all gathered there, the last of them will say of the first of them, 'Our Lord, these are the ones who led us astray, so give them a double punishment of the Fire.'" (7:38)

"Thus begins the affliction of these people. In this scene, friends and companions also come into view; these people revile one another, and now they have become enemies of one another. They rail at one another and demand from Allah that a severe punishment be given to one another. Yet they used to fabricate lies against the 'Lord' in the world and deny His signs. Now they call Him 'our Lord'. Now they are turning only towards Him and facing only towards Him, but the answer given to them by Allah, and the manner in which their supplication is accepted, is this."

Verse: "He will say, 'For each there is double, but you do not know.'" (7:38)

"The answer will be: each one has double punishment, but you do not know. For you and for all of them there is a double punishment."

When those people heard this decision, those against whom the complaint had been made mocked those who had made the supplication severely, and turning to them they said that we are all equally guilty.

Verse: "And the first group will say to the second group, 'You had no superiority over us, so taste the punishment for what you used to earn.'" (7:39)

"And the earlier group will say to the later group: (if we were deserving of blame, then) what superiority did you have over us? Now taste the punishment as a result of your earnings."

Here this grievous scene ends, and after it comes a commentary to establish that this end of theirs is a logical outcome, and it is explained that no change in it is possible at all. This commentary comes before the scene of the truthful believers, and is entirely the opposite of that grievous scene.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verses 40–41:

Verses 40–41

Now pause and let your imagination dwell on this. It is a strange scene. A camel is being made ready to pass through the eye of a needle. It is said that they must wait until this needle's eye opens up wide enough for a camel to pass through, and only then can the doors of Paradise open for these disbelievers, and only then can their repentance be accepted. But the time has already passed. Now they cannot enter Paradise in the same way that a camel cannot pass through the eye of a needle. Therefore they will remain in Hell forever, and these people will be gathered there one after another. In it they will continue to blame one another, continue to curse one another, and continue to demand punishment for one another, yet all of them will remain afflicted by that same torment.

﴿Thus do We recompense the guilty.﴾ (7:40)

﴿For them there will be a bed of Hell, and above them coverings of fire.﴾ (7:41)

That is, their bedding will also be of the fire of Hell, and the word mihad (bed) is applied to it in a mocking manner. It will be a bed in which there is neither softness nor any comfort, and the covering over them will also be of fire. That is, they will be surrounded by fire from every side.

﴿Thus do We recompense the guilty.﴾ (7:40)

The wrongdoers are indeed the guilty, and they are those who associate partners with God and deny the signs of God. In the Qur'anic usage, these attributes are synonymous. Now, in contrast to this scene, look at the other scene:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verses 42–43:

Verses 42 to 43.

Those who believed and did righteous deeds according to their capacity (for Allah imposes upon no soul except that within its capacity), they are the companions of the Garden, wherein they will abide forever. They will be the owners of these gardens by the grace and mercy of Allah, and He has made them inheritors and owners of these Gardens. And this is because they adopted righteous deeds after faith, and these gardens are the recompense for their having followed the Messengers and gone against Satan. They obeyed the commands of Allah, the Most Merciful and Most Generous, and disobeyed Satan, the accursed; yet all of this was made possible only by the mercy of Allah. Had it not been for the mercy of Allah, it would not have been possible for them to do any of this. The Prophet ﷺ expressed this very theme in a hadith: "None of you will enter Paradise solely on account of his deeds." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His mercy and grace."

Note: There is no contradiction between this verse and the blessed saying of the Prophet ﷺ, because the sayings of the Prophet ﷺ are also based on revelation. The disputes that the Islamic sects have raised on this subject are based on misunderstanding; these disputes were based merely on personal desires. Allah knew that man is a weak, feeble and helpless creature. He cannot, by his deeds alone, reach the level of deserving Paradise, nor can he enter Paradise on the basis of deserving any single blessing in the world. Therefore Allah made it incumbent upon Himself that He would be Most Merciful and Most Generous, and would accept the few good deeds of human beings, and on the basis of those few deeds would write their names for Paradise, but this would purely be His grace and generosity. Thus they will be deserving of Paradise on account of their deeds, but the bestowal of entitlement on the basis of those few deeds will be due solely to the mercy of Allah.

On one side, these deniers, liars, criminals, wrongdoers, disbelievers and polytheists, the people of Hell, will curse one another, quarrel among themselves, and their hearts will boil with rancour and enmity, though in the world they were companions and friends. On the other side, those who believed and did righteous deeds will be brothers in Paradise, loving friends, sincere allies and close companions, compassionate to one another, and the shade of love will be upon them.

﴿And We will remove whatever rancour is in their breasts﴾ (7:43)

Nevertheless, they were human beings who believed; they lived their lives as humans. Many times they became displeased with one another in the world, but they concealed that displeasure, and resentment arose in their hearts against one another, but they overcame that resentment; yet some traces of it remained in their hearts until the end.

Qurtubi, in his tafsir Ahkam al-Quran, says: "The Prophet ﷺ said that rancour (ghill) will lie outside the gates of Paradise like the droppings of camels; Allah will have cast it out from the hearts of the believers." And it is narrated from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: "I hope that I, Uthman, Talhah and Zubair (may Allah be pleased with them all) will be among those about whom it was said: ﴿And We will remove whatever rancour is in their breasts﴾."

When the people of Hell are surrounded by fire on every side, on the other side the people of Paradise, in their gardens, will have rivers flowing beneath them, and a cool, pleasant breeze will be blowing through the whole atmosphere.

﴿Rivers will flow beneath them﴾ (7:43)

On one side the people of Hell will be cursing one another and grappling with each other, and on the other side the people of Paradise will be praising Allah and acknowledging His favours.

﴿And they will say: "All praise is for Allah, who guided us to this. We could never have found guidance had Allah not guided us. Indeed the Messengers of our Lord came with the truth."﴾ (7:43)

On one side, the people of Hell will be told, by way of scorn, mockery and to bring shame upon them:

﴿He will say: "Enter into the Fire among the nations of jinn and men who passed away before you."﴾ (7:38)

﴿And they will be called out: "This is the Paradise which you have been made to inherit, for what you used to do."﴾ (7:43)

In this way, a complete contrast between the people of Paradise and the people of Hell has been presented in these verses. Now these scenes proceed further. Now before us is a new scene: the people of Paradise have descended into Paradise and are content, and the people of Hell have also become certain that this is their eternal end. So the people of Paradise now taunt them, and they too respond in helplessness.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verses 44–45:

This call, how deeply mocking and how bitter it is, only those who know the language can fully grasp. The believers are firmly certain that Allah's promise is true and that His warning is inevitable, yet they still question the people of Hell, and in reply they can only utter the single word "Yes" (ہاں). Upon that one "yes" the reply ends and the exchange is cut off, and a voice is heard:

﴿Then a caller will call out among them: "The curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers, (44) who turn people away from the way of Allah and seek to make it crooked, and who disbelieve in the Hereafter."﴾ (45)

From this verse it becomes clear that "wrongdoers" (ظالمین, al-zalimin) is synonymous with "disbelievers," because it is these very people who turn others away from the path of Allah. They want to divert people from the straight path and set them on a crooked one, and these same people deny the Resurrection.

The attribute that they wish to make the way of Allah crooked shows what the plan of those who want to hinder the common people from the path of Allah is. Their method is to propose a crooked path; they do not set people on the straight path. They desire crookedness and flee from "straightness" (سیدھ). There is only one form of steadfastness: that a person adopts the methodology (منہاج, minhaj) and Shariah of Allah. Every path other than this is crooked, and whoever intends another path will eventually arrive at the abode of disbelief. Disbelief means that a person becomes a denier of accountability in the Hereafter, because if someone has certain conviction of meeting the Lord in the Hereafter, he would never turn anyone away from the way of Allah, nor would he himself deviate from the methodology and Shariah of Allah. In short, the portrayal of those who block the way of Allah in this verse is extremely accurate and comprehensive, and in every age the mindset of the enemies of religion is exactly this.

Now the scene shifts to a new area. This is the dividing barrier between Paradise and Hell. Upon that barrier too there are some of Allah's creatures seated; these people recognize the people of Paradise by their marks, and they also recognize the people of Hell by their marks.

Behold, see what impressions these people present about the people of Paradise and the people of Hell.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verses 46–50:

It is related in the narrations that the people who will stand on the A'raf (the heights) will be a group of human beings. Remember that the A'raf will be a place between Paradise and Hell. These will be the people whose good and bad deeds are equal in weight. Neither will their good deeds be able to take them into Paradise with the people of Paradise, nor will their bad deeds be able to take them into Hell with the people of Hell. These people will be in an intermediate state, awaiting the grace and mercy of Allah. They will be able to recognise the people of Paradise by their signs, for the faces of the people of Paradise will be bright and white, a light will flow before them, and their faith will be apparent. These people will also be able to recognise the people of Hell by their signs, for their faces will be black and their faces will be ashen, or they will recognise them by the mark that will be placed on their noses, as in Surah al-Qalam: "Sanasimuhu 'ala al-khurtum" (68:16), "We shall brand them upon the nose." So these people of the A'raf will greet the people of Paradise, and the greeting will be of such a manner that they will hope that they too will soon be deemed worthy of entering Paradise. And when they look at the people of Hell, their glance will be fleeting; they will not willingly choose to look at them. Upon seeing them, they will begin to seek refuge in Allah, saying: O Lord, do not make us their companions.

"And between them there is a barrier, and upon the A'raf will be men who recognise each by his marks. And they will call out to the companions of Paradise: 'Peace be upon you.' They have not entered it, though they are hoping to. And when their eyes are turned toward the companions of the Fire, they will say: 'Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people.'" (7:46–47)

After this, the companions of the A'raf turn their attention to the great criminals. These were well-known types of people, and the signs of Hell were also evident upon them. Upon them they make this remark: Where has your assembly and your might gone that you had in the world? In this manner they shame them.

"And the companions of the A'raf will call out to men whom they recognise by their marks, saying: 'Your gathering has not availed you, nor has that which you used to be arrogant about.'" (7:48)

Then these people of the A'raf, recognising the leading figures of Hell by their signs, will call out: "See, today your gatherings have not benefited you, nor has the equipment on which you relied as something great." Now consider your own condition, where you lie; what benefit did your assembly give you, and what protection did your arrogance give you? Now these people remind those great criminals that you used to say about the people of faith that they had gone astray, and that these people are deprived of the mercy of Allah.

"Are these the ones about whom you swore that Allah would not give them any of His mercy?" (7:49)

Now observe where you stand, and also observe what the commands of Allah are regarding them. They are:

"Enter Paradise; there is no fear upon you, nor shall you grieve." (7:49)

Indeed, there is also a voice heard from the people of Paradise, which is both hopeful and pleading for mercy. The reply that comes from the other side is extremely bitter, painful and instructive. Consider it carefully.

Thus the scenes of this long panorama appear and pass away. For a moment we see the Hereafter, and at the same time a glimpse of the world is shown. For a moment we are with those who are burning in the Fire, who thought that they would not be presented before Allah, and who had denied the signs of Allah, although a clear and detailed Book had already come to them, whose details were based on the knowledge of Allah. They cast it behind their backs and adopted the conjectures and doubts of their own choosing. In the very next moment we see these same people in the world awaiting the outcome of this Book, waiting for the threats written in it to materialize. They are warned of this evil end, but in that scene it has already come to pass.

These are wondrous scenes which were presented on the pages of this Book, and in this manner only this eloquent Book could present them. Thus this long depiction ends here, and upon it comes the final comment from Allah, in which people are given a clear reminder of these scenes of the Resurrection and are warned what the outcome will be for those who reject the Messengers of Allah and the signs of Allah.

It is said that the people await the outcome described in this Book. So this is its outcome, and at that outcome there will be no room for repentance. No intercession will avail in the difficulties, and it will not be possible to give a second chance for a trial.

Thus this scene ends, and a person remains lost in it. When this scene ends, the observer feels as if he has returned to the world from the field of the Resurrection. It seems that in the blink of an eye we went to the Hereafter and came back.

These whole scenes are based on the journey of life: the long journey of life, the gathering and dispersal, the reckoning and accounting, and reward and punishment. Whereas in the earlier lesson, humanity began its journey, when the forefather of mankind was in Paradise, and because of his lapse, mankind descended from Paradise.

Thus the Holy Quran takes a person and his conceptions from one place to another; the records of time and place are folded up, distances are erased, and a person is taken on a tour of the heavens and the earth, and this tour is conducted in a few moments, so that he may take heed and pay attention to the words of those who warn. And at the beginning of Surah al-A'raf, Allah the Exalted said excellently:

"A Book has been sent down to you, so let there be no constriction in your heart about it, that you may warn thereby, and as a reminder for the believers. Follow what has been sent down to you from your Lord, and do not follow other than Him as protectors. Little do you take heed." (7:2-3)

Thus the scenes of this long panorama appear and pass away. For a moment we see the Hereafter, and at the same time a glimpse of the world is shown. For a moment we are with those who are burning in the Fire, who thought that they would not be presented before Allah, and who had denied the signs of Allah, although a clear and detailed Book had already come to them, whose details were based on the knowledge of Allah. They cast it behind their backs and adopted the conjectures and doubts of their own choosing. In the very next moment we see these same people in the world awaiting the outcome of this Book, waiting for the threats written in it to materialize. They are warned of this evil end, but in that scene it has already come to pass.

These are wondrous scenes which were presented on the pages of this Book, and in this manner only this eloquent Book could present them. Thus this long depiction ends here, and upon it comes the final comment from Allah, in which people are given a clear reminder of these scenes of the Resurrection and are warned what the outcome will be for those who reject the Messengers of Allah and the signs of Allah.

It is said that the people await the outcome described in this Book. So this is its outcome, and at that outcome there will be no room for repentance. No intercession will avail in the difficulties, and it will not be possible to give a second chance for a trial.

Thus this scene ends, and a person remains lost in it. When this scene ends, the observer feels as if he has returned to the world from the field of the Resurrection. It seems that in the blink of an eye we went to the Hereafter and came back.

These whole scenes are based on the journey of life: the long journey of life, the gathering and dispersal, the reckoning and accounting, and reward and punishment. Whereas in the earlier lesson, humanity began its journey, when the forefather of mankind was in Paradise, and because of his lapse, mankind descended from Paradise.

Thus the Holy Quran takes a person and his conceptions from one place to another; the records of time and place are folded up, distances are erased, and a person is taken on a tour of the heavens and the earth, and this tour is conducted in a few moments, so that he may take heed and pay attention to the words of those who warn. And at the beginning of Surah al-A'raf, Allah the Exalted said excellently:

"A Book has been sent down to you, so let there be no constriction in your heart about it, that you may warn thereby, and as a reminder for the believers. Follow what has been sent down to you from your Lord, and do not follow other than Him as protectors. Little do you take heed." (7:2-3)

**Lesson 76: At a Glance**

In the first two lessons we traveled through the story of the beginning of humankind, its descent from Paradise, the field of gathering and resurrection, and the scenes of Paradise and Hell. In the next lesson we journey through *Malakut al-Samawat wal-Ard* (the dominion of the heavens and the earth). The aim is to observe the inner workings of this expansive universe. Before the creation of humankind, listen to the account of how the whole universe was created. Attention is drawn to reflect on the secrets and mysteries of this universe and to consider what its story of creation is. Reflect on its sights and phenomena. Consider the succession of night and day moving through the rotation of the heavens. Look at the sun and the moon, and observe the binding of the planets and stars in the vastness of space. Consider the circulation of winds in the atmosphere and their effects, the clouds and rain, and then the dead earth which, after the mercy of rain, becomes fresh and fertile, one moment lifeless and the next full of crops and fruits.

The story of the creation of humankind, within the domains of God's sovereignty, has already been related. After that, the beginning and end of humanity's long journey have been described. Before this, it was explained what the outcome of following Satan and of arrogance in submitting to God's signs and commands would be. It has also been shown what the jahili (pre-Islamic ignorant) concepts and customs are, and what value the law that humans make for themselves holds in the sight of God. After these subjects, a person is taken into the vastness of the universe, so that he may return to his Lord, who is its Creator, who subjects it, and who governs this vast and boundless universe through His system of divine decree and destiny. For this He has established a fixed order (*namus*). It is He who created the universe, and He alone holds the supreme sovereignty of authority.

Through this journey into the dominion of the heavens, a profound impression is conveyed: this entire universe is obedient to its Lord. Therefore, within this unimaginably vast and wide universe, the arrogance and rebellion of this small human being is disobedience to the universe itself. By such conduct, a person rebels simultaneously against the order of nature and the order of the Shari'ah. Therefore, while living within this universe, a person should not adopt such an attitude.

﴿Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly. Indeed, He does not like transgressors. And do not cause corruption on the earth after it has been set in order, and call upon Him in fear and in hope. Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good.﴾ (7:55–56)

Making religion sincerely for Allah, and the submission of all humankind to the worship of Allah, is a small part and a little branch of that great servitude and submission which the vast and boundless universe continually offers before the Lord of majesty. This is the thought and the concept which the entire Qur'an seeks to establish with great excellence in the heart, mind, and beliefs of a human being. I say that whatever heart and mind opens the doors of thought and perception and turns toward this whole universe and the laws hidden or manifest within it, will inevitably be affected by it, firmly and deeply, and will come to realize from the depths of its heart that the One who created this universe and its laws is supremely great, and that the same Creator alone deserves supreme sovereign authority. This reflection is the first step which leads a person toward accepting the call of the prophets. Then a person fully submits to the commands of Allah, the Lord of the worlds, just as the whole universe is in submission, and thus the person walks in step with the universe.

The Qur'an makes the recognition of the reality of the universe the first rung in explaining the reality of divinity, and in this way it prepares all humanity for the servitude of Allah alone. In this manner it introduces human consciousness and personality to the reality of worship. A person attains the taste of servitude with complete tranquility, and becomes certain that he and this universe spread around him are both walking together on the path of worship of the Lord.

The purpose of establishing, from the whole universe, the proof of Allah's worship is not merely rational argument, namely that since the universe is subjected to Allah's control, it is fully obedient, and with the utmost submission, deep and complete, it is bound by Allah's command and decree, therefore a human being too should be like this. The Qur'an's aim is not only rational argument; it also seeks to generate within a person another sentiment, a feeling that a person and this whole universe are companions and partners in this worship and servitude, and that a person can perform this worship with complete tranquility. In this way, a person becomes a member of the caravan of the universe, which is obedient to its Lord.

Thus every human being worships willingly, content with the decree. No external compulsion is forcing him; he is not worshipping under coercion but out of love and tranquility. Because of this worship he comes into harmony with the whole universe. Therefore such a person does not seek escape routes from servitude, nor does he wish to free himself from this obligation, because through this understanding servitude becomes his nature and a source of joy for him. It is a worship that frees a person from every servitude other than to Allah, and makes him a servant of the exalted and majestic Lord, who is the Lord of the worlds.

This very worship is the embodiment of faith and gives it flavour. Through this worship the meaning of Islam becomes manifest, and life, spirit and freshness arise within Islam. This is the foundation upon which Islam must stand, and this foundation must be firmly strengthened. Only after that should laws and the Shari'ah be given to a servant. Only after that should the acknowledgment of rules and regulations come. This is why the method and style of the Qur'an first creates in a person this consciousness and taste, strengthens it, and this is a most firm and solid method.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 7, verse 54:

Verse No. 54.

The Islamic doctrine of tawhid is a belief that eliminates every kind of human conception concerning the being and attributes of Allah. It also negates any notion of the modes (kayfiyat) of Allah's actions, because "there is nothing like unto Him" (﴿لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ﴾). Accordingly, the human imagination cannot draw any picture of Allah, because human imagination and human reason would superimpose upon Him those images which it derives from its environment, and into it would enter the forms that man sees; whereas the Being of Allah is such that none other being is like it. Therefore the human imagination cannot draw any picture of Him. And when the Divine Being lies outside the sphere of imaginative depiction, then the modes of Allah's actions also lie beyond the realm of reason. Man can only do this: the traces of the Divine Being and of the Divine acts can alone become the object of our understanding and perception.

Accordingly, questions such as: how did Allah create the heavens and the earth? How then did Allah settle upon the Throne? And what is the Throne like upon which the Lord, may He be exalted, settled? All these questions are vain questions and are contrary to the principles of Islamic concepts and beliefs. Asking such questions is itself a vain matter, and anyone who is familiar with these principles of Islamic concepts and beliefs will never attempt to answer these questions. Some groups among the Islamic sects have attempted to answer these questions, which was an extremely regrettable pursuit. The history of Islamic thought is full of such debates, and these debates arose at the time when Islamic thought was afflicted with the disease of Greek [philosophical] speculation.

As for the six days in which Allah created the earth and the heavens, this too is an unseen reality, the true knowledge of which belongs to Allah alone. At that time man did not exist, so that he could say anything about that creation and the time of creation. Nor can man say anything about the other creatures of Allah. The verse states: ﴿مَا أَشْهَدْتُهُمْ خَلْقَ السَّمَوَاتِ وَلَا خَلْقَ أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ ("I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor their own creation") — you did not witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of your own selves. After this, whatever anyone says on these subjects will not be based upon any certain principle.

These may be six stages, they may be six modes, and they may be six days of Allah. The Days of Allah are not like those days which we observe as a result of the movements of celestial bodies, because before the creation of the universe those celestial bodies did not exist by which we determine time. Apart from these, these days could be something else as well. Therefore no human being can determine definitively what is meant by the number six of days. Whatever humans have said on this matter is, in any case, human conjecture based upon speculation and estimation. It is surprising that some people regard these estimates as knowledge and science, which is clear arrogance and is founded upon mental and spiritual defeat. This is tantamount to bowing before science, which is itself an uncertain thing and is very often based upon hypotheses.

We do not pollute this verse with those hypotheses, because due to those hypotheses no addition is made to its meaning. Let us begin a journey through this vast and wide universe. Let us cast another look at the verse.

﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ اسْتَوَى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ النَّهَارَ يَطْلُبُهُ حَثِيثًا وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ وَالنُّجُومَ مُسَخَّرَاتٍ بِأَمْرِهِ أَلَا لَهُ الْخَلْقُ وَالْأَمْرُ تَبَارَكَ اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ (54)

"Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then settled upon the Throne. He covers the night with the day, which pursues it swiftly, and [He created] the sun, the moon and the stars, subjected by His command. Surely, His is the creation and the command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds."

This magnificent universe that we see, which is extremely vast, is created by Allah, and Allah is dominant over it and exalted above it. He runs it with power and management; He covers the night with the day and then makes the night pursue the day. This sequence continues in a constant revolving form; night and day keep moving one after the other. He who holds the sun, moon and stars in His control is the Guardian, the Disposer and the Manager. He is your Lord. He alone deserves to be Lord. He trains you through His natural system; you gather according to His system; He makes laws for you by His command; He judges among you according to His law. He is the Creator and He is the Sovereign. Just as no one shares with Him in creation, so no one shares with Him in political sovereignty. This is the real issue which is the spirit of this lesson: regarding divinity, lordship, political sovereignty and supreme authority, considering Allah alone and without partner, and so on. Its requirement is that man, throughout his whole life, be bound by the Shariah of Allah, and this is the principal theme of this entire surah. Sometimes it is discussed in the context of matters of clothing and food, and sometimes in another form, as was explained in Surah al-An'am in the context of livestock, crops and vows and offerings.

Keeping in view the objective of the Holy Quran, we should also not let slip from our sight how high the standard of the beauty of these scenes is, how full of life and movement they are, and how much signification and guidance lies within them. How excellent a style the Holy Quran has adopted to achieve this great objective. Along with the revolution of night and day, the revolution of thoughts and concepts and the free movement of reflection in this universe, the pursuit of the day by the night and its failure to catch it, is such a striving that human intuition cannot pass over it with heedlessness and carelessness; man cannot help being affected by this constant motion. Rather, man always remains in a state of expectation and hope.

Motion and life in this universe naturally appear beautiful; then, presenting the revolution of night and day before a living and purposeful Being for man's contemplation is an extremely beautiful mode of expression. No human mode of expression can present it with such beauty; this is the absolute inimitability of the Quran.

When a person becomes accustomed to a scene, the effects of its beauty and charm vanish because of that habit. Man passes through these scenes like a dull-natured person, unaffected. The Holy Quran presents habitual scenes and sights in such a manner that they cease to be ordinary, routine scenes; it presents them in a new style, and the effects of that mode of expression are produced in such a way that it is as if man is seeing this scene for the very first time. Look at the scenes of the revolution of night and day under discussion: these are not ordinary, familiar, commonplace scenes, but rather night and day appear like living humans chasing one another, and they appear as realities and persons possessing will and spirit. In this movement and race, night and day are shown as companions and familiar with man, and their motion is expressed as the motion in which people chase one another.

Similarly, the sun, moon and stars are also presented in this scene as if they were living spirits, upon whom Allah's commands descend; they move in accordance with those commands and move with complete obedience and loyalty. They are in such discipline that they receive orders and act upon them, going wherever they are directed, just as living, uniformed soldiers receive orders.

The fact is that by this mode of expression man is moved with joy, immediately becomes ready to carry out the commands of Allah, and considers himself a member of the caravan of the loyal ones of the universe; and the grip of the Quran upon man appears in the manner of someone who is in the captivity of a king. Remember that the Quran addresses human nature. This nature was created by the Creator who speaks to man in the form of the Quran, and Allah is thoroughly acquainted with the secrets and mysteries of human nature.

When the matter reaches this point, when understanding and intuition arise within human beings and they become companions of the living and everlasting scenes of this universe, before this they used to pass through these beautiful scenes like heedless and dull-natured people, unaffected. And when man becomes certain that these scenes are subjugated in Allah's hand, obedient to His command, and do not disobey in the slightest degree the laws and ordinances of their Creator, then at this point the Quran turns man's attention to his Lord: call upon your Lord with utmost humility and reverence; since He is your Lord, therefore attach yourself to Him and observe the bounds and limits of Allah. Do not encroach upon Allah's political sovereignty, and do not, leaving aside the Shariah of Allah on this earth, follow your own desires, especially when Allah has arranged the interests of mankind through His system.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verses 55–56:

Verses 55–56

These instructions are given at a time when the one who reflects is psychologically fully prepared to accept them. He is in a state of supplication and turning back to Allah, and after contemplating this magnificent cosmos he stands before Allah in a state of humility and lowliness. Khufyah (secrecy) means: do not cry out and shout; call upon Him in a soft, low voice, because it befits the majesty of Allah that a person calls upon Him in a very gentle and low voice, and in a manner that shows that Allah is near and hears.

Muslim narrates: Hadrat Abu Musa (may Allah be pleased with him) reports that we were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a journey. In another narration it comes that we were in a ghazwah (military campaign), and the people began to recite Allahu Akbar loudly. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O people, be gentle and call upon Him in your hearts. You are not calling upon one who is deaf, nor upon one who is absent; you are calling upon the One who hears, who is near, who is with you."

Here the style of the Qur'an is creating in people the sense that the Being of Allah is exalted, near, and that in the time of supplication and calling upon Him, the Qur'an practically seeks to create a bearing and form which produces the feeling that the one calling out is ashamed to shout and cry out because of the superiority of the Divine Being. Those in whose hearts the greatness of Allah is firmly established keep away from noise and clamour in the presence of Allah.

In short, in this atmosphere of humble supplication, lowliness and submission, Allah forbids people from claiming for themselves that sovereignty which they used to claim in the days of Jahiliyyah, because the right of sovereignty and supreme authority belongs to Allah alone. Along with this, the prohibition also comes: refrain from causing corruption on the earth, since through the system of the Islamic Shari'ah Allah has set it right. The one who calls upon Allah in humility, supplication and utmost secrecy, the One who is both near and hearing, obviously does not spread corruption on the earth after its reform, because between these two impressions there is a deep inner and psychological connection. The method of reform in the Qur'an is that it works with the deep thoughts and psychological inclinations of hearts, and only that Being can adopt this method who is Subtle and All-Aware.

Verse: "Call upon your Lord in humility and in secret. Indeed, He does not like transgressors. And do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation, and call upon Him in fear and in hope. Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good." (55–56)

Fear so that you may be saved from His wrath, and hope so that He may be pleased with you and grant reward. Those who worship Allah do so as though they see Him, and if they do not see Him, then their state is such that they consider that Allah sees them. As comes in the content of the hadith, this is ihsan, according to the definition of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Once again the Qur'an turns over another page of this open universe for human contemplation. This page lies open before us at all times, yet we pass by it heedlessly; we take no impression from it, and we do not hear its call. This is the page to which a reference was made in the preceding verse in the context of the mercy of Allah. Here that same page is opened as an example of the mercy of Allah: rain is falling from the heavens, various kinds of crops are growing from the earth, and the earth comes back to life after death, that is, it becomes green and fresh.
