Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 7, verse 57:

Verse No. 57.

Here, within this universe, the signs of the lordship (rububiyyah) of God are recorded: for instance, the activity in the universe, control over it, its well-ordered system, and the limiting and determining of its forces. All these matters are manifestations of God's great operations, and they are matters which show that no one other than God can be Lord. He alone is the Creator and Provider, the Causer of causes, and these causes He has prepared for His creation.

The wind blows at all times; at all times it lifts and drives the clouds across this universe. At all times rain falls from the clouds. Yet all these matters are manifestations of God's grace and mercy, as is the reality. This fact lies beyond our observation. It is something new, which has been woven into the context of the discourse and presented here in an extremely effective, moving and vivid manner, as though the scene were before our eyes.

It is God who drives the winds, and they carry His mercy. They bring provision of joy to people. These winds move according to the laws of nature that God has imposed upon this universe. To understand that this universe did not bring itself into existence, nor did it establish these laws of nature for itself, does not require any great amount of intellect, whereas in the rational conception of life in Islam, the events that occur in this universe take place according to the cosmic laws that God has set for this universe and decreed. The occurrence of all happenings is in accordance with these laws; the occurrence of all individual events is also in accordance with this same law. Therefore, the blowing of winds at a particular time and in a particular region also takes place according to this general rule and God's decree.

Thus, these winds also move according to God's practice (sunnah) and God's law, but according to a specific measure these winds are driven toward dead lands and deserts, and all this occurs by God's command. The rain that falls in any place falls according to a fixed measure. The growth and produce that result from it likewise occur specifically by God's decree, and this whole process takes place in accordance with the system of this universe.

In short, according to the Islamic conception of life, no event here occurs freely or by mere chance. Every movement, every change and every transformation, from creation up to the manifestation of events, takes place in accordance with a predetermined decree and sunnah at its appointed time. Likewise, from the Islamic standpoint, the notion that this universe is utterly helpless and that God created it and then left it to its own course is also false. He has established the laws of its motion; now it is bound by the laws of its motion, and behind this motion there is no longer any will.

The Islamic view is that creation takes place by God's will and volition. After that, the practice (sunnah) of God is put into effect among creatures. But every movement of this universe occurs in accordance with the decree of God, and in every movement God's sunnah is seen to be operating, and the measure of every movement is fixed. All this takes place in accordance with that divine will, which holds supremacy even over the laws of God.

This is a concept possessed of a living and luminous heart and mind, and according to it ... this universe is neither utterly helpless and dead. This universe does not sleep; it is awake, and it is not self-willed, but its custodian and overseer is continually attentive to it. Whatever happens here happens through a governing will. Every movement occurs according to the law, and before every movement the believer awakens; he observes God's decree and sunnah at work, carrying out their tasks. Thus the heart of the believer becomes full of praise of God, and he remembers God. He does not move heedlessly like lifeless machinery, blind and deaf.

This conception of life produces modesty (haya') in the heart of the believer and fervent perception in his mind. He sees the workings of the Hand of Power in all movements and events, and in every movement and every occurrence he glorifies and extols God night and day.

Now at this point the Holy Qur'an links this flowing worldly life with the life of the Hereafter. The creation here and the resurrection in the Hereafter appear as one and the same process. According to God's will, this is possible in the same way as this life flowed forth in this world.

﴿Thus We bring forth the dead, that perhaps you may take heed﴾ (57)

"Behold, in the same way We bring the dead out of their state of death, so that perhaps you may learn a lesson from this observation."

On this planet the forms and patterns of life are various, yet despite this variety of life, the miracle of the existence of life upon this universe is one and the same. This commentary points to this very thing: just as living bodies emerge from the dead here, so too in the Hereafter the dead will be brought back to life. The God who produced these various forms and patterns of life on this earth is able to resurrect human beings in the Hereafter. The power and capacity that can bring the living out of the dead here, why should that Being not be able to grant life again to the dead in the Hereafter?

﴿So that perhaps you may take heed﴾ (57)

"Perhaps you may learn a lesson from this observation."

This is an obvious and great truth, yet people, although they see it, do not wish to see it, and they seek to present idle fancies and vain delusions as reality.

The Holy Qur'an concludes this journey through the vastness of the universe and this reflection on its mysteries with an example. This parable concerns a righteous, pure heart and an unrighteous, impure heart. This parable too is drawn from the observation of this universe and from this journey of study, so that it appears in harmony with that journey, and human nature may firmly fix it in the mind.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 7, verse 58 (part 1 of 3):

Verse No. 58.

In the Qur'an and the Sunnah, a good heart is likened to fertile soil and good land, while wicked hearts are likened to barren earth and waste land. Therefore, good seeds produce a good harvest in good land, and it brings forth fruit and flowers; in the same way, righteous thoughts and good ideas arise in a good heart. It becomes the abode of pure consciousness and concepts. Human inclinations, tendencies, resolutions and determinations take root within it, and later they take practical form, exactly in the way that every kind of produce is obtained from the earth and fruits of various colours and various tastes appear.

﴿And the good land - its vegetation comes forth by the permission of its Lord, but that which is bad does not yield except meagerly.﴾ (7:58)

The good land is one that is soft and easy to work, while the bad one is painful, demanding of great labour, and narrow. Guidance, admonition and reminder rain down upon a good heart, just as rain falls from the clouds upon good land. If the heart is pure, like a good and fertile land, it opens up; it accepts guidance and admonition and, becoming even purer, succeeds. If the heart is corrupt, like a wicked and barren land, the doors of that heart close, it becomes hard, and it takes the path of evil and corruption. Instead of certainty, doubts and suspicions arise in that heart, just as thorny bushes grow in barren land.

﴿Thus do We vary the signs for a people who give thanks.﴾ (7:58)

The plant of gratitude can grow only in a pure heart, and this shows that admonition has had an effect upon the heart and that it is taking the path of acceptance. For people who possess such hearts, Allah repeatedly and in various ways presents His signs and proofs, because only such people benefit from these statements and set right their days and nights.

Gratitude to Allah is the special theme of this surah. In this surah, along with warning and reminder, this theme has been mentioned especially; we have already pointed to this earlier, and we will again mention, alongside warning and reminder, the other special feature of this surah.

Lesson No. 77 at a glance:

In this lesson we walk alongside the caravan of faith. These are its leaders, these are its banners, and these are its markers. This caravan moves across the long plains of the history of this earth and speaks with all of humanity. In this long journey, whenever humanity deviates into misguidance, this caravan of the people of truth blocks its way and places it upon the Straight Path. Humanity departs from the straight path when it comes under the domination of satanic desires. Satan is always watching for the opportunity to lead humanity astray, to cool his desire for revenge, and to put the bridle of carnal lusts in the mouth of humanity and throw it into Hell. When Satan begins this scheme, the caravan of faith of the prophets appears; the prophets and their followers stand before humanity as towers of light, and the breezes of the Garden open up for humanity. This dignified caravan performs the duty of warning them of the scorching blast of Hell, and it delivers them from the whisperings of the accursed Satan, because he is humanity's eternal enemy.

This is a most beautiful scene. Upon the long highway of life a fierce battle between truth and falsehood is ongoing. The reality is that human history is passing in a most intricate manner, because man makes history, and he himself is an intricate creature. He is composed of two elements: one is the earthly matter from which his clay was prepared, and the second element is the spirit that was breathed into that earthly body, and because of that breathing of the spirit man was called man. Thus the union of these two contrary elements was completed through the power of Allah's hand, by pairs. Therefore, the human being advances through history with great complexity. His self, his deeds and his ideas are also complex. Man, with this particular nature and temperament, holds a particular angle of relationship with this vast universe and its horizons, the details of which we have given in the story of Adam and Iblis. In one way it relates to divine reality and becomes the subject of Allah's decree, His will, Allah's power, His strength, and His mercy and compassion. He is also linked with the higher world and the angels. Then he also deals with Iblis and the great Satan. He is also connected with this observable universe and its laws of nature. He also adopts a conduct toward all things of this earth, and relations are established with other human beings of his own kind, and thus he becomes connected with the entire observable world along with this nature of his. He has a link with the harmonious forces of this universe and also a dealing with its opposing and contrary forces.

In short, upon this mutually turbulent and intricate ocean of history, human history travels its journey. At times his self appears strong, and at times lost on the way; at times he is pious and guided, and at times weak; at times he is attached to the unseen world, and at times he remains lost in the world of observation. At times he is busy in the world of material things, and at times he wanders in the world of the spirit and the world of the heart; but in the end he appears helpless before the decree of Allah. All these colours appear in his history. Therefore, an explanation of human history is possible only if these contrary constituent elements are kept in view.

Nowadays some people explain human history solely from an economic angle; some write its history solely from a political angle; some write its history from the standpoint of biology and bodily structure. Some write history solely on the basis of the spirit, others solely on the basis of the self, and others solely on the basis of reason. Those who study man in a superficial manner, although a comprehensive study of man is necessary. Likewise, its explanation of history must also be multi-faceted and all-encompassing. The Islamic explanation of human history is the all-encompassing explanation, in which the historian dives deep into the vast ocean of humanity and brings out every reality. The Islamic historian, after this comprehensive and deep study, casts his eye upon its events. (See the chapter "Haqiqat-e-Insan" in the discussion of the basic elements of the Islamic conception of life.)

Here we now stand before a great historical ocean. Previously we have seen scenes of the creation of humanity. In that scene there was an assembly of all worlds. All the creatures with which man was destined to have dealings were gathered. All horizons and all creatures and elements were visible or hidden; all were present in that assembly. Arriving at that gathering, we came to know what the capacity of this new creature is and what its fundamental characteristics are. This assembly of the higher world was convened in its honour, and in it he received the final honour, namely that the angels were commanded to prostrate to him. At that time Allah announced that this is the new creation. Then we also saw another glimpse of that scene in which his weakness came to the fore and he fell into the hands of the enemy. Then what happened? What was to happen: he was sent down to the earth and left free to determine the nature of his relations with all the elements of this earth.

We saw that Adam, as a believer, was descending upon this earth. He was seeking forgiveness from Allah for his shortcoming and lapse; a covenant was taken from him that he would fulfil the duties of khilafah upon the earth and would follow the commands that would come from Allah. He would not submit to Satan or to carnal desires, and in this regard he would take as provision the experience he had gained of being expelled from Paradise.

Now centuries have passed, and the turbulent waves of the boundless ocean of history have made him quite experienced. He has remained for a long time amid this entire universe, its environment, and the contrary forces at war with one another in it. He has also remained in conflict with his conscience and his inclinations. Therefore, in this lesson, some glimpses of the long history of Adam's descendants are shown: how he has passed his life amid the conflicting inclinations of this earth.

We see that man forgets. Many times he forgot his lesson. We see that many times weaknesses arose from him and occurred. Satan overcomes him, and this happens many times. Therefore it is necessary that he be guided again and again and delivered from calamities.

When he was sent down upon this earth, he had repented, he was guided, and he was established upon the belief in Tawheed; but in the very next scene we see that he has again gone astray, has become a polytheist, and is fabricating lies against Allah. But in this turbulence of historical waves, a signpost and the arrangement of the mission of messengers have been provided for him. He is repeatedly returned to his Lord, and it is Allah's great mercy and compassion that He did not leave him without support.

In this surah we are observing the long journey of the caravan of faith. For the guidance of this caravan, the prophets and messengers have raised the banners of guidance. Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him), Prophet Hud (peace be upon him), Prophet Salih (peace be upon him), Prophet Lut (peace be upon him), Prophet Shu'ayb (peace be upon him), Prophet Musa (peace be upon him), and Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) came for the guidance of humanity. We see that these honourable ones, in accordance with Allah's guidance, take people by the hand and hold them back from the path by which Satan wishes to lead them into the Hellfire. Satan's helpers too are seen busy in this work. These are the arrogant ones who in every age have considered themselves above the truth. Then we also see in these scenes glimpses of the continuous struggle between guidance and misguidance. On one side is truth and on the other falsehood; the leaders of truth are the prophets and messengers, and the leaders of falsehood are the devils among jinn and men. In the final stage of this journey we see how those who denied are struck down, their corpses are seen scattered everywhere, and we also see that the believers are successful and joyful. This is a long series of reminders and admonitions that appears in this lesson. In the Qur'an, the narration of stories is not necessarily according to historical sequence, but in this surah the historical sequence of the stories has also been kept in view, because in this surah it is intended to keep in view the long journey of humanity as well. It is also intended that it be seen how, in this long human journey, the prophets and messengers repeatedly provide guidance to man. Whenever he strays from the right path, these people take his hand. Whenever Satan has taken the leadership of humanity and ordered that it be led toward Hell, the prophets and messengers have made efforts to stop it.

The summary of the signposts shown in this lesson we present as follows:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 7, verse 58 (part 2 of 3):

That humanity began with a believing, rightly guided person who held to the belief in Tawhid (the Oneness of God). In later ages, people strayed and became holders of polytheistic beliefs. The causes of this straying were the tendencies and inclinations that Allah had placed within the self of man, or the elements and means that lay hidden in this world and became the cause of his misguidance. Whenever man fell into misguidance, a Messenger appeared on the stage of the world and began to present to him the very call which this misguided person had once believed in and held before his misguidance. After the arrival of a Messenger's call, people were always divided into two groups. One group took the path of destruction, and the other group was revived anew. Those who were revived were the people who returned to the path of guidance, and they realised that their Ilah (God) is one Ilah, and they completely submitted before that One God. They heard the call of that Messenger who was saying to them: "O my people, worship Allah alone; indeed there is no ruler for you other than Allah." So this is the fundamental point upon which the entire religion of Allah rests, and throughout the long history of humanity all the Messengers called only to this belief. Whichever Messenger came, he presented to his people this same declaration. In circumstances when his people had been ensnared by Satan in the net of misguidance, they had forgotten the original belief and had gone astray. They had associated countless partners with Allah. Within various jahiliyyahs (periods of ignorance), these partners took different forms. Upon the foundation of these idol-worships, a struggle between truth and falsehood has continued in human history, and upon the basis of this struggle Allah, the Exalted, has always seized those who denied and saved those who believed. The Qur'an has recorded these calls in one and the same wording, although the Prophets had been calling in different languages. The call which they gave in different ages and in different languages, the Qur'an has expressed in these words: "O my people, worship Allah alone; you have no ruler other than Allah." The purpose of this was to show the reality that throughout human history the Islamic call has remained one, indeed it has been presented in one and the same wording. This text and these words present this belief fully and in a comprehensive and exclusive manner. Just as the context of speech also shows this, that one Messenger after another comes onto the stage and repeats the same words. From this it appears what method the Qur'an adopted for the presentation of the Islamic worldview?

From this point, this reality comes forth on its own: there is a great difference between the method of the Qur'an and the thinkers of modern times who conduct comparative study of religions. The Qur'anic method is that the beliefs which the Messengers brought were not to undergo any development or change, nor have there been any initial or final stages of reflection upon these beliefs. Those who describe an evolutionary and gradual development of the fundamental beliefs of religions, and along with this read Islamic doctrines in an evolutionary form, and make statements which Allah has not made in the Qur'an. Just as the Qur'an clearly expresses that the Prophets always gave one and the same call. The Qur'an states this call in one and the same expression, namely: "O my people, worship Allah alone; indeed there is no ruler for you other than Allah."

[Qur'an 7:59] "O my people, worship Allah alone; you have no ilah other than Him."

And this Ilah to whom all the Messengers called is the Lord of the worlds, and He will take account from people on a great day. Not a single one of the Messengers passed who called people to his own tribe, or who summoned people to the lord of some nation or some lineage. Nor did any one of the Messengers call to two ilahs, or propagate many ilahs. None of the Messengers called to the worship and servitude of the sun, the moon, the stars, spirits or idols. Likewise, no system has been established by Allah in which there is no concept of the Hereafter, unlike what some people say who call themselves experts in religions, who study the various jahiliyyahs of the world and then claim that the results they reached are the religions known in this world, and that no other religion existed in those ages.

The reality is that upon this earth Messengers came one after another, and they presented solely and exclusively the belief in Tawhid and pure Tawhid. They gave the view that only Allah is the Lord of the worlds, and that He will certainly take account of all on the Day of Resurrection. But after the end of each prophethood, jahiliyyah again overspread the world, and the causes of its spread were partly within human beings and partly those factors and motives which existed in a highly complex form within the environment provided to man. These deviations appeared in the form of various concepts and beliefs, and today's experts on religion, in fact, leaving aside the original religion, study these deviated religions, and they think that upon the lines they have derived, religion and creed in the world have taken their present form through a gradual evolutionary journey.

Nevertheless, the command of Allah is more worthy of being followed, especially for those who write on the subject of religion, who speak in favour of Islam and defend it. As for those who do not believe in the Qur'an at all, we do not address them; Allah nonetheless declares the truth, and He is the best of judges.

Every Messenger, whenever he came, first called his own people. They began the work of the Islamic call among their people at the time when the people had deviated from the straight path and from the belief upon which the previous Messenger had left them. Thus, first, humanity was the people of Tawhid, and they acknowledged the Lord of the worlds. Their belief was the same as that of Adam (peace be upon him) and his wife. After this, with the passage of time and because of the causes which we have mentioned, they deviated from that belief. Then Nuh (peace be upon him) came. He called people again to be firm upon the Tawhid of the Lord of the worlds. At the conclusion of his call a great flood came; the believers were saved, and the people of denial were drowned in the flood. The people of Tawhid took possession of this earth and made it populated. The lesson of this reconstruction of the world was given to them by Nuh (peace be upon him) through his offspring. When more time passed, these people again went astray, and after that Hud (peace be upon him) came, and at the conclusion of his call they were seized by a severe windstorm. In this way the story continued in this manner and the journey of history went on.

Each of these Messengers was sent to his own people. He addressed them thus: "O my brethren of the people, worship Allah alone; for you there is no other ilah besides Him." And every Messenger said to his people: "Indeed, I am a sincere and trustworthy counsellor for you."

From these words it appears how intense was the Messengers' sense of their great responsibility; they also knew what a dreadful end awaited their people in the situation in which they were entangled, both in this world and in the Hereafter. There was a strong desire in the hearts of the Messengers that their people be guided, because they were from among them and the people were from them. But at that time the chiefs of the people blocked their way and rose up against the command of truth. They refused to bow before the Lord of the worlds. These chiefs refused to accept that the system of life should be Allah's alone and that within that system there should be worship of Allah alone. This is the foundation upon which the whole mission of all Messengers rested, and upon it all religions established by Allah were built. But the Messengers raised the word of truth with great clarity and frankness, in the face of all tyrannical powers and all chiefs, and each time their people were divided into two ideological factions. Ties of nationality and kinship among people were cut, and in their place brotherhood was established upon the basis of one ideology. Those who had been members of one nation became two communities, and it appeared that there was neither any kinship between them nor any relation of a unified nationality. After this struggle, victory comes, and through it a decision is made between the two communities. Allah separates the community of guidance from the community of misguidance. Now the denying arrogant ones and chiefs are seized, and those who obey and submit are saved. It has never happened that a people were not divided ideologically and yet victory from Allah came. It has always happened that a people is divided ideologically, and then the people of truth prevail; the people of Allah become purely devoted to the worship and servitude of Allah. They line up against the tyrannical powers and separate themselves from their own people. This is the observation which is clearly seen during the study of the history of the prophetic call.

In all these Messengerships one matter has been focused upon: that all people should adopt the worship and servitude of the One Lord, because only the Lord of the worlds deserves worship. It is our duty to take the right of worship and sovereign authority from all other creation and give it to the Lord of the worlds. No aspect of human life can be reformed without its belief. After the statement of this common principle of all Messengerships, the Qur'an has not given the details of the call of these Messengers, because the details of the religions of all Messengers were based upon this central principle. No matter was outside this belief. Since this principle was extremely important and foundational, the Qur'an has laid such stress upon it that it has stated it separately. Just as we said in our commentary on Surah al-An'am, the central theme of all the Meccan Qur'an is precisely this, but in the Medinan portion too, wherever the occasion arose, the subject was discussed in accordance with that context.

The reality is that the religion of Islam is a solid reality, a system, and to present this reality there is a method and procedure. And the method of Islam is not of lesser importance than the religion of Islam. Therefore we should ascertain what that great reality is with which this religion came into the world. Likewise, to understand the religion of Islam and to establish it, we should adopt the same method through which this reality has been presented. And the summary of this method is that the belief in Tawhid should be presented repeatedly, emphatically and in a distinctive manner. This is why in this Surah this method has been stated again and again, in the most emphatic words and in a very clear and simple style, and this method is evident throughout all the narratives of this Surah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 7, verse 58 (part 3 of 3):

The stories narrated in this surah show what the temperament of faith is, what the temperament of disbelief is, and what effects each has upon the human soul. Here it is repeatedly explained what kinds of hearts are receptive to faith, and what kinds of hearts are inclined to disbelief and denial. Those who accepted the call of the Messengers had no arrogance or pride in their hearts, and they felt no obstacle in accepting the call of the Messengers and bowing before it in submission. For them it did not seem strange that Allah should send a man from among them as a Messenger, to convey His message to them and to warn them of the evil end. As for those who denied any Messenger, they have always been people who took the path of sin because they regarded themselves as great, and were people of status. Instead of establishing the sovereignty of Allah, they imposed their own authority upon the people, and in no way were they ready to give up this usurped authority. Nor were they ready to obey and submit to an ordinary man from among themselves. These are the people for whom the Qur'an uses the word "mala'" (the chiefs). These rulers were great people, people of power and authority, and from here the real secret of this religion becomes known. This secret is the matter of the supreme sovereignty of Allah and the establishment of Allah's rule. These great people understood well the results of the words of the Messenger: "O my people! Worship Allah alone; you have no ruler besides Him," and "I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds." They understood that if sovereignty and rule belong to Allah, and the Messenger of Allah is this man, then it is obvious that all their greatness would end, and all their powers would automatically be transferred to the one who represents the Lord of the worlds. This is why they became barriers in the way of this call, and as a consequence they became among those destined to perish. These people became so devoted to this supreme authority of their own that their coming generations also followed their path, and fell into the path of Hell in the same way, the end of which was nothing but destruction. In short, the pictures of the slaying grounds of those who denied, which are drawn in these stories, are in accordance with the Sunnah of Allah, the Lord of the worlds, which does not change. These people completely forgot the signs of Allah and turned away from the path of Allah. A warning came from Allah through the Messengers, and they considered acknowledging the worship of Allah to be an insult to themselves. They took pride in their prosperity and demanded, "Bring the punishment quickly." On the contrary, they threatened and harmed the Messenger and the believers, and the believers remained steadfast against this and held firmly to their convictions. Then the punishment of Allah would come. This is the history of humanity.

The very last point is that the nature of the arrogant force of falsehood is such that it is not prepared to tolerate even the existence of truth. Even if truth, in the face of falsehood, withdraws into seclusion and leaves the decision between truth and falsehood to Allah, falsehood will still not tolerate it. Rather, falsehood will pursue it and strive to drive it to the furthest limits, and will try to defeat it. Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) said to his people: "If there is a group among you that has believed in the message with which I have been sent, and a group that has not believed, then be patient until Allah judges between us; He is the best of judges." But they did not accept this offer of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him), and they could not bear that truth should exist before their eyes and flourish. No falsehood can bear that a group should remain present in the field which worships Allah alone and rejects the sovereignty of all tyrannical powers. The arrogant ones among the people of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) said: "O Shu'ayb! We will surely expel you and those who have believed with you from our town, or you must return to our system and our community." But Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) clearly rejected their proposal: "He said, 'Even though we may be unwilling? If we return to your system and your community after Allah has saved us from it, we would indeed be fabricating a lie against Allah.'"

This dialogue shows that it is obligatory upon the people of the call to engage in this struggle against tyrannical powers, and they must understand its nature well. No strategy and no wisdom can save the bearers of the Islamic call from this confrontation, because the tyrannical powers will rest only when they cause the Islamic call to deviate from its principles, and these forces will not be satisfied until the callers to truth return to their misguided community. Yet Allah has removed from their hearts these deviant communal ideas and placed in them only the ideas of the supreme sovereignty of Allah. Therefore the confrontation between these two forces is inevitable and cannot be avoided. When the confrontation is inevitable, then bearing its hardships is also inevitable. And this will continue until victory is attained, and until they burn their boats and chant the song of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him): "We have put our trust in Allah. O Allah, judge between us and our people in truth, for You are the best of judges." (ʿAlā Allāhi tawakkalnā) (7:89). Now the Sunnah of Allah proceeds, and it has continued throughout the whole of human history. This commentary is sufficient on these stories. Now the verses of the Qur'an, with details.

**Lesson 77: Explanation of the Verses**

**Verses 59 to 93**

Before the account of this stage of humanity's journey, there was mention of another cosmic community of believers, one that appears to move through this universe. Earlier, at the end of the previous section, believers who never deviate in the least from the command of God were described in these words:

﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days; then He established Himself above the Throne. He covers the night with the day, which it pursues urgently; and [He created] the sun, the moon, and the stars, subjected by His command. Unquestionably, creation and command belong to Him. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ (7:54)

The Qur'an often brings together two truths: that the whole universe is obedient to God, and that the command of God must prevail over all human beings. In other words, just as the universe in which human beings live is obedient, human beings too should be obedient to God. Your Islam should be like the Islam of this entire universe, which is bound by its laws. The obedience of the whole universe affects the heart of the believer in this way. It shakes him strongly and moves him to submit to God. It is not fitting for him that the universe spread around him should obey God while he rebels against the One God within it.

In short, the call of the messengers is not a novel call. It invites people to the truth that runs through the whole universe, that is embedded in the conscience of all creation, and that also exists within human nature itself. Whenever human nature is overcome by desires (shahawat) and appetites, this nature calls out to a person from within his conscience. In this way, Satan cannot take a person astray and take the reins of his life into his own hands. This is the truth that is expressed in various ways throughout all the stories of this section.

**Verses 59 to 64**

Here the story is taken up with great brevity, whereas in other places, where details were needed, they are also given, such as in Surah Hud and Surah Nuh. This is because here the purpose is only to point to those signposts of the path that we have just mentioned: what the nature of the Islamic worldview is, what the method of spreading it and conveying the Islamic call is, and what the reaction of the people is after the call begins, and what the feelings of its caller are. Here we will point only to those signposts for which this story has been brought here.

﴿Indeed, We sent Noah to his people.﴾ (7:59)

This is the sunnah (established way) of God: that He sends to every people a messenger from among that people. He speaks to them in their own language. God has granted this consideration to every nation in order to win their hearts, and so that its message may be easy to understand and so that they may come to know one another. Yet these facilities are beneficial only to those whose nature has not been corrupted. As for those whose nature is corrupted, this arrangement also seems strange to them. They do not accept the call, and they consider themselves too exalted to believe and obey. Therefore they demand that angels come and deliver the message to them. This is mere pretext. Even if angels had come, these people would still not have accepted. Whatever method had been adopted, they would not have believed.

When Noah (peace be upon him) was sent as a messenger, he began his call with the same words with which all the messengers who came after him began.

﴿He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him."﴾ (7:59)

These words do not change until the end. This is the fundamental principle without which Islam cannot be realized. It is the cornerstone of human life, and without it the edifice of humanity cannot stand. This very principle guarantees that people's viewpoints will be one, their aims will be one, and the bonds among them will be of one kind. This is the principle through which a human being can be freed from enslavement to his own desires and also freed from enslavement to other human beings like himself. Through it a person can control his boundless human desires and regulate reward and punishment.

The truth is that the religion of Islam is a complete system of life. Its foundational principle is that God's sovereignty and rule should be established over the entire life of human beings. This is the meaning of our worshipping Allah alone, and this is the meaning of the phrase that there is no ilah (sovereign) other than Allah. Just as God's sovereignty is present in the creation of the universe, in its nurturing, its management and its destiny, and just as this sovereignty is present in the creation of a human being, in his nurturing and his destiny in the elements of his constitution, so too this sovereignty should be established in the practical life of a human being. His practical life should be organized according to the Shari'ah of God. For example, in acts of worship and in all other matters of life, God should be served as a complete package. If this does not happen, then a person commits shirk (association of partners with God), and in practice he acknowledges that there are other sovereigns besides Allah.

Noah (peace be upon him) spoke these brief words to his people and warned them of their evil end. He advised them as a compassionate brother advises a brother, and as a compassionate leader advises his people and family, that if they denied the truth, the consequence would be very dreadful.

﴿Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous day.﴾ (7:59)

From this we learn that the concept of the Hereafter exists in its complete form even in the most ancient religion, the religion of Noah. He says that he trembles at the evil end awaiting them on the Day of Reckoning. This shows what the Qur'an's conception of Islamic and religious beliefs is, and how it differs from the conception of those so-called experts on religions who also arrange the history of religions in an evolutionary manner. These people are unaware of the Qur'anic methodology.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 7, verse 60:

Verse: "The chiefs of the people who disbelieved among his people said, 'Indeed, we see you in clear error.'"

"The chiefs of his people replied: 'We see that you are plainly misguided.'"

This very statement was made by the polytheists of Arabia about the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): that he had become irreligious, and that he had turned away from the religion of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). When a person crosses the limits of error, he considers those who call him to the path of guidance to be misguided. And when a person's nature becomes distorted, he too reaches that point of wilfulness. Thus values change, and the standard for distinguishing truth from falsehood changes. Man becomes subject to his carnal desires. Unless a person adopts the values and criteria of Allah, because these values and criteria are unchanging and never deviate.

Today, those who take guidance from Allah are called misguided by the jahiliyyah (ignorance) of the modern age, and whoever takes guidance merely from modern jahiliyyah, falls into the filthy sewer of Western civilisation, and immerses himself in that repugnant environment, they call him guided and progressive.

What does modern jahiliyyah say about the woman today who does not expose her flesh and does not bare her body, and who does not accept this degraded condition? This world calls that pure, clean and righteous woman of the modern age reactionary; she is taunted with backwardness and rusticity, and modern jahiliyyah has engaged its entire media and communication apparatus for the purpose of destroying this purity, cleanliness and dignity of our women and casting her into that filthy pool of sexuality, which is most repugnant in appearance.

What does this jahiliyyah say about those people whose priorities are above games and play, who are above the obsession with films, cinemas and television, and who wish to keep themselves away from the indecencies and debaucheries of dance, song and wine? It says that these people are rigid and dull-witted, that they are lost, uncivilised and uneducated. This jahiliyyah is constantly occupied with the task of casting all people into that filth, so that all of them live their lives in debauchery and immorality. In short, jahiliyyah is jahiliyyah in every age; it changes forms and appearances, but its essence remains the same.

Hadrat Nuh (peace be upon him) assures them that he is not misguided. He explains to them what his call is and what the source of this call is: that he did not initiate this call through his own thought and reasoning, nor is it his personal desire. He is the Messenger of the Lord of the worlds and the bearer of prophethood. He admonishes with utmost trustworthiness and integrity in accordance with the instructions given to him by Allah, and the teachings he gives are also from the Lord of the worlds. These teachings descend upon his heart, and he has a continuous connection with the Lord of the worlds, whereas you people do not maintain a connection with Allah.

"O my people! There is no error in me, but I am a Messenger from the Lord of the worlds. I convey to you the messages of my Lord, and I give you sincere counsel, and I know from Allah what you do not know." (7:61–62)

There is a missing link in the context of the story here. By his call to the Messenger, they had in effect expressed their astonishment: how did Allah send one man from among human beings as a Messenger? And how is it that the message of Allah reaches one person while other people are not even aware that the message has come? This link in the sequence of events is expressed in the verses that follow.

Next verse: "Are you astonished that a reminder from your Lord has come to you through a man from among yourselves, so that he may warn you, that you may guard yourselves against evil, and that mercy may be shown to you?" (7:63)

Being chosen by Allah from among one individual to be His messenger is indeed astonishing, but the station of the human being is entirely unique. He deals with the worlds and is connected to them. On the other hand, he is also connected to Allah, because Allah Himself breathed soul and life into his body. Therefore, if Allah makes one of these human beings a Messenger, and Allah, who knows very well whom to choose for this office, selects him, then this person receives guidance directly from Allah, because Allah has placed within his body this capacity and ability. This is the secret because of which man is man, and for this reason he is honored and esteemed in the sight of the Creator of the universe.

This is why Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) says: "So that he may warn you, that you may guard yourselves against evil, and that mercy may be shown to you." The mission of the Messenger is to warn people, so that their hearts may tremble, they may be prepared for piety, and ultimately they may partake of the mercy of Allah. Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) had no other purpose beyond this. This is the lofty and exalted goal for which Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) was working.

However, it is a characteristic of human nature that when it crosses a certain limit, it no longer employs reflection and thought, and warning and admonition no longer benefit it.

"But they denied him. So We saved him and those with him in the ship, and We drowned those who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a blind people." (7:64)

We have seen that they did not accept sincere counsel and the warning of a real danger, and they closed their eyes. For this reason they denied, and for this reason they reached the end that the Qur'an mentions.

Now the cart of history moves a little further ahead, and the Qur'an moves along with it. We now stand before the people of 'Ad, the people of Prophet Hud (peace be upon him).

"O my people! There is no error in me, but I am a Messenger from the Lord of the worlds. I convey to you the messages of my Lord, and I give you sincere counsel, and I know from Allah what you do not know." (7:61–62)

There is a missing link in the context of the story here. By his call to the Messenger, they had in effect expressed their astonishment: how did Allah send one man from among human beings as a Messenger? And how is it that the message of Allah reaches one person while other people are not even aware that the message has come? This link in the sequence of events is expressed in the verses that follow.

The commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah al-A'raf (7), verses 65–74:

This is the same message and the same mission, the same matter and the same outcome. It is the same Divine practice (sunnat Ilahiyyah) that continues in force, and the same law of God upon which this universe stands. There is one law and one code.

The people of 'Ad were from the descendants of Nuh (peace be upon him), or from the descendants of those who sailed with him in the ark. Some narrations state that their number was thirteen. Obviously, all of these people followed the religion of Nuh (peace be upon him), and the religion of Nuh was the religion of Islam. They worshipped Allah alone and did not take anyone else as a deity besides Him. Their belief was that Allah is the Lord of the worlds, and Nuh (peace be upon him) had taught them this.

﴿And I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds﴾ (7:67)

"I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds."

But when a long time passed and these people spread across different regions of the earth, Satan thoroughly misled them, and made them subservient to their own desires and appetites. The greatest desire of a human being is the desire for property and possessions. These people amassed wealth and goods in disregard of the law of the Shariah, and therefore the people of 'Ad, the people of Hud (peace be upon him), considered this call to worship Allah alone and obey Him to be very unpleasant.

﴿And to 'Ad, their brother Hud. He said: "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Will you not then be wary of Allah?"﴾ (7:65)

"And to 'Ad We sent their brother Hud. He said, 'O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. Will you not then guard against wrongdoing?'"

This is the same message that Nuh had earlier delivered, and for which the people of Nuh denied him, and the punishment that came upon them as a result is well known. After Nuh (peace be upon him), Allah made the people of 'Ad His successors (khulafa'). The Qur'an does not specify the dwelling place of the people of 'Ad here, but other surahs make it explicit that they lived in al-Ahqaf. These are great sand dunes between Yamamah and Hadramawt. In short, these people went down the same path on which the people of Nuh had previously walked. They neither heeded the admonition nor took a lesson from the events of Nuh's people. This is why Hud (peace be upon him), in his address, further says: "Do you not fear Allah?" This is a rebuke for their conduct, and they are being warned of that terrible and evil end.

In short, the chiefs of this people found it extremely displeasing that one of their common men should rise and warn them, and that he did not properly consider their status and position. Therefore they attributed to their prophet the claims that he was foolish and a liar, and in making such accusations they felt no shame at all.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verses 66–68:

Verse: "The chiefs of those among his people who disbelieved said, 'Indeed, we see you in foolishness, and indeed, we think you are among the liars.'" (7:66)

These were the answers of the elders, which were merely a mockery, empty of reflection and proof. The reply of the Prophet (Hud) was:

Verse: "He said, 'O my people, there is no foolishness in me, but I am a Messenger from the Lord of the worlds. I convey to you the messages of my Lord, and I am a sincere and trustworthy advisor to you.'" (7:67–68)

He denied, with great truthfulness and seriousness, that he was foolish or lacking in understanding. Likewise, he denied that he was astray, because, as Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him) had done, he had already told them the source of his message and its purposes. He had also told them that he was a trustworthy advisor, and he said this to them in a tone of deep sincerity, with truth and clarity.

It is necessarily established here that the people of Prophet Hud (peace be upon him) were astonished at his ideas, just as the people of Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him) had been astonished earlier, that Allah could choose someone from among ordinary humans as a Prophet and make him a Messenger. Thus Prophet Hud (peace be upon him) repeats the very same point that Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him) had made. It appears that the spirit of these two personalities is one; only their bodies differ.

Verse: "Are you astonished that a reminder from your Lord has come to you through a man from among you, so that he may warn you?" (7:69)

After this, he draws their attention to the circumstances that were clear from their actual situation: that Allah, after the people of Nuh, granted them the position of vicegerency on the earth, gave them physical strength, and they possessed bodily vigour like the dwellers of the mountains; and likewise, they were given authority on the earth in political and social terms.

The commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 69:

Verse: "And remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah and increased you in physical stature. So remember the bounties of Allah that you may prosper." (7:69)

"Remember, your Lord made you successors after the people of Noah (peace be upon him) and gave you robust bodies. So remember the wonders of Allah's power; hopefully you will attain success."

The authority over the earth and the physical strength that were bestowed upon them made it their duty to give thanks for these blessings, to fear Allah's seizure, and to dread the evil end that befell the nations before them. For they had made no covenant with Allah that the operation of His sunnah (way/law) would not apply to them, since Allah's unalterable sunnah admits of no change, and it continues to operate in this universe according to the system Allah has established. Mentioning the blessings is intended to point to the need to give thanks to Allah for them, and giving thanks means maintaining the means of these blessings, for success in this world and the Hereafter lies in that.

But when corruption and deviation enter human nature, people no longer employ reflection and contemplation. Thus, on hearing this call, they became inclined to denial and rebellion, and adopted evil conduct. They cut short the discussion and ended dialogue, and soon began asking for the descent of punishment. Admonition became burdensome to them, and they began to mock the warning.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 70:

Verse: "They said, 'Have you come to us so that we would worship Allah alone and abandon what our fathers used to worship? So bring us what you threaten us with, if you are of the truthful.'" (7:70)

This is a picture of the humiliating slavery of traditions and of their present circumstances. The hearts and minds of human beings are captives of circumstances. This is a kind of slavery and imprisonment in which a person loses his highest faculties. He is deprived of free thought and reflection. Thus, these people too were deprived of the right to free opinion and free belief. It appears that these people are slaves to their customs and rituals. The imitation of forefathers (taqlid-i-aba') rules over them, and they are captives of their personal desires and carnal appetites, and these people have closed upon themselves all the doors of knowledge, recognition and light.

Their condition has become such that they are ready to commit suicide in order to escape from the truth, and they want to see the punishment quickly. They do not even want to consider how much foolishness and ignorance they are afflicted with. Thus they say to their adviser and trustworthy prophet, "If you are truthful, bring that punishment with which you frighten us?" And this is the reason why Allah Almighty very soon has them receive a plain and decisive answer from His Messenger.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 71:

Verse: "He said: 'Abomination and wrath from your Lord have already befallen you. Do you dispute with me over names which you and your fathers have named, for which Allah has sent down no authority? So wait, and I too am with you among those who wait.'"

Hazrat Hud (alayhis salam) warned them of the evil end about which their Lord had informed him, and whose decree had already been made concerning them, and which was now not to be averted. This was the wrath of Allah, and when the wrath of Allah descends upon someone, it is never averted. He then said that you seek punishment hastily, yet you do not reflect upon your beliefs and how feeble those notions are; yet you seek punishment hastily. "Do you dispute with me over names which you and your forefathers have set up, for which Allah has sent down no authority?"

The partners you have set up besides Allah are mere names upon names, and have no reality. These names you and your forefathers have fabricated of your own accord, merely from yourselves; Allah has sent down no authority for them. Allah has neither permitted them, nor do you have any proof or argument.

The Qur'an repeatedly says in this context, "for which Allah has sent down no authority." This expression reveals a great truth: every matter, every law, every custom, in short every thought and conception that has no proof from Allah behind it, is baseless, light, ineffective, perishable and void, and human nature regards such a thing as light. But when a matter comes from Allah, it is weighty, enforceable and profound, because behind it stands Allah's proof.

In the world we hear very glittering words, read countless religions and ideologies, see countless false and baseless conceptions, and observe countless rites and customs, which are further strengthened for the people of the world; but when the word of Allah comes, all these things melt like ice, because the word of Allah carries such power and heat that these things cannot endure its heat.

This is why Hazrat Hud responds with great assurance, confidence, tranquility and a challenging tone: "So wait, and I too am with you among those who wait."

Everyone who calls to Allah possesses this tranquility and strength; they are certain that falsehood is weak, light and without weight, even if it appears swollen and seems very great. The caller is certain that behind him stands the power of truth and that he has divine support. Therefore, without waiting further, it is said:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 72:

Verse: "فَأَنجَیْنَاہُ وَالَّذِیْنَ مَعَہُ بِرَحْمَۃٍ مِّنَّا وَقَطَعْنَا دَابِرَ الَّذِیْنَ کَذَّبُواْ بِآیَاتِنَا وَمَا کَانُواْ مُؤْمِنِیْنَ" (72)

"Finally, by Our mercy, We saved Hud and those who were with him, and We cut off the roots of those who had denied Our signs and were not believers."

This is the reality from which no one can escape. It is said that We cut off their roots. (Dabir) In Arabic, this refers to the last person who is at the tail end of a caravan. In short, this second page of the history of those who denied is now also turned over, and once again history sees what the end is for those who did not benefit from admonition. The details of the destruction of these people, which the Quran gives in other places, are not given here. Therefore, in this brief overview, we too follow the Quranic style and stop here, and we will give further details where the other details of this story are given.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verses 73–79:

Verses 73 to 79.

Here the page of the book of human history turns once more. On this page a great wave rises from the depths of the boundless sea of history. The ark of humanity has once again turned away and gone backwards, and now it is in the grip of complete jahiliyyah (the state of ignorance of divine guidance). A new scene of the conflict between truth and falsehood appears before us, and a new place of slaughter for those who deny and reject is about to come into view.

﴿And to Thamud We sent their brother Salih. He said: "O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him."﴾ (7:73)

This is the same word with which this universe began and with which it will end. The direction of belief, conduct and outlook is the same as that which is adopted in da'wah (the call to Islam). It is the same manner of speech and discourse that has continued since the first day. This is the method of preaching in the case of all the prophets.

Yes, here one element has been added. Behind the da'wah of Hazrat Salih (peace be upon him), alongside argument, a miracle now also appears. And this miracle, which came in response to the demand of the people of Thamud themselves, is a manifestation of Allah's perfect power, and it is for the confirmation and support of the da'wah of Hazrat Salih (peace be upon him).

﴿There has certainly come to you a clear proof from your Lord. This is the she-camel of Allah, a sign for you.﴾ (7:73)

Here, the main purpose from the context is that the Islamic call is one in its principles. It is shown what the end of those who believe in it is, and what the outcome is for those who reject and deny this call. Therefore, the important highlights of the stories are given. The detail is not given here because they demanded a miracle in this way and in response Allah showed them a miracle. Rather, it is only said that they were given the call and after that a miracle was shown to them. Regarding the she-camel, too, it is only said that it was a sign from Allah. It was the she-camel of Allah and a miracle. From this manner of speech it is understood that it was an extraordinary she-camel, or that its origin came about in a miraculous manner, due to which it was called a sign of Allah. For this reason it was called by the words "the she-camel of Allah," and it was a sign that the prophethood of Hazrat Salih (peace be upon him) is true. Regarding this she-camel, we are content with only as much information as is certain, and such hints are better than those narrations which are not certain. Accordingly, it is said:

﴿So leave her to graze in the earth of Allah, and do not touch her with harm, lest a painful punishment seize you.﴾ (7:73)

This is the she-camel of Allah; let her graze freely on the earth of Allah, and if you touch her with an evil intention, the punishment of Allah will descend upon you.

After presenting this miracle and warning about this sign, Hazrat Salih (peace be upon him) begins to admonish and remind the people, and advises them to reflect upon his call and also to cast a glance at human history, and to thank Allah that, by destroying other nations, He gave you opportunities.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 74:

Verse: "And remember when He made you successors after 'Ad and settled you in the land, so that you take for yourselves palaces in its plains and carve out the mountains as dwellings. So remember the favours of Allah, and do not act wickedly in the land, spreading corruption."

"Remember the time when Allah made you successors after the people of 'Ad and gave you such a standing in the land that today you build magnificent palaces in its level plains and carve its mountains into houses. So do not be heedless of the wonders of His power, and do not cause corruption in the land."

Here it is not stated where the people of Thamud lived. But in another surah it is mentioned that they dwelt in al-Hijr, which is the region between Hijaz and Syria. Hadrat Salih (peace be upon him) reminds them to consider how greatly Allah has blessed them, from which it becomes clear that they were highly developed on the earth and were a power politically. The indication of their geography shows that there were mountains there as well as level areas. They built magnificent palaces in the level areas, and they also carved the mountains to make dwellings. Thus, in this brief verse, a reference is made to their culture and their civilisation. Hadrat Salih (peace be upon him) also tells them that after 'Ad, the people of Thamud rose to prominence, although these people did not live in the land of 'Ad. Indeed, it is clear that they possessed a civilisation that emerged after the civilisation of 'Ad, and their kingdom extended over distant areas beyond al-Hijr. Thus they held the office of khalifah fi'l-ard (vicegerent on the earth), and therefore Hadrat Salih admonishes them that your task is not to spread corruption in the land, and you should not be proud of your grandeur and splendour. You should keep in view the end of the earlier nations.

There is another gap in the narrative context that is not mentioned here: some people accepted Hadrat Salih's (peace be upon him) call and became obedient, while others rejected it out of arrogance. The influential people of any region always accept the Islamic call last, because the purpose of this call is that people should give up their greatness and their godhoods and accept only the one God as great and King, who is the Lord of the worlds. Before this, these great people always try to oppress the weak who have thrown off the yoke of tyranny from their necks and have become free from all slaveries except that of Allah. Accordingly, the great and influential people of Hadrat Salih's (peace be upon him) nation oppress those weak people who believed, and they create various kinds of sedition and corruption against them.

The verse: "The eminent ones of his people who were arrogant said to those who were considered weak, to those among them who had believed: 'Do you know for certain that Salih is one sent from his Lord?' They said: 'We indeed believe in that with which he has been sent.' (75)"

The sardars of his people who were proud, said to the weak folk, those who had come to faith among them: "Do you really know that Salih (peace be upon him) is a messenger from his Lord?" They replied: "Indeed, we believe in what he has been sent with."

This question from the influential people was asked as a threat and to intimidate. These people considered it very shameful that these poor folk had also become supporters of Salih and were confirming Hadrat Salih (peace be upon him)?

But the reality is that when weak people accept faith, they no longer remain weak. Faith fills their hearts with strength and courage. Peace and certainty are born within their hearts; they have confidence in their beliefs, and therefore the threats, intimidation and warnings of worldly people no longer have any effect on them. Neither does mockery and ridicule affect them. Now they do not take the arrogant into account and they declare their faith. And in reply, these arrogant people also make it clear, in a threatening tone, that very well, we are plainly rejecting this call.

The verse: "They said: 'Indeed we believe in what he has been sent with.' (75) Those who were arrogant said: 'Indeed we are disbelievers in that which you have believed in.' (76)"

They replied: "Indeed, we accept the message with which he has been sent." Those claimants of greatness said: "We are deniers of that which you have accepted."

Although Salih (peace be upon him) had come with clear proofs, after those proofs and miracles there was no room for doubt. The reality was that these leaders of the people did not deny because there was any lack of proofs and miracles before them, but rather they denied because they did not want to accept a system of governance in which only the obedience of the Lord of the worlds would be practiced. The issue was one of sovereignty and supreme authority. The truth is that a lofty and deep desire for sovereignty and power is found in the human heart, and this is the very place from which Satan attacks man.

Thus, after their verbal denial, they proceeded to disbelieving action and laid hands on the she-camel of Allah, which in reality had been brought as a miracle in support of the prophet of the time, and about which the prophet of the time had earlier warned them that they should refrain from laying hands on it, otherwise they would be afflicted with a painful punishment.

The verse: "The eminent ones of his people who were arrogant said to those who were considered weak, to those among them who had believed: 'Do you know for certain that Salih is one sent from his Lord?' They said: 'We indeed believe in that with which he has been sent.' (75)"

The sardars of his people who were proud, said to the weak folk, those who had come to faith among them: "Do you really know that Salih (peace be upon him) is a messenger from his Lord?" They replied: "Indeed, we believe in what he has been sent with."

This question from the influential people was asked as a threat and to intimidate. These people considered it very shameful that these poor folk had also become supporters of Salih and were confirming Hadrat Salih (peace be upon him)?

But the reality is that when weak people accept faith, they no longer remain weak. Faith fills their hearts with strength and courage. Peace and certainty are born within their hearts; they have confidence in their beliefs, and therefore the threats, intimidation and warnings of worldly people no longer have any effect on them. Neither does mockery and ridicule affect them. Now they do not take the arrogant into account and they declare their faith. And in reply, these arrogant people also make it clear, in a threatening tone, that very well, we are plainly rejecting this call.

The verse: "They said: 'Indeed we believe in what he has been sent with.' (75) Those who were arrogant said: 'Indeed we are disbelievers in that which you have believed in.' (76)"

They replied: "Indeed, we accept the message with which he has been sent." Those claimants of greatness said: "We are deniers of that which you have accepted."

Although Salih (peace be upon him) had come with clear proofs, after those proofs and miracles there was no room for doubt. The reality was that these leaders of the people did not deny because there was any lack of proofs and miracles before them, but rather they denied because they did not want to accept a system of governance in which only the obedience of the Lord of the worlds would be practiced. The issue was one of sovereignty and supreme authority. The truth is that a lofty and deep desire for sovereignty and power is found in the human heart, and this is the very place from which Satan attacks man.

Thus, after their verbal denial, they proceeded to disbelieving action and laid hands on the she-camel of Allah, which in reality had been brought as a miracle in support of the prophet of the time, and about which the prophet of the time had earlier warned them that they should refrain from laying hands on it, otherwise they would be afflicted with a painful punishment.

The Quranic verse (7:77) is rendered as follows:

﴿So they hamstrung the she-camel and defied the command of their Lord, and said, "O Salih, bring upon us what you threaten us with, if you are indeed one of the messengers."﴾

Their wilful disobedience is evident here after their sin and defiance. The word "ʿutuww" (overweening arrogance, insolent rebellion) is used for their disobedience and arrogance, so that the picture of their psychological state is clearly presented, the state which leads them to demand the descent of the punishment and to regard the Prophet as insignificant. Without any delay, the announcement of their destruction is now made.

"So a terrifying calamity seized them, and they remained lying prostrate, face-down, in their homes."

So the terrifying calamity came upon them, and as a result they were thrown face-down, so that they would receive a punishment fitting their arrogance and rebellion. For the thunderclap and the shaking had frightened them, and they fell face-down, motionless. Their condition was the fitting punishment for their rebellion and arrogance. The psychological portrayal of the words is worth observing.

Now, leaving them lying face-down in this way, the discourse turned toward Prophet Salih (peace be upon him), whom they had denied and to whom they had issued a challenge. Here is his commentary.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 79:

Verse: "So he turned away from them and said, 'O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the message of my Lord and advised you sincerely, but you do not like sincere advisors.'" (7:79)

And Salih went out from their settlements saying: "O my people, I conveyed to you the message of my Lord and I gave you much sincere advice, but what can I do, since you do not like those who advise you sincerely?"

It is testified here that Prophet Salih (peace be upon him) had fully conveyed the message, and that by their arrogance and disobedience they themselves made themselves deserving of that end. Here another page of the history of the deniers is folded up. And those who insult and deny a warner are deserving of an evil end.

Now the cart of history moves forward and we arrive in the age of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). But the story of Ibrahim is not related here, because what is sought here is the mention of those arrogant disobedient ones who were destroyed. This is the elaboration of the verse and theme that was introduced at the beginning of the surah.

The verse: "And how many a town have We destroyed" (7:4). These stories come as the details of this theme, while the people of Ibrahim were not destroyed, since Ibrahim (peace be upon him) made no demand to Allah for their destruction, but rather he withdrew from them and their idol-worship, leaving them. Therefore here the story of Lut is brought. He was the nephew of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and his contemporary. In this story there is a warning, and a denial by the people, and in the end the destruction of the people, and this has a connection with this series of stories and the theme.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (*Fi Zilal al-Quran*, Urdu translation) on Surah al-A'raf, verses 80–84:

The story of Lut (Lot) describes a corruption of human nature of a particular kind. In the earlier narratives, nations were destroyed over the most fundamental principle of life, the belief in the Oneness of God (*tawhid*) and the unity of divine sovereignty (*hakimiyyah*). But this corruption of nature was also a fundamental matter, and it was related to *tawhid* and to the question of sovereignty. The truth is that acknowledging God's lordship (*rububiyyah*) and worship (*ubudiyyah*) necessarily requires full obedience to the Qur'an and the Sunnah. The divine law (*sunnah ilahiyyah*) is that God created men and women as two distinct kinds, and made their union a means through which they become a means of completion for one another, thereby providing for the continuation and propagation of the human race. For this reason God assigned each sex its functions, gave each the physical and psychological capacity suited to the other, and arranged for the survival of the human species through their union. Then He placed a deep pleasure in that union for both, and made it a natural pleasure, so that they would come together with attraction and affection, accept the responsibilities of preserving the human race, and bear all the difficulties that come in this path: pregnancy, childbirth, the nursing and upbringing of children, the maintenance of offspring and wife, the duty of training children, and the mutual responsibilities of the whole family. This is despite the fact that, compared with other animals, the rearing and upbringing of human children is an exceptionally long and patience-testing process.

Since this duty is so fundamental and basic, and the survival of the human race is impossible without it, deviation within it has been declared a fundamental crime, just as even the slightest deviation in the belief in *tawhid* is intolerable. Therefore, deviation in the system of life and in the belief in *tawhid*, and the deviation of homosexual lust, have been declared crimes of the same degree.

In the story of the people of Lut, the deviation is clearly visible. It is a deviation from nature, and Prophet Lut (peace be upon him) tells them that they have initiated a new moral lawlessness, and that no nation before them had committed this moral corruption.

﴿And We sent Lut, when he said to his people, "Do you commit an indecency that no one in the worlds has committed before you? Indeed, you approach men with desire instead of women. Rather, you are a people who exceed limits."﴾ (7:80–81)

The accusation that Prophet Lut (peace be upon him) makes against them, that they exceed limits, and the reproach he gives them, mean that going beyond the sound natural order that God has established for humanity is excess (*israf*). Furthermore, the powers of reproduction and procreation that God has given them have a proper purpose, which is to be spent on the growth of life in this world. Instead, they waste these powers on barren ground and use them merely for fleeting pleasure and lust, although the pursuit of desire and pleasure should also follow the natural way. If anyone strives for pleasure in opposition to the divine law, it shall be considered misguidance and an act contrary to nature. Moreover, such an act is also contrary to morality, for Islamic morals are natural morals, and there is no corruption or deviation within them.

The physical and psychological make-up of woman is such that the man derives true pleasure from her. Even here the purpose is not merely the attainment of pleasure, but through this union one also obtains mercy and blessing, in that the continuation of the chain of life is being ensured in accordance with the divine law. As for the physical sameness between man and man, no healthy pleasure is obtained from it. Rather, a person feels filth in it, and therefore sound nature does not accept such a union.

In this matter, a person's beliefs and conceptions also play a great role. In today's age, the jahiliyyah prevalent in Europe spreads this sexual lawlessness with great shamelessness, and this lawlessness is the result of nothing but ideological lawlessness.

In our age, the Jews want to destroy all non-Jewish nations morally, and their institutions of propaganda and publication work day and night toward this end. These people want to destroy non-Jewish nations ideologically and morally. They have continually claimed that sexual disorder arises because women observe *purdah*. But facts show the opposite, because in Europe and America there is no rule or restriction on the union of any man and woman, just as animals come together when the need arises. Yet in these open societies, acts contrary to the natural order are also far more numerous than in other societies, and homosexuality is practised not only among men but also among women. If anyone has doubts, let him read the books of Mr. Kinsey, *Sexual Relations Among Men* and *Sexual Relations Among Women*. Nevertheless, despite this reality, these false media keep repeating their false claim and say that this evil practice spreads in a society because of women's *purdah*. They make this propaganda for the purposes which they have expressed in the *Protocols of the Elders of Zion*. Now, let us turn once again to the Qur'anic story and hear how they answered their Prophet.
