The verse: "And the answer of his people was only that they said, 'Expel them from your town; indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure.'" (7:82)

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran):

"And the answer of his people was only that they said, 'Expel them from your town. Indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure (yatatahharun)!'"

It is a strange matter: the one who is pure is being driven out of the village, while dirty, filthy and impure people are deemed worthy of living within the settlements. Yet this is nothing surprising. The jahiliyyah (the state of ignorance and rejection of divine guidance) of the modern age is doing exactly this. Is it not rejecting those people who adopt purity and do not defile themselves with those filths? It calls this progressiveness, and names it the freedom of men and women. In today's age, this jahiliyyah is closing the doors of sustenance upon such pure people; it has made their survival difficult. The sources of their wealth have been narrowed, and their ideas and concepts are suppressed. Jahiliyyah cannot even bear to see anyone adopt purity, because the only people acceptable to this jahiliyyah are those who are filthy, impure and involved in evils; its heart is narrow towards pure people. In every age, the mentality of jahiliyyah has been this.

So they are quickly brought to their end, and all other details are left out here.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verses 83–84:

Verse: "So We saved him and his family, except his wife; she was among those who remained behind. And We rained upon them a rain, so see how was the end of the criminals." (7:83–84)

"Finally, We delivered Lut and his family, except for his wife, who was among those who stayed behind... We brought them out safely and sent down a rain upon that people. Now see what was the end of the criminals?"

The enemies of Allah had become a threat to the servants of Allah, so Allah delivered His servants, and an ideological separation was made between the disobedient groups and the obedient ones. Although she was Prophet Lut's (peace be upon him) wife, his wife could not escape destruction, because her ideological alliance was with those people who were destined to be destroyed.

Severe rains overtook these people, and within those rains were tremendous storms. It appeared as though all the people had drowned in the rain, and the water surged forth like waves. Thus that land was purified of those impure people, because they had become spiritually impure and had become defiled with filth. So they lived in filth, and within that filth death overtook them.

Now the last page of the history of the nations that denied the truth is turned. This page concerns the nation of Shu'ayb, that is, the people of Madyan, from among the nations of that era.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 7, verse 85–86:

Verses 85 to 93.

This story is comparatively longer than the others, because in addition to the Islamic concept of life it also contains some other matters. Although it follows the same style of presentation that was adopted in the earlier stories.

﴿And to Madyan We sent their brother Shu'ayb. He said: "O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him."﴾ (7:85)

This call is the fundamental belief of Islam, and it has been the foundational word and emblem of the call of every prophet. Every prophet begins his call with this and then proceeds to the other details.

﴿Indeed, there has come to you a clear proof from your Lord.﴾ (7:85)

In the context here, there is no mention of a sign and guidance in the same way as the mention of a sign in the story of Salih. In other surahs of the Quran too, there is no mention of any miracle presented by Prophet Shu'ayb (peace be upon him). Yet in this verse there is an indication that Prophet Shu'ayb (peace be upon him), like the other prophets, also presented a miracle. As a result of that miracle, his demand from his people was that they should not cause any shortfall or excess in measure and weight, that they should avoid all the ways of corruption on earth, and also refrain from evil deeds such as highway robbery and armed plunder, and not put the people of religion into trial merely because of their religiousness.

﴿So give full measure and weight, and do not deprive the people of their things, and do not cause corruption on the earth after it has been set in order. That is better for you, if you are believers. And do not sit on every path threatening and turning away from the way of Allah those who believe in Him, and seeking to make it crooked. And remember when you were few and He multiplied you. And observe how was the end of the corrupters.﴾ (7:85–86)

From this prohibition we learn that the people of Prophet Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) were a polytheistic people. They did not only worship Allah alone; they associated the creatures of Allah with Him in the authority of legislation. These people did not follow Allah's just law in their dealings, but had devised rules of their own for settling their mutual affairs. Perhaps it is in this very matter that they committed shirk, and this is why they dealt dishonestly in buying and selling; besides this, the matters of corruption on earth, highway robbery and armed plunder were also widespread among them. Moreover, they also harassed those who were pious and devout, and turned them away from the straight path of Allah. They disliked every kind of steadfastness in the way of Allah. They wanted people to walk on wrong paths, in which lay their material interests, and to abandon the Islamic system, in which lay their loss.

Prophet Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) begins his call with this very word: that they should worship and submit to Allah alone, establish His sovereignty in the world, and implement His religion and command in all affairs of life.

Prophet Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) begins his call with this fundamental and basic matter, because he knows that all the affairs of life depend on this principle, and that human morality and his mutual conduct flow from this foundation and source, and as long as this principle is not established and firm, no human action can remain established and firm.

Alongside the call to worship Allah alone, the call to establish one's whole life on the straight path of monotheism, the call to implement the divine law and to abandon corruption on earth, he also directs them to the fact that they should give thanks for the grace and favour of Allah upon them and for the blessings He has bestowed upon them: "Remember when you were few and He multiplied you." ... If you do not give thanks for these blessings and remain determined to persist in corruption, then ... "observe how was the end of the corrupters."

Prophet Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) wishes that his people adopt the attitude of justice, fairness and generosity of heart, and that they not put into trial those who have believed and become followers of Allah's guidance, and whom Allah has guided to His religion. These people should not try to block the path of those people from every side, nor close the doors of life upon them, nor frighten or threaten them. If they do not believe, then at least, in this conflict between the believers and the disbelievers, they should remain neutral and wait to see the outcome.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 87:

﴿And if there is a group among you who believe in that with which I have been sent, and a group who do not believe, then be patient until Allah judges between us, and He is the best of judges.﴾ (7:87)

"If one group among you believes in the teaching with which I have been sent, and another group does not believe, then wait patiently until Allah makes a decision between us. And He is the best of those who decide."

Hazrat Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) advised them to adopt a just arrangement, and this was the final limit to which he could grant them concession; he could not step back from it even a single pace. That is, that their people should remain neutral in this struggle between disbelief and Islam, wait and watch, and not persecute the Muslims. Let the people adopt whatever religion they wish, until Allah Himself makes a decision.

However, the tyrannical forces (ṭāghūt) can never tolerate the existence on this earth of even a modest presence of faith, especially in the form of a community that does not obey ṭāghūt. A community of Muslims on this earth that is devoted only to Allah, that acknowledges no authority other than the sovereign authority of Allah, that in its personal life accepts no law other than the law of Allah, and that in its collective life believes in no system other than the system of Allah, is seen by ṭāghūt as a threat to its very existence. Even if such a community is itself limited within its own sphere, and at present does not confront the forces of ṭāghūt, and is waiting for ṭāghūt to reach its natural end, the mere existence of such a community is itself a danger to ṭāghūt.

The reality is that the forces of ṭāghūt have made it binding upon themselves to remain at war with the forces of Islam, even if the forces of Islam wish to avoid war, because the very existence of truth is a terrifying thing for those forces, and ṭāghūt trembles from truth at all times. The very existence of truth is the cause of the beginning of this struggle. This is the Sunnah of Allah. If anyone thinks that he is upon the truth and falsehood does not rise against him, then such people of truth should reflect on whether they are indeed upon the truth or not.

﴿The chiefs of those of his people who were arrogant said: "O Shu'ayb, we will surely drive you out, and those who believe with you, from our town, or you will return to our religion."﴾ (7:88)

"The chiefs of his people, who were engrossed in the pride of their greatness, said to him: 'O Shu'ayb, we will surely expel you and those who believed with you from our town, or else you must return to our religion.'"

This is the naked arrogance of ṭāghūt. It insists that it will continue this battle against truth, and it is simply impossible that truth and falsehood can co-exist, or that a compromise can be reached between them.

But theoretical forces are not affected at all by the threats of falsehood. Truth does not slip, and it does not hesitate in speaking. Hazrat Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) is not prepared to retreat from this position. The final concession from his side was that people be left free to adopt whatever creed they wish, to enter whichever authority they choose, and that both opponents await the decision of Allah. This is the point beyond which no bearer of truth as a caller can retreat, regardless of the intense pressure from the forces of ṭāghūt. If a caller retreats from this point, he is in effect bidding farewell to the truth whose representative he is, and indeed betrays it.

When Hazrat Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) received this threat from those arrogant ones, that either he should abandon his ideas and return to our religion, or else he should be ready to leave our territory, he clearly declared that he could never do so, because he does not wish that after the evil day from which Allah has saved him, he should re-enter it. Now he turns to Allah, and with hands raised in supplication he says: "O Allah, now You Yourself judge between us and our enemies, and help us, for You are the best of helpers."

Maulana Sayyid Abul A'la Maududi, in his article "Tehreek-e-Islami ki Buniyadein" (The Foundations of the Islamic Movement), states:

"Whoever has even a little insight into the problems of human life cannot remain unaware of this truth: the final decision on the making and marring of human affairs depends on the question of who holds the reins of human affairs. Just as a vehicle always moves in the direction in which the driver takes it, and the other people sitting in it are compelled, willingly or unwillingly, to travel in that direction, so too the vehicle of human civilisation moves in the direction in which those people wish to go who hold the reins of civilisation. Obviously, when all the resources of the earth are under the control of such people, when the reins of power and authority are in their hands, when the lives of ordinary people are bound to them, when the means of shaping and moulding thoughts, ideas and ideologies are in their possession, when the building of individual character, the formation of the collective system and the determination of moral values are in their authority, then under their guidance and rule humanity as a whole cannot in any way refrain from following the path on which they wish to drive it.

If these leaders and rulers are God-fearing and righteous people, then inevitably the whole system of life will proceed on God-worship and goodness and righteousness. Even wicked people will be compelled to become good; good deeds will be nurtured and flourish, and evils, if they are not eradicated, at least will not be able to grow. But if the authority of guidance, leadership and rule is in the hands of those who are estranged from God and wander in wickedness and debauchery, then automatically the whole system of life will proceed in rebellion against God and in tyranny and immorality. Ideas and beliefs, knowledge and manners, politics and economics, civilisation and social life, morals and dealings, justice and law, all will collectively deteriorate. Evils will flourish greatly."

"After this explanation it can easily be understood what importance this matter has in religion. It is obvious that the religion of Allah first of all wants people to remain wholly servants of the Truth, and that no yoke of servitude to anyone other than Allah should be upon their necks. Then it wants the law of Allah alone to become the law of people's lives. Then its demand is that corruption be eradicated from the earth, that the evils which bring Allah's wrath upon the inhabitants of the earth be uprooted, and that the good deeds which are pleasing to Allah be promoted. None of these objectives can be achieved in the manner that the leadership of humanity and the management of human affairs rest in the hands of the leaders of unbelief and misguidance, while the followers of the true religion remain merely subordinate to them, living under their concessions and allowances and remembering God only in passing. These objectives necessarily demand that all the people of goodness and righteousness who seek the pleasure of Allah should build collective strength and, staking everything, strive to establish a system of truth in which the office of imamate, guidance, leadership and rule is in the hands of the faithful and the righteous. Without this, that purpose cannot be attained which is the real purpose of religion; therefore in religion the establishment of a righteous imam and the setting up of a system of truth has a central importance, and after neglecting this matter no action can be such that by it a person may attain the pleasure of Allah.

Consider: why is so much emphasis placed in the Qur'an and Hadith on adherence to the community and on hearing and obeying, that if anyone secedes from the community, fighting against him becomes obligatory, even though he professes the declaration of Tawhid and is punctual in prayer and fasting? Is the reason for this not this alone: that the establishment and continuance of righteous leadership and the system of truth is the true aim of religion, and the achievement of this aim depends upon collective strength; therefore whoever harms collective strength commits a crime for which compensation can be made neither by prayer nor by affirming Tawhid? Then look: why has jihad been given so much importance in this religion that the Qur'an declares hypocrisy upon those who shy away from it and turn their backs on it? Jihad is nothing but another name for striving for the system of truth, and the Qur'an declares it to be the touchstone by which a person's faith is tested. In other words, one in whose heart there is faith cannot be content with the domination of the system of falsehood, nor can he hold back his life and wealth from striving for the establishment of the system of truth. Whoever shows weakness in this matter, his faith itself is doubtful, and then what other action could benefit him?"

"At this time there is not enough opportunity for me to explain this issue fully before you, but what I have said is quite sufficient to fix in mind the truth that from the standpoint of Islam, the establishment of a righteous imamate has central and purposeful importance. Likewise, the purpose of this call of Islam is that people's spiritual and ideological world and their material and financial world should also strive, struggle, wage jihad and fight against these tyrannical powers, and give every kind of sacrifice. But by sacrificing in this path, they are in fact delivered from the continual sacrifices that are humiliating and worthless in comparison. Islam invites people to strive for the station of honour and dignity, and it is for this reason that Hadrat Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) said:"

But the more firmly Prophet Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) stands against falsehood, raising the voice of truth with his strength and challenging the leaders of his society, the more he bows before the will and pleasure of Allah and submits to the decree of Allah. This is because Allah's knowledge is vast and all-encompassing, while human knowledge is limited. No human being can adopt resolve and certainty in the face of Allah's knowledge. As far as the Lord, the Exalted, is concerned, the proper conduct for a Muslim is to submit completely before Him.

Prophet Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) and the believers have limited knowledge, while the knowledge of the Lord of Majesty is unlimited. Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 91:

Verse: "So the earthquake seized them, and they remained prostrate in their homes" (7:91).

"Then the tremor overtook them, and they were left lying face-down in their homes" (7:91 in the Urdu rendering: "مگر ہوا یہ ایک دہلا دینے والی آفت نے ان کو آلیا اور وہ اپنے گھروں میں اوندھے پڑے کے پڑے رہ گئے").

Ar-rajfah is a calamity that shakes and terrifies and throws people face-down. They were made to recall their threats and their acts of aggression, for it was they who used to inflict torment upon the believers. Now Allah answers their claim in the very words they used. They used to say: "If you follow Shu'ayb, you will surely be ruined" (7:90 and 7:91 context: "La'in ittaba'tum..."). They spoke this as a threat to the believers. Allah answers them in kind: it was not those who obeyed Shu'ayb who were ruined, but those who opposed him.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 92:

Verse: "Those who denied Shu'ayb—it was as if they had never dwelt in those homes. Those who denied Shu'ayb, they were the losers."

"Those who denied Shu'ayb were destroyed, as though they had never dwelt in those homes. Those who denied Shu'ayb were, in the end, the ones who were ruined."

In the blink of an eye, we saw them lying face-down in their own homes, motionless, as though they had never built those houses, and as though no trace of them remained in those homes.

Now their pages of history are folded up in this manner, and they are left in disgrace and humiliation. The Messenger, who was their brother, separates from them, because their paths are separate and their ideologies are separate. Now, in this scene, it becomes apparent: the Messenger, who was their brother, separates from them, because their paths are separate and their ideologies are separate. Now, in this scene, it is seen that their end is also separate, and now, upon this evil end of theirs, not even their own brother feels any regret at how they have been reduced to nothing.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 93:

Verse: "So he turned away from them and said, 'O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and advised you sincerely, so how should I grieve over a disbelieving people?'" (7:93)

Shu'ayb left their settlements saying: "O brethren of my people, I have conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and fulfilled the right of sincere advice to you. Now how should I grieve over a people who refuse to accept the truth?"

This is because they are one millah (community of faith) and these people are another millah. The believers are one qawm (people) and they are another qawm. As for lineage and kinship of nation, in this religion it has no standing at all. It carries no weight with Allah. Here, "so-and-so son of so-and-so" is nothing. In this religion the only bond is belief and ideology, and upon it depends unity and cohesion.

**Volume 3 begins.**

**Lesson 78: At a Glance**

Within the discourse of this surah, this lesson serves as a pause. Previously, the stories of the peoples of Noah, Hud, Salih, Lot and Shu'ayb (peace be upon them) were related. In this pause, a general commentary is offered on them. The purpose of this pause is to explain the divine way (sunnah Ilahiyyah) that operates continuously on this earth, and which the divine decree has enforced upon the deniers of the inhabited world. Here the word "qaryah" (town) is used, which refers to a great city or a prominent established civilization. This divine way is the one unchanging and inviolable law, and its enforcement by God applies to all deniers. Human history is shaped by this divine way; indeed, the real aspect of human history is the divine way itself. The purpose and aim of this divine way is that it afflicts those who deny with sorrow and suffering, so that perhaps their hearts may soften, become tender, turn towards God, and come to know well the reality of God's divinity and their own reality of servitude.

If, even then, they do not pay heed and do not come to their senses, God then increases His blessings upon these deniers. Doors of facilities and blessings open for them from every side, they are granted respite, and their population then grows. Immersed in comfort and luxury, they become engrossed in indulgence, and this becomes a trial for them. They think that the difficulties they have faced were also faced by their forefathers before them, and that the affairs of the world continue along such a course, with ups and downs. ﴿And they say: Adversity and prosperity touched our forefathers too﴾ (7:95). They remain immersed in such thinking and live a heedless life, until the grip of God seizes them, and they do not realize that within abundance, plenty, and hardship lies the wisdom of God. They fail to grasp the wisdom of God within this trial. Those upon whom the wrath of God falls, and who are heedless and careless, do not fear the consequences of their end. They live a life of ease and luxury in the same way that animals live. It is in this state of intoxication that the punishment of God descends upon them. Had they believed and adopted a God-fearing attitude, this would not have been their condition; rather, blessings from the heavens would have descended upon them, sustenance would have come to them from the earth and from the heavens, and God would have sent down upon them that state of tranquility by which their lives would have been spent in utmost peace. After such peace and abundance, no state of decline or ruin would have come upon them.

After this, God warns those who were made the inheritors of the earth and the holders of power after those who were destroyed. They are told to protect themselves from heedlessness and arrogance, to remain alert at all times, and to fear God. They are directed to the historical reality that in human history God has destroyed many peoples one after another, and has provided opportunities to other peoples in their place, but they did not take a lesson from the fate of those who perished. Therefore, the law of retribution (mukafat) of God awaits the people of those towns, and clear examples of it exist in human history.

This pause concludes with an address to the Messenger (ﷺ). He is told: ﴿These are the towns whose stories We relate to you﴾ (7:101), so that you may be made aware of the reality of these people and told that their end came in accordance with the divine way. It is said: ﴿And We found most of them not keeping any covenant; indeed, We found most of them to be defiantly disobedient﴾ (7:102). This last Messenger and the community of this last Messenger are the heirs of the moral wealth of all the messengers, and it is only this Messenger and his community who truly benefit from and take admonition from these historical events and reports.

**Explanation of verses 94 to 102**

Here, the context of the discourse does not aim to narrate a specific incident; rather, its aim is to explain the general divine way. The purpose here is not to describe the particular features of any one people, but to explain the workings of God's system of divine decree and destiny (qada wa qadar). Accordingly, attention is drawn here to God's order (namoos) by which this entire system of the universe operates, and by which all events take place. Because of this order, human history journeys forward in this world, and prophethood is also a part of the divine order upon this earth, for the divine order itself is, in essence, a broader and greater prophethood. The fact that events in this world occur not without any plan, but in accordance with divine decree, in accordance with His wisdom, and in accordance with the goals and objectives He has set, and that the final outcomes occur in accordance with the divine will (mashiyyah), and that this will operates in accordance with the divine way (sunnah), and that both this order and this way have been established by the divine will.

The events that befell those past towns occurred in accordance with the way established by God's unrestrained will, and in the same manner, later peoples too will be governed by this universal order.

According to the Islamic conception of life, human will and effort are an important factor in the shaping of history, but human effort and human will remain within the wide scope of God's unrestrained will, and the system of divine decree surrounds them. ﴿And God encompasses all things﴾ (4:126). Human will and effort, while remaining within the system of divine will and divine decree, harmonize with the movement of the entire universe. Humanity and its efforts are both influenced by this universe and influence it. It is, as it were, a great wonder of factors and scenes from which human history is formed, and this scope is very vast. In comparison, the economic interpretation of history, the physical interpretation of history, and the geographical interpretation of history appear as extremely limited and small circles, whereas the Islamic conception of history has a very broad scope. In comparison, these limited circles appear as games devised by humans, and as disjointed lines.

﴿And We did not send a warner to any town without seizing its people with distress and hardship, so that perhaps they might humble themselves﴾ (7:94).

Never has it happened that We sent a prophet to a town without first afflicting its people with hardship and severity, in the hope that they might become humble.

This matter is not carried out as mere sport and amusement, because God is far too exalted to afflict people with hardship and severity, and to bring upon them physical and financial troubles, merely for the purpose of sport and amusement. This conception is not consistent with the majesty of God: that people should be afflicted with grief and calamity so that a deity may take revenge upon them and satisfy his spite. This is just as such stories are famous about deities in all idolatrous religions, and from which it becomes known that the work of those deities is to remain constantly engaged in pointless pastimes and acts of vengeance, and to inflict the harshest retaliation for the ordinary offenses of humans. The question is: why then are people afflicted with hardships and difficulties by God? Only so that those whose nature has not been wholly distorted, and in whom some measure of goodness remains, that nature may awaken, and those hearts which still have some flexibility, and which have not become entirely like stone, may soften, and that this weak human being may turn towards God, who is the Subduer and the Compeller, and that they may turn to Him in humility and supplication, seeking His mercy. And through this expression of humility and supplication, they may proclaim that they are servants of God, because servitude to God is the true purpose and aim of human existence, although the reality is that God has no need for humans to humble themselves or to express servitude. It is the human's own need and the purpose of human existence.

﴿And I did not create the jinn and humankind except that they should worship Me. I do not seek provision from them, nor do I seek that they should feed Me. Indeed, God is the Provider, the Possessor of mighty strength﴾ (51:56–58). "I created the jinn and humankind only so that they may worship Me. I do not desire sustenance from them, nor do I desire that they feed Me. Indeed, the Provider and the Possessor of firm power is God alone."

And in a sacred hadith it comes: "If all of humankind and the jinn were to unite in the worship and servitude of God like the heart of one person, this complete unity would add nothing to the sovereignty of God; and if all the jinn and humankind were to unite in disobedience to God like the heart of one person, they could not diminish anything from the sovereignty of God." But the declaration of servitude by people, and the expression of humility and submission before God, are beneficial to themselves. Human life and the economic system of humans are also reformed by this. When people express the servitude of God alone, they become free from all servitudes and bondages other than the servitude and bondage of God. They are also saved from the servitude of Satan, who is intent on misguiding humans, and it was stated at the very beginning of this surah that Satan's aim is precisely to lead humans astray. Similarly, by adopting the servitude of God, a person is also freed from the servitude of fellow humans, and they become ashamed to follow Satan, and thus their condition becomes such that by no word or deed do they deserve the wrath of God. Even in difficult circumstances they turn towards God and humble themselves, and they proceed with steadfastness on the path that leads them to freedom, in which their moral purification takes place. They do not become slaves to their desires and passions, and they rise above the servitude of other individuals.

Thus, God's method is that a prophet is sent to the inhabitants of every town, so that they may reject him, and then they are seized. The beginning of this seizure takes the form of afflicting them with psychological and spiritual suffering, and making them taste the pain of bodily and financial penalty, so that by bearing these afflictions their hearts may be revived. It is a rule that when a human is afflicted with grief and sorrow, the weaknesses within their personality are removed, refinement enters them, and from within them the dried springs of goodness and blessing burst forth fresh. The living hearts become more sensitive, and the human turns towards the shade of God's mercies. Then, when the gentle breezes of God's mercy begin to blow upon a weak person surrounded by distressing moments, such a person feels the utmost peace and tranquility.

﴿That perhaps they might humble themselves﴾ (7:94).

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 7, verse 95:

ثُمَّ بَدَّلْنَا مَكَانَ السَّيِّئَةِ الْحَسَنَةَ "Then We replaced the evil state with good." After that, We changed their hardship into ease. Hardship gave way to gentleness, narrowness gave way to abundance, poverty gave way to blessings, sickness gave way to health, the scarcity of children gave way to a multitude of children, and in every matter scarcity was replaced by plenty, and fear was replaced by security. Thus all the means of comfort and luxury became available, and provisions for enjoyment, food and drink were made ready. Yet, according to Allah's principle, all of this was in fact a kind of trial.

If a person is afflicted with calamities and put to the test, then sometimes people endure it with patience, and most people bear it. For severity often creates defensive strength in the opposing party. A person who is oppressed and subjected to severity sometimes gains strength by remembering Allah, provided that some trace of goodness still remains in him. Such a person turns towards Allah, humbles himself and pleads, and under the shade of the remembrance of Allah he attains tranquility and peace. Let it be known that the horizons of the remembrance of Allah are vast, its fields are broad and long, and the promises that Allah makes to those who remember Him contain good tidings for them. But when Allah tests someone through an abundance of wealth, this trial is far more severe than poverty and destitution. Because of wealth, a person becomes heedless. Then he adopts rebellion, and very few people can remain patient in such a state, and such few are then the true servants of Allah.

ثُمَّ بَدَّلْنَا مَكَانَ السَّيِّئَةِ الْحَسَنَةَ حَتّٰي عَفَوْا وَّقَالُوْا قَدْ مَسَّ اٰبَاۗءَنَا الضَّرَّاۗءُ وَالسَّرَّاۗءُ "Then We replaced the evil state with good, until they multiplied and said, 'Our forefathers too were touched by hardship and ease.'"

That is, these people multiplied and spread over the earth, began living a life of luxury and indulgence, all the facilities of life were provided to them, and they began to do everything. No caution or fear remained an obstacle in their path. From the word ʿAfaw (عَفَوْا), which indicates an abundance of something, there is also an indication of a psychology of carelessness. They came to regard everything as trivial and light. In every matter, whether it related to the material world or to conduct, they became careless. This psychological and practical condition is found among all those people who possess abundance of wealth and live a life of great ease, especially when they have remained immersed for a long time in pursuit of luxury, whether they are individuals or nations. It is as if seriousness and awareness have departed from their hearts and minds, and they do not like to be serious even in great matters. They spend with open hands, indulge themselves on a wide scale, remain constantly lost in luxury and deal with matters with extreme carelessness, and commit such crimes that, on hearing of them, the hair stands on end; and these people commit such acts with great boldness. They do not fear the wrath of Allah. They feel no shame before the common people. Every kind of disgrace proceeds from them with great carelessness. They do not perceive the divine law (sunnah Ilahiyyah) operating in this universe. They do not understand these trials, and they think that these affairs simply keep going on in this way, that they have no known cause, and that this universe is not running according to any plan, and that (our forefathers too had good and bad days) qad massa aba'ana al-darra'u wa al-sarra'u: "We have passed through the period of difficulties; now our good days have come, and these days are passing very pleasantly, and they are passing without any plan."

This is the final limit: when these people sink into heedlessness, forget every admonition and become engrossed in amusement, pleasure and rebellion, then at this limit an evil end overtakes them, and this is in accordance with the divine law.

فَاَخَذْنٰهُمْ بَغْتَةً وَّهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُوْنَ "Then We seized them suddenly while they perceived not."

At last We seized them suddenly, and they were not aware of it. They were given this punishment for their heedlessness, arrogance and distance from Allah. They had given their desires free rein. They did not hesitate in committing any evil deed. And the last drop of the fear of God had dried up in the vessels of their hearts.

This is the sunnah of Allah, and in this universe it keeps running on this course. This sunnah operates among the creatures of Allah in accordance with His will. The caravan of human history keeps moving forward with human will and action, within the vast domain of Allah's power and will. And the noble Qur'an explains this divine law clearly for people, and repeatedly warns and admonishes them about it. This trial is a trial of the punishment of Allah, and in it a person is tested by being afflicted with calamities and difficulties, and in it a person is commanded to remain alert at all times and to protect himself from an evil end, because the law of recompense for deeds operates here, and the law of recompense is inescapable. Therefore, whoever does not remain alert, who does not adopt the path of the fear of God, and does not take precaution, will be doing wrong to himself, and he will bring upon himself a punishment that will not be averted. And Allah does not decree anything upon any soul.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 96:

This is another aspect of Allah's constant practice (sunnat jariyah). If the people of the towns had believed and accepted instead of denying, and had taken the path of taqwa (God-consciousness) instead of wickedness, Allah would have opened for them the doors of blessings from the heavens and the earth. ﴿Blessings from the heaven and the earth.﴾ And He would have continued to give them without reckoning; blessings would have rained upon them from the heavens and from the earth. In view of the manner of expression the Qur'an has adopted, we may describe this as abundance of every kind, not restricted to any single category of need. Abundance of every type and every kind.

In this verse and in the verse before it, we encounter a great truth. This truth relates both to human ideas and to the realities of human life, and also to the realities of this entire universe. It also states the important factor and driving force of human history. The systems of life devised by human beings have completely ignored this important factor, and even denied it.

That factor is faith, belief, and fear of God. The matter of faith, belief and fear of God is not something separate from the realities of human life, nor is it something separate from human history. Rather, belief in Allah and fear of Allah are the things because of which Allah sends down the blessings of the heavens and the earth. This is Allah's promise, and no one fulfils a promise more faithfully than Allah.

We who are believers in Allah, our way is to take this promise of Allah with a believing heart. We confirm it, we do not even feel the need to understand its causes and mechanisms, and we do not hesitate for a moment in affirming the meaning and implication of this verse. This is because our faith is faith in the unseen, and as a requirement of that faith we confirm this promise of Allah.

After this, we again reflect upon this promise of Allah, because Allah Himself has commanded that you reflect upon the Qur'an, and after reflection we also come to know the nature and reality of this matter.

From belief in Allah it becomes clear that the nature of the believer is alive, and that the capacity to perceive and accept natural realities is present within him. The perception of such a person is true, and his human foundation is sound and whole. And the mind of such a person has such breadth that he can perceive the realities of this universe. All these matters are guarantors of a person's success in practical life.

Belief in Allah is a force that drives a person forward. It gathers the scattered powers of human personality and places them on one direction and course, and within that direction the human personality advances with the help of Allah's power, strives for the establishment of Allah's supreme sovereignty on this earth, and engages in building this globe. As a result, mischief and corruption are uprooted and cast out from this globe, and humanity engages in the development and construction of this earth, and thus a person remains successful in practical life.

Firm belief in Allah frees a person from slavery to his own desires and from slavery to other human beings. There is no doubt that only the person who is a slave of Allah alone and free from all other slaveries can establish the correct system of the rightly guided caliphate (khilafah rashidah) on this globe. Such a person will be stronger than those who are slaves of one another or slaves of their own desires.

The fear of God is a wise awakening. Through it a person is protected from moral defects such as rebellion, arrogance and deviation. His activities acquire moderation, and the style of his life becomes serious. A person's entire striving becomes cautious, and he does not commit rebellion and go beyond his limits, and he keeps his life within righteous bounds.

The picture of the life of a righteous person is that his life is balanced and based on moderation. He creates a balance between moving forward and the obstacles in the way. He works on the earth while keeping his gaze lifted toward the heavens. He is free from caprice, rebellion and transgression, and there is always the fear of God in his heart. Such a person possesses a righteous, productive and beneficial character, and it is such a person who deserves Allah's help, and in whose heart is the fear of God. Over such a person the shadows of Divine blessings descend. Goodness and blessing become widespread in his affairs, and success casts its shadow over his life. Outwardly his life seems to run according to causes and means, but in reality an unseen power is his helper.

The blessings that shade the believers and the people of taqwa are of various kinds, and the details of them are not given in this verse, but they certainly exist. From the indications in this verse it is understood that blessings are descending upon them from every direction. Springs of blessing gush forth from every side, the details of which are not given. Therefore, what is meant is every kind and category of blessing; they descend in every form and shape, some of which are not even in people's imagination, and some of which they do recognise.

Those who think that belief in Allah and fear of Allah are merely a matter of private worship, with no connection to a person's practical and collective life, have in fact not understood the reality of faith. They should look and see that, in Allah's view, faith does have a connection with practical and collective life. Allah bears witness to this, and Allah's testimony is sufficient testimony. And He links it to matters about which people well know that they are matters of practical and collective life.

﴿And if the people of the towns had believed and been mindful of Allah, We would certainly have opened for them blessings from the heaven and the earth, but they denied, so We seized them for what they were earning.﴾ "If the people of the towns had believed and adopted the way of taqwa, We would have opened for them the doors of blessings from the heavens and the earth, but they denied, so We seized them for the evil they were gathering."

Some people observe that the position of certain nations in this matter is as follows: "We are Muslims, and the doors of provision are closed upon us, and our share consists of nothing but drought and ruin. We see that there are nations which are neither believers in Allah nor among the people of taqwa, yet the rain of provision pours upon them from every side. They possess immense power and are influential in the world. So the question is: why does the divine practice mentioned in the above verse not apply to us?"

In fact, such people have taken only the apparent and superficial aspect of this issue. Those who say "we are Muslims" do not claim to be believers and God-fearing. Nor have these people adopted a attitude of purely serving and being slaves to Allah. In their practical life the testimony of "there is no god but Allah" is not present; rather, these people are serving some of their own kind as slaves. "These masters" have become their gods and make laws for them. Not only laws, but they also prescribe for them values of good and evil. I say that such people are not believers at all. The duty of the believer is precisely to remove those who have become the supreme authority over them. The first action of the believer is that he does not make anyone among his own kind a lord and god who imposes on them his own laws and his own system. When the forerunners of those who make such claims were true believers and Muslims, the whole world bowed before them, the rain of the blessings of the heavens and the earth fell upon them, and their Lord's promise with them was true, because they themselves were true.

As for those upon whom the doors of provision have been opened, this too is a part of Allah's practice: ﴿Then We replaced the bad condition with good, until they multiplied and said, "Our forefathers too experienced hardship and ease."﴾ "Then We changed their misfortune into prosperity, until they flourished greatly and said, 'Good and bad days have always come to our forefathers as well.'" The favours bestowed upon these people are in fact a trial and test for them, and this trial is more dangerous than the trial of calamity. There is a great difference between the favours upon disbelievers and the favours upon the believers. The blessing of Allah sometimes shows its colours even in a small thing. When a person benefits well from a little thing and feels joy and contentment with peace and tranquillity, on the other hand there are great developed and wealthy nations who live a life of anxiety and dissatisfaction, although apparently they live in complete peace and security, and no bond remains between their individuals. Restlessness prevails among the members of society, and these nations are close to being utterly destroyed. There is abundance of equipment, but contentment is lacking. Everything is in plenty, yet the people are of wicked conduct; their very prosperity is pointing towards a bad future for them, and this prosperity is a cause of Allah's retribution upon them.

The believers receive blessings in many forms: there is blessing in the things they need, blessing in the human self, blessing in human consciousness, blessing in pure lives, and as a result of these blessings life grows, and within it peace and tranquillity arise. It is not that conveniences are abundant everywhere while a person is in hell, afflicted with physical and psychological exhaustion.

This is the constant practice of Allah, to which human history also bears witness, and immediately after whose mention the address turns toward the heedless. After knowing the circumstances in which the deniers were destroyed and punishment came upon those who were the cause, which produced a comprehensive tremor in the consciousness and intuition of the reader, because those people showed heedlessness in their ease, in the trial of Allah's favours and in the goods of life, and could not understand the wisdom of Allah, that these were in fact their trial. In such circumstances the context now turns to those heedless ones who are absorbed in their present state. Such people are warned that at any time of the day or night the punishment of Allah may seize them, in circumstances where they are engrossed in amusement and play and are heedless in sleep.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verses 97–98:

Do the people feel so secure, even after observing the Sunnah of Allah (sunnatullah, the established way of Allah), that Allah tests them by giving them prosperity and abundance, and by afflicting them with hardships and calamities? After that He seizes the ungrateful, the disobedient and the deniers, and destroys them. The sites of their destruction and ruin are before your eyes: those who were destroyed, and who populated those towns well and then left them to those who came after them once they had perished. Do they feel secure that the punishment of Allah may come upon them suddenly, while they are heedless and unaware, and they be afflicted and destroyed?

The punishment may come at some time of the day, or at night, at a time when they are heedless. Remember that a person is so immersed in sleep that no consciousness or will remains within him, and he has no power to do any work. He cannot take precautionary measures, nor can he defend himself against even an ordinary insect. What then will he do against the power of Allah, so great? Against that power no human being, however alert, strong and wise, can contend.

In short, this punishment may come upon them during the day, when they are at play. In play a person has no awareness; he is absorbed in the game and his attention is fixed only on his opponent. As for an attack from Allah, one cannot resist it even with full preparation and full alertness; so what will he do when he is heedless?

The punishment of Allah is so severe that whether they are awake or asleep, in no state can they stand before it. Whether they are at play or in a serious condition, they cannot resist it. However, the Qur'anic context presents before the human being those moments of his life, so that a sense of his own weakness and helplessness is fully created in human consciousness, and he becomes cautious and takes care of his protection. When a devastating attack comes, and it comes in circumstances where a person is completely in heedlessness and carelessness, and he is seized in total unawareness, then in such circumstances his defence is extremely weak. As for the punishment of Allah, whether a person is aware or unaware, his helplessness before it will be boundless.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verses 97–98:

Do the people feel so secure, even after observing the Sunnah of Allah (sunnatullah, the established way of Allah), that Allah tests them by giving them prosperity and abundance, and by afflicting them with hardships and calamities? After that He seizes the ungrateful, the disobedient and the deniers, and destroys them. As for an attack from Allah, one cannot resist it even with full preparation and full alertness; so what will he do when he is heedless?

The punishment of Allah is so severe that whether they are awake or asleep, in no state can they stand before it. Whether they are at play or in a serious condition, they cannot resist it. However, the Qur'anic context presents before the human being those moments of his life, so that a sense of his own weakness and helplessness is fully created in human consciousness, and he becomes cautious and takes care of his protection. When a devastating attack comes, and it comes in circumstances where a person is completely in heedlessness and carelessness, and he is seized in total unawareness, then in such circumstances his defence is extremely weak. As for the punishment of Allah, whether a person is aware or unaware, his helplessness before it will be boundless.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 99:

By the "plotting" (makr) of Allah is meant the hidden arrangement by which they are kept unaware, so that people may keep fearing Allah and remain cautious regarding the commands of Allah. And those who do not fear will remain in loss, because the result of ease-seeking, heedlessness, transgressing limits and carelessness can only be manifest loss (khusran mubin). Do these people feel secure from the plotting and arrangement of Allah, when these are the very people whose forefathers were destroyed, and after them these people were made the heirs of this world, and those who were destroyed because of their own heedlessness, so that in their destruction there is no guidance and lesson for them?

Meaning: Indeed, the Sunnah of Allah is unalterable and the will of Allah continues to operate. If Allah were to seize these people for their sins in the same way He seized their forefathers, who could save them? Or if Allah were to set a seal upon their hearts and deprive them of the very ability to be guided, so that they remain forever deprived of guidance, and their attention is turned away from the signs of guidance, and both their worldly life and their Hereafter are ruined, then who would come to their aid? The destruction of earlier peoples, the succession of these present people after them, and the working of Allah's Sunnah in this matter, all these affairs provided them with abundant means of reflection, guidance and taqwa. It was expected of them that they would fear Allah and abandon that temporary, artificial well-being in which they considered themselves secure. Had they set aside this heedlessness, they would have been reformed and would have taken a lesson from these events. Would that they had done so!

The warning given in this verse does not intend that people should constantly tremble in fear of an unknown punishment and of sudden future destruction, always living in uncertain circumstances, fearing that a punishment may descend upon them at any moment. For constant anxiety, fear of a punishment that may come at any time, and the constant dread that some calamity may befall at any moment, are matters that paralyse human powers, and a person may be deprived of the excellence of knowledge and action. In such despair, a person may withdraw from the continuous work of building and developing this earth. The purpose and aim of this warning is not to paralyse a human being; its sole purpose is that a person should awaken, that there should always be within him the sense of God-fearing, that he should always keep watch over his own soul, learn a lesson from the events that have passed in the world, and come to understand the causes behind human history. His connection with Allah Most High should remain constant, and a life of luxury should not make him heedless and arrogant.

From Allah there is a promise to people that He will grant them, in the Hereafter, peace, tranquillity, His pleasure and contentment in both this world and the Hereafter; but this will occur when they keep their awareness of Allah alert, and, out of taqwa and fear of Allah, do not involve themselves in pollutions. They placed their trust in Allah in preference to their material strength. They relied upon the resources that are with Allah rather than their limited material means. Those who trust in none but Allah had hearts filled with the wealth of faith. They were content in the remembrance of Allah, and they kept their desires and satanic impulses under control. They lived on this earth as reformers, in accordance with Allah's guidance. They did not fear people, but feared Allah alone, and Allah alone is deserving of being feared.

In this manner we can well understand this lasting warning of Allah's punishment, a punishment that is unalterable and that accords with those measures of Allah which man cannot comprehend. Thus we can understand that the purpose of these Qur'anic verses is not merely to spread terror and dread, but to create awakening among people; it is not to create restlessness among people, but to instil in them a sense of loss. It is not desired that life be suspended, but that people be protected from heedlessness and rebellion.

The method of the Islamic and Qur'anic system of education is that it reforms both the changing patterns of human psychology and the problems and conduct of nations and societies, and treats each according to its circumstances. To some it gives the wealth of peace, tranquillity and the hope of trust in Allah; and for others it prescribes the remedy of fear, awakening and a stern warning, so that they desist from their evil deeds and fear the punishment of Allah which may overtake them at any moment, especially when they become deluded by placing their trust in material life. Allah is, in any case, well aware of His creation; Allah is Subtle and All-Aware.

Here the discourse on the perpetual Sunnah comes to an end. The human conscience has been touched with awareness of this Sunnah, and very excellent indications have been given. Now the address turns back to the Prophet ﷺ, and he is told what the final outcome was for the people of those towns collectively, what temperament of disbelief emerges from that outcome, what temperament of faith emerges, and what the general conduct of these two types of people appears to be from the history of the nations of the world.

This is a commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 101:

These stories were from Allah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had no knowledge of them. They were taught to him (ﷺ) through revelation.

﴿And their messengers certainly came to them with clear proofs.﴾ But these signs had no effect upon them, and they kept on denying the messengers, just as they had denied before these signs. Even these signs and miracles could not lead them to faith. It was not that there was a shortage of evidence before them; rather, the true state of affairs was that their hearts had been sealed, their perception had died, and they were not attentive to guidance. What was lacking was that their natural disposition had died; they were not affected at all, and therefore they did not accept the call. When their hearts were not turned toward the arguments of faith, and the indications of guidance were not even reaching them, Allah also left them in that state and set a seal upon their hearts, and for them all the paths to accepting the truth were closed.

﴿Thus does Allah seal the hearts of the disbelievers.﴾ Behold, in this way Allah seals the hearts of those who deny the truth. This was the disposition of the majority of them.

The covenant referred to here may be the covenant of human nature, which is mentioned at the end of this surah: ﴿And when your Lord brought forth from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves, [saying], "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we have testified."﴾ "O Prophet, remind the people of the time when your Lord took out from the loins of the children of Adam their offspring, and made them witnesses against themselves, asking: 'Am I not your Lord?' They said: 'Indeed You are our Lord. We bear witness to it.'"

The covenant may also mean the covenant which their forefathers made with their messengers, that they would believe, but those who came after them broke it, as has always happened in every age of ignorance (jahiliyyah): with the passing of time, the people of faith gradually move towards ignorance until they finally become fully immersed in it.

Whatever the covenant may be, the distinguishing feature of those who were destroyed was that they were not bound by any pact or agreement, and they did not hold firm to anything. These people kept changing according to their own desires. Their disposition had also become such that they did not stand by their word and did not adopt a truthful conduct. Rather, most of them were found to be defiant (fasiq), that is, found to have deviated from their religion. And this was because they kept changing at all times and did not respect any covenant; rather, they had become slaves to their interests. A people who do not remain faithful to their promise with Allah, who do not remain steadfast in their religion and the path of guidance, and who do not take guidance from Allah, will evidently be scattered and disunited. They deviate from the path of truth, and evidently they become defiant. Thus this was the condition of the people of those towns, and therefore this was their end.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 103:

Lesson No. 79 At a Glance

This lesson narrates the circumstances and events concerning Pharaoh, his courtiers and Musa (peace be upon him). These are the links of the story that relate to his claim of lordship, and to the drowning of him and his army. Among the intermediate links are: the contest with the magicians, the triumph of truth over falsehood, the faith of the magicians and their words, "We believe in the Lord of Musa and the Lord of Harun," then Pharaoh's threat of severe punishment against them, and the display of the elevation of faith and Islam in their hearts and minds, and their preference for faith and Islam over their own lives. After this comes the mention of the oppression by Pharaoh against the Children of Israel, then the descent of Allah's punishment upon the family of Pharaoh and the people of Egypt, such as drought and the destruction of every kind of produce, then the flood, the locusts, the frogs and the blood-rain, and the people's submission before the spiritual power of Musa, asking him to pray to the Lord of the worlds so that they may be relieved of this punishment. But when this calamity was removed from them, they would soon return to their former state and declare that they were not prepared to accept whatever signs and miracles he showed. Thus, through these repeated misdeeds, the proof is completed against them, and they are drowned, because they denied the miracles and showed heedlessness in this trial. All these matters take place in accordance with the established practice of Allah, that He tests people both by hardship and affliction, and by granting them prosperity and abundance. After this come the events in which the people of Musa, when they pass these trials, are granted authority in the land by Allah. And after the severity and calamity of slavery, having granted them authority in the land, they are again tested and granted abundance.

We have designated the events mentioned above as one lesson, and the events that Musa (peace be upon him) faced from his people as the second lesson, since the subject of the two is different.

The manner in which the story is begun here shows what the purposes of bringing this story are. It begins with these words:

ثُمَّ بَعَثْنَا مِنْۢ بَعْدِهِمْ مُّوْسٰي بِاٰيٰتِنَآ اِلٰى فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَا۟ىِٕهٖ فَظَلَمُوْا بِهَا ۚ فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الْمُفْسِدِيْنَ ۔ "Then after them (the nations mentioned above) We sent Musa with Our signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs. But they wronged Our signs. So see what was the end of the corrupters."

It is made explicit here what the purpose of bringing this story is, namely that in this world the end of the corrupters has always been one and the same. Thus, after the purpose of the story is expressed, the appropriate links with its necessary theme and subject are brought in succession.

This story also shows living and moving scenes. There is movement and there is dialogue, there are impressions, and there is the outline and identification of various people and characters. Throughout it there are guidance and indications, there is a lesson to be learned, and there is clarification of what the features of the call to Allah are, what the nature of the call to tyranny is, and that all tyrannical powers in reality claim lordship and sovereignty. And in the soul in which the longing to call to the Lord of the worlds has settled deeply, the fear of tyrannical powers completely disappears. Then such a person sets out on this path and does not regard any promise or threat.

Lesson No. 79: Explanation of Verses 103 to 137

Earlier in this surah, the people of the towns that were mentioned had denied the call to truth and were destroyed. After them, Musa (peace be upon him) was sent. The story begins at the point where Musa (peace be upon him) and Pharaoh face each other, and a summary is given of how Pharaoh and his clique receive the call to truth, and an indication is also given of the end they reached. They wronged these signs and miracles by rejecting them, that is, they committed disbelief and polytheism. In the Holy Qur'an, the word fisq (transgression) is often used for disbelief and the word zulm (wrongdoing) for polytheism, because there is no greater wrong and no greater transgression than disbelief and polytheism. Those who disbelieve or associate partners with Allah in reality wrong a great truth, namely the sovereignty of Allah and the doctrine of tawhid. And these people in reality also wrong themselves, because by this they make themselves deserving of destruction and ruin, both in this world and in the Hereafter. Then such people commit the wrong against the common people of taking them out of the servitude and worship of the one Allah alone and making them slaves of various tyrannical powers, and regarding these as lord and supreme authority. And what greater wrong could there be? Thus disbelief is wrongdoing, and disbelievers are wrongdoers, as the Holy Qur'an adopts this manner of expression. Moreover, whoever adopts disbelief and wrongdoing leaves the straight path and walks on wrong ways, and, falling into various deviations, becomes a transgressor and a evildoer, and in the end becomes deserving of Hell rather than Paradise.

Pharaoh and his clique wronged the signs of Allah, that is, they refused to accept them. Therefore they reached a bad end.

فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الْمُفْسِدِيْنَ "So see what was the end of the corrupters." Every tyrannical system in which obedience is rendered to some law other than the Shari'ah of Allah is a corrupt system, and concerning it Allah's ruling is that such tyrannical powers cannot be among the reformers, but are rather corrupting powers.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 104:

The dialogues and events that took place at the first meeting between Musa (peace be upon him) and Pharaoh were as follows.

"Musa said, 'O Pharaoh, I have come as a messenger sent by the Lord of the worlds. It is my duty to say nothing about Allah except the truth. I have come to you from your Lord with a clear proof of my commission, so send the Children of Israel with me.' Pharaoh said, 'If you have brought a sign and are truthful in your claim, then produce it.' Musa threw down his staff, and suddenly it was a living, writhing serpent. And he drew out his hand from his pocket, and it shone white before all the onlookers. Upon this, the chiefs of Pharaoh's people said to one another, 'Surely this man is a highly skilled sorcerer. He wants to drive you out of your land. Now, what do you advise?' Then they all advised Pharaoh, saying, 'Put him and his brother off, and send heralds to all the cities to bring to you every skilled sorcerer.'"

This is the first confrontation between truth and falsehood, and between faith and disbelief. In this scene, on one side there is the call issued by the Lord of the worlds, and on the other side there is the tyrannical power that has claimed for itself all the rights of lordship and does not obey the Lord of the worlds in the affairs of life.

﴿And Musa said, "O Pharaoh, I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds."﴾

Observe the manner of address. "O Pharaoh!" He did not address him as "My Lord," as people commonly use that word for others without realizing who the true Lord and Master is. Rather, he addressed the king by his title with great respect. By this usage he told Pharaoh that he is only Pharaoh, and at the same time he disclosed to him the truth that "إِنِّي رَسُولٌ مِّنْ رَّبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ" (*innī rasūlun min rabbi l-ʿālamīn*), "I am the representative of the Lord of the universe." The truth that Musa (peace be upon him) presented is the same truth that all the messengers before him also presented: that the sovereignty of all the worlds belongs to Allah alone. He is the one Ruler, and obedience to Him is necessary throughout life. As for those today who say that in matters of belief too there has been change and evolution, and who do not exempt the revealed religions from this principle, their view is false. For from Adam (peace be upon him) to the last of the prophets, the creed of all the messengers has remained one and the same. In it, Allah alone has been the Ruler and the one obeyed. It was never the case that there were first beliefs in many gods, then in three gods, and then the belief in one God became established. This is the case with Islam. As for jahiliyyah (ignorance), the disagreement and turmoil within it has no limit: the worship of spirits, the worship of many gods, the worship of the sun, the worship of two gods, the polytheistic worship of one God, and godless ignorance, and so on. Therefore, the revealed religions, the teachings of the messengers, and the ideas of the jahili religions cannot be judged by one and the same standard.

In short, the confrontation that took place between Musa, Pharaoh and his clique is the same situation that every prophet faced in his own age, both those who came before Musa and those who came after him. In every age, rulers thought that this call was a conspiracy against their power, just as Pharaoh thought that it was in truth a movement against his supreme authority. When someone presents the creed that Allah alone is the Lord of the worlds, its meaning is that all other sovereignties apart from the sovereignty of Allah are null and void, and all those people besides Allah who impose their own laws upon the masses are in reality tyrants (taghut). And this proclamation Musa (peace be upon him) presented with the claim that he is a messenger of Allah, the Lord of the worlds, that what he speaks he speaks from Allah, and that it is his duty from Allah to convey this call to the people.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 105:

﴿Certainly it is incumbent upon me that I should not say of Allah anything except the truth.﴾ "My position requires that, in speaking in the name of Allah, I say nothing but the truth." For the Messenger who is aware of the reality of divinity can say nothing about Allah except the truth, because he is aware of the station of Lordship and the rank of Majesty.

﴿I have come to you from your Lord with a clear proof, so let the Children of Israel go with me.﴾ "I have come to you from your Lord with a clear proof of my commission," and this is a proof that is an evident demonstration of the truth of my claim that I am from the Lord of the worlds.

Now, under the banner of this great truth, and under the doctrine of Allah's universal Lordship and all-encompassing sovereignty, Moses made the demand that Pharaoh let the Children of Israel go back to their homeland with him.

The Children of Israel were only servants and slaves of Allah. Therefore Pharaoh had no right to make them his own servants and slaves, because no human being can be the slave of two masters, nor can he be the worshipper of two gods. One who is a servant of Allah cannot be the servant of anyone else. On the one hand Pharaoh was making the Children of Israel slaves to his own desires, and on the other hand Moses was declaring that Allah alone is the Lord of the worlds. The mere declaration of Allah's Lordship negates the claim that the slavery into which Pharaoh had put the Children of Israel has any validity.

The declaration that Allah alone is the Lord and Sovereign of the worlds is in itself the charter of human freedom, and with this declaration a person is freed from the slavery, obedience and law of anyone other than Allah. He is freed from human slavery, from slavery to his own desires, from slavery to human customs, and from slavery to human law and human movements.

Therefore it cannot be that someone declares Allah's Lordship of the worlds and yet still claims allegiance to the slavery of some other than Allah. With this declaration, the sovereignty and authority of any non-Allah cannot coexist, nor can the law of anyone else coexist with it. Those people who declare that they are Muslims, and after that enforce in their lands laws made by human beings like themselves or made by themselves, and whose lands are governed by the authority of someone other than Allah, are the victims of a great misunderstanding, and they cannot be Muslims even for a moment. How can it be that they are subject to the sovereignty of a non-Allah and yet enter the religion of Allah? The law prevailing among them is not the law of the Shariah, and yet they are Muslims. The reality is that in such circumstances they remain upon the religion of their rulers and officials, but not upon the religion of Allah.

It was precisely this doctrine that led Moses to make the demand of Pharaoh that he let the Children of Israel go back with him. Read again these phrases: "O Pharaoh, I am a Messenger of the Lord of the worlds," and "So send the Children of Israel away with me." The demand for the freedom of the Children of Israel rests upon this foundation, that I am a Messenger of Allah, and the logical consequence of prophethood is that people be freed from slavery. These are inseparable matters.

Pharaoh and his clique had also fully understood the meaning of this proclamation of Allah's lordship (rububiyyah). This matter was not hidden from their eyes. They well knew that with this call their rule would certainly come to an end. A great revolution would be brought about by this call. For their rule's claim to legitimacy, this proclamation was a challenge, and it was open rebellion and opposition. But they thought that they could prove Moses to be a liar in claiming that he was a messenger of the Lord of the worlds, so they immediately demanded miracles.

﴿He said: "If you have brought a sign, then produce it, if you are among the truthful."﴾ Pharaoh said, "If you have brought a sign and are truthful in your claim, then present it."

Pharaoh adopted the path of demanding miracles because, if it were established that Moses was not a messenger of the Lord of the worlds and was making a false claim, then his call would end right there, his momentum would collapse, and those people who no longer had conviction would say whatever they wished. They would be claimants of an assertion without proof, and it would pose no danger to them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verses 107–108:

The reply of Hadrat Musa was this: ﴿So he threw down his staff, and behold, it was a serpent, plainly visible. And he drew out his hand, and behold, it was white to the beholders.﴾ Musa threw down his staff and suddenly it was a living, writhing serpent. And he drew out his hand from his pocket, and before all the onlookers it was shining.

Through the sudden manifestation of great miracles at the hands of Hadrat Musa, those people were left astonished. The staff had become a serpent, and its reality had changed in such a way that there was no longer any doubt about its being a serpent.

(Mubin) means clearly, visibly, living. In another form it is said: ﴿then behold, it was a moving serpent﴾ — so it suddenly became a serpent that moves about. Hadrat Musa was of reddish complexion. When he drew out his wheat-coloured hand, it came out gleaming like a bulb. But this whiteness was not due to disease; it was a miraculous whiteness. When he concealed the hand again in his garments, it returned to its original state, that is, it became wheat-coloured once more.

This was the proof of Hadrat Musa's claim to prophethood. His claim was that he was the messenger of the Lord of the worlds. But the question is: did Pharaoh and his clique accept these miraculous proofs? Did they acknowledge the lordship and supreme sovereignty of the Lord of the worlds? If they had done so, then what justification would remain for Pharaoh's lordship, his authority, and his crown and throne, and what justification would remain for his clique to remain in the centres and posts that Pharaoh had bestowed upon them, and of which they were the cogs of Pharaoh's government? If they had acknowledged Allah as the Lord of the worlds, his authority would in practice have ended.

If Allah is acknowledged as the Lord of the worlds, the logical requirement of this is that Allah's Shariah and law be enforced within the country, because according to the Islamic doctrine of life, obedience to the commands of anyone other than Allah is not permissible. Therefore, according to this doctrine, Pharaoh's law and his commands become ineffective: those commands which contradict the Shariah, and which are not based upon the Shariah. If Allah, the Lord of the worlds, is established as the Lord of people, then they have no other lord whose commands and laws they obey; and when people obey Pharaoh's commands and laws, they do so because they have accepted him as their lord. The lord of people is the one whose laws they obey, and these people are within the religion of that lord.

But this matter cannot be accepted so quickly. Is it possible that the tyrant (taghut) would calmly relinquish his supreme sovereignty, and that his system would be declared false and null?
