Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verses 109–110:

Pharaoh and his clique were not so foolish as to be unaware of the consequences of Musa's (peace be upon him) proclamation and demand. Rather, they clearly understood Musa's (peace be upon him) message and declared it openly, but in a manner designed to turn people's eyes away from Musa's miraculous proofs. Thus Pharaoh and his clique charged Musa with being a great sorcerer. ﴿The chiefs of Pharaoh's people said: "Indeed, this is a skilled sorcerer. He wants to expel you from your land. So what do you advise?"﴾ Upon this, the chiefs of Pharaoh's people said to one another, "Surely this man is a highly skilled sorcerer. He wants to drive you out of your land. Now, what do you say?"

They cry out that the claim Musa has made has far-reaching consequences and is extremely dangerous. The result of it will be that he wants to expel us from the land of Egypt; to snatch away rule is what it means. He is plotting against our system of government; rather, he wants to bring about a revolution. In the modern age, this is all that can be said of it.

This land belongs to Allah, and the common people are created by Allah. If the rule of Allah is established over Allah's land and over Allah's servants, then all tyrannical governments that are established contrary to the Shari'ah of Allah end of their own accord. And the authority of those who have made themselves gods of the people comes to an end of its own accord, and the authority of those whom those tyrannical rulers have made holders of office and officials also comes to an end of its own accord.

In this way, Pharaoh and his clique found out how dangerous Musa's call was. And this is the very thing that all tyrannical forces recognise well in every age.

An Arab, on the basis of his natural understanding and perception, said that the Prophet ﷺ, who calls people to (La ilaha illallah, Muhammad Rasul Allah), offers a call that kings do not like. And another Arab thinker, on the basis of his natural shrewdness, said: if you continue this call, the Arabs and non-Arabs will go to war against you. These two Arab thinkers in fact knew well the meanings of the Arabic language. They knew that the proclamation of (La ilaha illallah) is open rebellion against rulers, because they understood well the meaning of Arabic. They knew that the testimony of the sacred formula in one heart and on one land cannot coexist with a rule other than Allah's and a rule contrary to the Shari'ah. The Arabs of that time did not understand the testimony of faith in the way that today's so-called Muslims understand it. The meaning of the testimony of faith for people today is very deficient, of a low grade and of a weak grade.

In this way, Pharaoh and his clique found out how dangerous Musa's call was. And this is the very thing that all tyrannical forces recognise well in every age.

An Arab, on the basis of his natural understanding and perception, said that the Prophet ﷺ, who calls people to (La ilaha illallah, Muhammad Rasul Allah), offers a call that kings do not like. And another Arab thinker, on the basis of his natural shrewdness, said: if you continue this call, the Arabs and non-Arabs will go to war against you. These two Arab thinkers in fact knew well the meanings of the Arabic language. They knew that the proclamation of (La ilaha illallah) is open rebellion against rulers, because they understood well the meaning of Arabic. They knew that the testimony of the sacred formula in one heart and on one land cannot coexist with a rule other than Allah's and a rule contrary to the Shari'ah. The Arabs of that time did not understand the testimony of faith in the way that today's so-called Muslims understand it. The meaning of the testimony of faith for people today is very deficient, of a low grade and of a weak grade.

Now negotiations began between Pharaoh and his clique. At that time there were many soothsayers and sorcerers in Egypt, and the soothsayers themselves also practised sorcery. In all idolatrous religions, sorcery forms a part of religion; accordingly, the soothsayers and attendants of those religions also practised sorcery. Seeing this situation, the modern experts of religions today draw the conclusion that there was a period when religion began with sorcery. And the more hardened atheists engage in idle talk that just as sorcery has come to be considered entirely a religion, in the same way every religion will also come to an end, and just as science has ended the age of sorcery, so too a time will come when religion will also come to an end. In any case, this is their folly, in which they are afflicted under the banner of science.

Pharaoh's advisors gave him the counsel that he should grant time to Moses and his brother, and summon great sorcerers from the far corners of his state, so that they might contest with Moses (peace be upon him) in sorcery. (Allah forbid.)

Despite his well-known Pharaonic arrogance, Pharaoh did not display rebelliousness in the matter of Moses (peace be upon him), and his conduct was more reasonable than the Pharaohs after the twentieth century. Today's Pharaohs confront the Islamic call with oppression, imprisonment and false methods.

Qur'an now leaves the intervening details and presents another scene: how Pharaoh's group gathered the people, and whom they gathered. Indeed, as the curtain rises, the magicians appear before us. This is a particularly effective and beautiful style of narration in the Qur'an's accounts of past events. It appears as though one scene is folded up and another brought forward.

﴿And the magicians came to Pharaoh. They said, "Surely there will be a reward for us if we are the victors." He said, "Yes, and you will certainly be among those brought near."﴾

So the magicians came to Pharaoh. They said, "If we remain victorious, shall we surely receive a reward for it?" Pharaoh replied, "Yes, and you will be among those brought near to my court."

These men were professional magicians, and likewise professional soothsayers, and their aim in both occupations was to earn money. In every age, professional religious scholars have considered it their duty to serve tyrannical powers and oppressive kings. Moreover, whenever the system of God's sovereignty has been suspended in the world, and the worship of God alone has ended, a taghut (tyrannical) system has been established in its place. When a taghut system is established, such rulers have needed professional religious people, and these rulers have paid those professionals for their profession, while those professionals have accepted this taghut system on religious grounds. Thus a mutual agreement has existed between the two, and taghut rulers have both paid these professional religious people money and made them close companions.

Pharaoh gave assurance that he would pay them wages for this task and that, in addition, they would be among his close favourites. Thus Pharaoh induced them to oppose Musa alone, with utmost vigour and sustained effort. But what did they know? The matter was not so simple that they could defeat Prophet Musa through glib talk or cunning. Here they were dealing with God, God's Messenger, divine miracles and extraordinary events, and realities and facts; it was not mere sleight of hand or imaginary sorcery.

The sorcerers were satisfied regarding the reward, and out of desire for a place among Pharaoh's close companions their heads were raised high, and they became ready for the contest. Now they turn towards Musa (peace be upon him) and challenge him, and as a result they reach that lofty station which Allah had decreed for them, and which they had never even imagined, and they were deemed worthy of a reward they had not expected.

﴿They said: "O Musa! Either you throw first, or we will be the ones to throw."﴾ Then they said to Musa (peace be upon him): Will you throw, or shall we throw? Musa replied: You throw first.

They left the choice to Musa: if you wish, throw your staff first, or we will throw. This shows that they were challenging with great confidence. They were fully certain of their success and trusted in their craft. In contrast, Musa was also extremely confident, and he answered carelessly: "You throw." He replied with a single word, which shows that he gave no importance to their trickery. Within the self of Musa there was complete certainty and tranquility. These matters and meanings are made apparent through the use of words in accordance with the manner of speech of the Noble Qur'an.

Just as Musa (peace be upon him) was confronted with a sudden situation, the context and manner of expression are such that every reader is suddenly confronted with a frightening situation. Musa (peace be upon him) was answering with great nonchalance, but suddenly he too was faced with an extremely terrifying and awe-inspiring situation, one which, on seeing it, makes a person fearful and makes him tremble.

﴿He said: "Throw."﴾ So when they threw, they bewitched the eyes of the people, terrified them, and produced a great magic. They threw down their staffs and ropes, and they bewitched the sight of the people and filled their hearts with awe, and they produced a truly great magic.

For us it is sufficient that the Qur'an itself also used the phrase "great magic" (siḥr ʿaẓīm) for the art of these people, and from this we can well understand how great their magic was. They bewitched the eyes of the people and filled the hearts of the people with awe, and an atmosphere of fear descended upon the environment.

Through the use of the word istarhabū (they struck terror), a picture of the atmosphere comes before us: namely, they created in the people a sense of being frightened, so that they were compelled to fear. And in Surah Ṭā-Hā it is also mentioned that Musa too became fearful within himself. Through all these words, one is convinced of the frightening sorcery of those people.

The Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verses 117–119:

But now another surprise comes forward. A great event takes place. Pharaoh, his clique and the magicians are all left astonished. All the people are struck dumb, and a great and countless silence falls over that vast arena upon all who witnessed this mighty act of sorcery.

﴿And We revealed to Musa: "Throw down your staff," and behold, it swallowed up what they were falsely fabricating. Thus the truth was established, and what they had been doing was proved void. So they were defeated there and then, and they returned humiliated.﴾

We signaled to Musa: throw down your staff. The moment it was thrown, in the twinkling of an eye it swallowed up that false illusion of theirs. Thus what was true proved true, and what they had constructed was rendered void. Pharaoh and his companions were defeated in the contest, and instead of being victorious, they turned back disgraced.

Falsehood always swells up, dazzles the eyes, overawes hearts, and most people begin to think that falsehood will remain dominant. It will sweep everything away like a flood and reduce all things to nothing. But as soon as it meets a serious, determined and firm truth, the air leaves it like a balloon, and it sinks like a bubble, shrinks like a porcupine, and becomes like a flame of grass that is extinguished within a minute. Now the scale of truth becomes heavy. Its foundations become firm and its roots become deep. The manner of expression the Qur'an has adopted here contains a reflection of this meaning. It gives the impression that truth possesses a great and heavy existence, its blow falls with great force, it remains established permanently, all other matters apart from truth dissolve into the air, and the threads and fabric of falsehood scatter. Truth overcomes falsehood and its followers, and after flourishing greatly and dazzling the eyes, this falsehood shrinks very quickly.

﴿So they were defeated there and then, and they returned humiliated.﴾ Pharaoh and his companions were defeated in the contest, and instead of being victorious, they turned back disgraced. But this surprise has not yet ended.

The commentary sits within a longer discussion, so I translate it as it stands.

In this scene, one unexpected view follows another. Now a great scene suddenly appears before our eyes. ﴿And the magicians were thrown down prostrate.﴾ ﴿They said, "We believe in the Lord of the worlds,﴾ ﴿the Lord of Moses and Aaron."﴾ The state of the magicians was such that it was as though something from within had cast them down in prostration. They said: we have accepted the Lord of the worlds, the Lord whom Moses and Aaron accept.

This is the awe and majesty of truth in the human conscience. The human consciousness is suddenly illuminated, and when a heart becomes ready to accept the truth, a lamp of truth is suddenly kindled within it, and it is filled with certainty. These magicians were well acquainted with the limits and the nature of their craft, and had Moses been a magician, they would have recognised him far sooner than others. The miracle that appeared at the hands of Moses lay beyond the domain of human power and of magic. A skilled craftsman quickly accepts the reality about his own craft, provided that reality is revealed to him, because the master of a craft is close to its reality, and his knowledge exceeds that of those who possess only superficial information. This is why the magicians abandoned the posture of challenge and defiance and became the very picture of submission and acceptance, because they were finding certainty within their hearts, and this reality had become part of their consciousness.

But no tyrannical power can understand how the human heart is filled with light, or how a person receives this expansion of breast in faith, or how the warmth of certainty arises in the human heart. Since these tyrannical forces keep people enslaved for long periods, they come to imagine that they have the power to bend affairs to their will and can change the hearts and minds of people. Yet the human heart lies between the fingers of the Most Merciful; He turns it however He wills. The announcement of defeat and the declaration of faith by the magicians were unimaginable and astonishing to Pharaoh, because there was not even a trace of faith in their hearts, and he had no knowledge of any working of faith in their consciences. Then this sudden declaration of faith was so dangerous to him that his rule was thrown into jeopardy; his feet had begun to slip. The magicians were not merely magicians, but were the priests, scholars and preachers of the places of worship of that time. When all the religious leaders of a country come to faith, it is no longer possible for the government to remain in its place, especially in circumstances of contest where they have come onto the field to confront it. In such circumstances, when the tyrannical system itself is in danger, the people of tyranny are ready to do anything at all.

Take note of the manner of this. You believed in him before I gave you permission. It is as if it were their legal duty to seek his permission to accept faith, and that in this matter they are not free to act on their own. Or the meaning is that their conscience and intuition should not stir, and that they are not free even in matters of their own awareness. If some light falls upon their hearts and insight, they should seek refuge and ask Pharaoh about this matter too. If some belief or conviction settles in their hearts, they are not permitted to act on it without Pharaoh's leave. In short, it is their duty to keep themselves away from every kind of new light.

But every tyrannical power is ignorant and dull, and alongside this, every tyrannical power is arrogant, proud and extremist. Moreover, every tyrannical power is extremely sensitive about its authority; it sees its rule endangered by such matters, and the tyrannical throne and authority appear to it to be shaking.

﴿Indeed, this is a plot that you have hatched in the city, to drive its people out of it.﴾ Surely it was a secret conspiracy that you people hatched in this seat of government, in order to dispossess its rulers of power. Well, now you will soon come to know its consequence.

And in another verse (﴿Indeed, he is your chief who taught you magic﴾). This is your great one who taught you sorcery. In any case, this matter is entirely clear. The call of Moses was a call to the Lord of the worlds, and every call that is made to the Lord of the worlds is extremely frightening. Wherever the call to the Lord of the worlds spreads, the tyrannical system does not remain at all. This is because a tyrannical system is founded precisely on the principle that in it the authority and law of other human beings are enforced instead of the authority and law of the Lord of the worlds, and humans act as lords on earth. They enslave people and make whatever laws they wish for them. In fact, these are two distinct systems of life which cannot possibly be combined in one place; rather, they are two separate religions and they have two separate lords. Pharaoh knew this reality well, and his assembly also knew it well. That is why, as a result of the call of Moses, the authority of Pharaoh was shaken, and now, when the sorcerers all fell down in prostration and declared that they had accepted the call of the Lord of the worlds, and that they believed in the Lord of Moses and Aaron, these sorcerers were the religious leaders and priests of that time, and in religious terms they had given Pharaoh the station of Lord of mankind. That is why Pharaoh threatened them with such brutal and deterrent punishment.

The Pharaoh's Terror, Torture and Harsh, Exemplary Punishment

Harshness, torture and severe, deterrent punishment: these are the means that every tyrannical (taghuti) system brings to bear against the truth. This is because the truth can never be confronted with argument and reasoning; instruments of violence are always used against the truth.

But when the human soul attains elevation of faith and the reality of faith takes firm root within it, it stands up against the great powers of this earth. It pays no heed to the revenge of the rebellious and the tyrants, and in the life of such individuals the way of life (nazariyah-i-hayat) gains superiority over worldly life, and this transient life appears insignificant in comparison with the eternal life to come. When the human soul reaches this station, it does not reflect on what it is, what it should abandon, what it is, what it will gain and what it will lose, or what difficulties it will have to create on this path, or what hardships it will have to bear. Because its goal shines brightly on the distant horizon, its gaze becomes lofty, and it no longer even looks down at the thorns on the path beneath it.

This is the person of true faith: neither fearful, nor do his feet waver; he neither bows down nor is he a slave. He is content with his end and has become pleased with this path. He is certain that he is returning to the Lord of the worlds, and he cannot now abandon this path.

﴿They said: Indeed, to our Lord we are returning.﴾ They replied: Whatever happens, our return is to our Lord alone.

The person who understands the nature of the battle between himself and the tyrannical system, and that this battle is an ideological battle, does not compromise, does not resort to battlefield tactics, and does not take the path of forgiveness and pardon, especially against an enemy whose aim is that the believers should give up their faith and their ideology.

﴿And you take revenge on us for nothing except that we believed in the signs of our Lord when they came to us.﴾ So the thing for which you wish to take revenge on us is nothing other than that when the signs of our Lord came before us, we accepted them.

The person who knows against whom he is arrayed, and against whom he is advancing, does not then ask his enemy for peace and safety. He asks only of his Lord, and asks that he be granted patience and steadfastness in this trial, and that he remain faithful to Islam.

﴿Our Lord, pour upon us patience, and cause us to die as Muslims.﴾ O Lord, pour upon us the bounty of patience, and take us from this world in a state of submission to Your command.

Now rebellion becomes powerless before faith; it meets a mind of understanding and a mountain of certainty. The mentality of rebellion and oppression is that those who adopt it think that just as they have dominion and control over the human body, so they have dominion over people's hearts and minds. And just as they command people's bodies, so they control people's minds. But it is inconceivable to them that any heart should disobey them, though this does happen, because hearts are in the hand of Allah. When a heart is connected to Allah and stands firm against rebellion, that rebellion becomes powerless. When hearts belong to Allah and their connection is with Allah, even the greatest power becomes powerless. Before the strength of faith, great rulers and tyrants are rendered helpless.

This is a decisive stance in human history. On one side are Pharaoh, his tyrannical system and his followers; on the other side are the powerless believing sorcerers, who were once sorcerers. Now they hold a historic stance. Their doctrine of life has prevailed over life and has gained superiority. Human resolve has triumphed over physical pain and suffering. Man has overcome Satan.

Indeed, this is a clear-cut stance in human history. Through this stance a true declaration of freedom has been made. What is the nature of freedom? Freedom is that a person rises with his creed and his convictions and stands firm against tyrants and rebels. And he regards as worthless that material power which controls human bodies but cannot reach the soul and convictions of a person; and when material powers become unable to subdue hearts, then from that point the birth of true liberty and freedom begins, and remember that this birth takes place in free hearts.

This is a clear-cut stance, and throughout human history it plainly shows that material power is helpless and powerless. Consider that these sorcerers, at first, were seeking only a modest reward from Pharaoh, and then they hoped to be seated in his court and to be granted nearness to the king. This insignificant group, after faith, now displays dignity before Pharaoh and stands ready to face the gallows and the rope. Yet materially, their surroundings remain in the same state as before, except that a small star has received hidden light, and now this small star, or rather this tiny particle, has entered a firm tower and a mortal individual has reached an eternal and everlasting power. A needle has been placed upon the heart of the believer; now the believer's heart receives the effects of divine power, natural sounds come from his conscience, and lights fall upon human insight. This sensation makes the heart of the believer feel it, while nothing changes in the material world. Yet a person rises above the material world and goes into a new world of which he could not previously even think.

Now the threat takes its course and intimidation keeps searching, but faith has already gone far along its path. It does not look backward; it has no hesitation, and it does not lose its way.

When the scene proceeds this far, the curtain falls and no further details are given, because here the beauty of this scene reaches its height, one point is completed, and an artistic beauty also reaches its perfection. The artistic perfection of the Qur'an is touching its limits here as well, and the reader's intuition also grasps the psychological purposes of the narrative, in complete harmony and within the particular style of expression of the Holy Qur'an. (See my book al-Tasweer al-Fanni.)

In the shadow of the Qur'an, standing before this engaging scene, we should pause and reflect a little.

Pharaoh and his companions regarded the believing of the sorcerers, and their acceptance of faith in the Lord of Musa and Harun, as a conspiracy against their system of government, and expressed that their rule and authority were in danger. This is because the principle on which the system of faith is established is contrary to the foundational principle of the Pharaonic system. We have already explained this matter earlier; here it is brought again for repetition and emphasis: in one heart, one country, or one system it cannot be that Allah is the Lord of the worlds and at the same time some human being is also the lord of people, with his laws prevalent and enforced among the people, because the religion of Allah is a complete system, and alongside it the Pharaonic religion is also a complete religion.

When the light of faith was kindled in the hearts of the sorcerers and they grasped the reality of faith and disbelief, they clearly understood that between them and Pharaoh there was such an ideological and principled difference, and that Pharaoh, who threatened retaliation, was threatening only because we had believed and had acknowledged Allah as the Lord of the worlds. And believing in this manner is a challenge to Pharaoh's system of government. Likewise, it is also a challenge to the higher structure and constitutional order of Pharaoh's rule. That is, the system of lordship of Pharaoh, which was founded on idolatrous conceptions, was uprooted. Whoever calls to the Lord of the worlds, the One without partner, should understand this reality well, because it is through this realisation that all the calamities and hardships became bearable for the people of faith. Now they stood ready for the gallows and the rope, because they had professed faith, and they knew that their religion and Pharaoh's religion were separate, since Pharaoh, by enslaving people and enforcing his own law, had denied the lordship of Allah over the worlds; therefore Pharaoh is a disbeliever. In this way every caller should clearly understand that he is calling to faith, and that those who obstruct his path are disbelievers and advocates of the Pharaonic system. And this enmity is purely for the sake of Allah (al-Bughd fi Allah). Behind it there is no other motive except the motive of faith.

After this, in this scene we see that before faith the whole of life and its comforts have no value. Before resolve and determination, mountains of grief and sorrow also crumble to pieces. Human strength triumphs over the satanic. This is an extremely uplifting and astonishing scene. The truth is that the beauty of this scene cannot be fully described. Read the texts of the Qur'an itself.

Now let us study this story further. The curtain rises, and before our eyes is another, fresh and striking scene. In it we see the parliament of disbelief. There is consultation and secret deliberation, and people are stirring one another up toward some harsh measure. The notables of wealth, humiliated by their open defeat in the first, open contest, appear enraged. For them it is unbearable that Musa and Harun should succeed and prevail in this way, and that the people who have believed should walk along with them at their ease. Yet among those who believed in Musa were a few weak people, who were constantly afraid of Pharaoh lest he put them to trial, as the Qur'an has stated explicitly in other places.

This parliament is thinking about taking severe action. These people are inciting Pharaoh against Musa and frightening him that if no strong action is taken against him, the consequences will be dangerous. The government's authority will be lost; dangerous new ideas will spread; people will regard Allah, the Lord of the worlds, rather than Pharaoh, as their Lord. So he is prepared, and flames of fire seem to issue from his mouth. He decides to take severe action against these people, to use force, and after moral defeat to employ the full measure of material power. The possessors of material power always do exactly this.

﴿And the chiefs of Pharaoh's people said, "Will you leave Musa and his people to spread corruption in the land and to abandon you and your gods?" He said, "We will kill their sons and spare their women, and we are certainly dominant over them."﴾

Pharaoh's claim was not that he was the deity and creator of this universe, or that he runs it, or that he has power over its natural order. Rather, he regarded himself as a lord and deity over his weak subjects, in the sense that he was the ruler and lawgiver, that his command and will were law, that they were and ought to be obeyed, and that this is also the claim of all rulers and kings, that their law prevails and affairs are settled by their command. This is the meaning of lordship (rububiyyah) linguistically. The people of Egypt did not serve Pharaoh in the sense that they prayed Pharaoh's prayers or fasted Pharaoh's fasts; rather, they had their own deities, just as Pharaoh had made deities for himself, and these people rendered worship to those deities. This reality is also shown by the words of the courtiers:

﴿and they abandon you and your gods﴾, and this reality is also established by the Pharaonic history of Egypt, that Pharaoh had a deity. Therefore Pharaoh was their lord and deity in the sense that these people were bound by his commands and prohibitions, and could neither disobey any of his orders nor violate any of his laws. And this is the lexical, real and technical meaning of worship; indeed, it is the true meaning: whoever obeys a law laid down by a human being is in effect worshipping him. The Prophet (ﷺ) also explained it this way. Regarding the explanation of "They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah," the Companion 'Adi ibn Hatim asked the Prophet (ﷺ) whether these people did not in fact worship anyone other than Allah. The Prophet (ﷺ) replied that these rabbis and monks made lawful for them what was unlawful and unlawful what was lawful, and they obeyed them in this; this is their worship of them. (Tirmidhi)

As for Pharaoh's statement, "I do not know of any god for you other than myself" (ما علمت لكم من إله غيري), the Qur'an itself has explained it, by reporting Pharaoh's words: "O people, is not the kingdom of Egypt mine, and do these rivers not flow beneath me? Do you not see? Am I not better than this one who is despised and can scarcely express himself clearly? Why have bracelets of gold not been bestowed upon him, or why have angels not come with him in procession?" (Al-Zukhruf 43:51–53). It is evident that in this he was comparing himself with Musa: he has bracelets and wears ornaments, that is, he is king and possessor of splendour and adornment, while Musa lacks this quality. Therefore the meaning of his words is that there is no ruler for you other than me; I am the ruler, I run this realm as I wish, and people cannot refuse my word; and in this sense sovereignty is synonymous with divinity. Indeed, the very meaning of divinity is this: a deity is precisely one who makes law for people, whether or not he claims divinity.

In light of this interpretation we can well understand the words of Pharaoh's chiefs: ﴿And the chiefs of Pharaoh's people said, "Will you leave Musa and his people to spread corruption in the land and to abandon you and your gods?"﴾

From their point of view, corruption on earth means that a person calls people to the lordship and sovereignty of Allah alone, because when someone accepts Allah, the Lord of the worlds, as deity and ruler, this automatically negates all other systems and rulers, since the Pharaonic system of rule rests on a principle other than Allah. In other words, that system rests on the lordship of Pharaoh, and this man is a proponent of the lordship of Allah. Therefore everyone is now, in the eyes of the Pharaonists, a corrupter on earth; he is a rebel and a revolutionary, seeking to overturn the established conditions of the country and to create new conditions to replace the present stable order, in which lordship and sovereignty belong to Allah alone and no human being has such rights. Hence the charge was laid against them that they are corrupters on earth and wish to abandon the worship of Pharaoh and his deities.

In truth, Pharaoh derived all his rights from the religion whose adherent he was. He believed that he was the beloved son of these deities, and the relationship of father and son which he advocated was not a physical or natural relationship, for people knew that Pharaoh had been born of parents who were Egyptians and human beings. This was a symbolic and allegorical sonship through which he obtained all the rights he had reserved for himself. When Musa and his people began the direct worship of the Lord of the worlds and abandoned the Pharaonic deities whom the Egyptians worshipped, then by this act the very ideological foundation was destroyed on which Pharaoh's kingdom had been built. Moreover, he gave his people no standing in his system of government, and those people, who obeyed him, were outside the religion of Allah and were defiant. Elsewhere it is said: ﴿So he made his people feeble-minded, and they obeyed him. Indeed, they were a defiant people﴾ (Az-Zukhruf 43:54). This is the correct explanation of history. If Pharaoh's people had not been a lightweight people, accustomed to immorality and wickedness, they would never have obeyed Pharaoh. A person who believes in Allah cannot be made light of by the tyrant, nor can any believer obey the tyrant, provided the believer knows that the matter is against the Shariah. This is why Musa's (peace be upon him) summons to Pharaoh and all the people to the Lord of the worlds, then his defeat of the sorcerers in the contest, their faith, and afterwards the people of Musa's believing in the Lord of the worlds and worshipping the one Lord, were all matters extremely dangerous to Pharaoh's system of government. Wherever there is a system in which one human being is the slave and subject of another, and within such a system someone begins to call people to the worship and obedience of the Lord of the worlds alone, this is a challenge to that system. Likewise, if someone calls to the testimony that there is no god but Allah, and this call is to the true meaning of that word, that people enter fully into Islam, and not to the partial performance of the rites of worship before Allah, then this call is a challenge to any existing system of disbelief.

For this reason, Pharaoh, in these circumstances, announced in harsh words that he would take severe measures to confront this danger, because his entire system of government was under threat.

﴿He said, "We will kill their sons and spare their women, and we are certainly dominant over them."﴾

In the period of Musa's birth too, this policy of genocide against the Children of Israel had been adopted. Pharaoh and his system of government were killing their sons. The Qur'an gives the details in Surah al-Qasas:

﴿Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and made its people into factions, oppressing a group among them, slaughtering their sons and keeping their women alive. Indeed, he was among the corrupters﴾ (Al-Qasas 28:4). That is, Pharaoh acted arrogantly in the land and divided its inhabitants into groups. Among them he humiliated one group, killing their sons and letting their daughters live; in truth he was among the corrupters.

This defiance remains in every age and in every place. Even today it adopts these same means, and centuries ago too these were its means.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 128:

Now the curtain falls again. Pharaoh and his nobles and courtiers are left in their scheming, their threats and their harsh fury, and now another particular scene of this story comes into view. It appears that Pharaoh has begun acts of persecution. In this scene Moses appears among his people. He speaks to his people with the heart of a Prophet and in the tongue of a Prophet, and from his words it is evident that he has a complete recognition of his Lord. He also knows well the continuing practice (sunnat jariyah) of the Lord, and he knows that no one can influence the plan of Allah or the decrees of His destiny. He advises them that they should bear these difficulties with patience, that they should be steadfast, and that they should seek help and support from Allah in enduring these hardships. He informs them of the true reality of this universe: that the earth belongs to Allah, that He grants it as an inheritance to whomsoever He wills, and that the final outcome belongs to those who fear no one but Allah, who fear only Allah. And when these people complain that, "O Moses, we were afflicted before you came and we are still afflicted after you have come, and these hardships show no sign of ending," he consoles them with these words: it may be that Allah will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the land, but then a period of trial for you will also begin.

Quran: "Moses said to his people, 'Seek help in Allah and be patient. Indeed the earth belongs to Allah; He causes whomever He wills of His servants to inherit it, and the good outcome is for the righteous.' They said, 'We were harmed before you came to us and after you came to us.' He said, 'It may be that your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the land, and then He will observe how you act.'"

The insight of the Prophet sees how the powers of Allah exercise control over this universe, how great the reality and power of Allah is, how the Divine practice (sunnah Ilahiyyah) operates continuously in this universe, and what privileges Allah has placed in it for those who bear hardships in the way of Allah.

For those who call to the Lord of the worlds, there is only one refuge, and it is a secure, protected and trustworthy refuge. They have only one Protector and Master, who is mighty and invincible. Therefore such people should show patience and perseverance until their Master issues His commands of victory and success for them. They should not be hasty in this matter, because a person does not know what is hidden for him in the unseen, and where his good lies.

This earth belongs to Allah. Pharaoh and his people are travellers here, and after their departure it is Allah's affair to bring whichever people He wills to this land and make them its inheritors. He does this in accordance with His continuing practices (sunan jariyah). Therefore those who call to the Lord of the worlds do not take into account that the tyrannical power they confront appears to be very firmly established on this land, and that there is no shaking in its foundations. This is because the owner of this land is Allah, and at a suitable time He takes authority from someone and hands it over to another of His servants.

The truth is that the final good outcome always belongs to the righteous, whether it becomes manifest after a long period or appears quickly. Therefore those who call to the Lord of the worlds should remove from their hearts every doubt about their final end, and should not suppose that those people of falsehood who now move about freely on this earth will remain in this condition forever.

This was the far-seeing insight of the Prophet, which was looking far ahead at the events occurring in this universe. But the Children of Israel, after all, were the Children of Israel.

(They said, "We were harmed before you came to us, and after you came to us.")

The words of these people carry a particular frame of mind; in them is a definite expression of their despair. They say that persecution was being inflicted upon us before you came, and it continues even after your coming. There is no change in its continuity. It does not appear to be coming to an end.

But the Prophet remains steadfast on his path and course. He advises them to remain occupied in the remembrance of Allah and to remain hopeful. The Prophet also gives them an indication that the enemy will surely be destroyed and that you will surely be granted the station of khilafah (vicegerency) on earth. But the Prophet remains steadfast on his path and course. He advises them to remain occupied in the remembrance of Allah and to remain hopeful. The Prophet also gives them an indication that the enemy will surely be destroyed and that you will surely be granted the station of khilafah (vicegerency) on earth, but the one who is granted this station in fact falls into a great trial.

(He said, "It may be that your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the land, and then see how you act.") He answered: "The time is near when your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you vicegerents in the land, and then see how you act."

Moses, with the mind, insight and perception of prophethood, is looking; he is seeing the Divine Sunnah (way) unfold step by step. This Sunnah, as promised, decides in favour of the steadfast, and likewise its decisions for those who deny the truth come at their appointed time. It is clear to him that the forces of tyranny are destined to be ruined and destroyed, and that the steadfast and the strivers will take their place. Therefore he moves his people forward on the path of perseverance so that the Divine Sunnah may decide in their favour. From the very beginning he knew that making the Children of Israel inheritors of the earth is a trial for them. It is not that they are Allah's beloved and favourites, as some Children of Israel assume about themselves, thinking that they will not be held accountable for their sins; for this world was not created without purpose, nor is it eternal, but rather the rise of every nation here is for the benefit of mankind.

(So that He may see how you act.) So that He may see how you act? Allah knows a thing even before it occurs. However, Allah does not punish anyone for a crime before he commits it; He does not punish until that matter actually happens from them, which He knew beforehand in His capacity as the Knower of the unseen.

Now the narrative leaves Musa and his people. The curtain falls on that scene, and another scene comes into view. In this scene we see Pharaoh and his people. Pharaoh is seen oppressing his own people with extreme cruelty, and the promise that Musa made to his people, and for which they were hoping, comes true. Now every statement of the Messenger is confirmed, because this story has been brought here for exactly that purpose.

This scene begins in very ordinary circumstances, and afterwards the atmosphere gradually grows harsher and faster, and before the curtain falls we see a terrifying storm in the sky. Everything is destroyed and laid waste. The face of the earth is cleared. Now no tyrant or rebel remains here, and no trace is seen of the associates and supporters of the tyranny. And we come to know that the Children of Israel endured their hardships with patience, and Allah gave them a good reward. Pharaoh and his party took the path of wickedness and debauchery and committed oppression, and they too reached a fitting end for their deeds. Allah's promise was fulfilled, and His warning also showed its effect, and those who denied the truth were treated in accordance with the Sunnah of Allah. Allah afflicted them with extremely difficult conditions. Let us study this in some detail.

﴿And We certainly seized the people of Pharaoh with years of drought and shortage of fruits, so that perhaps they would take heed.﴾

This was the first warning from Allah to them. The land was seized by drought, all kinds of crops were lost, and produce came to an end. The word "sinin" (years of drought) in Arabic terminology is used for dry years, famine, and severity. Famine in a green and flourishing land like Egypt was regarded as a punishment from Allah. Fear and dread arose among the people because of it, and in distress they would turn their attention toward the Higher World. But since the tyrannical powers and their officials keep people heedless, keep them away from religion, and people obey them, they do not think along the line that this is a punishment from Allah which has come upon them in the form of drought and so on. Because of the tyrannical powers, such heedlessness and carelessness arise among the people that they forget the warnings of Allah and do not acknowledge that there is a deep connection between faith, spiritual values and natural conditions. And the eye of the Knower of the Unseen is upon both the moral life of people and their natural conditions. Under a tyrannical system people's minds become so dull that they cannot see anything beyond what is sensed, and they descend to the level of animals, because animals too can perceive only what is sensed. If such people see some events which they cannot explain in natural terms, they still hand these significant events over to chance and coincidence. And they fail to understand the Sunnah of Allah and the law of nature working behind these events, which is operating throughout this universe.

(When, in the era of Khrushchev, Russia was afflicted by drought and all agricultural produce was lost, he said that nature was going against us. Yet he was a believer in atheistic communism and did not accept any unseen power. In short, these people forcibly blind themselves and do not want to see the hand of divine power. The question is: what is that nature which is going against them? It is none other than the Lord, Exalted is He.)

In short, Allah tried to warn the people of Pharaoh, although they were disbelievers, debauched and wicked. The superstitions of idol-worship had altered their nature, and they had no connection with the law of nature operating in this universe, according to which human life too moves on. For only those who have been granted true faith and the light of faith can truly comprehend this law of nature. It is only the believers who can perceive that this universe was not created in vain, nor will it remain purposeless forever, but true laws of Allah dominate over it. This is genuine scientific thinking. This thinking does not deny the Unseen knowledge of Allah, because there is no contradiction between true knowledge and science and knowledge of the Unseen. For behind both the universe and human life, the Being of Allah is at work, who "does whatever He wills" (fa'al lima yurid), and the demand of the Divine Being is that servants believe, and that Allah entrust them with the office of vicegerency on the earth. And He, who has always prescribed for mankind laws that have remained in harmony with these laws of nature and the ordinances of creation, has created a balance in this universe between human life and moral life.

Pharaoh and his associates and supporters could not understand that there is a connection between their disbelief, wickedness, their oppression of the family of Musa, and the punishment of drought. Especially in Egypt, where freshness, greenery and spring always prevail, and there is abundance and plenty of all kinds of fruits and agricultural produce. They could not understand that these difficulties were descending upon them because of their wickedness and debauchery.

In short, the people of Pharaoh in Egypt, even on seeing the deadly signs of great drought, were not alerted, and they kept their eyes closed. Their thinking was that whenever good days came upon them, they would say that this was their right and that they deserved it; but when drought and difficulties confronted them, they would say that all this was happening because of Musa. Because of the companions of Musa these difficulties were coming upon them.

When human nature deviates from the straight path, it fails to perceive that this universe is being run by the hand of divine power. Such people do not see Allah's system of qada' and qadar (divine decree and measure), under which all things come into being and all events take place. When this nature becomes corrupted to such a degree, it can no longer comprehend the laws of nature (nawamis-e-qudrat) present in this universe, even though these laws continuously operate here. Such people then interpret and explain the events of the universe as isolated incidents. They do not consider that any given event has any connection with a universal principle. Such people wander through barren valleys carrying bundles of superstitions. They do not agree upon any principle, nor do they adhere to any one path or custom; their thinking is not logical. People like Khrushchev also say that "nature" is acting against us. The question is: how is matter acting against them? But he does not even believe in (fa'al lima yurid) [the One who does whatever He wills]. It is astonishing that some people, while denying the fundamentals of religion and denying God and God's unseen power, still call themselves Muslims.

Pharaoh and his companions used to interpret the events occurring in the world in such a way that if the conditions of the world were good, they would say, "This is simply our own good performance, and we deserve it." And if conditions were bad, they would say that this has happened because of Musa (Moses) and his companions, meaning that they took omens (tiyarah) from them.

The question is: what is bad omen (tiyarah)? The word used here for it is tatayyur (watiyarah). Its literal meaning is the flying of a bird. The people of ignorance (jahiliyyah) could not understand that Allah's established way (sunnat Allah) operates in this universe, and that events occur here in accordance with certain principles of divine power. Looking at outward circumstances and under the influence of idol worship, they held firmly to certain strange superstitions. If a person intended to do some task, he would go near a bird's nest and make the bird fly out of it. If the bird flew from his right side, they would call it "sanih" (auspicious), and they would be pleased and proceed with the task. If the bird flew from his left side, they would call it "barih" (inauspicious), and considering it a bad omen, they would refrain from that task. Islam nullified this superstitious thinking and in its place gave a scientific approach to reflection and consideration, and left the outcomes to Allah's enduring sunan (established laws), so that whatever results emerge will appear in accordance with Allah's system of qada' and qadar. Islam left all matters to a scientific and intellectual approach, in which importance was given to a person's intention, his niyyah, his movement, and his struggle. And over the sphere of Allah's qada' and qadar, Allah's will (mashiyyah) encompasses everything.

(Alā innamā ṭāʾiruhum ʿinda Allāh wa-lākinna aktharahum lā yaʿlamūn) "Indeed, their omen is with Allah, but most of them do not know."

The single cause of the events that occur in this world is that they take place by Allah's command, and good things reach them from Allah's presence, which is a trial for them; and afflictions also come to them from Allah, and these too are for trial. "Wa-nabluukum bil-sharri wal-khayri fitnatan wa-ilaynā turjaʿūn" — "And We test you with evil and with good as a trial, and to Us you will be returned." Hardships that befall a person are the consequence of his own deeds; but most people do not understand this, and most of them do not even believe in divine decree at all. They express their views using the terminology of "scientific thinking," and some call it "non-cooperation of nature," as the communists do for example. But all these people are ignorant of the truth and unaware of it.

Let us move on: Pharaoh and his chieftains continue in their arrogance. Wounded in their self-esteem, they are in a great rage, and out of anger and obstinacy they say:

﴿And they said, "Whatever sign you bring us to enchant us with it, we will never be believers in you."﴾

They said to Moses, "Whatever sign you bring us to bewitch us with, we are not going to believe you."

This is the kind of animal-like willfulness that cannot be trained, on which admonition has no effect, and which cannot be refuted by any proof. It knows neither reflection nor contemplation, and before even hearing the arguments it rejects the matter; it blocks the very path of proof. This is the psychological condition into which every person falls who holds power in an oppressive manner and for his own interests, and whom argument has already defeated, indeed whom proof and evidence are pursuing, yet who, because of his interests, cannot face the truth, proof and evidence. When such conditions prevail, then the Absolute Almighty brings into action His special resources.

This was the drama of "trial." The meaning of the consecutive signs is that they were clearly showing the signs plainly. One trial after another was coming, and each preceding one was the logical result of the one that came next.

The Qur'an has gathered all these signs in one place, although these calamities came upon them one after another.

When every affliction came upon them, they would, under the pressure of their difficulties, bow before Moses and promise that if he prayed to God and they were delivered from it, they would certainly let the Children of Israel go with him. But whenever the punishment was lifted, their conduct would remain the same.

Each time they broke their word, and again they returned to the same state, which was a respite for them, and for which God had set an appointed time.

The context of the discourse brings all these signs together in one place, as though they all appeared at once. After Allah removed these difficulties, the Pharaohites broke their covenant, and only one breach is mentioned. This style was chosen because, whenever a sign came and then went away, they did not keep their promise again. This manner of expression is one of the styles of the Quran. Since the events were all of the same kind, their beginning is indicated in a single place, as though all these experiences came to one heart, and that heart had become so hard that no experience found its way into it, and no one took a lesson from it.

The Quran does not mention the detailed circumstances in which these signs came, and no raised (marfu') hadith mentions them either. In keeping with the approach adopted in Fi Zilal al-Quran, we leave them here in general terms, because the explanation of the Quran must come either from the Quran itself or from the established Sunnah.

We have adopted this approach to avoid Isra'iliyyat (narrations of Israelite origin, which are often baseless). Such Israelite narrations have become part of all the earlier tafsirs. No tafsir is free of them. The tafsir of Imam Tabari, although it is a refined and extremely valuable work, and the tafsir of Ibn Kathir, although it is a worthy work of great merit, are both not free of Isra'iliyyat.

Many narrations from Hadrat Ibn Abbas are also reported on this subject. Ibn Jarir Tabari has mentioned them in both his history and his tafsir, and one of these narrations is the following.

It is related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that when Musa came to the court of Pharaoh, he demanded of him that he send the Children of Israel with him. He refused. So Allah sent a tufan upon them, that is, heavy rain fell. When this rain continued for a long time, these people became frightened that it might be a punishment. The people of Pharaoh requested Hadrat Musa to ask his God to stop this rain. If it stopped, they would believe in him and send the Children of Israel with him. He prayed to the Lord, but they did not believe, nor did they send the Children of Israel with him. So that year their crops, fruits and fodder were so abundant as had never been before. They said that this was exactly what they had wished for. Then Allah sent locusts upon them. The locusts cleared the grass. When they saw that the locusts had licked up the grass, it was obvious that they would not spare the crops either. Again they requested Hadrat Musa (peace be upon him) to supplicate to the Lord that they might be freed from this calamity. If they were freed, they would believe and send the Children of Israel with him. Allah removed the locusts, and these people still did not believe, nor did they send the Children of Israel with him. They reaped the crop, stored it in their houses, and said, "Now we have brought the crop home." Then Allah sent weevils upon them. So a man would take ten measures of grain to the mill, and when he returned, it would be only three measures. Again they requested Musa to ask Allah that if He removed the weevils, they would believe and send the Children of Israel with him. He prayed, and this punishment also was removed. Still they did not believe, and they refused to send the Children of Israel with him. It happened that Hadrat Musa was sitting with Pharaoh when they heard the croaking of frogs. Hadrat Musa said to Pharaoh, "You and your people are going to be afflicted by this." Pharaoh said, "What mischief can frogs do?" Before evening, so many frogs swarmed that when anyone spoke, frogs would fall from his mouth. Again they requested Hadrat Musa to pray that Allah remove this punishment from them. They would believe and send the Children of Israel with him. Allah removed this punishment too. But the people of Pharaoh neither believed nor sent the Children of Israel. Then Allah sent blood upon them. Now there was fresh blood in their rivers, their wells and their vessels. The people complained to Pharaoh that the trial had now reached its limit, and there was no water left for them to drink. Pharaoh said that Musa had truly cast a spell. They said, "How could we be bewitched? Even the water in our vessels is fresh blood." Then they came again to Hadrat Musa and said, "O Musa, call upon your Lord. If this punishment is removed from us, we will certainly believe in you." He called upon his Lord, and Allah removed this punishment too. They again did the same: they neither believed nor sent the Children of Israel.

Allah alone knows what events actually took place. Nevertheless, the events mentioned in this narration do not contradict the Quran. These punishments were certainly sent down upon them by Allah in order to test them, and this is Allah's way with those who reject: He tests them again and again so that they might be persuaded.

The people of Pharaoh, despite their idol-worship and ignorance, and despite the oppression, torment and humiliation inflicted upon them by Pharaoh, used to seek refuge in the presence of Hadrat Musa so that he might ask his Lord, because Allah had made a covenant with Hadrat Musa that He would accept his supplication, and that he should pray that this calamity be removed from them. However, the rulers of Egypt would break their promise and not believe, because the system of government of that time was founded on the belief that Pharaoh was their lord and sovereign. These people feared the establishment of Allah's lordship and sovereignty in place of Pharaoh's, because they understood that the necessary consequence of believing in Musa was that Pharaoh's system of government would end, and that sovereignty within the land would belong to Allah alone.

As for those who are the proponents of modern jahiliyyah (ignorance), Allah repeatedly sends calamities upon their sustenance, yet they do not give up their way. When landowners and villagers perceive this and turn humbly in supplication to Allah, just as even the disbelievers have, at the level of the subconscious, a motive to turn back to Allah, then the people of today who are steeped in jahiliyyah and call themselves "scientific" say that this is belief in superstition and ignorance, and that such acts are done by the people of modern jahiliyyah to mislead people. In my view, the conduct of these people is worse than that of the ancient idol-worshippers.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 136:

Now the natural end comes into view, in accordance with Allah's sunnah (way). These people were tested by being afflicted with hardships, and they were also tested by being given abundance, but they did not give up their conduct. Now the event occurs that becomes a certainty. Pharaoh and his courtiers are destroyed. Now their respite has ended, and the end that they were bound to reach has drawn near. And the promise that Allah makes to the weak and the patient has also arrived, so the rebellious and the tyrants are destroyed.

﴿So We took retribution from them, and drowned them in the sea, because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them. And We made the people who had been considered weak inheritors of the eastern and western parts of the land which We had blessed. And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel, because they were patient. And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people had been building and what they had been raising up.﴾

Here, in the context of the discourse, the event of Pharaoh's drowning is related briefly, and its details, which are given in other places, are not given. This is because the theme here is only that Allah seizes the rebellious after a respite. Therefore this subject did not need the details of the stories, and in such a setting mere allusions are more effective, and such events have a better impact on the feelings.

﴿So We took retribution from them, and drowned them in the sea.﴾ In a single blow He finished their affair. They were rebellious, oppressive and arrogant. By casting them to the bottom of the sea, Allah showed that you are now lower than the lowest. And this is a fitting recompense for you.

Why? Because: ﴿they denied Our signs and were heedless of them.﴾ Because they denied Our signs and became careless of them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 137:

In keeping with this decisive manner, the other side of the picture is also given briefly and decisively. It was not that another oppressor came; rather, the weak ones established their authority in the land, that is, the Children of Israel became rulers. This was because at that time they met the standard of reform. But soon after, they went astray, and Allah imposed humiliation and exile upon them. This succession of the Children of Israel was not in Egypt, such that they sat upon the throne of Pharaoh; their system of government was established in Syria, and it was many years after the drowning of Pharaoh. At that time Musa had already passed away, and the Children of Israel had spent forty years wandering in the desert of Tih, as the Qur'an has stated in other places. Here, in the narration of the story, these links have been omitted, and immediately after the drowning of Pharaoh, in keeping with the occasion and the subject, the establishment of the authority of the Children of Israel is mentioned.

﴿And We caused the people who had been deemed weak to inherit the eastern and western parts of the land which We had blessed. And the fair promise of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel, because they were patient. And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people had been building and what they had been raising up.﴾

The meaning of "ya'rishun" is that they used to construct buildings; it may also mean that they used to trail grapevines over their rooftops.

We humans can think only within the bounds of time and space, and we say that this event occurred after or before such-and-such, because we can understand events only after their occurrence and passage. We say that the rise of the Children of Israel and their authority came after the drowning of Pharaoh. But Allah, the All-Knowing, the All-Aware, and what has been and what will be, lies open before Him in its pages. The knowledge of Allah transcends place and time. His realm of exemplars is also exalted, and the realm of knowledge is, in comparison to His realm of exemplars, not even like that.

Now the curtain falls. On one side were scenes of destruction and ruin; on the other, the weak were taking their seats of power. A rebellious, arrogant, and haughty people were lying prostrate in the sea. All the superiorities, constructions, and comforts of life were lost to them. All the gardens and groves vanished from their sight; in the blink of an eye, everything was annihilated in their view. And in this depiction the Qur'an used a few words and made it, as it were, audible.

Allah presents this example before a small community in Makkah. The people of polytheism are inflicting persecutions upon them and expelling them from the city. Therefore a candle of hope is being lit for them. Wherever in the world people are working for the Islamic revolution today, this candle of hope is for them. The consequences they are enduring today, and the gallows and ropes they are kissing, indicate that Allah is certainly going to give them authority over the east and west of this world, because they showed patience; yet this is not as a reward but as a trial, to see what they will do.

Lesson No. 80: At a Glance

In this lesson, another link in the story of Prophet Musa (peace be upon him) continues. Now his concern is with his own people, the Children of Israel. These people have now been freed from their enemy. Allah has destroyed Pharaoh and his companions, and all the development and construction that they regarded as everything has been destroyed and laid waste. Today Musa does not have to confront Pharaoh and his taghut (tyrannical) system; the struggle against tyranny has been won. Today you have to fight on a new front: the jahiliyyah (ignorance) that is deeply embedded within the human personality. Today Musa is struggling against the humiliation and degradation that lies layered within the personality of the Children of Israel, the product of the era of slavery. Crookedness has entered their temperament, their hearts have become hard like stone, and on the battlefield they appear extremely cowardly. In facing the difficulties on the path of life and of higher life, they are extremely weak. And they have become slaves of personal inclinations. The reality is that humiliation, slavery and oppression destroy the personality of a human being. Living a long time in fear, secret activities, perversity, and hiding to escape torture and punishment, working in the darkness of night, and the constant fear of violence and calamity: this is an environment through which severe corruption and imbalance come into a person's nature.

The Children of Israel had remained for a long time under the most severe violence. For a long time, fear, dread, idol worship and the shadow of Pharaonism hung over them. Pharaoh would spare their daughters and slaughter their sons. This merciless violence might sometimes cease, but humiliation, slavery and a degrading life were permanently their fate.

Corruption had arisen in their personality. Their temperament had become unbalanced. Crookedness had entered their nature. Their thoughts had become corrupted. Humiliation, cowardice, spite and hatred were deeply ingrained in their psychology. Whenever any human community becomes the victim of such oppression, these qualities arise in them.

Hadrat Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) had been granted divine insight by Allah. He was well informed about human psychology. He had told all his officials and had given this instruction: "Do not punish people by striking them repeatedly on the face, for in this way you will humiliate them." He knew that people are humiliated by being struck on the face, and it is the basic policy of Islam that the subjects must not be disgraced and degraded, because in an Islamic state people are regarded as honourable. The policy and desire of Islam is that people should be honourable, and officials were forbidden from humiliating people by beating them repeatedly. Islam declared that people are not the slaves of rulers; they are the slaves of Allah and honourable people. They are respected above all besides Allah.

In the tyrannical system of Pharaonism, the Pharaohites had humiliated the Children of Israel by beating them repeatedly. Indeed, compared to the oppression inflicted upon them, such beatings appeared to be an ordinary matter. After the Children of Israel, the entire Egyptian nation was humiliated by repeated beatings by the rulers who came later; after the Pharaonic taghut, the Roman taghut likewise humiliated the Egyptians by repeated beatings. The Egyptian nation was delivered from these calamities only by Islam. When Islam came, it freed the Egyptian nation from the slavery of other human beings. Amr ibn al-As, the ruler of Egypt and the son of the conqueror of Egypt, became extremely angry when a Copt was struck with only a single whip, and that by the son of the conqueror of Egypt and the governor. He travelled for a month on a she-camel and brought this complaint to Hadrat Umar ibn al-Khattab. A complaint about striking with a single whip, although before the conquest of Egypt the Copt had endured many whippings inflicted by the Romans. This was the miracle of the Islamic revolution, which created a revolution among the Copts as well, even though they were not Muslims. Islam raised humanity from beneath the layers of humiliation and disgrace that had settled upon it, and granted it freedom. People rose in such a way that their body and soul became free, and they shook off the dust of humiliation from themselves at once. No non-Islamic system had given humanity so much freedom.

Now the task of Musa was that he had to remove the weaknesses that had arisen in his people's personality because of centuries of slavery and of living a life of humiliation under a taghut system. The Children of Israel had left Egypt and had crossed the sea. In the stories narrated in the Holy Qur'an, the personalities of these people are clearly visible. They are covered with the dust of slavery.

On the other hand, Musa (peace be upon him) confronts the remnants of jahiliyyah. Musa's struggle is now against the obstinacy, moral laxity and intellectual ignorance of those people which were deeply ingrained in their personality during that long period of captivity.

In this connection we shall see how tirelessly Musa endured hardships in order to remove these weaknesses. He has to deal with people whose nature has remained prostrate for centuries. Their condition was like that of a worm of filth which does not wish to come out of filth and considers humiliation and filth ordinary for itself.

In the struggle of Musa (peace be upon him) there is a lesson for every caller to the faith, especially for a caller who has to deal with people who have remained in humiliation and slavery for centuries, and who lived under a taghut system that was both oppressive and violent. Especially in circumstances where people also know that the path to which the caller invites is the path of salvation, indeed it is the only path of salvation, but because they have been scholars and believers for a long time, this call has become a habitual call for them and their religion has become a lifeless, formal religion.

In such circumstances the burden of responsibility on the shoulders of a caller doubles, and that is why such a caller needs a great measure of patience. It is the duty of such a caller to be patient with people's crooked understanding, their bad manners, their laxity of temperament and the slowness of their steps. At every stage he must patiently and with great seriousness endure the defeat of such people and their desires to return to jahiliyyah.

The story of the Children of Israel has been fixed in the Holy Qur'an for the Muslim ummah precisely because it contains great lessons for the Muslim ummah, and under this wisdom it has been brought repeatedly from different aspects, so that the Muslim ummah may benefit from this experience, and there is a great provision of provisions in this story for all callers who come after the Prophet ﷺ.

Lesson No. 80: Explanation of the Verses 138 to 171

---

This is the seventh scene of this story. In it the Children of Israel appear when, having been saved, they have crossed the Red Sea to the other side. Now, in contrast to the Pharaonic scenes, we face in them the rebellious, sin-loving and extremely crooked personality of the Children of Israel. These moral weaknesses are deeply layered in their temperament over the course of centuries of history. Not long had passed since Allah had delivered them from Pharaoh, who had kept them thoroughly humiliated. Pharaoh's people also shared in this, and this deliverance had come to them through Prophet Musa; Musa had launched this movement in the name of Allah, the Lord of the worlds. The Lord of the worlds destroyed their enemy, split the sea for their deliverance, and freed them from that humiliating life. They had only just come out, freed from the idol worship of Egypt and the land of oppression. But as soon as they crossed the sea and passed by a people who had an idol and who worshipped it, and every person was engaged in the worship of their idols, they immediately demanded of Prophet Musa (peace be upon him) that he should designate for them an idol like theirs, so that they too might begin similar worship. Yet the conflict between Musa and Pharaoh was based purely on the doctrine of tawhid, and it was on the basis of this doctrine that Pharaoh was destroyed and they were delivered.

(And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea, and they came upon a people devoting themselves to idols of theirs. They said: "O Musa, make for us a god just as they have gods.") The Children of Israel were made to pass through the sea by Us; then they went on, and on the way they passed a people who were devoted to their few idols. They said, "O Musa, make for us a god just as they have gods."

Contagious diseases affect the body just as spiritual diseases are also contagious, but contagious diseases spread only when germs for their spread exist within people. The Qur'an's portrayal of the temperament of the Children of Israel, which is extremely true, deep and comprehensive, clearly shows that these people were morally very feeble, weak in conviction and superstitious; they accepted misguidance just as petrol catches fire. As soon as they rose, they fell; they walked only a few steps on the straight path before suddenly starting to flee here and there, because the germs of misguidance had entered their hearts. They were far from truth. Their sense of perception had died, and their consciousness had been extinguished. When they suddenly see a people of idol worshippers occupied in idol worship, they forget the twenty or twenty-three years of Musa's struggle and the centuries of their own slavery, and they make the demand that idols be designated for them as well. Leaving aside the earlier miracles, just now the sea had split and they had passed through great mountains of water, and their enemy had been destroyed before their very eyes. Pharaoh and his cruel staff were all idol worshippers, and they used to incite Pharaoh against the Children of Israel in the name of that very idol worship. They forgot the words that the people of Pharaoh used to say: "Will you leave Musa and his people to spread corruption in the land and to abandon you and your gods?" Forgetting all this, they demand of their Prophet and Messenger that, just as miracles appeared at your word, now obtain from your Lord the approval of idols for us too, so that we too may begin idol worship. If these people had themselves begun idol worship, there would still have been some reason; but they had no such shame, and they sought permission for idol worship from the Prophet and from the Lord of the worlds. But these are the Children of Israel; anything can be expected from them.

Upon this demand Musa became very angry, as a messenger of the Lord of the worlds ought to be about his Lord. For every messenger is extremely jealous concerning the doctrine of tawhid, and shirk is intolerable to him. Accordingly he gave them an answer appropriate for them: "Qala innakum qawmun tajhalun" ("He said: 'You are a people who act in ignorance.'"). Here their ignorance is not restricted; so the meaning is that you are ignorant to the utmost degree. If this is used in contrast to knowledge, it means lack of knowledge; and if it is used in contrast to sound reason, it means foolishness, that is, you are utterly foolish and utterly devoid of both knowledge and sense. There is also an indication in this that those who deviate from the doctrine of tawhid are both ignorant and foolish, and that knowledge, science and wisdom lead a person to the doctrine of tawhid. Knowledge and reason can never reach any doctrine other than the doctrine of tawhid.

Knowledge and reason, by observing this whole universe, bear witness that it has one Creator and Administrator, and that this Creator and Administrator is also one, without partner. For the laws and regulations of this entire universe show that its Administrator is one. And however much reflection is made on this universe and inquiry is pursued into it, this is what comes to light: the uniformity of its laws and signs is proof of the unity of the Creator. Turning away from this or disregarding it can only be done by those who are utterly ignorant or foolish, even though they call themselves scholars and scientists.

Musa (peace be upon him) explains to the people that the idolatry they are engaged in is a very evil thing, and that their demand is a plainly unreasonable one. "Do you follow people who are themselves destined for destruction?" ﴿Indeed, these people — what they are engaged in is doomed to destruction, and what they are doing is null and void.﴾ The passage says: "This people's way is one that is destined for ruin, and the deeds they are performing are utterly false."

This is shirk (associating partners with God) and idol worship: the worship of idols, and an idolatrous civilization in which there are many lords, and beneath these lords there are thrones, seats, religious leaders, rulers and the ruled, and in which people determine their rights through idol worship. All these superstitions and illusions are based on a corrupt conception of life; they are false and baseless. These concepts and practices are destined to vanish from the world, and in the Hereafter too there is destruction for them.

Sayyid Musa (peace be upon him) becomes even more fervent in his speech, out of zeal for his way of life and for his Lord. His discourse grows more intense, and with indignation he reminds them that what had just happened at the seashore has already been forgotten by them; they do not even keep in mind their own rank and station.

(Qala aghayra Allahi abghikum ilahan wa huwa faddalakum ala al-alamin): "He said: 'Shall I seek for you a god other than Allah, while it is He who has favoured you over the nations of the worlds?'"

In this era, the superiority of the Children of Israel over all nations is evident, in that from among all the idolatrous nations they were chosen for the office of prophethood. What greater favour and greater kindness could there be than this? Prophethood is a great bounty and a great blessing. Moreover, at that time the Children of Israel were also chosen for this position: that they would be the supreme authority on this earth. In particular, it was decreed that the Holy Land would be freed by their hands, because at that time the Holy Land was under the occupation of foreign nations.
