The question is: after these honours, with what face are they now demanding that a deity be appointed for them just as other peoples have appointed deities for themselves, when Allah's great favour and grace had been upon them?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 141:

It is the manner of the Qur'an that the speech of the Prophets is mentioned alongside the speech of Allah, directly following one another. Thus, along with the narration of the words of Prophet Musa (peace be upon him), the speech of Allah also comes immediately after.

﴿And [Allah says]: Remember when We delivered you from the people of Pharaoh, who subjected you to a terrible torment, slaughtering your sons and letting your women live. And in that was a great trial from your Lord.﴾ And [Allah says]: Remember the time when We delivered you from the people of Pharaoh, who had you in the grip of severe torment: they slaughtered your sons and let your women live, and in that was a great trial from your Lord.

Bringing together the speech of Allah and the speech of His Prophets is in fact intended to honour the Prophets, and this is indeed the most excellent manner of showing esteem and honour.

These favours which were bestowed upon the Children of Israel, and which are recounted here, were present in their minds and hearts, and their observation of them was fresh. The mere reminder of these favours was sufficient to make them prostrate in gratitude. Allah, the Exalted, draws their attention to the fact that this is a place of lesson, and that all of human life, the difficulties and the deliverance from difficulties that follow them, is a trial for human beings. ﴿And in that was a great trial from your Lord.﴾ This is because none of these events was accidental. Everything was in accordance with the decree of Divine destiny, and it was a trial, and the purpose of the trial was to derive lessons, and the purpose was to separate the genuine from the spurious by subjecting the Muslims to experiences, and the purpose was that when they were punished, they would have no occasion for complaint, at a time when all these trials had no effect upon them.

Now this scene also comes to an end, and a second scene, far more interesting, comes into view.

This is the eighth scene. In it, Musa (Moses, peace be upon him) is about to meet his Lord, the Lord of the worlds. Musa makes great preparation for this momentous occasion. He appoints Harun (Aaron) as his successor, giving him counsel, and then sets out toward his destined goal.

The first stage of Musa's mission is now complete. In this stage the Children of Israel were freed from a life of humiliation and forced labour. Now they have come out of the sphere of the persecution and oppression of Pharaoh's people. Having abandoned the life of humiliation and slavery in the city, they now roam the free expanses of the desert, and they are moving forward toward the Holy Land. Yet they have not yet become fit for the great and essential mission of reclaiming the Holy Land. Indeed, it is a grand path strewn with thorns, for a people to attain positions of power on the earth and assume the duty of vicegerency (khilafah) on earth.

In the previous scene we have seen how idolatry and polytheism (shirk) had taken root in their hearts, to the point that, upon seeing an idolatrous people during their journey, they immediately demanded idols for themselves. The belief in the Oneness of God (tawhid), for which Musa had been specially sent as a messenger, had become shaken in their minds and hearts, and not much time had passed since then. Therefore there was a need for Musa to be given detailed instructions and sent back to them, so that, under the new guidance, he might organise and train this people, so that they could fulfil the great duty of freeing the Holy Land. For this purpose, Allah invited Musa (peace be upon him) to a meeting at a fixed time and place, so that he might receive directions directly from Allah. In this meeting, it was also intended that Musa himself be further trained, so that he too would be prepared for the difficult circumstances and arduous missions that lay ahead. The training course for Musa was fixed at thirty days; ten more days were then added. Thus this process continued for forty days. During this period Musa devoted himself to preparation for the meeting with God. He withdrew from the pleasures of this world and drew near to the higher realm, distancing himself from people and gaining closeness to the Lord of the worlds. His soul was purified, his inner self was illuminated, and thus he was made ready, through direct training from the Lord of the worlds, for the duties of the office of prophethood.

Before his departure, Musa (peace be upon him) gave his brother and successor, Harun, the following counsel:

﴿And Musa said to his brother Harun: "Take my place among my people, act righteously, and do not follow the way of the corrupters."﴾

Musa, speaking as he set out, said to his brother Harun: "After me, you are to take my place among my people, do what is right, and do not follow the way of those who spread corruption."

Musa well knew that Harun too was a prophet sent by Allah. Yet it is the duty of one Muslim to advise another, indeed advice is an obligation of one Muslim upon another. Moreover, Musa was well aware of the heavy responsibilities, and he knew his people, the Children of Israel, very well. Harun listened to the advice with an open heart and accepted it. He did not take offence, for advice is not pleasing to wicked people, since such people seek to be free of goodness, and advice is also burdensome to those small-minded people who consider themselves very great; when advice is given to them, these small-minded people regard it as an insult to themselves. The arrogant of small stature are those to whom you extend your hand, wishing to help them, and they push away your hand so that they may appear great to themselves.

As for what happened during these thirty nights and the further ten days of extension, Ibn Kathir says: "Allah had appointed thirty nights for Musa. The commentators say that Musa fasted during this period and ate nothing. When the appointed term was complete, he cleaned his teeth with a piece of bark from a tree. Upon this, Allah commanded him to complete forty days."

Now this scene is before you. It is a unique scene, and it is a distinctive feature of Hazrat Musa (peace be upon him). In it, the Lord of Majesty and the Lord of the Worlds addresses His servant directly. In this scene, a particle, a limited particle, and a perishable being is joined with an eternal and everlasting Being. At this point, a servant receives guidance directly from his Creator, while the Creator is eternal and everlasting, beyond all beyond, and the servant is upon the earth. But what was the nature of this contact? We are incapable of comprehending it. We cannot tell what the nature of speaking with Allah was. How Hazrat Musa (peace be upon him) received guidance here through what faculties of perception, and how the words came to him, are all concepts that are unimaginable for us humans, who possess limited power. This is because our power of perception is limited. Our capital of understanding is limited. Our experiences are event-based. But through the subtle mystery and the subtle consciousness that Allah has placed within human beings, we know that this speaking took place, and we have certainty of it, a conscious certainty. Yet when we ask about the mode, we should not cloud our certainty, because this relationship, the relationship between the limited and the unlimited, cannot fit within the limited measure of our perception.

We should fully bring this unique scene into our imagination, our nerves, and our existence. By gathering all our powers, all the powers of comprehension and perception, we should try to draw near to the concepts of this scene, so that we too may be able to share in the reality that Hazrat Musa perceived and the awareness he attained.

(When Musa came at Our appointed time and his Lord spoke to him, he said: "My Lord, show me Yourself that I may look upon You.")

"When he arrived at Our appointed time and his Lord spoke to him, he requested: 'O my Lord! Grant me the ability to see, that I may behold You.'"

This is a frightening scene. Hazrat Musa is hearing words from Allah, and in the state of his longing and the direction he is being drawn toward, and the direction in which his soul is rising, in such circumstances Hazrat Musa forgets what his own station is and what the majesty of Allah is, and he makes a demand for something that is impossible for the humanity of this world. And even if it were made possible, it would not be within the power of any human being. That is, he requests the sight of the Divine Being. In these circumstances of longing and hope, and in this atmosphere of love and union, he wishes to see the Divine Being in the world of witnessing. But the reply comes in a decisive manner: ﴿He said: "You will not see Me."﴾ And after this, the compassion of Allah appears, and the reason why "You will not see Me" is taught to you: it is that you do not have the capacity for it within yourself. ﴿"But look toward the mountain; if it remains firmly in its place, then you will see Me."﴾ Because the mountain is more firm than a human being. Moreover, it is not one that is affected, and it does not possess the capacity of receptivity compared to a human being. But despite this, what happened was this: ﴿When his Lord manifested His splendor to the mountain, He reduced it to dust, and Musa fell down unconscious.﴾

The question is: what was that manifestation like? We are not capable of describing any of its qualities. We cannot comprehend it, nor can we see that manifestation. We can see it only through that subtle spiritual connection, and this spiritual vision is possible only when the human soul becomes pure and clear and fully turns toward its origin and source. We cannot convey any state to the minds of readers through mere words, and words without meaning. Therefore we do not attempt to explain it through words. Moreover, the narrations that have come on this subject we also set aside, because none of those narrations is traced back to the Messenger (ﷺ) as marfu'. The Qur'an has given no detail about this matter.

Regarding the effects of this manifestation, the Qur'an says that it was reduced to dust and leveled to the ground. Hazrat Musa fainted because of human weakness. ﴿When he regained consciousness, he said: "Glory be to You! I turn to You in repentance, and I am the first of the believers."﴾

When he regained consciousness, he came to know the limits of human perceptive power, and he practically understood that by asking this question he had exceeded his limits. So he acknowledged: "O Allah, Your Being is pure. I repent. I have exceeded the limits. I am the first believer." The Messenger is always the first Muslim, the first to believe in the greatness of Allah. He is the first to believe in his prophethood and in the speech revealed upon him. Prophets are commanded by Allah to announce their faith first. This theme appears at several places in the Holy Qur'an.

Sayyid Musa saw this manifestation of Divine mercy for the second time with his own eyes. Now he is given the good news that he has been chosen for a unique mission. "You are the bearer of My speech and My message." The demand made to Pharaoh was: "Release my people." Now you have to work among your own people.

Allah Ta'ala told Musa (peace be upon him): "I have chosen you above all people to be My messenger" (﴿إِنِّي اصْطَفَيْتُكَ عَلَى النَّاسِ بِرِسَالَاتِي وَبِكَلَامِي﴾). The meaning is that He chose you from among all the people of your time to be a Messenger. Because prophets were sent before Musa (peace be upon him) and after him as well, the meaning of "choosing" and "preferring" (intikhab and istifa') here, according to the context, is in comparison with the people of that era. As for the attribute of speaking directly with Allah, Musa is unique in that quality.

The same applies to the command that Allah gave Musa: "Take what I have given you and be among the grateful" (﴿فَخُذْ مَا آتَيْتُكَ وَكُن مِّنَ الشَّاكِرِينَ﴾). This is guidance and direction from Allah, and a reminder that the only fitting response to these blessings of Allah is one: to be grateful. Since messengers are leaders, and leaders are examples for the people, it becomes the duty of the people as well to take Allah's guidance and to thank Allah for it. In this way, Allah's further blessings will descend upon them, their reform will be achieved, and by being connected to Allah they will be protected from rebellion.

Now a few words about the content and method of this mission, and how it was given:

(وَكَتَبْنَا لَهٗ فِي الْاَلْوَاحِ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مَّوْعِظَةً وَّتَفْصِيْلًا لِّكُلِّ شَيْءٍ) "And We wrote for him on the Tablets an admonition concerning all things and a detailed explanation of all things." Afterwards, We gave Musa, in the Tablets, guidance and admonition on every aspect of life, and clear direction on every dimension of it.

There are differences among the narrations and the exegetes regarding these Tablets, and some have given details about them. Most of these details are based on Israelite narrations (Isra'iliyyat) that have entered Islamic tafsir. None of these narrations traces back (marfu') to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Therefore, we stop at this verse and do not go further, because the details in those narrations add nothing to, and subtract nothing from, the reality of these Tablets. What the Tablets were made of, and what kind of script was inscribed on them, we have no details about, nor is there any need for them, because the real purpose is what was written on the Tablets. They contained all the matters related to the mission of Musa, such as the statement of Allah, the commandments of Allah's Sharia, further guidance for the reform of the people, the conditions of the community, and the matters due to which corruption had arisen among them, that is, their history and so on.

(فَخُذْهَا بِقُوَّةٍ وَّاْمُرْ قَوْمَكَ يَاْخُذُوْا بِاَحْسَنِهَا) "So take hold of them with strength, and enjoin your people to take the best of it." And He said: "Hold these guidances with firm hands, and command your people to follow their best meaning."

The important command from Allah was that you should take these Tablets and guidance with great strength and resolve, and strictly command your people to act upon these guidances, even if they are difficult, because they were most suitable and the best for the reform of their condition.

There are two purposes behind commanding Musa to receive the guidance in this manner. First, the Children of Israel had spent a long time in a life of slavery, and through a long life of slavery a moral corruption had arisen within them. Therefore, in dealing with them, sternness and seriousness were urgently needed, so that he could properly discharge the duties of prophethood and then the duties of the office of khilafah. Second, all those who work on the basis of a way of life should firmly establish themselves upon their beliefs.

Belief is very important in the sight of Allah. From the viewpoint of this entire universe, the ideology is also of great importance. That is, a person should have a clear and pure outlook regarding the governance of this universe and human history. Likewise, a person's thoughts about this worldly life and the life to come must be clear. Thus, a person's worship should be exclusively devoted to the divinity of Allah alone. After this, on the basis of this ideology, a system of life should be established that completely transforms human life and establishes an entirely new pattern for living. That system should not be one under which jahiliyyah operates, in which the divinity of anyone other than Allah is established. In short, there must be a detailed and comprehensive system for the whole of life based on this way of life. The establishment of such a system is necessary. In the sight of Allah, a clear belief and a system based upon it are of great importance. Regarding the creation of this entire universe, the existence of man within it, and then the history of this man, a person must firmly adhere to the Islamic way of life. A person should be serious about it, clearly declare his ideas, and do so in plain and decisive words. He should not be careless in this matter, should not be lenient, and should not seek concessions, because this is a very important and fundamental matter. The demands of this matter are so difficult that people who are soft-natured, flexible, and seek concessions cannot fulfill them.

However, holding firmly to the Islamic way of life and grasping it tightly does not also mean that a person becomes violent, complicated in temperament, or harsh in disposition, because this is not the disposition of the religion of Islam. Religion only demands that a person be serious for the sake of religion, speak clearly, hold decisive views, and be plainspoken. These qualities are separate from violence, harshness, dryness, and ill temper. There must in any case be a difference between being firm in one's convictions and being ill-tempered.

The truth is that the long life of slavery in Egypt had produced such moral weaknesses among the Children of Israel that instructions based on sternness were necessary for them. This is why whatever guidance was given to the Children of Israel contains great sternness, so that their habitual laxity, weak moral strength, and waywardness could be treated, and so that they might adopt correct thinking, a clear voice, and a clear manner in matters of religion.

All nations that have remained enslaved for a long time develop the same moral weaknesses. Slavery brings humiliation, helplessness, fear, subservience to taghut and so on, due to which such people become crooked in understanding, deceitful, lax, and averse to labour and hardship. In our own age, all nations that have been enslaved possess these qualities, because slavery changes people's consciences. Such people run away from ideologies, because they cannot fulfill the demands of an ideology. Whichever direction the world goes, these people go in that direction, and a person can very easily move wherever the wind blows.

Along with giving these instructions, Allah also gives Musa the good news that if you hold firmly to your way of life, you will be granted sovereignty over the earth, and you will become the masters of the homes of the fasiqun. (سَاُورِيْكُمْ دَارَ الْفٰسِقِيْنَ) "Soon I shall show you the abodes of the wicked." 

The closest meaning of this part of the verse is that it refers to the Holy Land, which at that time was in the possession of idolaters. It was a good news to Musa that you would take control of it. Although in the time of Musa the Children of Israel did not enter it, because at his time their moral training was not yet complete. Their morals were still not correct, for when they came before the Holy Land they said to their Prophet: "O Musa! In it there is a mighty people, and we shall not enter it until they leave it. If they leave, then we will surely enter." 

Among them, one or two were truly believing men who insisted that they enter the city and attack. These two were in fact people who feared Allah. Upon this, the Children of Israel gave Musa (علیہ السلام) this reply: "We will never enter this city as long as that people are in it. Go, you and your Lord, and fight; we shall sit here waiting." These verses make it clear how corrupted the temperament of the Children of Israel was, how crooked they were, and for what kind of people the mission and Sharia of Musa were meant. In such circumstances, it was a most suitable guidance that they should hold the Torah's instructions with strength and make their people act upon them with firmness.

Now, at the end of this scene, and at the conclusion of the dialogue between Musa and the Lord of Musa, the passage tells of the end of those who are arrogant and who turn away from Allah's miracles and guidance. It also tells what the characteristics of such people are, and their portrait is drawn in very clear colours, exactly in the manner of the Qur'an's style of depiction.

Here Allah announces His decree concerning those who act arrogantly on this earth without any justification and make themselves great. What kind of people are these? They are such that, whatever miraculous proof is presented before them, they will not believe. When they are invited to some good deed, they do not respond; and if they see some act of evil, they rush towards it. Therefore, the correct remedy for such people is to leave them to their own condition and to work with those who accept. These people are not believers. The signs and proofs that are manifest in this universe, and those signs and proofs that are in the books of Allah, [they will not accept], because they have already decided upon denial and decided upon turning away.

The words of the Qur'an tell how these people will be, and their movements and attributes are these: ﴿Those who act arrogantly on the earth without any right﴾. Those who make themselves great on the earth without any right.

Because none of the servants of Allah has the right to make himself great on the earth of Allah. Greatness is an attribute of Allah, and in greatness Allah does not allow anyone to share, for it is His cloak. Therefore, whoever among men makes himself great on this globe acts arrogantly without any justification, and the greatest arrogance is that someone reserves for himself the right of legislation on this earth and exercises his sovereign authority over the servants of Allah in place of Allah, and makes people follow his own laws. From this arrogance and greatness all other evils arise. It is the foundation of all mischief, and every kind of corruption is brought about by it. After this, other attributes of such people come: ﴿And if they should see every sign, they will not believe in it; and if they should see the way of right guidance, they will not adopt it as a way; but if they should see the way of error, they will adopt it as a way.﴾ If the straight path comes before them, they will not adopt it, and if they see the crooked path, they set off upon it. It is their nature that, upon seeing the straight path, they turn aside from it, and upon seeing the crooked path, they immediately proceed along it, and this is part of their nature, and they cannot go against it. This is their attribute. The Qur'an expresses it in this manner and tells that the decree of Allah's will has resolved to punish such people, and that punishment is that the doors of guidance are closed to them forever.

People of this kind are found in every society. It appears that these people shun the truth and have a strong inclination towards falsehood, and rush towards falsehood without planning and without thinking. The straight path of truth seems difficult to them, and the crooked path of falsehood seems easy to them. Such people run far from Allah's signs, proofs and miracles; they do not reflect upon them, and their faculties of understanding and perception are not affected by them. Nor do the indications of nature and truth make an impression upon them.

Glory be to Allah! Through these glimpses of the wondrous guidance of the Qur'an, such people stand out clearly. And upon seeing such people in their surroundings and society, a reader exclaims: Yes, yes, I know people of this kind. So-and-so is an instance of these Qur'anic words.

By inflicting such destructive and deadly punishments on people of this kind, Allah does not wrong them, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. This is the reward and punishment that those people rightly deserve who deny the signs of Allah, are heedless of them, and assert their greatness on the earth without right. Their way is that they turn aside from every path that is the path of guidance, and rush towards every path that is the path of misguidance. Such people are receiving the recompense of their deeds, and because of their conduct they have reached the very door of destruction. ﴿That is because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them.﴾

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 147:

And as for those who denied Our signs and denied the meeting of the Hereafter, their deeds have become worthless. Will they be recompensed except for what they used to do?

Habitat (ḥabiṭat) comes from the root ḥ-b-ṭ. It is said: "ḥabiṭat a'māluhum" (their deeds were nullified), when an animal grazes on poisonous grass, its belly swells, and then gas is released from it. This word is used for the power of falsehood because the deeds of falsehood appear to flourish and grow, but their reality is nothing; when the air leaves a balloon, nothing remains.

This is the appropriate punishment for those who denied the signs of Allah and rejected accountability in the Hereafter. But the question is: how do their deeds come to be destroyed and ruined?

From the doctrinal and creedal standpoint, our belief is that their deeds will be lost, even if outward circumstances appear such that this outcome for their deeds does not seem to be expected. But whoever denies the signs of Allah and does not hold firm conviction in accountability in the Hereafter, his deeds will ultimately be lost and ruined, and their status will be as though they were nothing.

But from the theoretical aspect too it is clear that those who deny those signs and miracles that are scattered across the pages of this entire universe, and for which there are also supporting signs and proofs presented by the Messengers of Allah, and who at the same time deny accountability in the Hereafter, the souls of such people are in fact distorted, and such people are rebellious against the nature and laws of this universe. Such a person has no genuine connection with this universe, nor are such people in harmony with the path of true struggle. Since the deeds of such people are opposed to the direction of the universe, its purposes, and the laws of Allah, these deeds, although they may appear dazzling, are without reality. Although they may appear successful in their plans, this is because these deeds are not based on the eternal, firm motives and principles that form the foundation of this entire universe. The aim and goal of these deeds is not what is the aim and goal of this entire universe. Their example is like a river that has been cut off from its source, and which will inevitably dry up sooner or later.

Those who cannot perceive the deep connection between these faith values and human history, and who cannot grasp the unalterable decree of destiny that has been fixed against those who reject these faith values, are precisely those about whom it has been said that they are heedless. And it is about them that this punishment has been announced: that they will not be able to perceive the established practice (sunnat jariyah) of Allah and the universal order (namus kulli). For their direction has turned away, and now the final judgment concerning them remains to be manifested.

Those whom the brevity of this worldly life has deceived, and who see that people heedless of the Hereafter are living very successfully in this world, have been deceived in the same way as the animal that is afflicted by a swelling due to eating poisonous grass. They think that this animal has become fresh and fat and is very healthy, whereas in reality it is about to die.

The nations that have been destroyed and wiped out in this world, and in whose place other nations have come and settled, do not take lessons from those earlier nations. They do not see the way Allah's sunnah operates in this universe. The decree of Allah and His system continue to operate; there is never any pause in it. Allah encompasses all people.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 7, verse 148:

During the time when Hazrat Musa (peace be upon him) was in the presence of his Lord, this was a unique meeting. For our limited eyes it is clearly impossible to encompass that scene; our souls cannot behold it, and our thought and our faculties of perception are amazed at it. In the absence of Hazrat Musa, his people adopted misguidance. They again fell into the spiritual diseases of Egypt and sank into the pit of idol-worship. They took a speaking calf-idol as their god and began to worship it.

In these circumstances, we now move forward from the ninth scene of this story, and before us comes its tenth scene. The ninth scene was in the exalted higher realm, whose scenes were filled with joy and light; the atmosphere of love and spring-like dialogue was before us. But suddenly there appears a scene in which people fall from heights into depths; after health they again appear as sick people. Instead of clear thinking, they are running after superstitions.

﴿And the people of Musa, after him, made from their ornaments a calf, a body which had a lowing sound.﴾

This is the disposition of the Children of Israel: at every step they adopt aimlessness. They do not ascend towards elevation, outwardly or inwardly; rather, it is written in their nature that they fall towards lowliness. As soon as the chain of guidance and direction is cut off, they set out on wrong paths.

When they saw, after crossing the Red Sea miraculously, that a people were engaged in idol-worship, they demanded of the Prophet that a similar god be made for them too. Upon this, Hazrat Musa checked them and firmly rejected this notion of theirs. When Hazrat Musa went to Mount Sinai and they saw a golden calf making a sound, with no signs of life in it, merely a body, this was a strange craft among the works of the Samiri. This man was a resident of Samirah; details about him are recorded in Surah Taha. He designed this calf in such a way that a sound like that of oxen came out of it. When they saw it, they surged from every side, and when the Samiri, out of mischief, said that this is your Musa's and your god, they fell upon it.

He said that the god whom Musa went to meet is right here. Musa made a mistake in determining the place and the time. They believed this especially because Musa (peace be upon him) had spent more than a month. When Hazrat Musa did not return even after thirty days, the Samiri said that Musa (peace be upon him) has made a mistake; the god is right here. Yet Hazrat Musa had taught them the worship of a Lord who was not visible, the Lord of the worlds. They did not even consider that this body is a craft of one of their own men, the Samiri. The picture the Children of Israel were presenting of their conduct was an extremely crude image of humanity. The Holy Qur'an, expressing wonder at this picture, gives a lesson to the polytheists of Makkah: do you not see the condition of the idols you worship?

﴿Did they not see that it does not speak to them, nor guide them to any way? They adopted it, and they were wrongdoers.﴾

Who is a greater wrongdoer than one who worships a body which he himself has made, while it is Allah who creates humans and their works? The true Creator is Allah.

Among them was Hazrat Harun, but he could not stop them from this crude misguidance. Among them were also some wise and believing people, but they too could not build a dam against the flood of this foolish mass, especially since it was made of gold.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 149:

At the end, when the excitement subsided, people's senses returned, the reality came into view, and they realised that they had gone astray and had committed open shirk, then ﴿And when they were overcome with remorse, and saw that they had indeed gone astray, they said, "If our Lord does not have mercy upon us and forgive us, we will surely be among the losers."﴾ Then, when the illusion of their self-deception was broken, and they saw that in truth they had gone astray, they said, "If our Lord has not shown mercy to us and overlooked us, we will be ruined."

The expression "saqata fi yadihi" (suqita fi aydihim) is used when a person's stratagem and plan fail before him. When the Children of Israel saw that the error they had become entangled in could no longer be cleared, since what was to happen had already happened, then, helpless in such circumstances, they said: "If our Lord has not shown mercy to us and has not overlooked us, we will be ruined."

From this it becomes clear that until that time there was still in them the capacity for reform, and their hearts had not yet become as hard as they later did, to the point that the Qur'an had to say that they became like stones, or even harder than stones. In any case, when they came to know that they were in error, and that for them there was no path to success except the mercy and forgiveness of Allah, they repented in this manner, and this makes clear that at that time these people were capable of reform.

This events took place while Moses was standing in the court of the Lord of Majesty, speaking directly with Allah. He did not know what his people were doing behind him. Had Allah informed him, he would have known at that very moment. In any case, now the scene that followed upon Moses' return comes before us.

...

﴿وَلَمَّا رَجَعَ مُوْسٰٓي اِلٰى قَوْمِهٖ غَضْبَانَ اَسِفًا﴾ "And when Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved."

When Moses (peace be upon him) returned and saw these circumstances, he flared up with anger. His words and his actions show that he was in a state of intense anger, and the expression of that anger appears in these words: ﴿بِئْسَمَا خَلَفْتُمُوْنِيْ مِنْۢ بَعْدِيْ ۚ اَعَجِلْتُمْ اَمْرَ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ "On arriving, he said: 'Evil is what you have done as my successors after me! Did you wish to hasten the command of your Lord?'" Likewise, his action also shows his anger: he seized his brother by the beard and pulled him towards himself.

﴿وَاَخَذَ بِرَاْسِ اَخِيْهِ يَجُرُّهٗٓ اِلَيْهِ﴾ "And he seized his brother (Harun) by the head and dragged him towards himself."

This anger of Moses was entirely justified, because he had suddenly been confronted with a situation he had not expected. It was a revolutionary state of affairs. ﴿بئسما خلفتموني من بعدي﴾ "Evil is what you have done as my successors after me." I had left you on the right path, and you changed it into misguidance. I left you while you were worshipping God, and when I returned you were worshipping a calf, although it was merely a body and made a sound like a bull. ﴿اعجلتم امر ربكم﴾ "Did you not have the patience to await the command of your Lord?" That is, you did not wait for the decision of your Lord, you did not wait for His punishment, and you did not wait for the period for which He had summoned the assembly. ﴿والقى الالواح واخذ براس اخيه يجره اليه﴾ "He threw down the tablets and seized his brother by the head and dragged him towards himself." This action shows that he was severely agitated. Since those tablets contained the word of Allah, the demand of reverence was that he should not have thrown them to the ground, but at that time he was in severe anger and could not restrain himself. He seized his brother by the hair, although his brother was a righteous servant and a prophet. Harun appealed to brotherly feelings so that his anger might cool and he might adopt a conciliatory attitude. After that, he presented his defence and explained that he had committed no fault. ﴿قال ابن أم إن القوم استضعفوني وكادوا يقتلونني﴾ "He said: 'O son of my mother, the people overpowered me and nearly killed me.'"

Now, by using the words "son of my mother," Harun was reaching out to his brother's feelings with great warmth and emotion. And the circumstances were such that, had Harun resisted them more strongly, they would have resorted to violence. He depicts this situation in the words, "they nearly killed me," and therefore he was blameless.

﴿فَلَا تُشْمِتْ بِيَ الْاَعْدَاۗءَ وَلَا تَجْعَلْنِيْ مَعَ الْقَوْمِ الظّٰلِمِيْنَ﴾ "So do not let the enemies rejoice over me, and do not place me with the wrongdoing people."

By this second sentence too, Harun tries to calm his brother's feelings. When two brothers have a common enemy, brothers keep regard for each other's position. And thirdly, he says that you should not place me and the wrongdoers in one row. The wrongdoers are those who committed disbelief, and I did not take part in their wrongdoing. I am innocent.

Now Moses' emotions cool down, and he accepts the apology as reasonable. He turns to his Lord and seeks forgiveness and compassion.

﴿He said: "My Lord, forgive me and my brother, and admit us into Your mercy, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful."﴾

So Moses said: "O my Lord, forgive me and my brother, and admit us into Your mercy; You are the most merciful of all those who show mercy."

Now the decisive word comes forward, and the final decision rests with Allah, glorified is He. Allah connects His own statement directly to the words of His servant Musa, and this is a manner of honouring him from Allah's side.

﴿Indeed, those who took the calf (as a deity) will be overtaken by wrath from their Lord and humiliation in the life of this world.﴾

This is both a command and a promise. Indeed, those who made the calf into a god, wrath is about to befall them, and they will remain in humiliation in this worldly life. This is also a permanent principle and sunnah of Allah: those who do wrong and then repent, Allah forgives them. Since Allah had knowledge that the worshippers of the calf would not repent, a decision was made concerning them, because Allah knew that they would not set their way right and would not benefit from this principle. History bears witness that this is exactly what happened. The Children of Israel kept disobeying one after another, and Allah kept forgiving them again and again, until they became deserving of permanent wrath. ﴿And thus do We recompense those who fabricate lies.﴾ We give such punishment to those who fabricate falsehoods. Whoever fabricates falsehood until the Resurrection, this is a continuous punishment; whenever the crime occurs, this will be the punishment, whether the fabrication comes from the Children of Israel or from others.

Allah's promise is always true. Upon those who made the calf into a god, Allah has written humiliation, and they will always be those upon whom wrath is cast. The form of this wrath is that until the Resurrection, peoples will be set over them who will continue to inflict the worst torment upon them. Whenever it becomes known that these people are acting arrogantly on the earth and gaining dominance over the unlettered and backward people, and, as the word "Goyim" used in the Talmud's language for such people, these people began to take unfair advantage through their financial and propaganda power, or they established systems of government and through them began to launch their plans, or they began to expel the servants of Allah from their homes and began oppressing them, and whenever misguided governments began to walk alongside them, as this position of theirs is apparently visible in today's age. Although all these matters are not contrary to or in conflict with Allah's aforementioned decision against them, rather, because of the aforementioned self-initiated actions of these people, they are hateful to the people of the world and are gathering the material that will ultimately become the cause of their destruction. The people of Palestine are a target of their oppression because the people of Palestine have no religion, and the people of Palestine are not true Muslims. These people fight under other banners besides the religion of Islam, they gather and disperse under them. These people have not gathered under the banner of the Islamic worldview, and this is why they are unsuccessful and failed. And although the small community of Israel apparently appears to be progressing, these conditions will not last forever; this is a temporary period. In it, the strength and the weapon that is their only tool has been lost from the Muslims. It is the only system, the only banner, namely the Islamic banner, under which they dominated the world for a thousand years. Under this very banner they prevailed, and without it they will always be defeated. At this time the Muslim ummah is passing through a phase of shrinking and disappearing. This disappearance is due to the poison that global Judaism and global Crusaderism have spread within the Muslim ummah. And global democracy, Zionism and Crusaderism keep a close watch over the Muslim world so that its conditions do not improve. But these conditions will not remain the same forever; after this disappearance the Muslim ummah will certainly attain rise and manifestation. In the end, the coming Muslims will find the weapon of their Islam. Who knows when the whole world will come to its senses and rise against Jewish oppression, so that Allah's promise is fulfilled and they fall again into that pit of humiliation which Allah has written upon them. If all of humanity does not awaken against the Jews, then our conviction is that the Muslim ummah will certainly awaken.
