Purpose: this was a pause and a moment for reflection, so that the outcome of those who made the calf into a deity might be considered for a while. Now the previous scene concludes as follows.

﴿And when the anger subsided from Musa, he picked up the tablets.﴾

Note the Qur'an's manner of expression here: it is as though anger (ghadab) is a personal entity that had gained control over Hazrat Musa and was driving and moving him according to its own will. And when it fell silent and left Hazrat Musa free, Hazrat Musa (عليه السلام) also came back under his own control. The tablets that he had thrown down because of anger, he took back into his hands. Now it is stated that the tablets contained the guidance of Allah, and for those who feared their Lord, they were a mercy; their hearts had opened to be set upon the right path, and they had filled their laps with the mercies of Allah. And who would be a more wretched person than one who has gone astray and lost his way, who finds no path before him? And no other soul is more wretched than the one that wanders aimlessly and is granted neither a clear path nor the wealth of certainty. The truth is that taqwa (God-consciousness) and fear of Allah are the very qualities by which hearts are opened, by which heedlessness is removed, and by which a person comes onto the right path and accepts the truth. Allah is the Creator of these lords (the lords of the people, that is, their desires and false gods), and He alone is the One who decides and announces this reality. It is obvious that no one knows the condition of hearts better than the Lord of the worlds.

Now the story moves forward, and a new scene appears on the screen. This is the twelfth scene of this narrative. In it, Moses is proceeding along with the seventy men he has chosen.

﴿And Moses chose seventy men of his people for Our appointed time.﴾ He selected seventy men from his people so that they would attend (with him) at the time We had appointed.

Narrations differ regarding the appointed time with Allah. Perhaps this time was set so that the Children of Israel might repent, and seek forgiveness from Allah for the disbelief and polytheism they had committed. In Surah al-Baqarah it is mentioned that the punishment prescribed for the Children of Israel as expiation for that sin was that they should kill their own people, meaning that the obedient among them should kill the disobedient. They did so, and continued killing until Allah forgave them and commanded them to stop. These seventy men were their wise and intelligent people, or their representatives. The words "Moses chose seventy men from his people, so that they would attend at Our appointed time" show that they were deputies or representatives.

The question of who these people were remains open. A severe earthquake seized them and they fell unconscious, as mentioned in other surahs, where they demanded of Moses that they wanted to see Allah openly so that they might accept the commands and the tablets revealed to him. This shows the disposition of these people. If this was the condition of their chosen ones, how would the condition of the ordinary people have been? And even more astonishing is that these people went to have repentance accepted.

Moses (peace be upon him) turns towards his Lord. He is requesting that You forgive the fault and show mercy. He is humbling himself and acknowledging the fault.

﴿So when the earthquake seized them, he said, "My Lord, had You willed, You could have destroyed them before, and me as well. Will You destroy us for what the foolish among us did?"﴾ When the earthquake seized them, Moses said, "O my Sustainer, had You willed, You could have destroyed them and me earlier. Will You destroy all of us for the deed of some foolish ones among us?"

This is an expression of complete submission and acceptance before Allah's power: that You could have destroyed us earlier if You had willed, and this expression of complete submission and acceptance is made as a preamble before the prayer for forgiveness. The prayer is: O Allah, are You destroying all of us because of a few foolish ones among us? By using the interrogative form, Moses conveys the impression that it is far from Your generous majesty to do such a thing. Thus this prayer is in the form of a question.

﴿It is but Your trial; by it You lead astray whom You will and guide whom You will.﴾ It is but Your trial, through which You lead astray whomever You wish and guide whomever You wish.

Moses (peace be upon him) explains the nature of what happens in this world: whatever befalls is a trial from Allah, and he states that he is not heedless of Allah's will as others are. This is the state of all trials. Those who recognize their reality and understand that it is a trial from their Lord and an examination through which they must pass, do so knowing it well and openly. But for those who are heedless of the reality of these events, these events and difficulties become a cause of misguidance. Moses (peace be upon him) expresses this reality for the purpose that follows, namely this request and prayer before Allah that He make them successful in this test.

﴿You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of those who forgive.﴾ You are our Guardian, so forgive us and have mercy on us, and You are the best of forgivers.

Since You are our Guardian, help us. We cannot emerge successfully from this trial without Your help and support. Along with this, we also need Your forgiveness and Your mercy.

The Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 156:

وَاكْتُبْ لَنَا فِيْ هٰذِهِ الدُّنْيَا حَسَـنَةً وَّفِي الْاٰخِرَةِ اِنَّا هُدْنَآ اِلَيْكَ ۔ اور ہمارے لیے اس دنیا کی بھلائی بھی لکھ دیجئے اور آخرت کی بھی ، ہم نے آپ کی طرف رجوع کرلیا۔

ہم مکمل طور پر تیری طرف لوٹ گئے ہیں ، تیری رحمت میں پناہ لیے ہوئے ہیں اور تیری جانب سے نصرت کے امیدوار ہیں۔ حضرت موسیٰ (علیہ السلام) نے تسلیم و رضا اور حکمت ابتلاء کو سمجھتے ہوئے مغفرت اور رحمت کی درخواست پیش فرمائی اور یہ حتمی اعلان کردیا کہ ہم اللہ کی پناہ گاہ کی طرف لوٹ گئے ہیں۔ اس طرح حضرت موسیٰ کی یہ دعا ہر مسلمان کے لیے خضوع و خشوع اور مقام کبریائی کے آداب کے عین مطابق ہے اور اس سے معلوم ہوتا ہے کہ ایک بندے کو اپنی درخواست کس طرح شروع کرنا چاہیے اور کس طرح اس کا اختتام ہونا چاہیے۔ اور اس کے بعد جواب یہ آتا ہے۔ قال عذابی اصیب بہ من اشاء و رحمتی وسعت کل شیئ۔ جواب میں ارشاد ہوا۔ سزا تو میں جسے چاہتا ہوں دیتا ہوں ، مگر میری رحمت ہر چیز پر چھائی ہوئی ہے۔

یہ اللہ کی بےقید مشیت کی حکمرانی کا اعلان ہے جس نے اس کائنات کے لیے اپنے اختیار سے ایک قانون وضع کیا ہے اور اسے اپنی مرضی سے جاری کیا ہے اور اس نے اپنے اوپر لازم کیا ہے کہ وہ اسے عدل و انصاف کے ساتھ چلائے گا۔ اور سچائی پر وہ چلے گا۔ کیونکہ عدل اللہ کی صفات میں سے اہم صفت ہے اور اللہ کی مشیت نہایت عدل کے ساتھ جاری رہتی ہے۔ اس لیے کہ اللہ نے اسی طرح کرنا چاہا ہے۔ لہذا عذاب اسی شخص پر آتا ہے جو اللہ کے نزدیک مستحق عذاب ہو ، یہی اس کی مشیت کا تقاضا ہے۔ اس کی رحمت نے ہر چیز کو اپنی لپیٹ میں لے رکھا ہے اور رحمت بھی مستحق رحمت کو ملتی ہے۔ یہ بھی اسی کی مشیت ہے ، کسی کو سزا دینے میں یا کسی پر انعامات کی بارش کرنے میں اللہ کی مشیت یونہی بغیر کسی منصوبے اور اتفاق کے نہیں چلتی۔ اللہ اس سے بہت برتر ہے۔

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 7, verse 157:

After establishing this principle, Allah now informs His Prophet Musa about certain events that are to come. This concerns the Muslim ummah, the final ummah, upon whom the rain of Allah's mercy will fall. This manner of expression shows that Allah's mercy is wider than this entire universe. Man cannot reach its limits; only Allah knows its extents. How great a mercy this will be.

﴿So I shall ordain it for those who fear Allah, pay the zakah, and those who believe in Our verses.﴾ ﴿Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written in the Torah and the Gospel with them. He enjoins on them what is right and forbids them what is wrong, makes lawful for them the good things and prohibits for them the evil things, and relieves them of their burden and the shackles that were upon them. So those who believe in him, honour him, support him, and follow the light that has been sent down with him, it is they who will be the successful.﴾

This was a great announcement, and it is evidence that the Children of Israel had been informed about the final Prophet in advance. This information was given through their great prophet Musa (peace be upon him), and it was given long before the final Prophet actually came. It was a certain announcement that he would be sent, that he would have these qualities, that his prophethood would be upon this method, and that the qualities of his ummah would be these. He would be an unlettered Prophet. He would enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. He would make lawful all good things and declare all evil things unlawful. He would remove the burdens that had been placed upon the Children of Israel because of their disobediences, and he would also open the restrictions in which they had bound themselves, provided they believed in him. The followers of that Prophet would be people who fear their Lord. They would pay zakah from their wealth and have certainty in Allah's verses. Those who believe in that Prophet would hold him in the highest reverence and honour him, support him, back him in every matter, and follow the light that is sent down upon him in the form of the Book of Allah. Such people will be among the successful.

Through the great prophet Musa (peace be upon him), Allah informed the Children of Israel well in advance, and so told mankind what His future religion would be, who would raise its banner in the future, who its followers would be, and upon whom His mercy would fall. Therefore, the followers of all heavenly religions now have no excuse for not acting upon this certain information.

This news was sent by the Lord of the worlds through Musa (peace be upon him), and it was announced at such an important time when Musa had gone with seventy chosen people to the appointed time for meeting Allah. This shows how heinous a crime the Children of Israel committed in their treatment of that Prophet, and that had they believed, there would have been many benefits for them, and by joining the believers they would have attained success.

This crime is being committed despite knowledge and proof, and history bears witness that the Children of Israel are a shameful people who have always opposed the final Prophet and the religion he brought. First the Jews continued this enmity, and after them the Crusaders took this task into their own hands. This is a most deceitful war, which they have declared against that Prophet and his religion. They are continuously engaged in this war, and have made it their practice.

Anyone who studies only the texts of the Qur'an concerning the People of the Book and their enmity to Islam, which are described in detail in Surah al-Baqarah, Surah Al 'Imran, Surah al-Nisa and Surah al-Ma'idah, will realise how comprehensive a war they waged against this religion, and with what cruelty and ruthlessness they fought against this religion.

And anyone who carefully reads the history after the Qur'an, from when the banners of Islam were raised in Madinah, an Islamic state was established, and from then until today, will find that these people left no stone unturned in trying to erase Islam, and they have always persisted in this.

The global Zionism and Crusaderism of the modern era have carried out actions against Islam that they could never carry out throughout the entire Islamic history. In this era they have plotted to eradicate this religion entirely from its roots. These people believe they will fight a final decisive battle against Islam, and for this they are adopting all measures, including those they have already tested throughout history, and they will also adopt all the modern methods they have now invented.

Today some simple-minded people who call themselves Muslims propose that all followers of religions should cooperate together against the atheists of the world. Yet these followers of religions are ready to slaughter every person who merely ascribes himself to Islam, and against the people of Islam they are waging wars whose features resemble the Crusader wars and the Inquisition courts of Andalusia. For example, they do this by establishing imperialist and colonial systems in other countries, or by creating conditions within independent countries through which they are constantly engaged in eliminating Islamic concepts. These people deny every kind of unseen belief, accept nothing except science and experiment, create moral corruption in the name of progress, convene conferences of orientalists to bring about changes in Islamic jurisprudence, declare usury lawful, and in addition to this, they wish to put the Islamic world on a wrong path concerning all prohibitions.

This is a savage war that these people have launched against Islam, although they were given the good news about Islam and the Prophet of Islam long ago. But instead of accepting it, they began this hostility and rancour against Islam and the Prophet of Islam.

Before the context unveils the next scene, there is a brief pause, and in this pause the address turns to the Prophet ﷺ, so that he continues to call all of humanity, and this is the ancient promise of Allah.

﴿Say: "O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all, the One to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth."﴾ Say, O Muhammad, to them: "O people, I am the Messenger of this God, to all of you, the One who is the owner of the kingdom of the heavens and the earth.

This is the final message. It is general for the whole world; it is not specific to any species or any race. The messages that passed before this message were local, or limited and for a limited period, and that period was the interval between the coming of one messenger and the next. During the times of those messages, humanity had taken only a few steps forward in progress, so that humanity would gradually progress and this caravan would reach the final message. In every message there has been some addition and amendment to certain rulings of the Shariah. Until the time of the final message came, this final message was, in its fundamentals and its branches, a complete message, and it was such that its principles could be implemented in the world in the form of new laws. And this final message came for the whole world, because the line of messengers ended with this final message. Now no other messenger will come. The Prophet ﷺ was chosen as an unlettered (ummi) Prophet so that his message would be a natural message, that he would convey whatever came from Allah, and that Allah alone would be his teacher. Therefore, this final message bears no stamp of any worldly teaching, and it is not influenced by human thoughts, so that the natural message reaches the nature of people and appeals to them.

﴿Say: "O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all."﴾ Say, O Muhammad, to them. O people, I am the Messenger of this God to all of you.

This verse is a Meccan verse in a Meccan surah. In it the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is commanded to announce his message for the whole world. This is a decisive reply to the People of the Book and the orientalists who say that Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, in Makkah, did not think about his message beyond the people of Makkah and the Quraysh, in a wide region. That is, that after the Quraysh, he extended his call to the Arabs, and after the Arabs, to the People of the Book, and he thought of spreading his call beyond the Arabian Peninsula to the whole world only when favourable circumstances encouraged him to do so. In reality, this is a great fabrication and is part of their ancient ideological war against Islam. And they continue this ideological war at all times.

The worrying matter is not why the People of the Book plot against this religion, nor why the orientalists, who are the leaders of the People of the Book and a formidable force fighting against Islam, do so. The worrying, and a very great worry, is that those who call themselves Muslims learn their religion from these embellishers, and with great pride they take them as teachers, and consider them their masters. They cite in their books the fabrications written by them. They take Islamic history too from such embellishers, and such deceived fools then also call themselves educated and cultured.

Now we return to the explanation of the verse. After commanding the Messenger of Allah to announce that his message is for all people, it is shown what the identity of the Lord to whom the call is being made is.

﴿The One to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. There is no deity except Him; He gives life and causes death.﴾ The One who is the owner of the kingdom of the heavens and the earth; there is no god except Him; He gives life and He gives death.

The Prophet ﷺ is a messenger for all people, and he is the emissary of the Lord who is the Lord of all creation, and they too are part of this universe. Allah is the one God and Sovereign. All people are His servants. The manifestation of your kingship and power is that you are the sole creator and the one who gives life.

Allah is the owner of the whole universe, He rules over all existence, He is the master of life and death. Therefore He alone is deserving that people follow His religion, and all His messengers are propagators of this very religion. In this way the Qur'an makes people recognise their Lord, so that they establish the system of their lives on obedience to this Messenger.

﴿So believe in Allah and His Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, who believes in Allah and His words, and follow him, that you may be guided.﴾ So believe in Allah and His sent Prophet, the unlettered one, who believes in Allah and His words; and follow him, so that you may hopefully find the right way.

There are very subtle indications within this call and invitation, and we should pause a little and reflect upon them.

٭ The first thing in this call and invitation is that you should believe in Allah and in the Messenger of Allah, and this faith is encapsulated in the blessed declaration: "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah."

٭ Without faith and affirmation in it, even the concept of Islam and faith is not possible. Yet here, before the invitation to faith, Allah is described and identified so that one believes in such a Allah, namely, "the One to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; there is no god or sovereign except Him; He gives life and He gives death." Therefore, the attributes of the God in whom faith is invited have been stated beforehand. Likewise, the attributes of the Messenger in whom faith is invited, so that all people accept him and obey him, have also been stated beforehand.

٭ Second, the unlettered Prophet also believes in Allah and in the words of Allah. This is clear, but within it is stated this important truth: before any call, there is a need that the caller himself believes in it, that the meaning of the call in his religion is clear, and that he has full certainty in it. That is why the Messenger who has been sent to all people "believes in Allah and in His words," and invites people to that very thing.

٭ Then, the demands of faith are also given here: that all people obey the Messenger, and also implement in their own lands the Shariah that he brought, and take his Sunnah as their guiding light. And this point is indicated thus: "So follow him, that you may hopefully find the right way." From this it is understood that if people do not obey the Messenger, there is no hope for their success. It is not sufficient that people accept faith in their hearts and then do not follow the Messenger. Practical following is in fact Islam.

The religion of Islam clarifies its nature and its essence on every occasion and in every context: Islam is not mere belief and ideology, nor is Islam merely the name of ritual worship. Islam is the name of complete following of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; all the guidance that descended upon the Messenger and all the Shariah laws that the Messenger established must be followed. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not only command that you obey Allah and His Messenger, nor only that you perform ritual worship in this way, but Islam has given a complete law and system, and has said that until you manifest the whole system of the Shariah and the Islamic law and system in your practical life, there is no hope of your success.

This is the religion of Islam, and no other picture of this religion is acceptable; only this form is acceptable, in which it is said: "(wattabiʿūhu) follow him, perhaps you will prosper." If only the doctrinal concept were desired, Allah would have sufficed by saying only this: "fa-āminū billāhi wa rasūlihi."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 7, verse 159:

What events took place after the severe earthquake in which seventy leaders of the Children of Israel were killed? Here it is only mentioned that Prophet Musa (peace be upon him) supplicated to Allah in extreme humility over their sudden death, but it does not tell us what became of those people. However, the way this story is related in other surahs shows that, because of Musa's supplication, Allah brought them back to life, and these people returned with Musa (peace be upon him) to their people like firm believers.

But before bringing the next links of the story, here the reality is stated that among the people of Musa there were also good people, who accepted the truth.

In the time of Musa there were good people among them as well. Among them was a group that spoke the truth and acted with justice. And even in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), some of the truth-seekers among them accepted Islam, especially those who found written in the Torah they had with them concerning the Unlettered Prophet. Their leader was his companion Abdullah ibn Salam (may Allah be pleased with him), and they would compare the Jews of that time with the prophecies about the Final Prophet that were present in the Torah. Moreover, the legal texts of the Shariah that they had were also in harmony with the Islamic legal system.

Now, after this important parenthetical point, the subject of the original story proceeds as follows.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 7, verse 160:

This was a special mercy of Allah, whose shade remained over Musa (peace be upon him). They committed kufr by worshipping the calf, and after making expiation for their mistake, their mistake was forgiven. They demanded to see Allah, and because of the earthquake their lives departed. Then, after the supplication and weeping of Musa, they were given life again. Similarly, they were divided into 12 groups according to their branches. They had 12 groups, and each group was a branch of one of the grandsons of Yaqub (peace be upon him). These people had carefully preserved their genealogies like tribes do.

﴿And We divided them into twelve tribes, as nations.﴾ And We divided this people into twelve households and gave them the form of permanent groups.

It appears that they were divided into these twelve groups merely for administrative purposes, in terms of the distribution of water, so that they would not encroach upon one another's rights.

﴿And We inspired Musa when his people asked him for water: "Strike the rock with your staff." And there gushed forth from it twelve springs. Every group knew its drinking place.﴾ And when Musa's people asked him for water, We revealed to him that he should strike a certain rock with his staff. So twelve springs suddenly burst forth from that rock, and each group fixed its own place for taking water.

A cloud was made to shade them because the desert had intense heat. Manna is a kind of sweet honey-like substance, and salwa is a quail-like bird. Thus, after providing water, all the necessities of life were made available to them.

﴿And We shaded them with clouds and sent down upon them manna and salwa. "Eat of the good things We have provided for you." And they did not wrong Us, but they were wronging themselves.﴾ We shaded them with clouds and sent down upon them manna and salwa. "Eat of the good things We have provided you," but after that, what they did, they did not wrong Us; rather, they continued to wrong themselves.

Here they were commanded to eat all the good things. It appears that at that time, because of their disobedience, certain good things had not yet been made unlawful for them.

Despite all these privileges, which are quite evident, these people were nonetheless ill-natured and always ready for sin and disobedience. From the final part of this verse, "and they did not wrong Us," it is understood that despite all these blessings and honours, the miraculous gushing of springs for them as a result of Musa striking the staff, the 21 springs that burst forth (as the text states), the shade of clouds over them in the scorching desert, and the provision of such praiseworthy food in the desert, they "wronged themselves": by committing kufr and wrongdoing they were themselves wronging themselves and making themselves deserving of punishment and torment.

Some examples of their wrongdoing will come later in the context, such as disobeying the commands of Allah and turning away from them. All these acts they committed against themselves; they wronged themselves. Allah is the Self-Sufficient King. If all creation disobeys Him, it causes no decrease in His kingdom, and if all creation becomes obedient, it causes no increase in His kingdom. By committing acts of disobedience, they in fact harm only themselves, both in this world and in the Hereafter.

Now observe how the Children of Israel responded to Allah's blessings and favours, and how their crooked nature chose to conduct itself.

...

They worshipped the calf, and Allah forgave them. They asked to see Allah, and an earthquake took their lives. Then Allah forgave them and brought them back to life. Allah bestowed great blessings upon them. Yet see how their crooked disposition is unwilling to walk the straight path. Without any justification they began to disobey, and they dared to alter the word that had been given to them. They were commanded: "Enter this city; it is yours." Which city it was is not named here, because the context does not require it. The condition imposed was that while entering the city they should recite a specific prayer in specific words, and enter prostrating, and give thanks for the victory granted to them, in exactly the manner in which the Holy Prophet (ﷺ) entered Makkah, prostrating upon his riding animal. Allah was promising these people that if they entered the city in this state, Allah would forgive all their faults, and that if any of them chose the path of greater goodness, Allah would shower upon them further of His blessings. But the condition of these people was such that some of them mocked and changed the very words of the prayer, and some changed the form of entry that had been prescribed. Why did they commit this disobedience? What benefit were they gaining by altering the words or by not prostrating? Nothing but the satisfaction of rebelliousness and crooked temperament!

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 162:

﴿So those among them who did wrong changed the word from what had been said to them.﴾ But those among them who were wrongdoers changed the statement that had been made to them into something else.

So now a punishment comes down upon them from the higher realm: Allah, who was sending down upon them manna and salwa, and over whom the clouds sent by Him were casting their shade, now sends down punishment upon them.

﴿So We sent upon them a punishment from the sky because they had been committing wrongdoing.﴾ And the result was that, as a consequence of their wrongdoing, We sent down upon them a punishment from the sky.

In this way, those among them who did wrong, that is, who disbelieved, wronged themselves, because they became deserving of the punishment of Allah. In this instance the Qur'an has not specified the punishment that was inflicted upon them, because the purpose and aim of this narrative is fulfilled even without specifying the punishment. The essential purpose and aim of the story is to show that those who disobey Allah become deserving of punishment, that Allah's warning becomes a reality, and that no disobedient person can escape the justice of Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 163:

Now the Children of Israel fall once again into disobedience and rebellion. This time they do not openly violate the commands of God, but resort to interpretation (ta'wil) and seek to escape from the commands. When they are tested, they do not show patience, because patience in trials and hardships belongs to those whose disposition is serious and who maintain self-restraint against personal desires and every kind of greed.

..

Here the Qur'an sets aside the account of the past conditions of the Children of Israel and begins to speak about those Children of Israel who were the descendants of the earlier Children of Israel and who were present in the time of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). These people were also in Madinah. The verses from "Wa-idh naqatna al-jabal fawqahum" onward are Madinan verses. They were revealed in Madinah as a dialogue with the Jews, and on account of their subject matter they were placed in this Meccan surah, so that the theme of the disobedience of the Children of Israel might be completed. God Most High commands the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to ask them about the event which is very famous among them and is recorded in their history. The Noble Qur'an regards the earlier and later Children of Israel as one and the same community. It also reminds them of the crimes that they committed in various periods, and in return for which God turned them into apes, and a punishment like transformation (maskh) descended upon them. Humiliation and the wrath of God were imposed upon them. Yes, those who conformed to the final Prophet of the end times will certainly have been safe from all these punishments, and because of this the burdens were lifted from their shoulders and the shackles that were upon them were opened.

Which was the town on the seashore? The Qur'an did not name it, because there was no need to name it, and the name of the village was in the minds of the addressees. The characters of this event were the leading people among the Children of Israel, and they lived in some coastal city. The Children of Israel had made the demand that a day of rest be fixed for them each week, a day for rest and worship, and on which their economic activities would be forbidden. The day of Sabbath was fixed for them. Now God, by putting them to the test concerning that day, wished to make them understand how they could free themselves from the allurements and greeds of life. And this was also necessary for the Children of Israel, because they had lived for a long time in the life of slavery, and the consciences of slaves change, and moral weaknesses arise within them. After physical liberation from humiliation and slavery, it is necessary that a person be freed from slavery mentally and morally as well, so that he may live a correct and righteous life. Especially those who occupy the station of a caller (da'i) to the truth; for them such moral training is an individual obligation (fard 'ayn). Then especially for those upon whom the responsibility of khilafah fi'l-ardh (vicegerency on earth) also rests and who occupy positions of government. In the matter of firmness of will and restraint over the self, the first trial was that of Adam and Eve, and they suffered a lapse; they tasted the tree of eternity under the seduction of Satan and coveted that their rule might become everlasting. And after them, every community to which God granted the office of khilafah fi'l-ardh was tested. Various peoples were certainly tested in various ways and under various circumstances.

But the Children of Israel did not succeed in this trial, because before this they had repeatedly broken their promises and repeatedly shown rebellion. The trial occurred thus: on the Sabbath day the fish would come near the shore. Their catching would become easy, but they could not catch these fish, because hunting on the Sabbath was forbidden. And their own desire was included in this prohibition. When it was not the Sabbath and they went out to hunt, the fish were not near, as they used to see them on the Sabbath. This was the matter which God wished, through the Messenger (ﷺ), to remind them of: let them recall what they did with this prohibition.

"And ask them about the town which was by the sea, when they transgressed in the Sabbath, when their fish came to them openly on their Sabbath day, and on the day they did not observe the Sabbath, they did not come to them. Thus did We test them because they used to transgress."

The reply: Here is the simple answer to the question of how this incident of the fish came about: it was an extraordinary event beyond the normal course of things, that the fish swam in large numbers near the shore, and if anyone caught them, he could catch them with ease. Today some people, by calling the laws established by God (qawanin kawniyyah) "natural laws" (qawanin tabi'iyyah), claim that nothing can happen contrary to them; this is merely their assertion. According to the Islamic conception of life, the matter is not like this. God, Glorified is His Majesty, Himself created this universe and placed within it the natural laws which He has deposited here. This is the will of God. The will of God is not bound by the laws He Himself has made, such that it cannot go against them. Even after these laws, the Divine will remains free. Those to whom God has given true knowledge are not unmindful of this point. If the wisdom and will of God required that the good of human beings lies in these laws of nature functioning correctly, this does not mean in any way that the will of God has become confined within the grip of these laws. At whatever time the will of God wishes that an event should occur contrary to these laws, it can happen. Especially in accordance with those laws, every particular event that occurs (even if a leaf falls) occurs in accordance with God's system of decree. It is not the case that these causes and effects have now become independent of the Divine will. We say that the system of natural laws too is bound by the will, so that whatever particular event occurs in accordance with natural laws, or contrary to them, occurs in accordance with God's knowledge and decree. Therefore, an event in accordance with habit and an event beyond habit are in reality one and the same. There is no self-operation in this order of the cosmos, as some superficial people appear to think. Some philosophers have now begun to understand this matter. (See Fi Zilal al-Quran, vol. 7, pp. 520, 522.)

In any case, this event occurred at a coastal settlement of the Children of Israel. Thus, in this trial, some people fall. Their resolves are defeated. They forget the firm covenant they made with their Lord, they begin to resort to stratagems, and stratagems and excuses are the old method of the Jews. When crookedness settles in hearts and fear of God disappears, a person seeks out only excuses. Then people play with the rulings of the texts, and the purpose and meanings disappear from sight. The fundamental point is that the protection of any law is not possible through its clauses and wordings. Adherence to a law and regulation is with the hearts, and hearts adhere to the law only when there is piety and God-consciousness (khashyah) within them. Only a pious heart that fears God can protect the law. And when a people wishes to protect a law with heart and soul, people cannot make excuses about it. But if the protection of a law is sought merely through governmental means, and compliance is enforced merely by fear of punishment, this can never happen in that way. Is it possible for a government to appoint a watchman over every individual, one who could keep complete watch over him both in solitude and in a crowd?

This is why all those legal schemes fail whose enforcing power is not the inner piety and inner inclination of the people, and likewise all those systems of life that some humans have devised for other humans, and in which the enforcing power is not based on the fear of God, remain unsuccessful. This is why all those institutions fail whose responsibility is the implementation of laws. Then the supervisory institutions over them also fail (corruption flourishes, and the anti-corruption institution becomes corrupt), and their work becomes superficial from beginning to end.

Accordingly, the people of that village began to make stratagems in connection with the violation of this law. It is said that on the Sabbath day they would set up barriers to encircle the fish, and when it was not the Sabbath they would quickly come and catch the fish. Then they would console their hearts thus: that they had, after all, not touched the fish on the Sabbath day. The fish would nevertheless be in the water, within their enclosures. And from among them a group of good people came forward. It criticized those who engaged in these stratagems; these people would admonish them, saying: fear God and do not do this. And a third group of righteous people also came forward, who said that those critics were doing a pointless thing, since those people had become involved in a matter for which admonition and criticism would be of no benefit. God has decreed that they be punished and destroyed.

The people of this seaside town were divided into three groups, or three communities. According to Islamic concepts, an ummah (community) is a collection of people who hold one ideology, whose thinking is alike, and who have one leadership. The ummah here does not mean the ummah of the ancient jahili (pre-Islamic ignorance) period, nor the ummah according to modern jahili concepts. According to jahili concepts, an ummah is a collection of people who live in one particular region and are under one government. This is not the Islamic meaning of ummah. It is a term of ancient or modern jahiliyyah.

In Arabic lexicon, the word ummah is also used simply for a population or a group of people. For example, ﴿When he arrived at the water of Madyan, he found there a group of people watering [their flocks]﴾. Ummah is also used in the sense of leadership and imamate: ﴿Indeed, Ibrahim was a [complete] ummah, devoutly obedient to Allah, inclining toward truth﴾. From this it is understood that Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was a separate ummah, meaning a leader. However, these linguistic meanings do not contradict the technical meaning of the word, which is a collection of people who share one belief and one outlook.

In short, the people of this village were divided into three groups. One group adopted rebellion. The second group stood in opposition to them, carrying out the duty of reform and admonition. The third group was neutral: it neither supported the rebels nor supported those who enjoined good. These three approaches to thought and activity are described here as three ummahs.

When advice and admonition brought them no benefit, and those who walked the path of misguidance kept walking on it, the punishment of Allah became inevitable for them. The warning that Allah had conveyed to them reached its time. Only those who forbade evil (﴿those who forbade evil﴾) remained among the saved, while those who were rebellious were seized by the punishment. The details will come later. As for the third group, which was neutral, the Qur'an says nothing about it. Perhaps the reason these neutral people are made nasiyan mansiyya (forgotten, utterly forgotten) here is that they have no importance and are not worthy of being mentioned here, because they did not adopt a positive stance but merely took up the weak position of negative refusal. Therefore Allah did not mention them either, even though they may have escaped the punishment.

The punishment inflicted on these people was because they had sunk into disobedience and defiance, and the Qur'an describes this as kufr (disbelief). Sometimes it is called zulm (wrongdoing), and sometimes fisq (transgression). In the Qur'an it is frequently the practice to describe kufr and shirk as zulm and fisq, and this manner of expression differs from the jurisprudential and legal terminology that was adopted in later ages. Therefore, the Qur'anic manner of expression is not bound by that jurisprudential terminology, because technical terms were determined later.

And what was this severe punishment? It was that the forms of human beings were changed into the form of monkeys, because they had cast themselves down from the rank of humanity. This was because they had abandoned the most distinctive characteristic of humanity, namely the will's dominance over human desires, and they became bound by desires as animals are. Therefore it was said to them: "Very well, then become animals, for this is the station you have chosen for yourselves."

As to how they became monkeys, and how their form was changed: did they themselves transform and become monkeys, or did monkeys begin to be born from them? Regarding this, there are numerous reports in the books of tafsir, and the Qur'an is silent on this point, and no report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has been transmitted concerning it. Therefore, we do not go deeper into this matter.

The creation of man too came about through the word "Be" (kun), and the change in his form also came about through the word "Be, you apes, despised and abased" (kūnū qiradatan khāsi'īn), meaning: "Become despised and abased apes." So they became despised and abased apes, because there is no command that can stand against the command of Allah, nor can anyone reject it.

After this punishment, Allah ordered an everlasting curse upon all of them, and excepted only those who would believe in the Last Prophet, because they had persisted in these disobediences for a long period, and now their period of disobedience had ended. The Will of Allah issued this lasting decree concerning them, which is irrevocable.

This is a standing decree, and it has been a fact since it was issued. From time to time God has sent some power to subdue the Jews, and in general this ruling will continue to operate in the future as well. God will keep imposing such powers upon them, and these powers will keep inflicting on them the same kind of punishment whenever they flourish and adopt an attitude of rebellion. God will keep sending such powers against them, and they will keep striking them with a severe blow, because this is a rebellious and insubordinate people: when they emerge from one act of disobedience, they enter into another. If one of their crookednesses is corrected, another crookedness arises within them.

At times it appears as though this continuous curse upon them may have ended, and that perhaps the Jews are now honoured and possessed of power. But the reality is that these are among the intervals of history. It is not known now whom God will impose upon them, or which nation will be imposed upon them after their periods of humiliation.

God has enforced this order upon them until the Day of Resurrection, and He has also informed His Prophet and his ummah of it in the Qur'an. Yet despite this eternal decision, God's attribute of mercy, forgiveness and pardon remains in its place. ﴿Indeed your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. By His attribute of swiftness of punishment, He seizes those people upon whom the descent of punishment has become true, as He seized the people of the seaside town. And by His attribute of mercy and forgiveness, He pardons everyone who has repented, such as those among the Children of Israel who believed in acknowledging the final Prophet, because the final Prophet was written about in their Torah. God does not take revenge upon anyone, nor is anyone wronged in His court. There, everyone is treated with justice; rather, in that court a pretext is needed for pardon and mercy.

Following this, the story moves forward along historical lines. After Moses, his successors, the prophets, and the generations who came after them in succession, the address now turns to the generation that existed at the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and to the contest between the Muslim community (jama'at muslimah) and them.

This passage too is Madani, and it has been placed here so that the account of the Children of Israel after Moses (peace be upon him) may be brought to completion. These are the conditions of the time when the Jews had spread far and wide over the earth. Their various groups had formed, and they had adopted different religions and beliefs. Their schools of thought and paths had diverged. Among them some were righteous and some were ordinary people. At times they were tested, sometimes by being made prosperous and sometimes by being made to suffer hardship, so that they might return to the straight path, find guidance, and walk upon the right way.

﴿And We divided them into nations upon the earth; among them are the righteous, and among them are others than that. And We tested them with good things and bad, so that they might return.﴾ We divided them into many nations, scattered throughout the land in pieces. Some of them were righteous and some were different from that. And We kept testing them with good and bad circumstances, so that perhaps they would turn back.

Trials from Allah are also a form of mercy, and through these trials a person keeps constantly remembering Allah and does not remain heedless, for heedless people fall into destruction.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 169:

The attributes of those who came after are mentioned here: these people were heirs of the Book, they read it, but they did not shape their lives according to it, and neither their hearts nor their conduct were affected by this Book. After Musa (peace be upon him), their condition became such that their faith had become their culture. It was a knowledge that they read, but whenever they saw any of the worldly aims, they would pounce upon it, whether it was lawful or unlawful, and they held the naive hope that Allah would surely forgive us. But after hoping for pardon, if any worldly interests came before them, they would again pounce upon them.

﴿Did not the covenant of the Book get taken from them, that they would not say about Allah except the truth, and they have studied what is in it?﴾ Was not a covenant taken from them in the Book that they would not say about Allah anything but the truth? And they have themselves read what is written in the Book?

Was not a promise taken from them in the Book that they would not argue about the Book of Allah with baseless proof and argument, that they would not resort to trickery to evade the demands of the explicit texts, and that they would say nothing from Allah except the truth? On the contrary, their conduct is that as soon as they see worldly interests they pounce upon them, and they sit with hopes that perhaps Allah will forgive us. And they who attribute wrong things to Allah justify themselves in this, because they are baseless hopefuls of forgiveness, although they know that Allah certainly forgives those who repent, but only those who have truly repented and have in practice abandoned sin, whereas their conduct is not such. Their state is that as soon as any unlawful gain appears before them, these people become restless and pounce upon it, although they know well the commands and demands of the Book of Allah.

Yes! They do read, but reading benefits only the person in whose heart the teaching settles; there are many readers far from the Qur'an in their hearts. These people teach the Book of Allah so that they may also interpret it, change its meanings, and through fatwas made to suit their own purposes obtain worldly benefits. The real point is that these people should read religion merely for the sake of reading, and not make it their outlook and belief, nor fear Allah and be apprehensive of His punishment.

﴿And the Hereafter is better for those who are mindful of Allah. Will you not then reason?﴾ The abode of the Hereafter is better for the God-fearing; do you not understand even this much?

Yes, this is the real point about the abode of the Hereafter, which belongs to those who fear Allah. Only in their way of life is there talk of the Hereafter, and only these people can get out of the sphere of the attraction of worldly interests. No heart and no system of life can be correct without this. The reform of a human being, of his self, his psychology, and his practical life, can also be achieved only through concern for the Hereafter. Otherwise, let it be told what motive could stop a person from being engulfed by all those aims. What could prevent a person from greed and avarice and from encroaching on the rights of others? And what is it that restrains the heart from desires and controls the human self's appetites? Amid the agitating struggle of life, what gives a person a satisfying sense of tranquility? Only the hope of the reward of the Hereafter, because of which a person can endure the deprivations of this world for the sake of the benefit of the Hereafter. Moreover, in the battle between truth and falsehood, in the war between good and evil, in the decision between worldly aims and otherworldly benefits, a person can remain steadfast, while evil is engaged in rebellion and falsehood is exceeding all bounds.

The truth is that in this agitating struggle of the world, only concern for the Hereafter and belief in the Hereafter can become a cause of certainty and peace for a person. For those who fear Allah, this is extremely beneficial. Such people act with forgiveness and overlooking, they remain above defilements, and they remain firm on the path of truth; tests that make feet slip and shake people do not affect only the one who is God-fearing and believes in the Hereafter. The hearts of such people are content and steadfast, and these people have full certainty of success.

In today's era, the proponents of communism wish to erase this unseen reality from the veil of our hearts. They want to erase the concept of the Hereafter from our beliefs and ideologies, and they want to kindle in our hearts that fire of frenzy which can be extinguished only by certainty of the Hereafter. Apart from disbelief in the Hereafter, the diseases of bribery, corruption, greed, oppression and negligence are found in abundance, and such people, wherever they are, are treacherous and thieves.

The claim that there is complete contradiction between the unseen world and the observed world, that is, between science and the unseen world, is a plague of the ignorance of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. As far as genuine scientists and people of knowledge are concerned, they rejected this theory long ago. Only the ignorant of the twentieth century occasionally recite it. This is an ignorance that does not keep any distance from human nature. That is why the lives of the victims of this ignorance fall into disorder, and this is now a comprehensive corruption, which as a result threatens the destruction of all humanity. But it is regrettable that this is an extremely cunning Zionist plan. Behind this Zionist plan lies the purpose that the true strength, which is the backbone of human life, be stripped from all the people of the world, so that these Zionists may make the whole world subservient to their aims; and these people spread this Zionist planners' plan everywhere through their drummers. In the situation that the Zionists have created throughout the world, all people are automatically implementing this plan in practice.

Concern for the Hereafter and fear of Allah are two most important issues of human life. The Qur'an gives to those who are running headlong behind worldly interests this lesson: that they should use their intellect: "The abode of the Hereafter is better for the God-fearing; do you not understand even this much?"

If the opportunity to decide is given to reason, and the influence of carnal desires is absent from it; if knowledge and science are taken in their true sense, and ignorance is not called knowledge, then the final verdict would certainly be that in comparison with this lowly world, the Hereafter is better. Taqwa and fear of Allah should become provision for the believers for both this world and the Hereafter.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 170:

وَالَّذِيْنَ يُمَسِّكُوْنَ بِالْكِتٰبِ وَاَقَامُوا الصَّلٰوةَ ۭاِنَّا لَا نُضِيْعُ اَجْرَ الْمُصْلِحِيْنَ ۔ جو لوگ کتاب کی پابندی کرتے ہیں اور جنہوں نے نماز قائم کر رکھی ہے ، یقیناً ایسے نیک لوگوں کا اجر ہم ضائع نہیں کریں گے "

This is a rebuke directed at those people to whom a covenant was given that they would hold firmly to the Book and study it, but despite the covenant they did not hold firmly to the Book. Although they did take hold of it, they did not act upon it, nor do they implement it in their ideology and practice, nor do they put it into effect in their system of life. Although this is an implied rebuke, the principles established in it remain for all generations to come.

The word tamassuk (holding firmly) conveys a meaning that presents before the mind a practical picture. The Qur'an has made a non-material thing tangible through tamassuk. The meaning is: hold this Book with strength and enforce its principles with seriousness and earnestness, in the way that Allah desires the Book to be taken: without obstinacy, without distortion, and without constriction. Therefore, seriousness, strength and firmness are one thing, and obstinacy, constriction and dejection are another. Seriousness, strength and firmness are not the opposite of ease (yusr), but they are the opposite of laxity (sahl-angari) and the flimsiness of character. This situation is not the opposite of breadth of heart (wus'at-i-qalbi), but it is the opposite of irreligiousness. It is not the opposite of consideration of circumstances and wisdom (hikmah), but it does not flow along with the current of circumstances and events. That events should conform to the Shariah is the policy; it is not the policy that we keep adapting the Shariah to the actual state of affairs.

Holding firmly to the Book of Allah, and observing prayer and the other rites of worship ('ibadah), are two important aspects of the Islamic system of life. Here, holding to the Book has been specified with a particular colour, namely the rites of worship; that is, along with the entire Islamic system of life, the rites of worship have been made obligatory for the reform of people. The meaning is that Islam's reform of society is not possible without both holding to the Book within it and the observance of worship within it; this is indicated by the words: "Surely We do not waste the reward of the reformers" (la nudi'u ajra al-muslihin). That is, we do not waste the reward of the righteous and the reformers. In other words, firmly holding the entire Book and acting upon acts of worship is the means of the reform of society.

If either of these two things is missing from a society, it falls into corruption. That is, the Book of Allah is not held firmly in it, and people do not judge their affairs according to the Book of Allah. Second, the worship of Allah is lost from it, which is the means of purifying the hearts. For if hearts are not pure, people will engage in trickery like the Jews in dealing with the commands of Allah, because there will be no taqwa (God-consciousness) or fear of God in their hearts.

The Islamic system is a complete system; it is interconnected. Through acts of worship the rust of hearts is cleared, and then human bodies accept the commands of the Book with uprightness; thus practical and spiritual reform is completed. This is Allah's method of reform, and apart from it we cannot adopt any other method of reform. Whoever does so will have misfortune and punishment as his destiny.

This passage is at the end of the story, where it is told how Allah seized the Children of Israel.

﴿And [recall] when We raised the mountain above them﴾.

This was an unforgettable covenant, because it was taken in circumstances that cannot be forgotten. This covenant was taken at a time when the mountain overshadowed them as though it were a canopy. They were thinking that it was about to fall upon them. This is because, as soon as the covenant was taken, they began to act rebelliously. Therefore the covenant was taken from them in such a state that, after it, they could not even think of breaking it again. In these extraordinary circumstances they were told: take the Book of Allah seriously, act upon it firmly, and after this pact do not show treachery, slackness or retreat; keep the guidance of the Book of Allah in mind. Perhaps in this way your hearts will be softened and your connection with Allah will remain intact.

But the Children of Israel remained the Children of Israel. Allah's word had come true for them; Allah had made them the superpower of their time. He showered blessings upon them. Yet they did not give thanks to Allah. They paid no regard to the covenant of Allah. They did not remember the covenant with Allah, and therefore they came to that end; otherwise, Allah does not wrong anyone.

Lesson 81 At a Glance

The theme of this lesson is the doctrine of Tawhid (the oneness of God) and the refutation of shirk (associating partners with God). The stories narrated throughout this entire surah also revolve around this same doctrine of Tawhid, in the sense that all the Messengers called people to this belief and all of them warned their people of the evil end of shirk. But after the reminder and the warning, the circumstances that had been warned of did come to pass.

However, in this lesson the issue of Tawhid is taken up from a new angle. It is discussed in depth, from the viewpoint of human nature (fitrah) upon which Allah has created man. When man was in the world of the seed (alam-e-dhurriyyah), Allah took a covenant from the whole of creation and from humankind, asking whether He was not their Lord. The acknowledgement of lordship was placed into human nature, and the truth is that human beings carry awareness of the existence of their Creator and Lord in the depths of their being. The question then arises: why, after this, were Messengers sent? The answer is that the coming of Messengers is purely for reminder, and a Messenger comes as a bearer of good tidings and a warner. He comes to reform those who have deviated from fitrah. Such people need to be reminded. The doctrine of Tawhid is in essence a covenant that has been settled between human nature and the Creator of nature since the earliest period of man. Therefore, man has no justification for breaking this covenant. Even if no Messenger had come to them for reminder, it is still Allah's pure mercy and favour that, despite this, He sent Messengers to reform the deviators, and people were not left solely to their intellects, because the intellect can make mistakes. Thus Allah sent Messengers so that people would have no argument left, such that beyond the demand of fitrah, Messengers too had come.

In this lesson the issue of Tawhid is taken up from this angle, and from this angle several lines are drawn.

The first is a historical line. In it, the historical role of a certain person is alluded to. Some narrations mention that his connection is with the history of the Children of Israel. But the more correct view is that he is not connected with any specific, determined event or particular time and place. Rather, this is a depiction of a psychological state that repeatedly occurs. For example, a person to whom Allah has given knowledge: the demand of that knowledge, and what is expected from it, is that he be guided and steadfast upon the truth. But suddenly this unexpected situation appears, that he flees from the demands of his knowledge. He derives no benefit from his knowledge, and he walks on the path of misguidance shoulder to shoulder with one who has no knowledge at all. Indeed, this learned person proves to be more mischievous, more misguided and more wretched than the ignorant one, and this happens when knowledge has not been given the flavour of faith. For it is through the hue of faith that this lamp of knowledge becomes luminous, and a beacon of light for the traveller.

Another line or thread may be observed. In it another story or example of the deviation of human nature is presented, showing how shamelessly man abandons Tawhid and adopts shirk. A married couple supplicates Allah, saying that if they are given a righteous child, they will surely give thanks to Allah alone. Up to this point they are in harmony with the demands of fitrah. But when the child is born, these people, contrary to expectation, associate others with Allah in the process of the child's birth, and a crookedness enters their fitrah.

A third line concerns the perceptive faculties found within the human being itself: if these faculties are not used properly, then a rational human being falls from the rank and station of humanity to the level of the animal, and the result is that he becomes deserving of Hell and becomes its fuel. The condition of such people is that they have hearts but no faculty of comprehension in them; they have eyes but no sight; they have ears but do not hear. Such people run after misguidance in such a way that there is neither return nor opportunity for return.

There is an allusive line: the guidance that is given is to keep the heart and mind awake, and to continually reflect upon every matter, to observe this system of the heavens and the earth, what Allah has created within them, and then that for everything He has fixed a time for its end. Therefore, you should give attention to the call of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and reflect that the bearer of this call is called mad and misguided.

In one line, severe criticism is directed at them, and this criticism concerns the gods they call upon besides Allah. Yet those whom they call upon lack even the basic attributes of divinity; indeed, even the ordinary signs of life are absent from them.

This lesson concludes with the instruction to you that you should challenge them and their gods to call upon something. It is said that you should announce complete disavowal of them, separate yourself from their deities and worship, and take refuge with the Protector besides whom there is no protector. "Alladhi nazzal al-kitaba wa huwa yatawalla al-salihin." My Protector is He who sent down the Book, and He supports the righteous.

Earlier, at the end of the previous lesson, a mountain was lifted over the Children of Israel and a covenant was taken from them, and this lesson began with mention of the great covenant made with humanity, which was settled with human nature. This covenant too is in the form of a scene which, in its beauty and majesty, is far higher than that scene.
