Lesson 81 – Explanation of Verses 172 to 198

....

وَاِذْ اَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنْۢ بَنِيْٓ اٰدَمَ مِنْ ظُهُوْرِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ وَاَشْهَدَهُمْ عَلٰٓي اَنْفُسِهِمْ ۚ اَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ ۭ قَالُوْا بَلٰي ڔ شَهِدْنَا ڔ اَنْ تَقُوْلُوْا يَوْمَ الْقِيٰمَةِ اِنَّا كُنَّا عَنْ هٰذَا غٰفِلِيْنَ ۔

And [O Prophet], remind the people of the time when your Lord brought forth from the descendants of Adam, from their loins, their offspring, and made them testify concerning themselves, [saying], "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we testify." This was lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were unaware of this."

This is an astonishing cosmic scene. Among all the concepts that have been transmitted to us in every language, no example of this concept is to be found anywhere. When human concepts and perceptive faculties have truly comprehended this concept, it appears to be a strange concept. Human cells have been taken from the entire cosmos, and they are addressed in the same way as a complete human being is addressed, and they too respond like a wise human being, since they possess the capacity for speech. These cells acknowledge, bear witness to the Tawhid, and affix their signature to this great covenant, and they are within the loins of human beings.

When a person beholds this beautiful, astonishing and unique scene, he is deeply moved in the depths of his personality. He sees within the minute cells the particles of the human race floating in the atmosphere. Each particle is alive at that moment, and each possesses complete capacity; within each particle are all the human attributes, and it merely awaits permission for development. From the unknown vastness of this cosmos it awaits manifestation and witness. These atomic beings accept this covenant. Although the worlds that come within our sight are known, this existing particle has not yet come upon the stage of visibility.

The Qur'an presented this beautiful, astonishing and unique scene in order to impress upon the mind this great truth, which is present and firmly established at a very profound level within the reality of this cosmos. The Qur'an presented this scene 1400 years ago. At that time, people did not have much scientific information about the creation of the cosmos. Human knowledge on this subject consisted of a few illusions. Later, in subsequent times, humanity discovered some facts about human nature and the creation of humankind. Thus these scientific discoveries, that within the gene are contained all the characteristics that appear in a human being in later stages, and that there is also present the characteristics of a complete individual who later emerges as a person, although it is in the form of a cell, have come to light. Within these cells is recorded the record of three thousand million human beings, together with all their characteristics. The volume of these cells is no more than one cubic centimetre, that is, the size of the eye of a needle, and if this information had been told to people at that time, people would have said that this person is mad. But Allah spoke the truth: "Sanurihim ayatina fi al-afaqi wa fi anfusihim hatta yatabayyana lahum annahu al-haqq." We shall show them Our signs in the horizons and within their own selves, until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Abbas: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Your Lord touched the back of Adam, and from it emerged all the seeds that Allah was going to create until the Day of Resurrection. Then Allah took a firm promise from them and made them witnesses against themselves, and asked: "Am I not your Lord?" Then they all replied: "Yes!" This narration is transmitted from Ibn Abbas both as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) and as a mawquf (traced to a companion) report. But the mawquf report of Ibn Abbas is stronger.

The question is: how was this scene, and how did Allah bring forth all the created beings and record their testimony against themselves? And what was the manner of addressing them, and how were the question and answer? The answer is that the modality of the acts of Allah is also among the unseen matters, and until a person possesses the mental faculty to perceive the essence of the Divine Being, it is not possible for him to perceive the modality of the Divine acts. For when the essence of a reality cannot be perceived, how can its derivatives, that is its modes, be perceived? As for all the acts that are attributed to Allah, such as: "Thumma istawa ila al-sama'i wa hiya dukhan" – then He rose over the heaven, and it was smoke; "Thumma istawa ala al-'arsh" – then He settled upon the Throne; "Yamhu Allahu ma yasha'u wa yuthbit" – Allah erases what He wills and establishes; "Wal-samawatu matwiyyatun bi yamînih" – and the heavens will be folded in His right hand; "Wa ja'a rabbuka wal-malaku saffan saffan" – your Lord will come and the angels will stand rank upon rank; "Ma yakunu min najwa thalathatin illa huwa rabi'uhum" – there is no secret conference of three but He is their fourth; and others, all these verses concerning the acts of Allah: these acts have certainly occurred and will occur, but the modality of them is difficult to perceive. This is because the conception of the modality is itself a branch of the conception of the essence. And the Divine Being is such that there is nothing like unto Him. Therefore the essence of Allah and the modality of His acts cannot be perceived, for in that case resemblance would necessarily follow, and nothing resembles Him. Every attempt to understand the acts of Allah through human acts has ended in error, because there is a difference between Allah and the created in essence. The attempts of philosophers and scientists to understand the modalities of Divine acts in the colour of human acts have proved fruitless.

Furthermore, it has also been interpreted that this verse refers to human nature. Allah has placed within human nature the acknowledgement of the Divine lordship, and by nature a person acknowledges the Lord, although certain external factors divert him from the straight path of nature.

Ibn Kathir says: The exegetes of the earlier and later generations have said that it means that Allah created people upon the nature of Tawhid, as has been transmitted earlier in the hadith of Abu Hurairah and Iyad ibn Himar al-Mujashi'i. Hasan al-Basri narrated from them, and whoever explained this verse in accordance with this said: Allah did not use the word Adam but said "Banu Adam," and He did not say "min zahrihi" but said "min zuhurihim" – "from their backs." The word "dhurriyyatahum" also shows that it refers to people who are born generation after generation in this world at various times, as in another verse where Allah said: "Wa huwa alladhi ja'alakum khala'if al-ard" – He is the One who made you successors upon the earth; "Ja'alakum khala'if al-ard" – He makes you successors on the earth; and in another verse: "Kama ansha'akum min dhurriyyati qawmin akharin" – as He produced you from the offspring of another people.

Then Allah said: "Wa ashhadahum 'ala anfusihim" – making them witness concerning themselves, He asked: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: Yes. That is, He brought them into existence and asked them, and they acknowledged it, that is at the time of birth. The scholars say that testimony is sometimes verbal, as in the Qur'an: "Qalu shahidna 'ala anfusina wa gharrat-hum al-hayat al-dunya wa shahidu 'ala anfusihim annahum kanu kafirin" – They said: We bear witness against ourselves, and the life of this world deceived them, and they bore witness against themselves that they were disbelievers. And sometimes it is circumstantial testimony, such as: "Ma kana li al-mushrikina an ya'muru masajida Allahi shahidina 'ala anfusihim bil-kufr" – it is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah while they bear witness against themselves to disbelief. That is, in those circumstances they bear witness to disbelief, although they do not call themselves disbelievers with their tongues. "Wa innahu 'ala dhalika lashahid" – and he is a witness to that. Likewise, a question is sometimes verbal and sometimes circumstantial: "Wa atakum min kulli ma sa'altumuhu" – and He gave you of all that you asked of Him.

Commentators say: if people were actually raised up and made to affirm this, and that affirmation were binding on them, then they should also have remembered it. If it is said that the report of the Messenger ﷺ about this event is sufficient, the answer is that the polytheists deny all the reports of the Noble Messenger, and this hadith was presented as proof against them. Therefore it is clear that what is meant is the fitrah (innate nature) upon which all human beings have been created, that they affirm Tawhid. For this reason, after this, all people are addressed with "an taqulu" (lest you say), that is, so that on the Day of Resurrection you cannot say, "We were indeed heedless of this," or say, "Only our forefathers were polytheists before us" ("inna ashraka aba'una").

Some hadiths also point to this fitrah. In the Sahihayn, Abu Hurairah narrates that the Messenger ﷺ said: "Every child is born upon the fitrah" (in some narrations: "upon the millah"), and then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Magian, just as animals give birth to perfect young. Is there any child born with its ears cut off?

In the Sahihayn there is a narration from Iyad ibn Himar. The Messenger ﷺ said: Allah says, "I created My servants upright; then the devils came to them and turned them away from their religion, and made unlawful for them what I had made lawful."

Ibn Jarir has transmitted the hadith of Aswad ibn Sari'. He said: I took part in four campaigns with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said that after a battle the people also killed the children. This reached the Messenger of Allah, and it weighed heavily upon him. Then he said: "What is the condition of those people who kill children?" A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, are they not the children of the polytheists?" Upon this the Messenger said: "The best of you are also the children of the polytheists. Every child that is born is born upon the fitrah, and remains upon that fitrah until he begins to speak. Then his parents make him a Jew or a Christian." Hasan said: "This is the meaning of the words of Allah: ﴿And when your Lord brought forth from the children of Adam, from their loins, their offspring﴾..." and so on to the end.

As for me, I do not consider this verse, in its literal meaning, to be far-fetched, since its occurrence is possible just as Allah has described it: "And remind them of the time when your Lord brought forth from the children of Adam, from their loins, their offspring, and made them testify concerning themselves" — and there is nothing contrary to reason in it. But the interpretation adopted by the commentators above, that it refers to the state of fitrah, is also not far-fetched; Ibn Kathir, Hasan al-Basri and others have adopted it. And Allah knows best.

In any case, it should be kept in view that human nature has made a covenant with Allah that it will ascribe partnerlessness to Him alone. The reality of Tawhid is deposited in human nature. When every child receives life, this covenant comes with its nature; it remains upon that fitrah until some external factor turns it away from that fitrah. These external factors make use of the natural capacity of man, for just as Allah has placed Tawhid in the fitrah, so He has also given the fitrah the capacity to accept guidance or misguidance. And the circumstances in which a child is born influence it.

The reality of Tawhid is not deposited only within human nature; the concept of Tawhid is also placed in this entire universe, since human nature is in any case a part of this vast natural system. Human existence is not severed from the existence of this universe. It too moves according to the same law by which the whole universe moves. Just as this whole universe accepts the commands and signs of Allah, so this small human being's nature also accepts the cosmic influences.

The law of Tawhid that governs this universe is clearly manifest in the form and shape of the universe. In it are the harmony of the cosmos, the mutual connection and proportion of its parts, the system of movement of this whole universe and its parts, the continuity of its laws and the constant flow of the entire universe in accordance with these laws, and then, according to the limited knowledge that man has so far attained, the particles of which this universe is composed and the rays emitted from the breaking and splitting of those particles — all of this is evidence of the oneness of the Creator of this universe.

Man is unveiling day and night the hidden secrets of this all-encompassing unity, from which the unity of the universe's temperament becomes known, the uniformity of its laws becomes known, and this uniformity is not automatic; rather everything is occurring according to the will of Allah and His system of destiny. In any case, we do not rely upon human discoveries either, since human knowledge is based on conjecture and estimation. Human knowledge is not certain knowledge, because the means of perception given to man are also not certain, and we cannot know with certainty what the Divine Law (namus-i-Ilahi) is. As far as human knowledge and the means of knowledge are concerned, man can only become acquainted with reality. Even regarding the greatest law of this universe, our true source of information and knowledge is only the Messenger of the Creator of the universe. The Qur'an, in any case, definitively tells us that a law of Tawhid pervades this universe, that this law of Tawhid was established by Allah, the Lord of Glory, and that this universe and all creatures dwelling in it are servants of that one Lord alone, and it is their duty to worship the Lord. As far as our knowledge is concerned, we can only see the flowing system of this universe, which is moving according to a fixed order.

This great law which Allah's will and destiny have established within this vast universe also operates within this small being of man, since man too is a working part of this universe. Man's own nature is also embedded in its disposition, and it is not even necessary that he have a rational awareness of his natural movements; he possesses, by his nature, an inner perception, and this perception of reality lies in the depths of his nature, and his self also possesses awareness of it. He acts in accordance with it, as long as corruption and disorder have not overtaken him. Because of that disorder and corruption, his inner perception grows dim, and man comes to follow temporary circumstances, and now he moves according to external factors, and his inner faculty abandons its work.

This law of fitrah is itself a covenant between Allah and the servant, and this covenant exists in the depths of human existence. From the time of his birth he is placed in every cell, and this covenant has continued from the time of Adam (peace be upon him) until today. Every cell of man affirms the lordship, and it is according to this affirmation and covenant, that is, the law of divine power, that he comes into the world. Therefore, after this natural covenant, man has no need of any further proof or argument, whether it be by the tongue of circumstance or by the tongue of speech. Consequently, it will not benefit man to say that he fell into heedlessness and was careless about the Book of Allah and the teachings of the Messenger of Allah. Nor can anyone put forward the excuse that when he entered the universe, there was nothing but polytheism among his forefathers and environment, and he had no means of accepting the belief in Tawhid; therefore he is not responsible for his beliefs and deeds. And this is the reason why Allah has made the matter clear and explicit.

This is a faithful rendering of the Urdu passage. Note: the Urdu text contains "سا کے باوجود," which appears to be a typographical fragment (likely "اس سب کے باوجود" or similar); I have rendered it as "despite all this" to keep the sense.

But the instructions ask for translation only, so here it is:

But it is an extraordinary act of mercy from Allah that He knew that human beings possess both the capacity for guidance and the capacity for misguidance, and that a person, despite that primordial covenant, may choose deviation. For the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said that human beings are led away from the straight path by the devils of both jinn and mankind, and that these devils of jinn and mankind skillfully exploit human weaknesses.

Allah, in His mercy, did not hold human beings responsible for guidance on the basis of their innate nature alone, nor did He call them to account merely on the strength of their rational faculty, natural perception and power of discernment. Rather, despite all this, Allah sent Messengers who presented verses and proofs in detail, so that they might remove the rust that has settled upon the nature, polish it, and free human beings from bondage to desires and appetites. Although Allah knew that human guidance could be achieved without Messengers and callings, through their innate capacity and intellectual power, nevertheless He has based the reckoning and accountability upon prophethood and the call.

These verses and guidance were revealed so that a person returns to the path of fitrah (innate human nature) and puts to use the capacity that exists within his fitrah. That is, through these natural faculties and rational perception, he was also able to rightly grasp the truth; yet Allah sent the Messenger and the guidance so that he might attain the path of guidance, and benefit from reminder and warning.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verses 175–177 (part 1 of 2):

Commentary on verses 175–177: Now an example is presented of deviation from the path of fitrah (innate human nature), in which a person breaks the covenant of fitrah and, after guidance, turns away from the signs and proofs of Allah. Allah scattered His signs and proofs before him; he could have seen them with his own thought and vision and reflected upon them. But he slipped away from them, in the manner of someone who slips out of his garment and falls to the ground, and he submitted to his base desires. He did not hold firmly to the covenant he had made with Allah, nor did those signs provide him with the means of guidance. Satan overpowered him, and he left the security of Allah's protection, going astray, restless, and running here and there.

But the Qur'an has presented the example of this person in a miraculous manner. In this example there is a dynamic scene in which the features of that person are clearly visible. The impressions of this scene are very real, the events are natural, and the expression is extremely vivid and full of suggestion.

...

﴿And recite to them the news of him to whom We gave Our signs, but he detached himself from them; so Satan pursued him, and he became of those who went astray.﴾

Here is a strange scene, a most modern artistic portrayal, a portrayal in words. A person is given signs and proofs; he is clothed with the robe of grace and favour, given the garment of knowledge, and provided with opportunities to take the path of guidance, to be joined to Allah, and to attain exaltation. Yet he removes himself from that state. He strips off the splendid robe and stands naked, and instead of loftiness and purity he smears himself in mud. He runs after the desires of the self. He has already broken the first, natural covenant; then he abandons the signs and proofs which held guidance for him. He is slipping out of the signs and instructions as though they were his very flesh and skin, and he is pulling himself out of them with tremendous struggle and great hardship, just as if a living person's skin were being peeled off. The truth is that the proofs of faith are clinging to the human body just as skin is bound to the body. He is slipping out of the signs; he is becoming naked, stripping himself of the flesh and skin that protected him, leaving the path of guidance and running after the desires of the self. Thus he falls from the heights of the horizons and is smeared in mud. Then Satan attacks him, and now there is no means left to save him. So Satan pursues him and brings him under his control.

Now we are suddenly before a very frightening scene. It is an extremely evil and disturbing sight. Before us is a creature that is smeared in mud and lying fallen on the ground. Suddenly this creature is transformed into the shape of a dog: if you drive it away, it still hangs out its tongue, and if you leave it, it still hangs out its tongue. In short, these dynamic scenes come before us in succession. Our power of imagination moves along with these scenes, moving with very vivid impressions. And when our imagination reaches the final scene, in which a dog is seen with its tongue hanging out, suddenly this comment is heard over the whole scene:

﴿That is the example of the people who denied Our signs. So relate the narratives, that perhaps they may reflect.﴾

This is the example of them. The truth is that the proofs of guidance and the causes of faith were found within their own nature, and these proofs and indications were also present in the universe spread around them, yet these people pulled themselves away from them. Now they were disfigured bodies, which hung suspended; having fallen from the station of humanity, they had descended to the level of animality. They were like the dog that is smeared in mud. They had the wings of faith and the proofs of guidance by means of which they could have flown up to the highest heavens, 'Illiyyin. Their creation too was in the best design, but alas, they chose the lowest of the low (asfal safilin) in preference to the highest (a'la 'illiyyin).

﴿Evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs, and they were wronging themselves.﴾

Is there any worse example than this, that someone should pull himself out of his own skin and be left utterly naked of guidance, and that someone should smear himself in mud for the satisfaction of base desires? Who would be a greater wrongdoer to himself than these people, who pull off their own skin and expose their own bones and flesh? They destroy their own supporter and helper, and they make their flesh naked and easy prey for the savage satanic beasts to tear at. Then Satan brings such a person down from the station of humanity to the station of animality, and he is left bewildered and distraught, just like a mad dog with its tongue hanging out.

It is part of the Qur'an that it depicts such a situation in such effective words that its inimitability is entirely clear.

The question arises: was there a specific example of such people at that time, or has a general matter been brought here in the form of an example? Is there anything in the body of narrations about the referent of these examples?

Some narrations state that there was a righteous man in Palestine. He lived before the time when the Children of Israel entered Palestine. A lengthy account is related of his deviation and his moral ruin. Nevertheless, such a person may also be an instance of this example. But since these Israelite narrations have entered Islamic exegeses, it is not necessary to accept all the details of this story as correct. Moreover, because the Israelite narrations contain great disagreement and confusion, a cautious attitude towards them is also necessary.

Narrations state that among the Children of Israel there was a man named Balam ibn Ba'ura; he was one of the tyrannical rulers of Palestine. Some have said that he was Umayya ibn al-Salt of the Arabs. Some narrations identify Abu 'Amir al-Fasiq as its referent. Some narrations state that this man was a contemporary of Musa (Moses, peace be upon him). Some narrations say that he was in the time of Yusha' ibn Nun (Joshua). Yusha' ibn Nun fought against those tyrannical rulers after the Children of Israel's forty years of wandering in the Tih. Whereas in the time of Musa (peace be upon him), the Children of Israel had declined to fight those giants; they told Musa, "Go you and your Lord and fight; we are sitting here." Some narrations state that the sign given to this man was the Greatest Name (ism a'zam), with which every supplication is accepted. Some narrations state that he was given the Book of Allah; he was a prophet, and after him there were great disputes about him.

In Zilal al-Qur'an, in keeping with our method, we do not go into these details, because the Qur'an has not indicated these details in its text, nor has any marfu' hadith from the Prophet ﷺ been reported on this subject. Nevertheless, the actual situation to which the Qur'an points is repeatedly reproduced in human history: a person is presented with signs and proofs; he knows their truth, but he does not accept them and does not correct his life in accordance with them. Many people who are given religious knowledge do not take guidance from their own knowledge; rather, they make their knowledge a means of distorting the Book, and they run after personal desires. The desires of these people, and the desires of those who gain control over them, that is, the interests of this temporary world, hold the reins of them in their hands.

We have seen many religious scholars who understand a truth well but do not come into line; they waver, and they even announce with their tongues things which they themselves do not believe to be true. Such people use their knowledge for distortion and deviation, use their fatwas in favour of those in power, and thus strengthen the rulers who are a challenge to Allah's sovereignty on this earth.

We have seen people who know and say that legislation is the sole right of Allah, and that whoever claims the right of legislation for himself is in effect claiming divinity, and whoever claims divinity is a disbeliever, and whoever accepts this right for any human being is also a disbeliever. Despite this, and while knowing this, he keeps no concern with those who call themselves legislators and claim lordship and divinity, and about whom that very scholar has issued a fatwa that they are disbelievers. Rather, this scholar even calls such people Muslims and calls what they do Islam; then, one year, he writes that interest is forbidden, and the next year, in his writings, he declares interest to be forbidden. Some of these people regard immorality and vice as a blessed matter; they give vice a name and title of Islam and bring it in Islamic dress.

Now, would this person not be an instance of the comment: one to whom Allah gave such signs and knowledge, and who slipped away from Allah's proofs and knowledge, upon whom Satan then tightened his grip, and who became among those who go astray? The person about whom the Qur'an gives news will be an instance of this. Allah gave him knowledge and the means of exaltation, but instead of travelling towards heights, he kept falling towards lowliness. Now read this comment of the Qur'an and this report carefully.

﴿And recite to them the news of him to whom We gave Our signs, but he detached himself from them; so Satan pursued him, and he became of those who went astray. And had We willed, We would have elevated him thereby, but he clung heavily to the earth and followed his own desire. So his example is like that of the dog: if you chase it, it pants with its tongue hanging out, or if you leave it, it still pants. That is the example of the people who denied Our signs. So relate the narratives, that perhaps they may reflect. Evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs, and they were wronging themselves.﴾

The one whose news the Qur'an gives matches the people of our age who are of this kind. This example fits everyone whom Allah has given knowledge but who did not act according to the requirements of that knowledge. He did not adopt the path of faith; he pulled himself away from Allah's blessings. He became a follower of Satan and a mere tool. Now he will keep wandering, with his tongue hanging out like a mad dog.

Notice how the Qur'an places this in our feelings. This person is running after the worldly aims with his tongue hanging out, and because of worldly aims he has pulled himself out of the divine favours. That he hangs his tongue out like a dog shows that such a person will never be satisfied by worldly aims. Whoever has the reins of his life in the hand of worldly aims cannot escape from them, even if you admonish him a thousand times. On this path he will keep circling government offices with his tongue hanging out, and he will continue to do so.

Study human life deeply. The example of this is present everywhere and in every age. Rather, ages pass and such people are seen everywhere; they come forward from every side. Those whom Allah protects are rare exceptions: they hold firmly to the signs of Allah, they rise towards heights instead of coming down to the lowlands of the earth, they suppress their base desires, which Satan cannot disgrace. These people do not put any halter in their nose; they do not go in the direction whose end is in the hands of those in authority. In short, this is a parable whose instances never end; they are always present. It is surprising that you search for such people far back in the history of the Children of Israel.

The Prophet ﷺ was commanded to recite these signs to his people and warn them that they should not pull themselves out of these divine signs. Therefore, after the Prophet ﷺ, we should recite these signs and explain to people that they should not pull themselves out of the strong refuge of these signs, and should not bring themselves to that end by abandoning the portion of Allah's knowledge that has been given to them. Nor should they place themselves in a situation in which a person runs after worldly desires, which have no end, with his tongue hanging out like a dog, and they should not wrong themselves in the way that even an enemy does not wrong his enemy, because by placing themselves in such a state they are wronging only themselves.

I have seen in our own times scholars who are extremely eager to inflict this kind of harm upon themselves. There are people who are spending all their strength in pursuit of a dwelling place in Hell. From morning till evening such people are strengthening their place in Hell, and day and night they wander after it with their tongues hanging out. Neither does advice have any effect on them, nor does any rebuke. In this very state, such people finally depart from this world. O Allah, save us! Keep our feet firm! Shower upon us the rain of patience, and grant us death and goodness in the company of the people of Islam.
....
The Qur'an has given, in the form of a parable, a report about a certain person, and we should reflect upon it at some length and again.
This is the parable of a man of knowledge upon whom the desires of the self and worldly pleasures place such a burden that he cannot bear it, and falls to the ground, and because of the pull of those desires he cannot advance a single step directly. He pursues his carnal desires, Satan pursues him, takes hold of him and begins to drive him according to his own will, and there is a bridle of carnal desires in his mouth.
Since knowledge alone cannot save a human being, the Qur'anic method therefore establishes a special method for the training of the human soul and for the promotion of Islamic life. Islam does not present knowledge alone, but gives knowledge a living and dynamic form, so that Islamic objectives appear both in the intellectual and conceptual world and in practical life.
The Islamic method is not that it presents Islamic beliefs merely in the form of theories, merely for research and inquiry, with no effect on a person's thought, outlook, action and striving. Such abstract researches are merely the outward form of knowledge; such knowledge cannot save a person from the grip of his carnal desires, nor can it raise him to prominence in the world, especially from base feelings and desires. Such knowledge cannot confront Satan; rather, it paves the way for Satan, and because of it a person adopts the slavery of Satan.
Islam is not interested in research about religion merely for its own sake. For example: "research" about the Islamic system, "research" about Islamic jurisprudence (fiqh), "research" about the Islamic economic system, research about Islamic scientific theories, Islamic research on the science of the psyche, and so on and so forth.
Islam brings Islamic beliefs in the form of beliefs that are dynamic, progressive, living, awakening, dominant and destined to be exalted. After they have taken hold of reason and thought, these beliefs immediately move a Muslim to fulfil Islamic objectives. When these beliefs take root in the heart and vision of even a dead-hearted person, they bring him to life, and the one who accepts these beliefs shakes himself off and rises up and begins striving for the exaltation of Islam. His nature immediately returns to the original primordial covenant, and this person becomes moved toward lofty aims, and the pollutions of the world cannot draw him toward themselves. He is never plunged into the mire of wickedness and depravity. The Qur'an presents Islam in the form of a method of thought and reflection, and it stands out distinctly from all the methods of the world. It came precisely so that it might lift the burdens of the world and deliver people from the misguidance of Satan.
The Qur'an presents Islam as a criterion and standard (mizan) for truth and falsehood. By this standard the perceptual faculties and intellects of people are tested, and the movements, tendencies and conceptions of people are judged according to it. Before Islam there was no standard in the world that could be put to use, and this balance and standard rejects whatever is worthless, and it will be thrown away.
Islam wishes to elevate humanity and bring it to a very lofty station, but on the highway of progress Islam wishes to lead it at a very gentle pace. It accomplishes this according to its own plan and its own calculations. In order to walk on this highway of progress, Islam gives people a detailed system of life; it gives them a detailed system of law, it gives them a settled system of economy, and for them it lays down the principles of society and the principles of politics. After laying down these principles, it gives people freedom, so that in the light of these principles they may devise for themselves detailed systems. They progress in this world day and night, yet the warmth of faith remains present in their hearts. They devise a genuine system of law, and through it they find solutions to all their needs.
In this way the Islamic system of life, in the form of Islamic living, guides the human self. As for those researches which are confined merely to theoretical prattle, the knowledge that results from them can neither benefit an individual against Satan, nor can it practically organize human life along Islamic lines, nor can it set human life on the path of progress. Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verses 175–177 (part 1 of 2):

Commentary on verses 175–177: Now an example is presented of deviation from the path of fitrah (innate human nature), in which a person breaks the covenant of fitrah and, after guidance, turns away from the signs and proofs of Allah. Allah scattered His signs and proofs before him; he could have seen them with his own thought and vision and reflected upon them. But he slipped away from them, in the manner of someone who slips out of his garment and falls to the ground, and he submitted to his base desires. He did not hold firmly to the covenant he had made with Allah, nor did those signs provide him with the means of guidance. Satan overpowered him, and he left the security of Allah's protection, going astray, restless, and running here and there.

But the Qur'an has presented the example of this person in a miraculous manner. In this example there is a dynamic scene in which the features of that person are clearly visible. The impressions of this scene are very real, the events are natural, and the expression is extremely vivid and full of suggestion.

...

﴿And recite to them the news of him to whom We gave Our signs, but he detached himself from them; so Satan pursued him, and he became of those who went astray.﴾

Here is a strange scene, a most modern artistic portrayal, a portrayal in words. A person is given signs and proofs; he is clothed with the robe of grace and favour, given the garment of knowledge, and provided with opportunities to take the path of guidance, to be joined to Allah, and to attain exaltation. Yet he removes himself from that state. He strips off the splendid robe and stands naked, and instead of loftiness and purity he smears himself in mud. He runs after the desires of the self. He has already broken the first, natural covenant; then he abandons the signs and proofs which held guidance for him. He is slipping out of the signs and instructions as though they were his very flesh and skin, and he is pulling himself out of them with tremendous struggle and great hardship, just as if a living person's skin were being peeled off. The truth is that the proofs of faith are clinging to the human body just as skin is bound to the body. He is slipping out of the signs; he is becoming naked, stripping himself of the flesh and skin that protected him, leaving the path of guidance and running after the desires of the self. Thus he falls from the heights of the horizons and is smeared in mud. Then Satan attacks him, and now there is no means left to save him. So Satan pursues him and brings him under his control.

Now we are suddenly before a very frightening scene. It is an extremely evil and disturbing sight. Before us is a creature that is smeared in mud and lying fallen on the ground. Suddenly this creature is transformed into the shape of a dog: if you drive it away, it still hangs out its tongue, and if you leave it, it still hangs out its tongue. In short, these dynamic scenes come before us in succession. Our power of imagination moves along with these scenes, moving with very vivid impressions. And when our imagination reaches the final scene, in which a dog is seen with its tongue hanging out, suddenly this comment is heard over the whole scene:

﴿That is the example of the people who denied Our signs. So relate the narratives, that perhaps they may reflect.﴾

This is the example of them. The truth is that the proofs of guidance and the causes of faith were found within their own nature, and these proofs and indications were also present in the universe spread around them, yet these people pulled themselves away from them. Now they were disfigured bodies, which hung suspended; having fallen from the station of humanity, they had descended to the level of animality. They were like the dog that is smeared in mud. They had the wings of faith and the proofs of guidance by means of which they could have flown up to the highest heavens, 'Illiyyin. Their creation too was in the best design, but alas, they chose the lowest of the low (asfal safilin) in preference to the highest (a'la 'illiyyin).

﴿Evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs, and they were wronging themselves.﴾

Is there any worse example than this, that someone should pull himself out of his own skin and be left utterly naked of guidance, and that someone should smear himself in mud for the satisfaction of base desires? Who would be a greater wrongdoer to himself than these people, who pull off their own skin and expose their own bones and flesh? They destroy their own supporter and helper, and they make their flesh naked and easy prey for the savage satanic beasts to tear at. Then Satan brings such a person down from the station of humanity to the station of animality, and he is left bewildered and distraught, just like a mad dog with its tongue hanging out.

It is part of the Qur'an that it depicts such a situation in such effective words that its inimitability is entirely clear.

The question arises: was there a specific example of such people at that time, or has a general matter been brought here in the form of an example? Is there anything in the body of narrations about the referent of these examples?

Some narrations state that there was a righteous man in Palestine. He lived before the time when the Children of Israel entered Palestine. A lengthy account is related of his deviation and his moral ruin. Nevertheless, such a person may also be an instance of this example. But since these Israelite narrations have entered Islamic exegeses, it is not necessary to accept all the details of this story as correct. Moreover, because the Israelite narrations contain great disagreement and confusion, a cautious attitude towards them is also necessary.

Narrations state that among the Children of Israel there was a man named Balam ibn Ba'ura; he was one of the tyrannical rulers of Palestine. Some have said that he was Umayya ibn al-Salt of the Arabs. Some narrations identify Abu 'Amir al-Fasiq as its referent. Some narrations state that this man was a contemporary of Musa (Moses, peace be upon him). Some narrations say that he was in the time of Yusha' ibn Nun (Joshua). Yusha' ibn Nun fought against those tyrannical rulers after the Children of Israel's forty years of wandering in the Tih. Whereas in the time of Musa (peace be upon him), the Children of Israel had declined to fight those giants; they told Musa, "Go you and your Lord and fight; we are sitting here." Some narrations state that the sign given to this man was the Greatest Name (ism a'zam), with which every supplication is accepted. Some narrations state that he was given the Book of Allah; he was a prophet, and after him there were great disputes about him.

In Zilal al-Qur'an, in keeping with our method, we do not go into these details, because the Qur'an has not indicated these details in its text, nor has any marfu' hadith from the Prophet ﷺ been reported on this subject. Nevertheless, the actual situation to which the Qur'an points is repeatedly reproduced in human history: a person is presented with signs and proofs; he knows their truth, but he does not accept them and does not correct his life in accordance with them. Many people who are given religious knowledge do not take guidance from their own knowledge; rather, they make their knowledge a means of distorting the Book, and they run after personal desires. The desires of these people, and the desires of those who gain control over them, that is, the interests of this temporary world, hold the reins of them in their hands.

We have seen many religious scholars who understand a truth well but do not come into line; they waver, and they even announce with their tongues things which they themselves do not believe to be true. Such people use their knowledge for distortion and deviation, use their fatwas in favour of those in power, and thus strengthen the rulers who are a challenge to Allah's sovereignty on this earth.

We have seen people who know and say that legislation is the sole right of Allah, and that whoever claims the right of legislation for himself is in effect claiming divinity, and whoever claims divinity is a disbeliever, and whoever accepts this right for any human being is also a disbeliever. Despite this, and while knowing this, he keeps no concern with those who call themselves legislators and claim lordship and divinity, and about whom that very scholar has issued a fatwa that they are disbelievers. Rather, this scholar even calls such people Muslims and calls what they do Islam; then, one year, he writes that interest is forbidden, and the next year, in his writings, he declares interest to be forbidden. Some of these people regard immorality and vice as a blessed matter; they give vice a name and title of Islam and bring it in Islamic dress.

Now, would this person not be an instance of the comment: one to whom Allah gave such signs and knowledge, and who slipped away from Allah's proofs and knowledge, upon whom Satan then tightened his grip, and who became among those who go astray? The person about whom the Qur'an gives news will be an instance of this. Allah gave him knowledge and the means of exaltation, but instead of travelling towards heights, he kept falling towards lowliness. Now read this comment of the Qur'an and this report carefully.

﴿And recite to them the news of him to whom We gave Our signs, but he detached himself from them; so Satan pursued him, and he became of those who went astray. And had We willed, We would have elevated him thereby, but he clung heavily to the earth and followed his own desire. So his example is like that of the dog: if you chase it, it pants with its tongue hanging out, or if you leave it, it still pants. That is the example of the people who denied Our signs. So relate the narratives, that perhaps they may reflect. Evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs, and they were wronging themselves.﴾

The one whose news the Qur'an gives matches the people of our age who are of this kind. This example fits everyone whom Allah has given knowledge but who did not act according to the requirements of that knowledge. He did not adopt the path of faith; he pulled himself away from Allah's blessings. He became a follower of Satan and a mere tool. Now he will keep wandering, with his tongue hanging out like a mad dog.

Notice how the Qur'an places this in our feelings. This person is running after the worldly aims with his tongue hanging out, and because of worldly aims he has pulled himself out of the divine favours. That he hangs his tongue out like a dog shows that such a person will never be satisfied by worldly aims. Whoever has the reins of his life in the hand of worldly aims cannot escape from them, even if you admonish him a thousand times. On this path he will keep circling government offices with his tongue hanging out, and he will continue to do so.

Study human life deeply. The example of this is present everywhere and in every age. Rather, ages pass and such people are seen everywhere; they come forward from every side. Those whom Allah protects are rare exceptions: they hold firmly to the signs of Allah, they rise towards heights instead of coming down to the lowlands of the earth, they suppress their base desires, which Satan cannot disgrace. These people do not put any halter in their nose; they do not go in the direction whose end is in the hands of those in authority. In short, this is a parable whose instances never end; they are always present. It is surprising that you search for such people far back in the history of the Children of Israel.

The Prophet ﷺ was commanded to recite these signs to his people and warn them that they should not pull themselves out of these divine signs. Therefore, after the Prophet ﷺ, we should recite these signs and explain to people that they should not pull themselves out of the strong refuge of these signs, and should not bring themselves to that end by abandoning the portion of Allah's knowledge that has been given to them. Nor should they place themselves in a situation in which a person runs after worldly desires, which have no end, with his tongue hanging out like a dog, and they should not wrong themselves in the way that even an enemy does not wrong his enemy, because by placing themselves in such a state they are wronging only themselves.

I have seen in our own times scholars who are extremely eager to inflict this kind of harm upon themselves. There are people who are spending all their strength in pursuit of a dwelling place in Hell. From morning till evening such people are strengthening their place in Hell, and day and night they wander after it with their tongues hanging out. Neither does advice have any effect on them, nor does any rebuke. In this very state, such people finally depart from this world. O Allah, save us! Keep our feet firm! Shower upon us the rain of patience, and grant us death and goodness in the company of the people of Islam.
....
The Qur'an has given, in the form of a parable, a report about a certain person, and we should reflect upon it at some length and again.
This is the parable of a man of knowledge upon whom the desires of the self and worldly pleasures place such a burden that he cannot bear it, and falls to the ground, and because of the pull of those desires he cannot advance a single step directly. He pursues his carnal desires, Satan pursues him, takes hold of him and begins to drive him according to his own will, and there is a bridle of carnal desires in his mouth.
Since knowledge alone cannot save a human being, the Qur'anic method therefore establishes a special method for the training of the human soul and for the promotion of Islamic life. Islam does not present knowledge alone, but gives knowledge a living and dynamic form, so that Islamic objectives appear both in the intellectual and conceptual world and in practical life.
The Islamic method is not that it presents Islamic beliefs merely in the form of theories, merely for research and inquiry, with no effect on a person's thought, outlook, action and striving. Such abstract researches are merely the outward form of knowledge; such knowledge cannot save a person from the grip of his carnal desires, nor can it raise him to prominence in the world, especially from base feelings and desires. Such knowledge cannot confront Satan; rather, it paves the way for Satan, and because of it a person adopts the slavery of Satan.
Islam is not interested in research about religion merely for its own sake. For example: "research" about the Islamic system, "research" about Islamic jurisprudence (fiqh), "research" about the Islamic economic system, research about Islamic scientific theories, Islamic research on the science of the psyche, and so on and so forth.
Islam brings Islamic beliefs in the form of beliefs that are dynamic, progressive, living, awakening, dominant and destined to be exalted. After they have taken hold of reason and thought, these beliefs immediately move a Muslim to fulfil Islamic objectives. When these beliefs take root in the heart and vision of even a dead-hearted person, they bring him to life, and the one who accepts these beliefs shakes himself off and rises up and begins striving for the exaltation of Islam. His nature immediately returns to the original primordial covenant, and this person becomes moved toward lofty aims, and the pollutions of the world cannot draw him toward themselves. He is never plunged into the mire of wickedness and depravity. The Qur'an presents Islam in the form of a method of thought and reflection, and it stands out distinctly from all the methods of the world. It came precisely so that it might lift the burdens of the world and deliver people from the misguidance of Satan.
The Qur'an presents Islam as a criterion and standard (mizan) for truth and falsehood. By this standard the perceptual faculties and intellects of people are tested, and the movements, tendencies and conceptions of people are judged according to it. Before Islam there was no standard in the world that could be put to use, and this balance and standard rejects whatever is worthless, and it will be thrown away.
Islam wishes to elevate humanity and bring it to a very lofty station, but on the highway of progress Islam wishes to lead it at a very gentle pace. It accomplishes this according to its own plan and its own calculations. In order to walk on this highway of progress, Islam gives people a detailed system of life; it gives them a detailed system of law, it gives them a settled system of economy, and for them it lays down the principles of society and the principles of politics. After laying down these principles, it gives people freedom, so that in the light of these principles they may devise for themselves detailed systems. They progress in this world day and night, yet the warmth of faith remains present in their hearts. They devise a genuine system of law, and through it they find solutions to all their needs.
In this way the Islamic system of life, in the form of Islamic living, guides the human self. As for those researches which are confined merely to theoretical prattle, the knowledge that results from them can neither benefit an individual against Satan, nor can it practically organize human life along Islamic lines, nor can it set human life on the path of progress. Regarding the parable given in this context, a brief commentary is now made upon it here (see the commentary on the next verse).

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 178:

The example of the one whom Allah gave His guidance but who departed from it. The commentary is this: true guidance is only that which comes from Allah. Whomever Allah wishes to guide is upon guidance, and whomever Allah leads astray, he falls into loss forever. Now he cannot gain profit in any matter.

Allah Almighty guides only the one who strives for guidance. In other surahs Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿And those who strive in Our cause - We will surely guide them to Our paths.﴾ And elsewhere: ﴿Indeed, Allah will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves.﴾ And elsewhere: ﴿And by the soul and He who proportioned it and inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness. He has certainly succeeded who purifies it, and he has certainly failed who instills it [with corruption].﴾

The one who abandons the proofs of guidance and chooses for himself the path of misguidance, Allah also leads him astray, because such a person closes his heart, his eyes and his ears to guidance. In this same context, the following verse conveys this very meaning.

And elsewhere it is said: ﴿In their hearts is a disease, so Allah has increased their disease.﴾ And in another verse: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and do wrong - Allah will not forgive them, nor will He guide them to a path, except the path of Hell, wherein they will abide forever.﴾

After reflecting upon all the verses that mention guidance and misguidance, and after establishing harmony and coherence among their meanings, only one explanation and reconciliation is possible, one which brings contentment to the heart and which is free from those theological disputations (lahuti jadaliyat) in which Islamic theologians (mutakallimin), Jews, Christians and the philosophers of other religions have always been locked in dispute. It is this: that in this universe the system of Allah's decree and destiny (qada wa qadr) operates within a vast circle of Allah's will (mashiyyah). Within this circle human beings have been created, and in accordance with this system of destiny, humans have been endowed with a twofold capacity for guidance and misguidance. Within human nature a primordial covenant has been placed, that he should attain the recognition of Allah alone and acknowledge His lordship. Then, alongside this twofold capacity for guidance and misguidance, human beings have been given the power of discernment (quwwat-e-tamyiza) of reason, which recognizes guidance and misguidance. Moreover, through the messengers, proofs and signs of guidance have been explained to them, so that if a thick layer has settled upon their nature, it may continue to be cleared. Yet alongside all these arrangements, the twofold capacity for accepting guidance or misguidance remains in them, and all these arrangements lie within Allah's circle of will, indeed within the wider circle of His will.

Within Allah's will, the system of Allah's decree and destiny continues to operate and does its work. Therefore, whoever within this circle chooses guidance takes the path of guidance; destiny guides him, and if he does not walk according to the proofs of guidance and the indications of nature, this destiny places him upon the path of misguidance. This is because that person did not make use of the reason that was given to him. He did not make use of the eyes and ears which were given to him to see the signs scattered throughout this universe. Then, those guidances which were sent through the messengers were also present.

But whatever path anyone takes, he remains within Allah's circle of will, and whatever event occurs remains within Allah's system of decree and destiny, and cannot be contrary to the power of Allah. This is because whatever knowledge any human being may have, it remains within the circle of Allah's will, since whatever happens occurs according to destiny. For in the universe only Allah's will operates, and destiny lies within that circle, since there is no other power besides Allah's power that could bring such systems and events into existence. In short, man moves within this vast circle, and it is within this circle that he continues to walk whatever path he takes.

This is the concept that comes to mind from the study of all these verses, provided that these verses are not presented against one another as a debate, but are read together, reconciled, and harmony is created among them. (For details see the book Al-Khasa'is al-Tasawwur al-Islami.) At the end comes this conclusion:

﴿Whom Allah guides - he is the [rightly] guided; and whom He sends astray - it is those who are the losers.﴾ That is, according to the explanation mentioned above, whoever takes the path of guidance, Allah grants him guidance; he reaches his goal. He is shown the way and walks upon that very path, and attains success in this world and the Hereafter. And whomever Allah leads astray according to the principles of His sunnah, he goes astray, and he remains in loss in every respect, even though he may appear wealthy outwardly. Yet he is in loss, because his wealth is without reality; it is mere wind. The truth is that such a person has lost his own self, and for one whose personality is lost and who has forfeited his own self, what profit will there be?

In the interpretation of the above verses, what we have said is also confirmed by the next verse.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 179:

A majority of jinn and humankind have been created for Hell, and they are preparing for it. So why is this their end? This declaration has two aspects. The first is that Allah had foreknowledge that this creation would take the path to Hell and would reach Hell. That they actually take the path to Hell is not affected by Allah's knowledge. Allah's knowledge encompasses everything and is eternal. Allah knew, long before the creation and the action of humankind, that so-and-so would take this path. Allah's knowledge does not depend on the occurrence of events; rather, it is already a part of the Divine Being.

The second aspect is that Allah, through His eternal knowledge which is with His Being, does not compel people in the world of events to do this and not to choose another path. Rather, they do so by their own capacity and by their own essence. Thus Allah says: "They have hearts with which they do not understand, they have eyes with which they do not see, and they have ears with which they do not hear." [7:179]

They were given minds and hearts so that they would open them and try to understand matters, whereas proofs of faith are scattered throughout the universe. Then, in the message that the Messengers gave, there are also proofs and miracles. If their hearts had insight and their eyes were open, they could have been guided. But they closed their eyes and did not look at the signs of God. They closed their ears and did not listen to the call of the Prophets. They rendered all their faculties inoperative, although these had been given for their benefit. They remained heedless like animals, therefore they are like animals, rather even worse than them. Those who are heedless of these signs and indications that surround them in the universe, who see such events and lessons-bearing incidents with their own eyes but do not see the hand of Allah in them, these people are indeed like animals, rather they are worse than animals. This is because livestock also have natural functions, and every animal fulfills them. As for jinn and humankind, they were given a thinking heart, a seeing eye, and hearing ears. When they did not think with their hearts, did not see with their eyes, and did not hear with their ears, and passed by heedless of the movement of this entire universe, and did not grasp its purposes and meanings, when their eyes did not see the indications present here, and the outcry of this entire universe did not affect their hearing, then certainly these people and others of this kind are worse than animals, which at least carry out their natural functions. And these people were created for Hell, and within the broad scope of Allah's will, according to the demand of Allah's system of decree and destiny, they have become deserving of Hell. They were not compelled to adopt this path; rather, through Allah's ancient knowledge, He knew that they would do so, and they would fill it and become the fuel of Hell.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 180:

After presenting the natural and cosmic covenant of tawhid (divine oneness) and the parable of those who turn away from that covenant, namely those who are given the revelations of God and yet slip away from them, the command now comes concerning those who are distorted and misguided, and who, in opposition to the Islamic call, represent shirk (associating partners with God) and kufr (disbelief). They corrupt God's names and misuse them, and they name their idols after them.

﴿And to God belong the most beautiful names, so call upon Him by them, and leave those who deviate concerning His names. They will be recompensed for what they used to do.﴾

God is worthy of the best names; call upon Him by them, and leave alone those who deviate from the truth in naming Him. What they do, they will receive its recompense.

Ilhad (deviation) means that a person departs from the truth. In the Arabian Peninsula, the deviating polytheists had altered and changed the names of God, and with slight modifications they had given these names to their own deities and idols.

By turning Allah into Allat, they named an idol after Him. By turning al-'Aziz into al-'Uzza, they named another idol. Here it is stated that the names of God must not be used for anyone else, and that it is the duty of the believers to call upon God alone by these names, and not to make any distortion or alteration in the wording, nor any imalah (vocalic inclination). And if the deviators misuse these names, the believers should not sit in their company. Let them be, and let their god deal with them. Soon they will return to God, and God will settle their account with them.

The command that one should sever relations with those who commit ilhad in the names of God is not confined only to that historical situation in which they used al-'Aziz for al-Lat and al-'Uzza. It is confined not merely to verbal distortion of the divine names; rather, its application continues to every kind of verbal and conceptual distortion, whether they distort or deviate. Whether they deviate in the concept of the deity, for example by asserting offspring for God, or commit a deviation of meaning by holding that God's will is confined within the laws of nature, or by declaring that God's actions and the modes of His actions resemble the actions and modes of human actions. Or they accept God as the deity of the heavens, the earth and the Hereafter, but in their view God has no political and legal sovereignty on earth. It is God's right to legislate for people; people themselves have the right to legislate for themselves, and they legislate according to their own reason, experience and interests. Hence, politically, in the view of such people, man is his own god and object of worship. Or some people are gods to other people. All these ideas fall under ilhad concerning the essence and attributes of God. Muslims have been commanded to protect themselves from these matters and keep away from them. For those who commit this kind of ilhad, there is the warning that they will be given a severe punishment for that deviation.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verses 181–183:

Commentary on verses 181 to 183: After this, the categories of people with respect to guidance and misguidance are now being described. Earlier it was mentioned that some people are, by nature, destined for Hell. They have hearts but do not think with them, they have eyes but do not see with them, and they have ears but do not hear with them.

Among them are also those who commit ilhad (deviation, distortion) in the names of Allah and use Allah's husna (beautiful names) in the wrong place. Among them is also a group that has held firmly to the truth and calls people towards the truth too. They issue judgments in accordance with the truth and do not deviate from it even by a particle's weight. There is a group that rejects the truth out of stubbornness and denies the signs of Allah. The first group is the one whose existence is firmly established on this earth. These people are steadfast and are the guardians of truth. And as for those who deviate and walk on crooked paths, these people place obstacles in their way. And when other people reject the truth and abandon it, these people hold the truth firmly. As for the opposing party, their end will be frightful, and against them Allah's plan will be firm.

﴿And among those whom We have created is a community who guide by the truth and do justice by it. But those who deny Our signs, We will lead them step by step (to destruction) from where they do not know. And I give them respite; indeed, My plan is firm.﴾ Among Our creation there is a group that guides precisely by the truth and does justice according to the truth. As for those who have denied Our signs, We will lead them gradually to destruction in such a way that they will not even know it. I am giving them respite; My scheme cannot be countered.

These bearers of the truth, if they were not present in humanity, humanity would not deserve honour and dignity. This group, which the Qur'an in Islamic terminology calls the ummah, is present in this world at all times in some form. It is the community that has one ideology, which is organized and bound together upon that ideology and creed, and whose leadership is also one. It is this ummah that is firmly upon the truth, acts upon the truth, and is the guardian of that reality. It bears witness to this ideology before people, and against misguidance Allah establishes testimony and proof through this ummah. And now consider its attribute.

"Yahduna bil-haqqi wa bihi ya'dilun": This group takes guidance from the truth, gives guidance of the truth, and does justice according to the truth. This means that the existence of this ummah cannot be terminated from this earth, even if the number of its members decreases. These people guide to the truth and are its followers, and these people are never silenced by any power from this call. They act upon this truth and call others towards it. They do not confine this truth to themselves but convey it to others as well. Around them there is such leadership, and that leadership has abandoned the truth, and they have forgotten that natural covenant which they had made with Allah. In short, the action of this group is positive, and they are not limited only to themselves but they carry this and convey it to others. And they lead with this truth.

Their duty does not end merely with giving the invitation to truth; rather, among their obligations is that they establish this truth in people's lives, make judgments according to it, and establish a system of justice in the world, and it is obvious that a system of justice cannot be established without this truth. This truth did not come merely to be taught as an academic pursuit, nor did it come merely as preaching and advice, but it came so that the truth would decide among people. First it makes decisions about people's doctrinal concepts and ideas, that which creed is correct and which ideology is wrong.

Thus, the truth first performs the task of purifying thoughts and corrects people's intellectual foundations. After this, by establishing people's connection with Allah, this truth corrects the rites of worship performed before Allah. And after this, by establishing the collective life of people upon this truth, it establishes it in the form of a system of life. By establishing the collective life and society of people upon the principles of truth, it enforces the laws and sharia of truth in this collective system. Thus the morals and habits of people, their customs, their conduct and dealings are organized and established upon truth, and all of this is based upon correct concepts and creeds. After this, the thought patterns, knowledge and cultural activities of people are also developed upon this system of truth. This is the duty that has been given to this ummah. Along with this, this ummah is distinguished and recognized, and this is the identity of this ummah.

In short, the character of this religion is completely clear, and no kind of misunderstanding or confusion about it is even possible. It is a firm character and it cannot change. Those who want to bring deviation into religion cannot, despite all their futile efforts, change this strict character of religion. These people make tireless efforts in this regard, continuously keep up their attacks, and want to change the viewpoint of this religion by employing every kind of means and resource, and they benefit from all experiences in this regard, throughout this entire world, against those who work for the revival of Islam and who, holding this truth to their chest, remain firmly established. These people use every tactic through their agents against them. They try to erase them, and they have established organizations and governments of their agents throughout all Islamic lands. Then these people encourage the religion-selling scholars in these lands, and these scholars carry out the work of distorting the religion of Islam. These people make the forbidden lawful and the lawful forbidden, soften the sharia of Allah, encourage every kind of immorality and debauchery, promote obscenity, and give Islamic labels to obscenity and debauchery. These people seek out those who are impressed by modern material progress and overawed by modern ideas, and they seduce them, seating them in their cradles. In this way, they remove Islam from its firm foundation and give it the colour of modern ideas, and thus introduce modern ideas, the symbols of modern civilization, and modern customs and laws into Islam under the name of Islam. These people give the impression that Islamic civilization was a historical accident and that it can never be revived in any form, nor can that accident be repeated. These people describe the glorious past of Islam as a thing of the past and want to stir the emotions of Muslims, and then they want to convince them that if Islam wishes to remain alive today, it can survive only by being confined to a creed and rites of worship; its political and legal system cannot function. For Islam, stories of past glory are better and sufficient. If not this, then it is possible to introduce such changes into Islam that it becomes subject to the conditions of the modern age, and it adapts itself to people's desires and their actual circumstances, and they seek to declare as Islam the secularist ideologies that they themselves are spreading in the Islamic world. These people make interpretations of the Qur'an that were not known in the earlier Qur'an, rather even Allah, Jibril and Mustafa (ﷺ) were unaware of them. Just as they want to change the Qur'an, they also want to change Islamic societies. And this is so that the religion of Islam does not find those workers who are suited to its work. In the Islamic world these people want to bring into existence a society that is drowned in sexual licentiousness, in a filthy pool, and people drowned in obscenity, adultery and immorality, who have no concern with any purpose other than worldly pleasure and indulgence, and who are so immersed in the world that they have no opportunity to hear the truth and the genuine guidance of the Qur'an, such that not even by mistake do Islamic teachings reach their ears.

This is the all-encompassing battle that is now being waged across the four corners of the world against this ummah and against this religion: the ummah that takes guidance from this religion, is its proponent, and wants to establish its system of justice in the world. This is the all-encompassing combat in which the enemies of Islam are employing every kind of weapon. They are throwing boundless and countless resources into it. Therefore, the enemy has brought forward all its strength, providing it with resources and giving it all means of dissemination and the most modern means of communication. Behind these forces stand international organizations and institutions, and were it not for this international support and guarantee, these agents of the enemies of Islam, these institutions and governments, could not stand even one day before the callers of this ummah.

But despite this all-encompassing battle and these vast campaigns, it appears that this religion is an extremely tenacious religion. This ummah, which strives for this religion, is extremely tenacious. Despite its small numbers, its scarce resources, and its weaknesses, it remains steadfast against this savage attack. Consider again.

﴿But those who denied Our signs, We will lead them step by step (to destruction) from where they do not know. And I give them respite; indeed, My plan is firm.﴾ As for those who denied Our signs, We will lead them gradually to destruction in such a way that they will not even know it. I am giving them respite; My scheme cannot be countered.

These people do not take into account this power, this divine power, and they continue the aforementioned campaign against Islam and Muslims, although the Muslim ummah has firmly held onto Islam and is gathered upon the strength of Islam. This is the power that those who deny the signs of Allah do not comprehend. They do not grasp the reality that Allah has granted these people respite, and that this respite is until a fixed time, and they do not believe at all that the plan of Allah is extremely firm. These enemies of Islam have formed alliances with one another and think that the rule of this earth belongs to them. But these people do not see the great power of God. In short, this is how Allah deals with those who deny: Allah keeps them in respite and grants them a long period of time for rebellion and disobedience. Thus these people are fully seized within Allah's scheme, and this plan is not that of an ordinary person; it is the plan of Allah, the Almighty and the possessor of firm power. But the enemies of Islam are heedless of the fact that the final outcome will belong to those who are God-fearing, who are upon the truth, who call to the truth, and who wish to establish the system of justice of the truth.
