This means that the existence of this ummah cannot be terminated from this earth, even if the number of its members decreases. These people guide to the truth and are its followers, and these people are never silenced by any power from this call. They act upon this truth and call others towards it. They do not confine this truth to themselves but convey it to others as well. Around them there is such leadership, and that leadership has abandoned the truth, and they have forgotten that natural covenant which they had made with Allah. In short, the action of this group is positive, and they are not limited only to themselves but they carry this and convey it to others. And they lead with this truth.

Their duty does not end merely with giving the invitation to truth; rather, among their obligations is that they establish this truth in people's lives, make judgments according to it, and establish a system of justice in the world, and it is obvious that a system of justice cannot be established without this truth. This truth did not come merely to be taught as an academic pursuit, nor did it come merely as preaching and advice, but it came so that the truth would decide among people. First it makes decisions about people's doctrinal concepts and ideas, that which creed is correct and which ideology is wrong.

Thus, the truth first performs the task of purifying thoughts and corrects people's intellectual foundations. After this, by establishing people's connection with Allah, this truth corrects the rites of worship performed before Allah. And after this, by establishing the collective life of people upon this truth, it establishes it in the form of a system of life. By establishing the collective life and society of people upon the principles of truth, it enforces the laws and sharia of truth in this collective system. Thus the morals and habits of people, their customs, their conduct and dealings are organized and established upon truth, and all of this is based upon correct concepts and creeds. After this, the thought patterns, knowledge and cultural activities of people are also developed upon this system of truth. This is the duty that has been given to this ummah. Along with this, this ummah is distinguished and recognized, and this is the identity of this ummah.

In short, the character of this religion is completely clear, and no kind of misunderstanding or confusion about it is even possible. It is a firm character and it cannot change. Those who want to bring deviation into religion cannot, despite all their futile efforts, change this strict character of religion. These people make tireless efforts in this regard, continuously keep up their attacks, and want to change the viewpoint of this religion by employing every kind of means and resource, and they benefit from all experiences in this regard, throughout this entire world, against those who work for the revival of Islam and who, holding this truth to their chest, remain firmly established. These people use every tactic through their agents against them. They try to erase them, and they have established organizations and governments of their agents throughout all Islamic lands. Then these people encourage the religion-selling scholars in these lands, and these scholars carry out the work of distorting the religion of Islam. These people make the forbidden lawful and the lawful forbidden, soften the sharia of Allah, encourage every kind of immorality and debauchery, promote obscenity, and give Islamic labels to obscenity and debauchery. These people seek out those who are impressed by modern material progress and overawed by modern ideas, and they seduce them, seating them in their cradles. In this way, they remove Islam from its firm foundation and give it the colour of modern ideas, and thus introduce modern ideas, the symbols of modern civilization, and modern customs and laws into Islam under the name of Islam. These people give the impression that Islamic civilization was a historical accident and that it can never be revived in any form, nor can that accident be repeated. These people describe the glorious past of Islam as a thing of the past and want to stir the emotions of Muslims, and then they want to convince them that if Islam wishes to remain alive today, it can survive only by being confined to a creed and rites of worship; its political and legal system cannot function. For Islam, stories of past glory are better and sufficient. If not this, then it is possible to introduce such changes into Islam that it becomes subject to the conditions of the modern age, and it adapts itself to people's desires and their actual circumstances, and they seek to declare as Islam the secularist ideologies that they themselves are spreading in the Islamic world. These people make interpretations of the Qur'an that were not known in the earlier Qur'an, rather even Allah, Jibril and Mustafa (ﷺ) were unaware of them. Just as they want to change the Qur'an, they also want to change Islamic societies. And this is so that the religion of Islam does not find those workers who are suited to its work. In the Islamic world these people want to bring into existence a society that is drowned in sexual licentiousness, in a filthy pool, and people drowned in obscenity, adultery and immorality, who have no concern with any purpose other than worldly pleasure and indulgence, and who are so immersed in the world that they have no opportunity to hear the truth and the genuine guidance of the Qur'an, such that not even by mistake do Islamic teachings reach their ears.

This is the all-encompassing battle that is now being waged across the four corners of the world against this ummah and against this religion: the ummah that takes guidance from this religion, is its proponent, and wants to establish its system of justice in the world. This is the all-encompassing combat in which the enemies of Islam are employing every kind of weapon. They are throwing boundless and countless resources into it. Therefore, the enemy has brought forward all its strength, providing it with resources and giving it all means of dissemination and the most modern means of communication. Behind these forces stand international organizations and institutions, and were it not for this international support and guarantee, these agents of the enemies of Islam, these institutions and governments, could not stand even one day before the callers of this ummah.

But despite this all-encompassing battle and these vast campaigns, it appears that this religion is an extremely tenacious religion. This ummah, which strives for this religion, is extremely tenacious. Despite its small numbers, its scarce resources, and its weaknesses, it remains steadfast against this savage attack. Consider again.

﴿But those who denied Our signs, We will lead them step by step (to destruction) from where they do not know. And I give them respite; indeed, My plan is firm.﴾ As for those who denied Our signs, We will lead them gradually to destruction in such a way that they will not even know it. I am giving them respite; My scheme cannot be countered.

These people do not take into account this power, this divine power, and they continue the aforementioned campaign against Islam and Muslims, although the Muslim ummah has firmly held onto Islam and is gathered upon the strength of Islam. This is the power that those who deny the signs of Allah do not comprehend. They do not grasp the reality that Allah has granted these people respite, and that this respite is until a fixed time, and they do not believe at all that the plan of Allah is extremely firm. These enemies of Islam have formed alliances with one another and think that the rule of this earth belongs to them. But these people do not see the great power of God. In short, this is how Allah deals with those who deny: Allah keeps them in respite and grants them a long period of time for rebellion and disobedience. Thus these people are fully seized within Allah's scheme, and this plan is not that of an ordinary person; it is the plan of Allah, the Almighty and the possessor of firm power. But the enemies of Islam are heedless of the fact that the final outcome will belong to those who are God-fearing, who are upon the truth, who call to the truth, and who wish to establish the system of justice of the truth.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 7, verse 184:

The Qur'an here warns those who, at that time, were engaged in intrigues against Islam in Makkah. But this verse is not restricted to the people of Makkah. In later times too, this has been and will be the treatment that the enemies of the Muslim ummah give it. Allah gives these opponents respite, but His plan is firmly established. Therefore Allah advises them that whatever they do, they should do it with their eyes open. They should use their hearts and minds, and should not include themselves among the creatures of Hell. Islam was advising the people of Makkah that they should carefully reflect on their attitude towards the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Do they not see that he is the bearer of truth and the caller to truth? Furthermore, the people of Makkah should reflect on the structure of the heavens and the earth and on the sovereignty (of Allah). Are there not scattered within it signs and miracles that lead to the truth? The respite that is being given to them is not very lasting and long. The time for the occurrence of Allah's plan is very near. Why have they become so heedless?

Islam strives to bring people from intoxication to consciousness, to awaken them from the heavy slumber of heedlessness, and to bring out human nature from under the layers that have settled upon it. It revives the consciousness of human beings. The Qur'an addresses the personality and humanity of a person and awakens those faculties through which they may accept the call of Islam. The Qur'an does not conduct mere rigid and dry debate. It draws out the true personality of a human being from beneath the deep layers of misguidance.

﴿Do they not reflect? There is no madness in their companion. He is only a warner, making (the consequence) clear.﴾ And have these people never thought? There is no effect of madness on their companion. He is only one who warns, who is clearly cautioning (before an evil end comes upon them).

In the propaganda war against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the greatest weapon of the Quraysh was to accuse him of being afflicted with madness, and their argument for it was: "Do you not see that he presents a speech that is completely different from the well-known styles of Arabic speech?"

The Quraysh who spread this propaganda knew well that they were telling lies. Narrations report that they knew well that the call which the Messenger carried was the truth, and that is why they were eager to listen to the Qur'an and could not restrain themselves from refraining from hearing it. Its hearing had profound effects upon them. The incident of Akhnas ibn Shariq, Abu Sufyan ibn Harb and Amr ibn Hisham Abu Jahl is well known: they would listen to the Qur'an secretly, hiding from one another. Once it happened that these three gentlemen came to listen to the Qur'an secretly. We have mentioned this incident in Fi Zilal al-Qur'an. Also well known is the incident of Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, who heard verses of Surah Fussilat directly from the Messenger ﷺ, and they shook him. And these reports are also well known: that these people would devise plans during the Hajj season to keep people away from the Qur'an. Walid ibn Mughirah would tell people that this is a highly effective sorcery. From all these reports it becomes clear that they had no doubt about Islam, the call to Islam, or the truth of the Qur'an, but rather they considered themselves great in opposition to this call. Then they feared that once they affirmed "La ilaha illa Allah, Muhammad Rasul Allah," Muhammad would become their ruler and sovereign authority, because the requirement of this declaration is that people leave the servitude of other humans and enter the servitude of Allah, and abolish all tyrannical powers.

The Qur'an is a strange and unique Book, and its style is also more distinctive than the common styles of speech among people, so the Quraysh exploited this to their advantage. Moreover, among the Arabs there was a similarity between diviners (soothsayers) and madmen; for example, among the Arabs too, people who were majdhub (in a state of spiritual rapture) would claim a connection with the higher realm and would say such things whose interpretation they could manipulate as they wished. Because of these reports, the Quraysh would also declare the Prophet ﷺ to be a majdhub or a madman, and would call his speech the speech of a majdhub or a madman.

The Qur'an invited these people to reflection and advised them to reflect upon Hadrat Muhammad ﷺ, whom they knew well, and they knew that he had never previously spoken such majdhub-like words. Furthermore, they themselves bore witness that he was truthful and trustworthy, and they also acknowledged his wisdom, understanding and gravity. When they made him the arbiter in the matter of the Black Stone, and the decision he made saved them from a very great civil war. Also, everyone would keep their trusts with him, and these trusts remained with him as long as he was in Makkah, and after he left, his cousin Hadrat Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) delivered them to their owners.

The Qur'an invites these people to reflect that the past of Hadrat Muhammad is an open book; you know everything about his life. What then is the reason that makes you call him a madman? Can the kind of speech that he is presenting be the work of madmen and lunatics? Certainly not.

﴿There is no madness in their companion; he is only a clear warner.﴾ There is no effect of madness on their companion; he is only one who warns, who is clearly cautioning.

There is no defect in his intellect; he is only one who speaks in clear terms. His speech is entirely different from the speech of a madman, and his circumstances of life are different from the circumstances of life of madmen.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 7, verse 185:

This is another window onto this wondrous universe, and an invitation to behold this great and vast cosmos with open eyes and an awakened heart. If one were to cast a careful glance upon this great universe, the human nature that lies buried beneath the thick veils of ignorance would emerge, and the paths of truth could open before the human personality. In this universe there are the wondrous workings of creation and deeds that are miraculous, and which point to the Absolute Powerful and the One without partner. Do they not reflect upon the creation of anything at all? Yet in this universe there are countless things worthy of reflection, upon which contemplation leaves the human intellect astonished, human thought powerless, and the intellect sets out in search of the craftsman and the maker of these workmanships. Then it wishes to know the will that brought this creation into being and set this system in motion for it.

Why is this creation the way it is? Apart from this, there were thousands of possibilities for this universe. Why did the universe not take another form? Leaving aside other methods, why did this universe proceed along this present course, and what is the power that keeps it running on this course? In this entire universe there is one single system of nature at work and pervading it: why? If behind it there is no single Active One who wills, then why does a single will and a single law appear to be pervading this whole universe and behind it, and why does a single decree and a single measure continue to operate?

A living body! Nay, rather a single cell is a great miracle whose wonders never cease. Its existence, its composition, its functions, the constant changes arising within it which continually protect its existence, and the arrangement within it for the renewal of the species across many generations; then the determination of its duties across all generations. Whoever studies this single cell, his conscience and his intellect can never be satisfied that this universe could run without a deity and a manager, nor can any intellect ever arrive at the conclusion that there could be another deity besides God.

This continuity of life through the system of reproduction is in itself a proof that this universe is running according to the law of a Creator and Manager; otherwise, over millions of years, what power is it that maintains a ratio of men and women for the purpose of procreation? Why does there never come an era in which only males are born, or only females? If such an event were ever to occur, the reproduction of the species would come to an end in that era. The question is: what power has maintained this ratio and balance generation after generation?

This balance operates perfectly in the system of the heavens and the earth; it is not confined to living creatures alone. There is complete balance in the structure of an atom and in the structure of any compound substance. Complete balance exists within all living and non-living creatures. And if this balance were to be disturbed even for a moment, this universe would collapse into ruin. Therefore it is a very important question: which is the Being that has established this balance in the heavens and the earth?

The people of the Arabian Peninsula, to whom this Qur'an first addressed itself, had not advanced so far in the sciences and arts that they could reflect upon the extremely subtle balance found in the system of the heavens and the earth, or carry out a scientific analysis of any single thing created by God. Yet human nature is attuned to this universe in its very depths. The connection established between human nature and the nature of the universe does not require scientific discourse. A balance exists between them. Every person whose heart is open and whose eyes possess insight can perceive this harmony and, by accepting its signs, can take the path of guidance.

When a human being, through his pure nature, finds these signs of the nature of the universe, he becomes certain that this universe has a God, and upon his sense this truth and conviction becomes so firmly imprinted that it never disappears. If man has committed any error, he has committed it regarding the attributes of God. The primary purpose of the sending of the messengers has been precisely this: that they introduced this God, and gave the correct conception of His attributes. As for the modern atheists, that is, the proponents of scientific communism, they are distorted people whose nature has become corrupted; indeed, in truth they deny nature, and if some signs are found in their own thought, they try to suppress them. One of them, when he rose somewhat high into the atmosphere of the sky and from there beheld the astonishing sight of the earth appearing as a small sphere within that vast atmosphere, his nature called out to him at that moment to just think, what is it that has suspended him in that atmosphere? But when he landed on the earth and the fear of violence from the government overtook him, he made the statement that he had not found God in the celestial atmosphere. That man suppressed the voice of his nature and the insistence of his nature, and he disregarded the lesson that existed for him in the system of the heavens and the earth.

God Almighty addresses humankind, because it is He who created humankind. He is well acquainted with human nature. At the end, they are warned about the event of death, which is hidden behind the veils of the future and is very near, and the appointed time of which is known in the realm of the Unseen, although these people are heedless of that time.

*"And has it not occurred to them that perhaps their term has drawn near? Then in what statement after this will they believe?"* And has it not even occurred to them that perhaps the term of their life has drawn near? Then after this warning of the Messenger, what other matter could there be in which they would believe?

How can they know whether their time is near or far, and why are they drowned in heedlessness, when they are well aware that they are in the power of God and that the time of their departure is concealed behind the veil of the Unseen?

The truth is that the remembrance of death, especially since it may come at any moment, is an effective means of shaking the human heart. Through its remembrance the doors of the human heart may open to guidance, and a person may see matters with realism. God, who sent down this Qur'an and who created man, knows that the thought of death surely leaves its impression upon every person, yet some people are so obstinate that, despite accepting this impression, they deny and display arrogance.

But God Almighty says that those who are not affected even by the report of departure, what could possibly affect them? This is the very thing that melts hearts and makes them soft. The mention of death given to the human personality in this verse shows the method the Noble Qur'an adopts in addressing the human personality. It addresses every aspect of the human personality; it leaves its impressions from every angle and every string. The Noble Qur'an does not address the human intellect alone, yet it does not leave the intellect idle either; rather, it addresses the human personality in all its dimensions and illuminates every corner of it. The Noble Qur'an also does not adopt the method of dry debate and argument. It revives intellect and thought so that a person may reflect, but its life should not be cold and rigid; rather it should be full of warmth, and the human personality should advance in a full-blooded manner. Those who call others to Islam should adopt this very approach, for the human being remains the same human being and no change has occurred in his creation. The Qur'an too remains the same Qur'an, and it will remain until the Day of Resurrection. The address that God has made to humankind stands as it is, however much the world may progress and however much circumstances may change.

The commentary now pauses briefly, and in this pause it also points to the sunnah of God that He has established in this very world regarding guidance and misguidance. That is, in accordance with the law that whoever strives for guidance with sincere seeking will be guided, and whoever turns away and makes no effort to grasp the proofs of faith and the signs of guidance will go astray.

This allusion is made in view of the circumstances of those people whom the Qur'an was addressing. It is the Qur'an's method and particular approach that, after narrating an individual event, it derives from it a general principle and presents it as an unchanging sunnah of God. The event itself is individual and, once it has occurred, becomes part of history, but the principle remains in its place and keeps coming before us again and again.

Why do those who go astray go astray? Because they neither take thought about guidance nor reflect upon events and matters. Whoever is heedless of the signs of God and does not reflect upon them, God leaves him astray, and whomever God has led astray according to His sunnah, he cannot find guidance, nor can anyone become a guide for him.

"Man yudlilillahu fala hadiya lah": whoever God deprives of guidance, for him there is then no guide. And the one upon whom God imposes misguidance, according to His continuing sunnah, is forever led astray, and he becomes blind from birth in matters of guidance. And then what happens?

"Wa yadharuhum fi tughyanihim ya'mahun": and God leaves them to wander blindly in their rebellion.

In leaving these people in that darkness, God does not wrong them, because their fault was that they had themselves closed their eyes. They had rendered their hearts inoperative and had stopped making use of their faculties of perception. They did not ponder the wonders of the creation of this world, and did not seek to attain the secrets of this universe. In particular, they did not accept the testimony of the reality of every created thing and its secrets, to which the preceding verses had alluded. The truth is that whenever a human being has looked around in this universe, he has seen its wonders; whenever he has opened his eyes, he has seen some sign. Whenever a person has studied his own self and his environment, he has come to know the miracle of his own creation, and he has seen every creature in his surroundings as a miracle. But when a person has made himself blind, he has become blind, and God has also left him in darkness. Then, when he began to rebel, God gave him respite in that rebellion, until he reaches the point of destruction. "And God leaves them to wander blindly in their rebellion."

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah al-A'raf, verses 187–188 (part 1 of 2)**

**Commentary on verses 187 to 188:** Those who are heedless of their surroundings, who have closed their eyes to their own environment, ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when the Hour, which is hidden in the unseen realm, will be established. Their question is like that of a person whose eyesight is so weak that he cannot see what is at his own feet, yet who wishes to see something on the distant high horizon.

---

The belief in the Hereafter, the establishment of the scales, and the occurrence of reward and punishment was a strange idea to the polytheists of Makkah, even though this belief was a foundational belief of the religion of Abraham, and the lineage of the polytheists of Makkah traced back to Abraham. This same belief was also a foundational principle in the religion of Isma'il, the sacrificed one of Allah. But after Abraham (peace be upon him), ages passed, and they moved away from the principles of Islam that were the foundational beliefs of the religion of Abraham and the religion of Isma'il. A time came when the belief in the Hereafter was erased from their very conception. This belief now appeared strange to them, and it had become almost contrary to their conscious view of life. Therefore, when they heard the call from the lips of the Messenger (ﷺ), and when he told them about resurrection and resurrection after death, and placed before them the circumstances of reckoning and accountability, this matter appeared to them as extremely strange and unlikely to happen. Elsewhere, the Qur'an has expressed their astonishment in these words:

﴿Those who disbelieve say: "Shall we show you a man who tells you that when you have been completely scattered into particles, you will then be created anew? Has he invented a lie against Allah, or is there madness in him?" No! Rather, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are destined for punishment, and they are the ones who are gravely astray.﴾ (Surah Saba)

Allah knew that no community could lead all of humanity unless the belief in resurrection after death was firmly established in its system of thought, and the duty of the Muslim ummah (community) is in any case to lead the whole world. Therefore, it was necessary for this ummah to regard the life of this world as a limited life, which is only a small part of a limited world. Without the belief in the Hereafter, it was not possible to produce a community of this kind, one that would have such a great objective before it.

The belief in the Hereafter creates expansiveness in human thought, and the human soul gains breadth. The longing for continuity of life, which is present within the human personality, is fulfilled. Then, for the discharge of the duties that the Muslim ummah bears, this belief is necessary. Furthermore, because of this belief, the base instincts of a person and his limited worldly desires are also brought under control. In addition, through this belief the sphere of a person's activity becomes wide, and the limited outcomes of the world cannot make him despair, nor can painful sacrifices prevent him from achieving his purpose. In good deeds, in spreading the Islamic call, and in leading people towards goodness, he does not feel any obstruction, even if the immediate results of his struggle are contrary to his wishes and there are painful obstacles in his path. This consciousness and these qualities are necessary for every individual and every group upon whose shoulders this great responsibility has been placed.

The belief in the Hereafter is a crossroads between two conceptions. One conception is the animal conception, which is confined within the limits of sense perception. The second conception is the human conception, which sees this world within a wide circle. It is evident that a group that has to carry out the task of leading all of humanity cannot carry out this task with an animal conception.

This is why, in the religion of Islam, belief in the Hereafter has been declared a foundational belief for the Muslim ummah. The religion of Islam has presented the belief in the Hereafter in an extremely deep, extremely broad, and extremely clear form. To such an extent that in the consciousness and practice of a Muslim, the world of the Hereafter is established more deeply, more broadly, and more clearly than this limited world. Although Muslims are, in any case, living in this world, it is this quality that enabled the Muslim ummah to carry out the task of leading humanity, and this leadership was a rightly guided leadership, which both Islamic and world history have understood well.

In Surah al-A'raf, this question comes before us on this subject, and it is asked with great astonishment. The polytheists actually regarded the belief in the Hereafter as an unusual thing. Their question shows that they considered the occurrence of the Resurrection to be ridiculous, and regarded it as entirely beyond possibility. This is why they asked this question:

﴿They ask you about the Hour: when will it come to pass?﴾

The Hour is an unseen matter, and Allah has reserved its knowledge for Himself. Allah has not informed any of His creatures about when the Hour will be established. Despite this, the polytheists used to ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when the Hour would come. This question was either asked as a test, or it was the question of a person who was amazed and regarded the matter as strange, or it was the question of a person who wished to insult the one being questioned and was asking it with contempt.

The words "ayyana mursaha" mean: when will the ship of the Hour anchor, and when will the Hour occur and come to a stop?

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was, in any case, a human being. He did not claim to have knowledge of the unseen. He was commanded to leave unseen matters to the Knower of the unseen, and to tell people that this subject is connected with the special attributes of divinity. He is a human being, and he does not claim anything beyond the sphere of humanity, nor does he wish to go beyond the limits of humanity. What he has is what was taught to him by his Lord, and it is up to Allah to decide what He tells His Messenger and what He does not tell him.

﴿Say: "Its knowledge is with my Lord alone. None but He will reveal it at its appointed time."﴾

This is because Allah has reserved the knowledge of the Hour for Himself, and its knowledge will be given to people only when its occurrence begins. It has not been revealed to anyone else.

After this, people's attention is directed away from the time of its occurrence to its reality and nature, and they are given the awareness that it will be a great and terrifying event, and its burden will be extremely heavy. Its burden is very heavy within the visible universe of the heavens and the earth. Above all, it will happen suddenly, and heedless people will be destroyed in their heedlessness.

﴿Its weight is heavy upon the heavens and the earth. It will not come upon you except suddenly.﴾

The meaning is that there will be a very severe time in the heavens and the earth, and it will come upon you suddenly. Therefore, it is better that your entire concern be directed towards preparing for it, so that when it comes suddenly, you will be ready for it. When it comes suddenly, no caution and no strength will be of any use at that time. At that time, only the precautions you have taken and the strength you have prepared in advance will be of use. At that time, life is sufficient, and you have enough free time at your disposal. Therefore, begin preparing for it now, and do not waste even a single minute, for the Hour may come in the very next minute.

After this, astonishment is expressed at the questions of those people who ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) such things. These people are ignorant of the nature of prophethood and the reality of the Messenger. Moreover, they are also unaware of the reality of the sovereignty of the Mighty Allah, and they do not know how humbly the Prophets of Allah conduct themselves before their Mighty Lord.

﴿They ask you about it as if you were eagerly searching for it.﴾

The meaning is: as though the Messenger constantly asks about it, or as though it were his duty to find out the exact time of the Hour's occurrence. It is evident that the Messenger does not ask his Lord about those matters which are the exclusive domain of the Lord of all the worlds.

﴿Say: "Its knowledge is only with Allah, but most people do not know."﴾

Because Allah has reserved it for Himself and has not informed anyone about it.

"But most people": but most people, regarding this truth...

This is not only a matter of the time of the Hour's occurrence. It is a fundamental principle regarding every unseen matter. Knowledge of the unseen belongs to Allah alone, and if Allah wishes, He tells some part of the knowledge of the unseen to someone, and He tells as much as He wishes, at whatever time He wishes. This is why people are not masters of their own benefit and harm. Sometimes people do something and intend that it will be beneficial for them, but in the end it turns out to be harmful for them. Sometimes they do something for harm, but in the end it turns out to be beneficial for them. Sometimes they do something reluctantly, disliking it, yet it turns out to be beneficial for them, and sometimes they do something that they love very much and pursue with great enthusiasm, yet it turns out to be harmful for them. Allah says:

﴿It may be that you dislike something while it is good for you, and it may be that you love something while it is bad for you.﴾

The poet who said the following also had this same meaning:

*Alā man yurīnī ghāyatī qabla madhhabī*
*Wa man ibnu wal-ghāyātu ba'da l-madhāhibi*

Who is there who can show me my destination before I set out? How can that happen? The outcome is known only after one has traveled.

In this verse, the human position regarding the hidden unseen is expressed. However broad a person's knowledge may be, and however much progress he may make in the field of learning, the door of the unseen remains closed before him, and the curtains of the unseen world remain drawn. The limits of his humanity will keep reminding him that the world of the unseen is beloved to his humanity, and it lies beyond his reach.

The status of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is great, and his nearness to Allah is also great in its own right. He is commanded to announce that at the door of the unseen world, he too is a human being like other people, and that he does not even own benefit or harm for himself, because he does not have knowledge of the unseen. He has no knowledge of his destination before setting out on the paths. No one is informed of the end of their actions in advance: if a person knew that the outcome of an action would be good, he would do it, and if he knew that its outcome would be bad, he would refrain from it. A person does something after thinking it over, but its outcome happens in the way that Allah's decree determines.

﴿Say: "I have no power over my own benefit or harm, except as Allah wills. And if I knew the unseen, I would have acquired abundant good, and no harm would ever have touched me. I am only a warner and a bringer of glad tidings to a people who believe."﴾

This is an important declaration. With it, the Islamic doctrine of tawhid (the oneness of God) has come forth in complete clarity and purity, and it has been freed from even the slightest trace of every kind of shirk (associating partners with God). The Divine Being stands alone in His attributes, and no one shares His special attributes, even if that partner is Muhammad (ﷺ), who is the beloved of Allah and His chosen one. The path to the door of the unseen is closed for him as well; the knowledge of all humanity stops at this door, just as other human beings stop here. In the same way, the duties of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) are also limited upon reaching this point.

﴿I am only a warner and a bringer of glad tidings to a people who believe.﴾

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is only a warner and a bringer of glad tidings. But only those people can benefit from his warnings and glad tidings who have faith in their hearts. Only believers understand the reality of the call that he carries. They alone understand what lies behind this call. Believers are, in essence, the distilled essence of humanity, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is the distilled essence of the believers.

This statement can be beneficial for a person whose heart is open, whose mind is illuminated, and who is ready to accept the truth. The truth is that the treasures of the Qur'an open their doors only to the one who is a believer. Only a believer can taste its fruit, and access to its secrets can only be attained by believers. It has been related from some Companions (ṣaḥābah) that Allah used to give them faith before giving them the Qur'an. It was faith through which they were given that taste for the Qur'an which has no parallel, and they possessed an understanding of its meanings and purposes which all other people are deprived of. It was the Qur'an through which they left, in human history, a store of miracles and astonishing achievements, and they accomplished these great deeds within a very short period of history.

This unique group had a true taste for the sweetness of the Qur'an. Their eyes saw by its light, they found its proofs, and they found them to be beyond the ordinary. But the only ones among the addressees of Muhammad (ﷺ) who experienced the sweetness of faith were those people. It was the Qur'an whose attraction drew their souls towards faith. But because of that faith, the secrets of the Qur'an were also gradually revealed to them.

These people lived in the Qur'an, and they lived for the Qur'an. This is why that group remained unique, and such people were never produced again. That is, such a large group, with such novelty and originality, never arose in the whole of Islamic and even human history. However, individual persons and exceptional people did appear from time to time in Islamic history.

They devoted themselves to the Qur'an for a long period. They were nourished only by the pure spring of the Qur'an, and they did not add any human speech or guidance to it, except that the sayings and ahadith of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were a guide for them. The sayings of the Messenger (ﷺ) were, after all, also part of the Qur'an. This is why the group of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) remained unparalleled.

Those who wish to do the same work that they did should adopt, as is fitting for them, the same approach that they adopted. They should live within this Qur'an, lose themselves in it for a long period, and, leaving aside all human writings, study only the Qur'an. Only in this way can they become what they were. (See Nishanat-i-Rah, Chapter One)

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah al-A'raf, verses 187–188 (part 1 of 2)**

**Commentary on verses 187 to 188:** Those who are heedless of their surroundings, who have closed their eyes to their own environment, ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when the Hour, which is hidden in the unseen realm, will be established. Their question is like that of a person whose eyesight is so weak that he cannot see what is at his own feet, yet who wishes to see something on the distant high horizon.

---

The belief in the Hereafter, the establishment of the scales, and the occurrence of reward and punishment was a strange idea to the polytheists of Makkah, even though this belief was a foundational belief of the religion of Abraham, and the lineage of the polytheists of Makkah traced back to Abraham. This same belief was also a foundational principle in the religion of Isma'il, the sacrificed one of Allah. But after Abraham (peace be upon him), ages passed, and they moved away from the principles of Islam that were the foundational beliefs of the religion of Abraham and the religion of Isma'il. A time came when the belief in the Hereafter was erased from their very conception. This belief now appeared strange to them, and it had become almost contrary to their conscious view of life. Therefore, when they heard the call from the lips of the Messenger (ﷺ), and when he told them about resurrection and resurrection after death, and placed before them the circumstances of reckoning and accountability, this matter appeared to them as extremely strange and unlikely to happen. Elsewhere, the Qur'an has expressed their astonishment in these words:

﴿Those who disbelieve say: "Shall we show you a man who tells you that when you have been completely scattered into particles, you will then be created anew? Has he invented a lie against Allah, or is there madness in him?" No! Rather, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are destined for punishment, and they are the ones who are gravely astray.﴾ (Surah Saba)

Allah knew that no community could lead all of humanity unless the belief in resurrection after death was firmly established in its system of thought, and the duty of the Muslim ummah (community) is in any case to lead the whole world. Therefore, it was necessary for this ummah to regard the life of this world as a limited life, which is only a small part of a limited world. Without the belief in the Hereafter, it was not possible to produce a community of this kind, one that would have such a great objective before it.

The belief in the Hereafter creates expansiveness in human thought, and the human soul gains breadth. The longing for continuity of life, which is present within the human personality, is fulfilled. Then, for the discharge of the duties that the Muslim ummah bears, this belief is necessary. Furthermore, because of this belief, the base instincts of a person and his limited worldly desires are also brought under control. In addition, through this belief the sphere of a person's activity becomes wide, and the limited outcomes of the world cannot make him despair, nor can painful sacrifices prevent him from achieving his purpose. In good deeds, in spreading the Islamic call, and in leading people towards goodness, he does not feel any obstruction, even if the immediate results of his struggle are contrary to his wishes and there are painful obstacles in his path. This consciousness and these qualities are necessary for every individual and every group upon whose shoulders this great responsibility has been placed.

The belief in the Hereafter is a crossroads between two conceptions. One conception is the animal conception, which is confined within the limits of sense perception. The second conception is the human conception, which sees this world within a wide circle. It is evident that a group that has to carry out the task of leading all of humanity cannot carry out this task with an animal conception.

This is why, in the religion of Islam, belief in the Hereafter has been declared a foundational belief for the Muslim ummah. The religion of Islam has presented the belief in the Hereafter in an extremely deep, extremely broad, and extremely clear form. To such an extent that in the consciousness and practice of a Muslim, the world of the Hereafter is established more deeply, more broadly, and more clearly than this limited world. Although Muslims are, in any case, living in this world, it is this quality that enabled the Muslim ummah to carry out the task of leading humanity, and this leadership was a rightly guided leadership, which both Islamic and world history have understood well.

In Surah al-A'raf, this question comes before us on this subject, and it is asked with great astonishment. The polytheists actually regarded the belief in the Hereafter as an unusual thing. Their question shows that they considered the occurrence of the Resurrection to be ridiculous, and regarded it as entirely beyond possibility. This is why they asked this question:

﴿They ask you about the Hour: when will it come to pass?﴾

The Hour is an unseen matter, and Allah has reserved its knowledge for Himself. Allah has not informed any of His creatures about when the Hour will be established. Despite this, the polytheists used to ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when the Hour would come. This question was either asked as a test, or it was the question of a person who was amazed and regarded the matter as strange, or it was the question of a person who wished to insult the one being questioned and was asking it with contempt.

The words "ayyana mursaha" mean: when will the ship of the Hour anchor, and when will the Hour occur and come to a stop?

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was, in any case, a human being. He did not claim to have knowledge of the unseen. He was commanded to leave unseen matters to the Knower of the unseen, and to tell people that this subject is connected with the special attributes of divinity. He is a human being, and he does not claim anything beyond the sphere of humanity, nor does he wish to go beyond the limits of humanity. What he has is what was taught to him by his Lord, and it is up to Allah to decide what He tells His Messenger and what He does not tell him.

﴿Say: "Its knowledge is with my Lord alone. None but He will reveal it at its appointed time."﴾

This is because Allah has reserved the knowledge of the Hour for Himself, and its knowledge will be given to people only when its occurrence begins. It has not been revealed to anyone else.

After this, people's attention is directed away from the time of its occurrence to its reality and nature, and they are given the awareness that it will be a great and terrifying event, and its burden will be extremely heavy. Its burden is very heavy within the visible universe of the heavens and the earth. Above all, it will happen suddenly, and heedless people will be destroyed in their heedlessness.

﴿Its weight is heavy upon the heavens and the earth. It will not come upon you except suddenly.﴾

The meaning is that there will be a very severe time in the heavens and the earth, and it will come upon you suddenly. Therefore, it is better that your entire concern be directed towards preparing for it, so that when it comes suddenly, you will be ready for it. When it comes suddenly, no caution and no strength will be of any use at that time. At that time, only the precautions you have taken and the strength you have prepared in advance will be of use. At that time, life is sufficient, and you have enough free time at your disposal. Therefore, begin preparing for it now, and do not waste even a single minute, for the Hour may come in the very next minute.

After this, astonishment is expressed at the questions of those people who ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) such things. These people are ignorant of the nature of prophethood and the reality of the Messenger. Moreover, they are also unaware of the reality of the sovereignty of the Mighty Allah, and they do not know how humbly the Prophets of Allah conduct themselves before their Mighty Lord.

﴿They ask you about it as if you were eagerly searching for it.﴾

The meaning is: as though the Messenger constantly asks about it, or as though it were his duty to find out the exact time of the Hour's occurrence. It is evident that the Messenger does not ask his Lord about those matters which are the exclusive domain of the Lord of all the worlds.

﴿Say: "Its knowledge is only with Allah, but most people do not know."﴾

Because Allah has reserved it for Himself and has not informed anyone about it.

"But most people": but most people, regarding this truth...

This is not only a matter of the time of the Hour's occurrence. It is a fundamental principle regarding every unseen matter. Knowledge of the unseen belongs to Allah alone, and if Allah wishes, He tells some part of the knowledge of the unseen to someone, and He tells as much as He wishes, at whatever time He wishes. This is why people are not masters of their own benefit and harm. Sometimes people do something and intend that it will be beneficial for them, but in the end it turns out to be harmful for them. Sometimes they do something for harm, but in the end it turns out to be beneficial for them. Sometimes they do something reluctantly, disliking it, yet it turns out to be beneficial for them, and sometimes they do something that they love very much and pursue with great enthusiasm, yet it turns out to be harmful for them. Allah says:

﴿It may be that you dislike something while it is good for you, and it may be that you love something while it is bad for you.﴾

The poet who said the following also had this same meaning:

*Alā man yurīnī ghāyatī qabla madhhabī*
*Wa man ibnu wal-ghāyātu ba'da l-madhāhibi*

Who is there who can show me my destination before I set out? How can that happen? The outcome is known only after one has traveled.

In this verse, the human position regarding the hidden unseen is expressed. However broad a person's knowledge may be, and however much progress he may make in the field of learning, the door of the unseen remains closed before him, and the curtains of the unseen world remain drawn. The limits of his humanity will keep reminding him that the world of the unseen is beloved to his humanity, and it lies beyond his reach.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verses 189–198 (part 1 of 3):

Commentary on verses 189 to 198:

The subject of the Oneness of God (tawhid) begins once again in the form of a narrative, and it explains the stages involved in the shift from tawhid to shirk. These are the stages of deviation of those who turned away from the religion of Ibrahim and became followers of the present polytheistic beliefs and practices. At the end it is shown how foolish and senseless is the worship of those gods whom they worship. At first glance, and after only slight reflection, it becomes evident that their thinking and conduct are false. At the end of this passage, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is commanded to challenge them: let these gods do whatever harm they wish to you, and declare also that my protector and helper is Allah, the Lord of the worlds, and that He is sufficient for my support. Now let us take a look.

﴿It is He who created you from a single soul and made from it its mate that he might find tranquility in her. And when he covered her, she bore a light burden and carried it about. But when she became heavy, they both called upon Allah, their Lord, "If You give us a righteous one, we will surely be among the thankful."﴾

﴿But when He gave them a righteous [child], they attributed to Him partners in what He had given them. But Allah is exalted above whatever they associate with Him.﴾

﴿Do they associate with Him those who create nothing, while they themselves are created?﴾

﴿And they cannot give them help, nor can they help themselves.﴾

﴿And if you invite them to guidance, they will not follow you. It is all the same for you whether you call them or remain silent.﴾

﴿Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah are servants like you. So call upon them, and let them respond to you, if you should be truthful.﴾

﴿Do they have feet by which they walk? Or do they have hands by which they strike? Or do they have eyes by which they see? Or do they have ears by which they hear?﴾ Say, "Call your partners, then plot against me and give me no respite."

﴿Indeed, my protector is Allah, who has sent down the Book, and He supports the righteous.﴾

﴿And those you invoke besides Him cannot help you, nor can they help themselves.﴾

﴿And if you call them to guidance, they do not hear. And you see them looking at you, but they do not see.﴾

This is a confrontation with ignorance (jahiliyyah) and its notions. When jahiliyyah turns away from the servitude and worship of Allah alone, it crosses the limits of misguidance and error, to the point that it is no longer ready to reflect and ponder. This passage depicts the stages in which a human being first takes the path of deviation and at last falls into the pit of complete misguidance.

﴿It is He who created you from a single soul and made from it its mate that he might find tranquility in her. And when he covered her, she bore a light burden and carried it about. But when she became heavy, they both called upon Allah, their Lord, "If You give us a righteous one, we will surely be among the thankful."﴾

These are the characteristics of the nature according to which Allah created man. Its demand is that man turn towards Allah, acknowledge the lordship of Allah alone without any partner, and that this acknowledgement be present both in fear and in hope. Here, the example Allah has set forth for this nature begins with the creation of man, and takes the nature of the relationship between husband and wife in the system of creation.

"Huwa alladhi khalaqakum min nafsin wahidatin wa ja'ala minha zawjaha liyaskuna ilayha." "It is He who created you from a single soul and made from it its mate that he might find tranquility in her."

Man and woman are one in terms of creation, which is why they have been called "a single soul," although the natural function of man and woman is distinct. Allah has created this difference in natural functions so that man may find tranquility with woman and she may be a source of comfort for him. This is Islam's concept of the reality of man, and Islam gives this impression regarding the mutual relationship and duties of spouses. This is a complete and true concept, which only Islam has presented, and it was presented fourteen hundred years ago, whereas in the distorted revealed religions the concept was that woman is responsible for all human suffering. She was regarded as impurity and a curse, and was called a dangerous snare of misguidance, and it was constantly enjoined that one should always feel threatened by her. Whereas in ancient and modern idolatrous religions and civilizations her status was that of rubbish, or if somewhere she was given any rank, it was only that she is the servant of the man and has no independent standing.

The true purpose of the union of spouses in Islam is that they come together, find tranquility, and live a life of rest in an atmosphere of peace and love, so that under the shade of the peace of the home children may be a shelter, and facilities may be provided for the precious asset of humanity, and the new generation may become bearers of human culture and civilization, capable of transmitting this trust to succeeding generations and of adding appropriately to it. Islam has not made the purpose and goal of this union of spouses fleeting pleasure and temporary passions, nor has it regarded it as enmity and conflict between man and woman. Nor has it declared one of the duties of man or woman important and thereby set it in opposition to the other. It has not made woman a claimant to the duties of man, nor assigned the duties of woman to man, as ancient and modern jahiliyyah have sought to confuse them. (For details see al-Islam wa Mushkilat al-Hadarah.)

Here, for the first meeting of man and woman, the Qur'an has adopted a most delicate and subtle manner of expression. "Taghashshaha": he covered her. This word conveys, along with the picture of intercourse, an atmosphere of peace and tranquility. The matter has been given the colour of union between two sexes, and not merely a concept of the union of bodies, so that the distinction between animal sexual union and human union may be shown. Similarly, the picture of pregnancy has also been given in a very fine manner. In the beginning it is in a very light form, and later it becomes a burden.

The second stage of pregnancy is heaviness.

"Falamma athqalat da'awa Allaha rabbahuma la'in ataytana salihan lanakunanna mina ash-shakirin." "But when she became heavy, they both called upon Allah, their Lord, 'If You give us a righteous one, we will surely be among the thankful.'"

Now, in this second stage, the pregnancy has become evident, the hearts of the spouses have become attached to it, and the time for hopes has come, that the child be sound, healthy, beautiful and righteous. These are the things which all parents wish for their children, while the child is still an embryo in the darkness of the mother's womb and in the realm of the unseen. In this state of hope, human nature awakens, and parents turn towards Allah; they acknowledge the lordship of Allah and hope for the grace and favour of Allah alone, because human nature feels in itself that the sole source of power, blessing and grace in this universe is the Divine Being. Thus, "da'awa Allah": both of them called upon their Lord, that if He gave them a righteous child, they would be among those who give thanks.

"Falamma atahuma salihan ja'ala lahu shuraka'a fima atahuma." "But when He gave them a righteous [child], they attributed to Him partners in what He had given them."

Some narrations report that this was a real incident, which befell Adam and Eve, because the children who were being born to them were misshapen and deformed. Satan deceived Eve into naming what was in her womb 'Abd al-Harith, so that the child would be born sound. Al-Harith was the name of Iblis. Thus the child would be born healthy. He similarly deceived Adam and made him say the same. Apparently this narration is of the Israelite type, because according to the Israelite and Jewish conception they hold Eve responsible for Adam's deception. Whereas Islam uproots this conception and holds that in the Jewish and Christian religions the truth has been deviated from.

We have no need, in explaining this verse, to turn to these Israelite narrations. In fact, this verse points to the deviations that gradually find their way into the human soul. In the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and in earlier periods too, it was the custom of the polytheists to vow their children to idols or to dedicate them to the service of churches and places of worship. They did this as a means of drawing near to Allah. In this matter, at first, the focus of their attention was the Divine Being, because after falling from the lofty station of tawhid and sinking into the pit of idol worship, they performed such vows and offerings at various shrines so that their children might survive, be sound, and not be exposed to dangers, just as even today people dedicate some of their children to saints and religious figures. For example, they do not shave the hair of a child until he has first been taken to the shrine of a saint and a pious person; sometimes they do not even circumcise him, and they take him to a tomb and shrine to have it done. Yet these people profess the shahada and acknowledge Allah, the One without partner, and despite this affirmation and acknowledgement they hold polytheistic tendencies. In short, the same people and the same notions are polytheistic.

"Fa-ta'ala Allahu 'amma yushrikun." "Allah is exalted above what they associate with Him." That is, He is free from the conceptions they hold about Him, and from the things they do in relation to Him.

But in our modern age too we see people caught in various kinds of shirk, and these are people who claim that they are Muslims and monotheists, and these modern shirks and idolatries of theirs are of the same form and kind as those mentioned in these verses.

Today people fashion new idols for themselves; some call them by the name of "nation," some call them by the name of "homeland," some call them by the name of "class," and so on. These are also idols, but they are non-embodied idols; they are not simple and embodied idols like those of earlier idolaters. In truth these too are the gods of those who worship them. They associate these idols with Allah in creation and in vows and offerings, just as the ancient gods were worshipped in the past. They offer sacrifices at the thresholds of these idols just as blood was shed on the altars of ancient idols and temples. And it was shed on a vast scale, and it was shed on a vast scale.

People acknowledge that Allah is their Lord, but they cast aside the commands, injunctions and Shari'ah of Allah, whereas they fully observe the laws and regulations of these modern non-embodied idols, regard them as sacred, and completely abandon the injunctions and laws of Allah in their favour. The question is: if these are not gods, if this is not shirk, and these people are not partners in the offspring of mankind, then what are they? By what words should we describe this modern idolatry of jahiliyyah? Clearly, it is nothing but idolatry.

I believe that the earlier jahiliyya (the age of ignorance, pre-Islamic paganism) was more respectful toward Allah. Its claim was that we assign a share of our children, our produce and our livestock to these deities so that through these means we might attain nearness to Allah. In their consciousness, Allah was exalted above those idols and deities. As for the modern jahiliyya, in its consciousness these unembodied idols are higher and more exalted than Allah, in that modern jahiliyya abandons the commands and laws of Allah and embraces the commands and laws of those idols.

Our position on idolatry is that it means all idolatry: not only when someone points toward an idol, as in the ancient times, or performs the rites that the people of ancient times performed in relation to idols. In modern idolatry, although the form and appearance of idols and the manner of performing rites before them have changed, the shirk (associating partners with Allah) that lies beneath them has by no means changed, and it remains in its same state. We must take note of this reality and not fall victim to deception in this matter.

For example, Allah's command is that a woman should adorn herself with chastity, dignity and nobility. But the command of "the homeland" is that, in order to obtain the maximum production, a woman should come out of the home and adopt the adornments of jahiliyya. She should become unclothed, work as a maidservant in hotels, just as the idol-worshipping "geisha" women do in Japan. Therefore, which deity is it whose commands are obeyed? Are the commands of Allah obeyed, or those of the deity of the homeland and the deity of production?

Allah's command is that the basis of society should be belief, that society should be founded on lā ilāha (there is no god), but the command of nationhood and homeland is that Islam's beliefs and concepts be negated from collective life, and that society be founded on nationalism or racism. Here too the same question arises: who is the deity? Allah, or the homeland and race?

Allah's command is that His Shari'ah must be observed. But a single human being rises up as a dictator, or a group of people rises up (the assembly), and says that this can never be. "The law shall be the law of the assembly." Now you tell me: is the assembly the deity, or is Allah, glorified is His majesty, the deity?

These are the examples according to which the whole world is operating, and all of humanity is familiar with these examples and has gone astray. This is the idol-worship that is current and prevalent at this time, and these are today's idols. In comparison with the ancient idols, these modern idols have come to the fore. The only difference is that these idols are not visible, whereas those earlier idols were embodied and could be seen, but there is no difference in their reality.

The address of the Qur'an was to that simple idol-worship, to the ancient jahiliyya, which was completely clear. The Qur'an was awakening them from that lack of understanding. It was unworthy of a creature like man. Therefore, while commenting on their condition, the Qur'an gave them an example in which their mental states were made manifest: ﴿Do they associate with Him those who create nothing and are themselves created? And they cannot give them help, nor can they help themselves.﴾ How foolish these people are, that they make partners with God those who create nothing, but are themselves created. They cannot help them, nor can they even help themselves.

The Qur'an explains to them that the one who is the Creator is the one who deserves to be worshipped, and none of the deities they worship is the creator of this world; rather, they themselves are creatures. What justification is there for these people to worship these idols? For what reason do they make these idols partners in their souls and in their children?

The argument and proof of creation, just as it was a proof against the ancient jahiliyya, is likewise a proof against the modern jahiliyya. Which of the new idols that modern jahiliyya has fashioned created the heavens and the earth, such that people make them partners in their lives, their children and their wealth? Then, among these modern idols, which idol is one that could become master of benefit and harm?

If human intellect and thought were left free, it would completely reject this situation and would never accept it. It is the desires and inclinations of people, and external misguidance and deceit, that cause people to worship these modern idols. It is external influences and conspiracies that are turning people back, apostate, to this modern jahiliyya, and in this modern form are afflicting them with shirk and idol-worship. Therefore, people worship the idols that they themselves have fabricated (nation, race, homeland), and these idols are not masters even of people's benefit and harm.

The humanity of the modern age is in need of being addressed with the teachings of the Qur'an, just as those teachings were conveyed to it in earlier ages. There is a need to lead humanity out of jahiliyya and bring it to Islam. It must be brought out from darkness into light, and its intellect and consciousness must be liberated from this modern jahiliyya. It must be freed from this modern intellectual filth in the same way that Islam freed humanity centuries ago. In the words the Qur'an used for the ancient jahiliyya, there is also an indication that no human being can be made a deity. Please reflect once more:

"How foolish these people are, that they make partners with God those who create nothing, but are themselves created. They cannot help them, nor can they help themselves."

In the forms of these verses, the masculine plural forms and the pronoun "we" indicate that some of these idols were rational beings. We cannot say that the Arabs regarded some human beings as their deities in the sense that they worshipped them and performed rites of servitude before them. Rather, they made human beings deities in the sense that in collective affairs they obeyed their customs and instructions, and in their disputes they decided according to their laws. That is, in terms of earthly sovereignty, the Qur'an calls this very act shirk, and it makes no distinction between this figurative idol-worship and their embodied idol-worship. From the Islamic point of view, both are shirk. In this very sense, the Jews and Christians had made their religious leaders lords, in that they accepted and regarded their rulings and laws as if they were the rulings and laws of God, although none of them performed rites of servitude before them as they would before God. Yet the Qur'an described this act of theirs as shirk and as departure from monotheism. This is the departure from tawhid (monotheism) that is referred to in "lā ilāha illā Allāh Muḥammad rasūl Allāh," and this expression is precisely in accordance with the point we made above about the modern jahiliyya. According to the ahadith, the Messenger (ﷺ) explained the verse "They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah" in exactly this way.

The shirk mentioned above in the form of the story of the couple was in fact the subject of every kind of shirk. The purpose was to organize against idol-worship those people whom the Qur'an was addressing, and to make clear to them that the idol-worship in which they were involved is extremely weak and foolish: they were taking as deities things that cannot create anything, but are themselves created. Not only can those things not bring you benefit or harm, but they are not even masters of their own benefit and harm. Whether these things are living humans or dead idols, all of them alike can neither create nor have power to give help to anyone. Since the purpose of the Qur'an in this parable was only this, after the parable the direction of address turns directly to the mushrikūn (polytheists) of Makkah. Abandoning the narrative style, it suddenly begins to address them directly. The subject is still the same: first there was parable and story, and now there is direct address concerning the reality of those deities.

...

As we have stated earlier, the idol-worship of the polytheists of Arabia was a simple idol-worship, completely weightless on the scale of human reason, even if that reason was extremely primitive and of the Stone Age. For this reason the Qur'an directs the intellect to the fact that the shirkī ideas they regard as true about these idols are a proof of extreme foolishness.

Just consider your idols: apparently they cannot walk, they have no hands to grasp with, they have no eyes to see, and they have no power of hearing in their ears. Whereas you have organs in which these faculties exist, so why do you worship idols that have lifeless organs?

Sometimes idol-worshippers say that by these idols their real intention is to indicate some bonds of respect or the ancestors. The Qur'an says: they too are like you, servants and creatures of Allah, and they themselves never created anything, nor do they now, nor do they have power over benefit and harm, nor over their own benefit and harm.

Since among the Arabs idol-worship was both outward idol-worship and an allusion to earlier human beings, the Qur'an used for them the forms of rational beings, and thus addressed them as men. The pronoun for rational beings points to the personalities toward which there was an allusion in the idols. Sometimes the idols were directly spoken of, and sometimes it was said, "they are servants like you." In any case, both kinds of shirk are false in the Islamic view. The Qur'an strives to liberate humanity from this humiliation, and it leads humanity to the heights of the tawhid that is worthy of humankind.

At the end of this discussion, critique and refutation, Allah instructs the Messenger (ﷺ) to challenge them. He should also challenge these helpless deities and place before them, in explicit words, his clear and pure views.

﴿Say, "Call upon your partners, then plot against me and give me no respite. Indeed, my protector is Allah, who has sent down the Book, and He takes charge of the righteous. And those you invoke besides Him cannot help you, nor can they help themselves."﴾ ﴿And if you call them to guidance, they do not hear. And you see them looking at you, but they do not see.﴾

Say to them, O Prophet: "Call upon your associates, then all of you together plot against me and give me no respite. My helper and supporter is the God who sent down this Book, and He supports the righteous. In contrast, those whom you invoke apart from God can neither help you nor help themselves. Moreover, if you ask them to come to the right path, they cannot even hear you. It appears to you that they are looking toward you, but in reality they see nothing."

This is the message that every caller to the truth must present before any jahiliyya. And the Prophet (ﷺ) delivered it exactly as his Lord had commanded him, and in his own time he challenged the idol-worshippers and their idols in this same manner.

﴿Say: Call your partners, then plot against me and give me no respite.﴾ O Prophet, tell them: "Call your associated partners, then all of you together plot against me and give me no respite." The Prophet (ﷺ) flung this challenge in the faces of them and their idols, and said: "Whatever plots you can devise against me, carry them out. As much as you are able, leave nothing undone; give me no respite." He gave this challenge in the manner of one who is certain of his purpose, and who has complete trust in his Creator and God, and who, against the conspiracies and powers of his opponents, relies upon his Lord.

﴿Indeed, my protector is Allah, who has sent down the Book, and He takes charge of the righteous.﴾ My helper and supporter is the God who has sent down this Book, and He supports the righteous.

He made it known on whom he relies: he relies only on Allah, who sent down the Book. From the descent of this Book it became known what his intention is: that the Messenger should present to people this Book, which contains the truth. It also became known that Allah has decreed that He will raise this truth high and make it dominant over every falsehood and the people of falsehood, and that He Himself will take charge of the protection and guardianship of the servants who call to it and who trust in Allah.

After the Messenger of Allah, in every age and every land, this will be the slogan and the goal of those who carry the call. "Say, O Prophet, to them: 'Call your associated partners, then all of you together plot against me and give me no respite. My helper and supporter is the God who sent down this Book, and He supports the righteous.'" Every bearer of the call has the duty not to rely on the supports and trusts of the world, and not to give any importance to the trusts of the world.

The reality is that the supports of the world have no importance; they are very frail supports, even if worldly supports are extremely strong and appear to be extremely powerful. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿O mankind, a parable is presented, so listen to it. Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah could not create a fly, even if they gathered together for that purpose. And if the fly should snatch away from them something, they could not retrieve it from it. Weak are the seeker and the sought.﴾ O people, a parable is given; listen to it carefully. Those deities you call upon besides Allah, if they all came together, could not even create a fly. Indeed, if a fly snatched something from them, they could not recover it. Weak is the one who seeks and weak is the one who is sought.

﴿The example of those who take protectors besides Allah is like the spider, which takes a home; and indeed, the weakest of homes is the home of the spider, if only they knew.﴾ The example of those who have taken guardians other than Allah is like the spider that builds a house, and the weakest of all houses is the house of the spider. If only these people had knowledge.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 7, verses 189–198 (part 3 of 3):

The one who calls to Allah places his trust in Allah. So what place do other guardians and supports retain apart from Allah? And what room do they have in the consciousness of such a person? Although other people may have the power to harm the caller, if anyone harms the caller, it also happens by the permission of Allah, who is the caller's Protector. It is not that Allah is powerless to support the caller, nor that Allah has withdrawn His support from the caller. Nor is it the case that Allah cannot help His friends. Why, then, has Allah granted the opponents of the callers this respite and permission to harm the friends of Allah? For their training, for separating the genuine from the counterfeit, and for making them (the believers) steadfast. Also, Allah lets the enemies of Allah have a long rope, grants them respite, and allows them to take the harshest measures and plans against them.

There was an occasion when Hadrat Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (رضي الله عنه) was being harmed by the polytheists of Makkah, and they were striking him with the soles of their shoes. They inflicted so many blows on his face that his eyes could no longer be seen on his blessed face. This supreme personality on this earth, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), was being subjected to such merciless torture, yet throughout this entire torment he kept saying, "O Allah, how forbearing You are! O Allah, how forbearing You are!" He believed wholeheartedly that the command of the Lord was at work behind this harm. He was fully certain that the Lord was not powerless to destroy these enemies of His. He also believed that Allah does not leave His friends without support.

When the polytheists tortured Hadrat Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, they did so merely because he began reciting the Qur'an in the shade of the Ka'bah, in front of a gathering of the polytheists. They beat him so severely that his head began to spin and it became difficult for him to stand. After this cruel torture he would say, "By Allah, these people were never more bearable and easier for me than they are now." He knew that these were the enemies of Allah, and he was also certain that the enemy of Allah is very easy and insignificant for a believer. Therefore, the friends of Allah should not give any weight to the enemies of Allah.

Hadrat Abdullah ibn Maz'un was under the protection of 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, a polytheist. He removed himself from 'Utbah's protection, because he did not like to live comfortably under the polytheist's protection while persecution of other Muslims continued. When he threw off 'Utbah's protection with contempt, the polytheists fell upon him. They inflicted such torture on him that he lost one eye. 'Utbah would watch him being tortured and invite him to return to his protection. He would say, "I am under the protection of a Being who is more powerful than you." 'Utbah would say, "O brother, your eye was safe and free from the harm that has befallen it." He would reply, "Not at all, by Allah! My other eye also longs that it too should be struck with what is better for it in the way of Allah." He knew that Allah's protection is stronger than the protection of servants. He was certain that the Lord would never leave him without support, even though He subjects the self to these hardships to exalt it and to test it. How well he said, "By Allah, my other eye also deserves this situation which is better for it in the way of Allah."

These are the examples of the group that was trained in the school of Hadrat Muhammad (ﷺ) and was raised under the shade of Allah's guidance.

O Prophet, say to them: "Call your associates, then plot against me together, and give me no respite. My supporter and helper is Allah, who has revealed this Book, and He supports the righteous."

What was the result of this persecution? They endured this torment from the polytheists. They trusted in Allah, who had revealed the Book and who is the supporter of the righteous servants.
