The prophethoods of that time were also meant for particular regions and short periods, and their address was also limited to those who were present at the time. The prophethoods did not apply to later generations who had not seen those miracles. Those miracles were beneficial only for those people, and were not beneficial for those who came later and had not seen them. "What is heard is not like what is seen."

The Qur'an is so much of a miracle that no material miracle is a miracle in comparison to it. Whatever era one takes, and from whatever aspect one takes it, the Qur'an is astonishing. It is a miracle not only for a particular time or a particular generation, but is a miracle until the Day of Resurrection. It is a miracle in its words and in its meanings.

Consider its verbal and expressive aspect. The eloquence that existed among the Arabs in the age of jahiliyyah was, from their perspective, a clearly evident miracle. The style of speech to which they were accustomed, and in which they took pride among themselves in their markets and festivals, consider how it was a miracle from that aspect at that time, and is so today as well. No human being has been able to reach those heights until now, although the Qur'an challenged them at that time and is challenging them today. Among humans, those who are acquainted with the expressions of speech, and who understand how far human beings can reach in eloquence, know well that in its style of expression the Qur'an is a miracle and will remain a miracle. And these experts in style, whether or not they have believed in the Qur'an, acknowledge its inimitability, because before the principles on which this challenge is based, believers and disbelievers are equal. The elders of Quraysh used to read the challenges of the Qur'an day and night, but they had no means of answering them, even though they denied the Qur'an and did not like it at all. Even today every ignorant person finds these challenges of the Qur'an, but has no means of answering them, and it will be so in the future as well.

Along with this verbal and stylistic inimitability, this Book has miraculous effects on human nature, provided that the barriers between human nature and this Book are removed even for a moment. Those people whose hearts have become black and upon whose hearts layers of the dust of jahiliyyah have settled, sometimes their hearts too shake off the dust and rise up, and when they hear the Qur'an, their hearts too are agitated, and their hearts are enveloped in the enchanting effects of the Qur'an.

Many people speak, and the speech of some contains principles, doctrines, various ideas and tendencies, but the effect of the Qur'an on human nature is a unique effect. Its particular effects fall upon human hearts when it is recited. The truth is that the Qur'an completely takes into its grip those who read it. The Quraysh used to advise their followers, who were easily swayed, and in fact they were advising themselves as well: ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during its recitation, so that perhaps you may overcome.﴾ (41:26)

They felt the effects of the Qur'an within their own souls, and they thought that they would not be able to resist these effects. Today, the great ones of our modern age also want to divert people's attention away from the Qur'an, but the Qur'an is still dominant and effective today. If one or two verses of the Qur'an are placed within human speech, they clearly appear distinct. Their effect is separate from other speech. Their effect on human sensibility reaches to the depths, and through it human speech appears completely different and separate, even though human speech has been adorned with great artifice and embellishment.

Now consider the subject and content of this Book. For discussion of the content and subjects of the Qur'an, the brief pages of Fi Zilal al-Quran have no room, because in terms of subject and meaning it is a boundless ocean. How can it be said within such brief pages?

In any case, the Qur'an has taken every aspect of man and human personality as its subject of discussion. It has taken human personality from every direction. In a single flow it speaks on the various aspects of human personality. Through every door of human personality this Book enters. Every thought among human thoughts and every emotion among human emotions has been made a subject.

When the Qur'an discusses the matters of the human self, its method of discussion is quite unique. It takes what the human mind, heart and nature perceive, brings its clear form before him, and gives its judgment on that subject with regard to human natural needs. This Book awakens the hidden powers of man and places them on the healthy path.

Then the method of the Qur'an is so wise that it takes human nature and leads it upward step by step, stage by stage, with great gradualness, with gentleness and ease. Man advances on this path with great zeal and enthusiasm; his path appears to him completely clear and plain, and he progresses as a person climbs one step at a time to a height and reaches the summit of heights without any hardship. And, proceeding on this path, he advances with knowledge and insight, zeal and enthusiasm, steadfastness and certainty, confidence and hope, and with comfort and tranquillity, keeping before him the whole truth of this universe, whether great or small.

The wondrous method and manner of the Qur'an is that it awakens human nature from a point about which no one can imagine how awake and sensitive that point is, or in which direction human nature is more capable of acceptance. Therefore human nature awakens precisely in that aspect and responds to Qur'anic guidance with enthusiasm, because the One who revealed this Qur'an is also the Creator of that nature. And for this reason Allah is nearer to man than his jugular vein. (cf. 50:16)

The method or content that the Qur'an presents in this style and method has such vast aspects that speech and discourse cannot encompass them. That is why it has been said: ﴿Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord are exhausted, even if We brought the like of it as a supplement.﴾ (18:109) And in another verse it is said: ﴿And if whatever trees are on the earth were pens, and the sea, with seven more seas added to it as ink, the words of Allah would not be exhausted.﴾ (31:27)

The writer of these lines, by the grace and kindness of Allah, has been engaged in the very deep study of the Qur'an for fifteen years. During this period he has cast his gaze over the various aspects of the subjects of this Book. In the various fields of knowledge acquired by man, where the reach of the human mind has extended and where human minds have not yet reached, I have also studied what humans have written as their own human effort regarding some aspects of these subjects. But I have found the truth that the bounty of the Qur'an is very general, vast and open. In comparison with it, human knowledge is a small lake; rather it is a small well or a hole; rather it is a pond that has become foul due to constant stagnation.

I cast an overall glance over this universe in the light of the Qur'an. I thoroughly studied its temperament, its nature, its creation and origin, its development, and the hidden secrets behind it. I contemplated the hidden and concealed attributes of this universe, and especially its living creatures. I also particularly studied the writings that man has written about this universe through his knowledge and experience. (For details see the book Khasa'is al-Tasawwur al-Islami and others.)

Then I carefully studied the existence of man, his psychology, his origin, his development, his hidden capacities, the spheres of his activities, the structure of his existence, his impressions, his inclinations, and his other conditions and secrets about which humans have also provided some information, such as the sciences of calculation and the various topics of biology, human beliefs and religions, and their collective philosophies. (See Islam wa Mushkilat al-Hadarah and others.)

Then I studied the systems of human life as well. In these systems I studied human activities, and I deeply studied human relations and disagreements within them. I also reflected on schemes for renewing and reforming human relations. And I studied, regarding them, those topics about which many schools of thought and on which humans have worked, such as political, economic and social issues. (For details see my book Nahw Mujtama' Islami.)

After studying human sciences and arts in all these fields and on all these subjects, when I read the Qur'an carefully, I found that there are very many verses on these subjects in which detailed guidance is given, and that the treasure of knowledge in the Qur'an is extremely real, solid and vast.

While reflecting on these subjects for many years, I never felt the need to seek help from anything outside the Qur'an. Yes, the circumstances and hadith of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) are needed in any case, because that speech too is among the traces of the Word of Allah. What humans have said on these subjects apart from the Qur'an and Sunnah is extremely weak and deficient. Even if it is correct, it is still not satisfying. The writer of these lines found the Qur'an detailed and satisfying in comparison with every human writing.

What I am saying, I say after a long period of reflecting on the Qur'an and, in the need to seek solutions to human problems in the light of the Qur'an and Sunnah, after practically living in the shade of the Qur'an. I am not adding anything to your knowledge of the Qur'an by describing its excellences, nor can all humans add to its perfection by praising it.

The truth is that in the world there is a most unique group and a precious generation, namely the Companions (ṣaḥābah) (may Allah be pleased with them). Their training, their knowledge and their guidance had this Book as their source. This very Book had made them. After them, no group of comparable standard has been produced among humans, nor is any group comparable to the Companions known to us in human history before them. It was they who brought about a deep and vast revolution in human history. But this great revolution and this great event have not really been studied deeply by humans.

The community of the Companions (Sahabah) brought about a revolution in human history for which there is no parallel in the whole of human history, and in truth it sprang from the same source, namely the Qur'an. Among all the miracles that were manifested at the hands of the Messengers from Adam (peace be upon him) to Muhammad (ﷺ), this miracle, the miracle of the great revolution in humanity, is superior to all those miracles and outweighs them, because it is a real miracle that can be examined and observed. In short, the community of the Companions was a unique miracle in human history.

The first formation of Islamic society was from this unique community. After that, for more than a thousand years, Islamic society remained alive and radiant, and the laws of the Islamic Shari'ah were enforced in it. This society remained bound by Islamic values, the Islamic standards of good and evil, and Islamic guidance and indications. This thousand-year Islamic society was in truth another historical miracle, especially when a historical observer compares this Islamic society with other human societies. Those other jahili societies may claim superiority over the Islamic society in material progress, but they cannot claim superiority in human civilization and culture.

The truth is that people today are immersed in modern jahiliyyah (ignorance). They derive their psychological needs, their collective needs, and the well-being of their lives from some source other than the Qur'an. Just as the followers of the jahiliyyah of Arabia demanded extraordinary signs and miracles apart from the Noble Qur'an. The simple ignorant people of Arabia could not see this great miracle of the Qur'an because they were afflicted with very deep ignorance and unawareness, and their personal interests also contradicted the teachings of the Qur'an. Therefore, they were deprived of attaining the wonders of the Qur'an.

As for modern jahiliyyah, it is deprived of seeing the wonders of the Qur'an not because of ignorance but because of the arrogance of its educational standards, although these doors of knowledge were opened by Allah Himself. However, they have confined knowledge within the material world. Moreover, under the human needs that the world faces today, human life has become very highly organized in order to fulfil those needs, and the worshippers of modern jahiliyyah are afflicted with extreme pride in terms of organization and formation. There is no doubt that because of many experiments, the life of the modern age has become very organized and firm, and it has also become complicated because of diverse needs. And people who are devoted to this modern life have become afflicted with pride. Furthermore, for fourteen hundred years the Jewish and Zionist lobby has been afflicted with enmity towards Islam, and in these fourteen hundred years it has not suspended its conspiracies against Islam and the Qur'an even for a moment. The policy of the Jews has been to make Muslims heedless of their Book, so that they do not take guidance from it, because the Jews and Christians have learned through their long experience that as long as Muslims continue to follow the guidance of the Qur'an, these people cannot gain control over them. But there is one condition for this: Muslims must hold fast to the Book of Allah in the way that the incomparable community of the early era, the community of the Companions, held it firmly. It must not be that they recite its verses well and recite them beautifully, while their practical lives are entirely contrary to its teachings. This is a most wicked and reprehensible conspiracy of the Jews, and it is continually being put into action against Muslims. The final result of this conspiracy is the condition in which those nations are afflicted which bear Muslim-like names, although they cannot become Muslims until they enforce the Divine Shari'ah in their individual and collective lives. In short, the result of this very conspiracy is that the traces of this religion are being erased everywhere. Opportunities are not provided to Muslims to organize their lives according to the guidance of the Qur'an, and to make the Qur'an the arbiter in all their differences and disputes as the Muslims of the early generations used to act according to the guidance of the Qur'an, making their laws and principles in the light of the Qur'an.

Today the condition is that the people of the Qur'an have abandoned the Qur'an. Apart from the beauty of recitation and proper chanting, they do not study it, and they use it for nothing except amulets and charms. This condition is due to a deep and reprehensible Zionist and Crusader conspiracy, due to the ignorance and pride in knowledge of Muslims, and due to the general corruption of Muslims' thought and outlook.

In the ancient era, the worshippers of jahiliyyah used to keep people heedless of it in such a way that instead of listening to it and reflecting upon it, they demanded the occurrence of events that break the customary order. In the modern age, the ignorant keep Muslims away from this Qur'an, and they put in their hands Qur'ans of their own making, and through the modern means of communication and media they impose their own constructed ideas on people's minds. Regarding this Qur'an, the decision of the All-Knowing, the All-Aware is this:

﴿This is a source of insight from your Lord, and a guidance and a mercy for a people who believe.﴾ (Al-A'raf 7:203)

And since this is the station of the Qur'an, guidance is given directly as to what your attitude towards the Qur'an should be:

﴿When the Qur'an is recited, listen to it attentively and remain silent, that you may receive mercy.﴾ (Al-A'raf 7:204)

The Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 7, verse 204:

This surah concludes with this verse, and the opening of the surah had begun in a way that alluded to this same Book. ﴿Kitab unzila ilayka fala yakun fi sadrika harajun minhu litundhira bihi wa dhikra lil-mu'minin.﴾ ﴿This is a Book revealed to you; so, O Prophet, let there be no hesitation in your heart about it. Its revelation has the purpose that you warn by means of it, and that it be a reminder for the believing people.﴾

When the Qur'an is being recited, there are differing reports about remaining silent at that time. Some scholars say that this refers to the Qur'an recited in the prayer, where the imam recites aloud, and so it is obligatory upon the follower (muqtadi) to remain silent. When he is listening to the imam in an audibly recited prayer, it is prohibited for him to recite. *La yunazi'ul-imam al-Qur'an*: let there be no dispute with the imam over the Qur'an. This narration has been related by Imam Ahmad and the compilers of the Sunan. Imam Tirmidhi called it a hadith hasan, and Abu Hatim al-Razi called it a hadith sahih. They related, through al-Zuhri and Abu al-Ukaysha al-Laythi, from Abu Hurayrah, that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had finished an audibly recited prayer, he addressed the people and asked: "Has anyone among you recited along with me just now?" A man said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah, I did." The Messenger (ﷺ) said, "I say, what is wrong with me that I am being disputed with regarding the Qur'an?" After that, the people refrained from reciting along with the Messenger (ﷺ) in the audibly recited prayers, because they had heard this guidance of the Messenger (ﷺ). Similarly, Ibn Jarir in his tafsir also related, through Abu Dawud Ibn Abu al-Hind and Bashir Ibn Jabir, a narration from Ibn Mas'ud that he heard some people reciting along with the imam; so when he had finished the prayer, he said: "Has the time not yet come for you to understand? Has the time not come for you to use your intellect and obey the command of Allah? Allah says: ﴿When the Qur'an is recited to you, listen to it attentively and remain silent.﴾"

Some scholars hold the view that this verse actually gives Muslims guidance that they should not adopt the attitude of the polytheists, who, when the Prophet (ﷺ) recited the Qur'an in the prayer, would come and listen. Therefore some of them said to others: "Do not listen to this Qur'an, but rather make noise during its recitation, so that perhaps you may prevail." ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise in it, that perhaps you may overcome.﴾ In response to this, this verse was revealed: ﴿When the Qur'an is recited, listen to it attentively and remain silent.﴾ Imam al-Qurtubi says that it was revealed concerning the prayer. He related reports on this matter from Abu Hurayrah, Ibn Mas'ud, Jabir, al-Zuhri, Ubayd Allah Ibn Umayr, Ata and Sa'id Ibn al-Musayyib.

Allamah Ibn Jarir has also related its occasion of revelation. He related from Ibn Mas'ud, through the chain of Abu Kurayb, Abu Bakr Ibn Ayyash, Asim, and Musayyab Ibn Rafi', that some of us used to greet one another in the prayer, and so this verse was revealed: ﴿When the Qur'an is recited, listen to it attentively and remain silent, that perhaps you may be shown mercy.﴾

In its explanation, Imam al-Qurtubi says that Muhammad Ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said that when the Messenger (ﷺ) recited the Qur'an, the people would repeat it after him; when he recited *Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim*, they too would say the same. They would do this throughout al-Fatihah and the entire surah. This practice continued for a time, and then this verse was revealed: ﴿When the Qur'an is recited to you, listen to it attentively and remain silent, that perhaps you may be shown mercy.﴾ From this it is understood that remaining silent means not reciting aloud, as those people used to do in obedience to the Messenger of Allah.

This was the view of Imam al-Qurtubi concerning this verse. Qatadah says that when the prayer was taking place, a person would come and ask the worshippers how many rak'ahs they had prayed and how many remained. Then this verse was revealed. A similar report is transmitted from Mujahid, that Muslims would speak during the prayer as the need arose, so this verse was revealed: *la'allakum turhamun*. As for those who hold that this command is restricted to the recitation that takes place in the prayer, their argument is based on a narration of Ibn Jarir. He related from Humayd Ibn Mas'adah, Bishr Ibn Jurayri, and Talhah Ibn Ubayd Allah Ibn Umayr that this person said: "I saw Ubayd Allah Ibn Umayr and Ata Ibn Abi Rabah debating with one another while a reciter was reciting the Qur'an. Do you not listen attentively, and do you not become deserving of what Allah has promised, namely *la'allakum turhamun*?" They looked at me, then returned to their discussion. I repeated my words a second time; they again looked at me and then returned to their discussion. I repeated my words a third time, and they looked at me again and then returned to their discussion. Then I repeated my words a third time, and they looked at me and said: "This concerns the prayer." ﴿When the Qur'an is recited, listen to it attentively and remain silent, that perhaps you may be shown mercy.﴾

After quoting this narration, Allamah Ibn Kathir says that Sufyan al-Thawri, Abu Hashim and Isma'il Ibn Kathir related from Mujahid the same narration that the verse ﴿When the Qur'an is recited, listen to it attentively﴾ concerns the prayer. Many people have related this same narration from Mujahid. Abd al-Razzaq related from al-Thawri that if recitation is taking place outside of the prayer and someone is speaking, there is no harm in it.

Some scholars say that just as this command applies in the prayer, the same command applies to the Friday sermon (khutbah) and the two Eid sermons. Sa'id Ibn Abi Jubayr, Mujahid, Ata, Amr Ibn Dinar, Yazid Ibn Aslam, Qasim Ibn Mukhaymirah, Salamah Ibn Bassar, Shahr Ibn Hawshab and Abdullah Ibn al-Mubarak also held this view. However, al-Qurtubi says: "This position is weak, because the portion of the Qur'an within the sermons is small, and silence is obligatory in all of them." Ibn al-'Arabi and al-Naqqash have said that this verse is Meccan, and in Mecca there was neither a sermon nor an obligatory Friday prayer.

Imam al-Qurtubi says that the scholars of tafsir are unanimous that listening attentively to the Qur'an and remaining silent is required both in the obligatory prayer and in non-obligatory prayer. In linguistic terms, listening to the Qur'an and remaining silent is obligatory in every matter, unless there is a specific proof.

Among the reports on the occasions of revelation mentioned earlier, there is nothing that indicates that this verse is restricted to the prayer, or that there is a distinction between obligatory and non-obligatory prayer. For the ruling rests upon the generality of the words of the verse; one does not look at the specific occasion on which the verse was revealed. The closest view is that this verse is to be taken as general, and that no text should be regarded as restricting it. What is more fitting to the greatness and reverence of the Qur'an is that wherever the Qur'an is recited, silence should be observed, and since it is the speech of Allah, reverence for Allah lies in this as well. When Allah Himself says that when the Qur'an is being recited, you should remain silent and listen, and that in this lies hope of mercy for you, then there is no proof that this practice should be restricted to the prayer; rather, wherever the Qur'an is recited, it should be treated in this same manner. The soul of a person should turn wholeheartedly toward it, and this courtesy and reverence is the guarantee that a person will be shown mercy in this world and the next.

The truth is that by turning away from and neglecting the Qur'an, people have fallen into a great loss. Sometimes a person listens carefully to a single verse, and as a result strange and wonderful impressions are imprinted upon his heart and mind, and the doors of understanding and action open for him. He attains tranquility of heart, joy and spiritual states, and a great change arises in his thinking and conduct; and these effects and this distinction can be grasped only by one who has tasted them.

Continuous study of the Qur'an, reflection upon it and contemplation, not merely recitation with melody, produces deep reflection and contemplation in a person's heart and vision. A person is granted a highly far-reaching power of perception and is inspired with the most certain knowledge. Vitality and a power of initiative arise within him; he becomes a possessor of a resolute, positive outlook and a firm determination. These understandings are not attained through any other discipline or any other means of knowledge apart from contemplation of the Qur'an.

Through the midst of Qur'anic concepts, a person comes to know the realities of this universe. He discovers and unveils new realities about life. He acquires a clear, deep, precise and profound awareness of the realities of human life, human needs, human temperament, and human nature and disposition, and this awareness is obtained through purely Qur'anic worship and rulings. A person who has studied the Qur'an deals with this universe and with human life in a very different spirit, and his way of acting toward this universe and toward humanity is not what it is for a person whose upbringing has taken place only within the atmosphere of merely human learning and knowledge.

This atmosphere is the atmosphere of hope for Allah's mercy, and it is the same in prayer and outside prayer. Therefore, we cannot restrict this atmosphere of Allah's mercy to the prayer on any grounds, and the view that is correct is the one transmitted by al-Qurtubi.

This surah ends with the instruction to turn towards the remembrance of Allah, whether it is in the prayer or outside it, in ordinary circumstances.

Ibn Kathir says: "Allah commands that He be remembered at the beginning of the day, at the end of the day, and with great frequency. In another place He commands that He be glorified and worshipped at these times: ﴿So glorify your Lord with His praise, before the rising of the sun and before its setting﴾. This command was given at a time when the five prayers had not yet been made obligatory, on the night of the Isra'. It should be noted that this verse is Meccan, yet in this verse the words ghuduw and asal are used. Ghuduw means the first part of the day. Asal is the plural of asil, just as iman is the plural of yamin." The phrase tadarru'an wa khifyah means: remember Allah in your heart with utmost humility, fear and hope. Remember Him with the tongue as well, but not loudly. That is why it is said dun al-jahr min al-qawl, meaning in a low voice. The recommended way of remembering Allah is that it should not take the form of shouting and crying out. When the Companions asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), "Is our Lord near, so that we may call Him in a low voice, or is He far, so that we must call Him loudly?", Allah revealed these verses: ﴿And when My servants ask you about Me, say: I am near. I respond to the call of the caller when he calls upon Me﴾ (2:186).

In the Sahihayn (the two Sahihs of al-Bukhari and Muslim), there is a report from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari. He says that on one of the journeys, the people began to call upon Allah in a loud voice. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to them: "O people, keep your voices to yourselves. You are not calling upon one who is absent or deaf. The One you call upon is All-Hearing and near, and He is closer to any of you than the neck of his mount."

Ibn Kathir does not accept the view of Ibn Jarir and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam that this means that one who is listening to the Qur'an should remember Allah in a low voice. He says that they did not present any proof for their opinion. The reality is that it refers to the general remembrance of Allah by the servants morning and evening, so that they do not become heedless. This is why, in the mention of the angels at the end of the verse, it is said that they remain occupied in the remembrance of Allah night and day, and that they go forth in their worship and remembrance.

﴿Indeed, those who are with your Lord do not disdain His worship﴾ (7:206).

This is mentioned so that Muslims may follow them, obey Allah, remember Him abundantly, and perform worship.

From what Imam Ibn Kathir has written on this subject and the hadiths he has quoted, it becomes clear how the Qur'an was training the Muslims of the first era. The Prophet (ﷺ) too was continually training the Arabs psychologically and informing them of very subtle truths about the knowledge of their Lord, and was telling them what the reality of the universe spread around them was. From the record of the questions of these people and the answers from Allah and from the Messenger of Allah, it can be known how great and far-reaching a revolution was brought about in their thought and conduct. This was the astonishing achievement of the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of the Messenger. It was a great and far-reaching revolution, which was a source of mercy for these people. Would that people knew!

It is worth noting that the remembrance mentioned in these texts is not merely verbal remembrance. It refers to remembrance of the heart, because a remembrance that does not move the heart of the believer and the one who remembers, that does not affect his intuition and consciousness, and whose effect does not appear in a person's being and actions, and which is not performed with humility, supplication and fear, is not considered remembrance. In some circumstances it would even be regarded as disrespect towards the majesty of Allah. The meaning of remembrance is that a person remembers Allah with the utmost courtesy, the utmost humility, and the utmost fear and hope, and along with remembering Allah, he also contemplates Allah's greatness and majesty, and prays that he may be protected from Allah's wrath. Only through such remembrance can a person attain spiritual radiance.

When the tongue moves together with the conscience and the heart, and the lips accompany the spirit, this should be in such a way that there is no difference between humility and submissiveness. It should be in a very quiet voice, not in the form of shouting, clamour and tumult. Nor is a melodic or singing style appropriate, nor a theatrical or festive manner.

Let us cast another look at the verse: ﴿And remember your Lord within yourself, humbly and in fear, without loudness of speech﴾ (7:205). O Prophet, remember your Lord morning and evening, within your own self, with humility and fear, and with the tongue too, in a low voice.

The words bil-ghuduwwi wal-asal, "morning and evening", mean the times when the day rises and the final times of the day, in such a way that it covers both parts of the day. The heart of a person should be attached to Allah. The remembrance of Allah is not restricted to these times; the remembrance of Allah should be present in the heart and vision at all times. The constant watch of Allah should remain over the heart at every moment. These times have been specifically mentioned because at these times a notable change occurs on the pages of the universe: night gives way to day and day gives way to night. A sensitive person sees in his environment the changes and transformations in the great works of Allah. The outward conditions of this universe change. Allah knows well that at these times the heart and the self of a person are closer to acceptance. In the Qur'an, guidance to remember Allah is given many times at such times, when the universe too has an effect on the heart and vision of a person, and thus the heart of a person softens and becomes well prepared to establish a connection with the Divine Being. For example, in times of difficulty: ﴿So be patient over what they say, and glorify your Lord with His praise before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and glorify Him during parts of the night and at the ends of the prostrations﴾ (50:39–40). Be patient over what they say; glorify your Lord with His praise, glorify Him before the rising of the sun and before its setting. Glorify Him in the night too, and after the prostrations. ﴿And during the night, glorify Him, and at the ends of the day, that perhaps you may be pleased﴾ (20:130). And glorify during part of the night, and at the extremes of the day, perhaps you may be pleased.

﴿And remember the name of your Lord morning and evening, and prostrate to Him during part of the night, and glorify Him through a long night﴾ (76:25–26). Remember your Lord morning and evening, prostrate before Him during a part of the night, and glorify Him through a long night.

There is no reason here for us to say that the command to remember Allah at these times was revealed before the obligation of the prayer, whose times are known, and that now there is no need or command for remembrance at these times. This is because the remembrance being described here is broader than the prayer, and the times of this remembrance are not restricted to the times of the obligatory prayers.

This remembrance can take forms other than the prayer. It may be remembrance of the heart, or it may be with both the heart and the tongue. It is even more general than these forms. Constant awareness of Allah at all times, and the continuous presence of the majesty of Allah in the heart and vision, and in every state, whether openly or secretly, in small matters or great matters, in movement and in stillness, in intention and in actions, in short, remembering Allah in every condition, is the essence of these verses. The remembrance of morning and evening is specifically mentioned because at these times the heart and vision of a person are prepared for acceptance, and Allah knows that at these times human beings are affected by cosmic influences.

﴿And do not be among the heedless﴾ (7:205). That is, do not be among those who are heedless of the remembrance of Allah. Those upon whose lips and tongues the name of Allah does not come, and in whose heart and vision there is no contemplation of God, who do not remember Him in a way that the beating of the heart is attached to it, the result of which is that they do not walk on the paths on which Allah does not wish them to walk, and of which, if Allah were to see them, they would be ashamed. They take account of Allah in every matter, small and large. Such is the remembrance that is the meaning of these verses. If the remembrance of someone has no effect on his deeds and his conduct, and he does not follow Allah, then that remembrance is not remembrance, nor is it the remembrance required by this verse.

That is, remember Allah and do not be heedless of Him. Let your heart not be unaware that He is constantly watching. A person is in great need of his connection with Allah being maintained at every moment. Only in that case can he be protected from satanic whisperings. Allah says: ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan should come to you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is Hearing and Knowing﴾ (7:200). At the beginning of this surah there was a detailed account of the confrontation between Adam and Iblis. Then, throughout this surah, the story of the caravan of faith has been related, and the obstacles which the satans of jinn and men have continually placed in the path of this caravan have been described. For example, a detailed mention was made of the example of the person to whom Allah gave His signs, but who escaped from them. Satan pursued him and included him among the group of the misguided. At the end of the surah, mention was made of the incitement of Satan, and it was commanded that in such a state the remedy is that you take refuge in Allah. He is the Knower and the Hearer. In short, the Qur'an is a continuous and coherent discourse, and at its end it is commanded that you always remember Allah with the utmost humility, and beware of heedlessness. This command comes during a discourse in which Allah commands the Prophet (ﷺ) to make pardon and forgiveness his way: enjoin what is good, and turn away from the ignorant. Therefore, the remembrance of Allah is in reality the complement and final stage of the signs of the Islamic revolution's journey, and it is the provision by means of which the traveller can cross the most difficult stages.

Now Allah presents to the Muslims the example of the angels brought near (to Him), those upon whom Satan's enticement has no effect. This is because there is no deficiency in their creation, nor do they have appetites or inclinations. They are engaged day and night in the remembrance of Allah. In the worship of Allah they neither fall short nor become arrogant, although in the matter of worshipping and glorifying Allah, man is more in need of it than they are. Man's path has more difficulties, and Satan's enticement affects him quickly. Man can also commit ruinous negligence. Man's striving is also limited; if he does not have the provision of the remembrance of Allah, then reaching the destination is itself difficult for him.

...

Worship and the remembrance of Allah are among the fundamental methods of the religion of Islam. They are not merely a method of knowledge and recognition, nor are they connected with theological dialectics; rather, they are connected with conduct (suluk), action and practical movement. Through them, the practical world of man is meant to be changed. The roots of man's practical life lie within the self of people, and the treasures of the foundation of action lie within man. Practically bringing people out of jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance) and admitting them into the Islamic way (manhaj) is a difficult task, and it requires an extremely continuous struggle. Patience like that of Ayyub (Job) is needed against the difficulties of this path, while the strength of the caller (da'i) is limited. Therefore the caller needs additional strength alongside this limited power. This strength is not obtained merely through knowledge, recognition, proof and argument. Its source is worship, connection with Allah, and the help of Allah. This is the provision that never runs out, and this is the wellspring of help that is required on this long and dangerous path.

The beginning of this surah was with these words: "Kitab unzila ilayka" — "This is a Book that has been sent down to you. So let there be no constriction in your heart about it, (O Prophet). Its purpose of revelation is that you warn the deniers with it, and it is a reminder for the believers."

Throughout the surah, the stories of the caravan of the people of truth are related, and the messengers of Allah led this caravan in their respective times. The accursed Satan repeatedly blocked their way on the road. The satans among jinn and humans tormented them, the tyrants of this world inflicted oppression upon them, and the agents of the tyrannical (taghut) systems stood in their way. These were the people who, mounted upon the necks of people, were enslaving them.

Indeed, this is the provision of this path, and this is the equipment of the honored travelers of this road.
